Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

Surah Hud(1) begins with the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:
﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm, then set out in detail, from One Wise, Aware.( 1 )﴾: The verse begins with separated letters (huruf tawqifiyya) from among the letters with which some surahs of the Noble Qur'an begin. That is, each of these letters is pronounced on its own. The letter, as we know, has a name (ism) and a designated sound (musamma), and when we write or speak we write or pronounce the sound of the letter, not its name.
But some surahs of the Noble Qur'an begin with letters that we read by their names, while in other cases they are pronounced by their sounds.
If we wish to know the difference between the two, we read at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara "alif. lam. mim," although it is written: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim( 1 )﴾(2) [al-Baqara]. So we pronounce it with the sounds of the letters, contrary to our reading of the words of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Did We not expand(3) your breast for you?﴾ [al-Sharh], which we pronounce with the names of the letters... Why?
Because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard them in this way from Jibril (peace be upon him), and the Qur'an is originally something heard, and you do not recite the Qur'an unless you have heard the Qur'an; so that you learn how to read the separated letters by the names of the letters, and read the rest of the verses by the sounds of the letters.
In the past, before we memorised the Qur'an, we used to "correct the board" (tashhih al-lawh), meaning that a jurist (faqih) would read first so that he might teach us how to read before we memorised.
What tires people is that they want to read the Noble Qur'an without sitting with a jurist or listening to a reciter of the Qur'an.
We say to them: the Qur'an is not an ordinary book that you read. The Qur'an is a book with a distinctive character. The forms of the letters vary: sometimes we pronounce the name of the letter, and sometimes we read the sound of the letter.
The saying of the Truth, glorified be He, ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ at the beginning of Surat Hud makes us notice that, among the wonderful things about the openings of the surahs, which begin with these letters, is that the Qur'an is always built on continuity (wasl). You do not come to the end of a verse and stop; no, the whole Qur'an is connected, just as we read the words of God, glorified be He: ﴿Dark green(4)( 63 ) So which of the bounties(5) of your Lord will you two deny?( 65 ) In them are two fountains gushing(6)( 66 )﴾ [al-Rahman].
Although there is a pause between each verse and another, the verses are all built on continuity.
And at the end of Surat Yunus the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿...And He is the best of judges.( 109 )﴾ [Yunus].
If it were not connected, you would pronounce the final letter as sukun (pausal), but you read it with a fatha (accusative), because it is connected to what follows it (bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim).
And it is remarkable that although the openings of the surahs consist of letters built on continuity, we read each letter with a pause, so we do not say "alif lam mim" with the i'rab (grammatical vowelling) of "alif lam mim," but we say "alif lam mim."
Likewise, at the beginning of Surat Maryam we read "kaf ha ya ayn sad," and we do not read the letters with their grammatical vowelling, and this shows that it has a wisdom which we do not know.
In the Qur'an there are verses that begin with a single letter, such as the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder( 1 )﴾ [Sad], and the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an( 1 )﴾ [Qaf], and His saying, the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe(7)( 1 )﴾ [al-Qalam]. We note that the letter in this surah is not a verse, but you read the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Ha-Mim( 1 )﴾(8) [al-Shura], which is a verse, and likewise you read the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Ayn-Sin-Qaf( 2 )﴾ [al-Shura] as a verse, even though these are separated letters, and you read the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ayn-Sad( 1 )﴾ [Maryam] as a verse on its own.
And you read the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Ta-Ha( 1 )﴾ [Ta-Ha] as a verse on its own. Likewise you read the Truth: ﴿Ya-Sin( 1 )﴾ [Ya-Sin] as a whole verse.
You will also find ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad( 1 )﴾ [al-A'raf] as a verse, and ﴿Ta-Sin-Mim( 1 )﴾ [al-Shu'ara and al-Qasas] as a verse.
We also find ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra.. ( 1 )﴾ [al-Ra'd] joined to what follows it in a single verse.
And you read at the beginning of Surat al-Naml: ﴿Ta-Sin( 1 )﴾ joined to what follows it in a single verse.
So the matter has no fixed pattern. This means that for every situation and every letter there is a wisdom. Wisdom is found when we reflect on the material world in life, so we become aware of the lessons of God, glorified be He, in the perceptible signs of creation, and we find the proof of God's truthfulness in what we do not know.
An example of this: when a person stays in a luxury hotel, he finds a key for each room, and this key opens only the door of one room. But on each floor of the hotel there is a key held by the person in charge of the floor, called the "master of keys," and it opens all the rooms of the floor. They made this so that no guest could open another guest's room.
With scientific progress they have now given each room an electronic card: as soon as a person enters it from a particular slot in the door, the door opens. Each room has its own card, and also the floor manager of the hotel has one card that opens all the rooms of the floor.
When you read the openings of the surahs, understand that every verse has a key, and every letter in these openings may resemble a key; and if you do not have the key with the teeth that opens the door of the room, the surah will not open for you.
So the Book of God has keys, and we read separated letters as a verse, or we read them as part of a verse.
And before recitation you say: "I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan"(9), to free yourself from the distractions that contradict the method of the Speaker of the Qur'an; then you place the particular card, such as the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim( 1 )﴾ [al-Baqara]. Then the door of recitation opens for you.
Thus we know that there is a key, and that there is an opener.
Take the openings of the surahs as keys, and each key has a particular shape and cut; if you carry it to another surah, it will not open it.
Here the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, which consists of three letters, like ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, and it appears in five surahs of the Noble Qur'an: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim and al-Hijr.
But ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ is read as a verse, while here at the head of Surat Hud it is part of a verse, although you read it, like Surat Yunus, Surat Hud, Surat Yusuf and Surat Ibrahim, as a verse.
Likewise ( al-Mus ) is four letters which you read as a verse in Surat al-A'raf, and there are four letters at the beginning of Surat al-Ra'd, which you read as part of a verse in Surat al-A'raf.
So there is no rule for these letters that open the surahs; rather, each letter has a particularity whose secrets have not yet all been revealed(10), and for this reason some exegetes said: "God knows best what He intends."
Here the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm( 1 )﴾ [Hud]. God, glorified be He, says once of the Qur'an that it is a ﴿Book﴾, and once He says ﴿Qur'an( 61 )﴾ [Yunus].
The Qur'an is recited, and the Book is written; God willed this so that He might show you that the one who preserves the Qur'an has two places: the breasts (sudur) and the lines (sutur). If the breast strays, remember the line.
For this reason, when the early Muslims wished to collect the Qur'an and match what is in the breasts with what is in the lines, they established foundations for that delicate process, the most important of which was the necessity of two witnesses for every verse. They paused at the last two verses of Surat al-Tawba(12), and found only one witness, Khuzayma, and they accepted Khuzayma and wrote the two verses on his testimony, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had given him a distinction when he said of him: "Whoever is witnessed for by Khuzayma, his testimony suffices him"(13).
So the application of the description "Book" to the Qur'an is because it is written, and it is "Qur'an" because it is recited.
Writing in ancient times was not an easy matter; only what was precious was written, or because the Qur'an is a Book in that it was originally written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).
When the Truth, glorified be He, describes the Qur'an, saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm.. ( 1 )﴾ [Hud], the root ḥ-k-m(14) indicates a perceptible matter, namely the perfection of construction, such that corruption is prevented from it; there is no defect in it, no contradiction, no opposition and no collapse.
There must be geometric balance for every opening in a building, so that the openings in the building are not aligned on a single line, and cracks appear in the walls or the whole building collapses. This is the firmness of a building in the world of the perceptible. The Truth, glorified be He, willed to describe the Qur'an, which encompasses the whole method, as: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm.. ( 1 )﴾ [Hud]. So take from this firmness what prevents your corruption, because the Qur'an came in a form that prevents corruption within it; and when corruption is removed from it, there will be reform and righteousness.
If you look at the Noble Qur'an in the Preserved Tablet, you will find that it descended all at once, from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, and then revelation came afterwards according to the events that required rulings, and the Truth, glorified be He, scattered in the Qur'an rulings, distinctions and stars.
So the Qur'an was first made firm, then it was set out in detail(16).
For this reason the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm, then set out in detail.. ( 1 )﴾ [Hud].
The great divisions of the Qur'an are the surahs, and the small divisions are the verses. The Muslims, wishing to encourage memorisation of the Qur'an, divided it into thirty parts (juz'), each part into two halves (hizb), and each half into four quarters (rub'), but the detail that has come to us from the Qur'an is that it is surahs, and each surah is a collection of verses.
It may be that the meaning is that the Qur'an was made firm and set out in detail because it was sent down as a comprehensive method from God, glorified be He.
When you look at it you find it varied: at one time it speaks of belief and its summit; at another it speaks of prophethood and its prophetic procession, and miracles; at another it speaks of rulings; at another it speaks of stories, ethics and cosmic matters. And at another it speaks of the science of inheritance(17).
So it is detailed in wording or in meaning, and it deals with many meanings, and every meaning that belief requires, the summit of testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God; and it deals with particulars down to the finest details.
Or it means "firm in its descent," because it descended once to the lowest heaven, and then was set out in detail according to events. This is more conducive to the soul's attachment to each star of the Qur'an when it descends at the time it is needed.
When you prepare for yourself a small pharmacy at home, you may bring in all kinds of medicines, but if you get a headache you may search for aspirin tablets and not find them. But if you send to the large pharmacy, you will find the aspirin when you need it.
Likewise, when you are thirsty, you may open your home refrigerator and not find the water bottle even though it is in front of you, because of the eagerness of thirst.
So the descent of the Qur'an in stages, which God, glorified be He, willed, is so that the human soul may be refreshed while it loves to receive the Qur'an.
For this reason the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿And a Qur'an We have divided(18) that you might recite it to the people at intervals(19), and We have sent it down in gradual revelation( 106 )﴾ [al-Isra'].
It has come in the Qur'an on the tongue of the disbelievers: ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?.. ( 32 )﴾ [al-Furqan].
So the reply comes from the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿...Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have arranged it in measured arrangement( 32 )﴾ [al-Furqan].
Had the Qur'an been sent down once to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), people would not have attended to everything in it; but God, glorified be He, willed that the Qur'an be sent down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in stages(20), so that in every star there would be strengthening for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the different situations. The Messenger of God (ﷺ), and likewise his community after him, need many reinforcements according to the events that confront them. For this reason the Truth, glorified be He, said: ﴿...Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have arranged it in measured arrangement(21)( 32 )﴾ [al-Furqan].
So whenever the believers hear a star of the Qur'an, they are better able to understand it, memorise it, and apply the rulings that came in it.
God, glorified be He, did not send down one single verse, but sent down verses, as evidenced by the fact that whenever they brought up a ruling, He, glorified be He, sends down the truth regarding that ruling in greater detail; for this reason He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And they do not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and better explanation( 33 )﴾ [al-Furqan].
And if the Qur'an had descended all at once, how would it address their questions which came in the Qur'an: ﴿They ask you...

1 Surat Hud is the eleventh surah in the order of the surahs of the Qur'an, and it is Meccan according to al-Hasan and Ikrima and others. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatada said: except one verse, which is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day...(114)﴾ [Hud]. Its number of verses is 123.
It is named after the Prophet of God Hud (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Thamud. The name of the Prophet Hud is mentioned in it 5 times. It is mentioned in Surat al-Shu'ara verse 124, and in al-A'raf verse 65.
The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said of it: "Hud and its sisters have made me grey: al-Waqi'a, 'Amma yatasa'alun, and idha al-shams kuwwirat." Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (1/358).
Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah said in "Nawadir al-Usul": fear produces greyness, for fear stupefies the soul and dries the moisture of the body, and under every hair there is a source from which it sweats; when fear dries its moisture, the sources dry up, the hair dries and turns white, as you see green crops with their water: when their water goes, they dry and turn white.
So the soul is stupefied by the threat of God and the terrors of what news has come from God, and so it withers, and that threat and terror which came dry up its water, and from it greyness appears.
Surat Hud mentions the nations and what befell them of the swift punishment of God, so when people of certainty recite it, there appear before their hearts His kingdom and authority and the glances of His seizing His enemies; if they died of fear, it would be their due, but God, blessed and exalted is His name, is gentle with them in those moments so that they may read His speech. Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3319).
2 ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ is mentioned at the opening of six surahs: al-Baqara, Al 'Imran, al-'Ankabut, al-Rum, Luqman, and al-Sajda. It is counted as an independent verse.
3 That is, We expanded it in meaning, and removed from you constriction and worry. The intended meaning: We pleased you and gladdened you. Or it is the physical splitting of the breast. Or both together. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
4 Mudhammatan: black from the intensity of their greenness and the abundance of shade, and this is a metaphor for complete bliss (and it is a description of the two gardens mentioned in God's saying: ﴿And besides them are two gardens( 62 )﴾ [al-Rahman]).
5 Al-ala': the bounties, singular ili or ila (with kasra or fatha on the hamza). God said: ﴿...So remember the bounties of God that you may prosper( 69 )﴾ [al-A'raf], and God said: ﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you doubt?( 55 )﴾ [al-Najm]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].
6 Nadilatan: two springs gushing with water that do not cease; their water flows abundantly, and nadakha is an intensive form indicating abundance. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, p. 470] and [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
7 Yasturun: they write. From satara al-kitab, i.e., he made it into lines.
8 ﴿Ha-Mim﴾: mentioned at the opening of seven surahs: Ghafir, Fussilat, al-Shura, al-Zukhruf, al-Dukhan, al-Jathiya, and al-Ahqaf. It is counted as an independent verse, and God knows best its meaning. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]. They are called al-Hawamim.
9 God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan( 98 )﴾ [al-Nahl]. From 'Ata', who said: seeking refuge is obligatory for every recitation, in prayer or otherwise. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/165), Dar al-Fikr edition, and attributed to 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf and Ibn al-Mundhir.
10 Al-Suyuti said in "al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an" (3/21): "The preferred view regarding them is that they are among the secrets which none knows but God, the Exalted. From 'Amir al-Sha'bi: he was asked about the openings of the surahs and said: indeed every book has a secret, and the secret of this Book is the openings of the surahs."
Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (1/37): "The total of the letters mentioned at the openings of the surahs, with repetitions removed, is fourteen letters, namely: a l m s r k h y ' t s h q n; they are gathered in your saying: nass hakim qati' lahu sirr." 
11 What is meant here is the collection of the Qur'an in the time of Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him), after killing among the reciters of the Qur'an intensified in the battles. 'Umar advised him to collect the Qur'an, so he sent for Zayd ibn Thabit (may God be pleased with him) and said to him: "You are a young man of intelligence, we do not suspect you, and you used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so trace the Qur'an and collect it." Zayd began to collect it from palm-leaf stalks ('usub, i.e., palm fronds), flat white stones (likhaf), and the breasts of men. See al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an (1/165).

١٢ هاتان الآيتان هما: ﴿لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم (١٢٨) فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم (١٢٩)﴾ [التوبة]..

١٣ أخرجه الحاكم في مستدركه (al-Mustadrak) (٢/١٨) والطبراني في معجمه الكبير (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir) (٤/١٠١) من حديث خزيمة بن ثابت. قال الهيثمي في المجمع (٩/٣٢٠): "رجاله كلهم ثقات" (thiqat: trustworthy, reliable narrators)..

١٤ أحكم الأمر: أتقنه. قال تعالى: ﴿ثم يحكم الله آياته (٥٢)﴾ [الحج]، أي: يبينها ويجعلها متقنة مقنعة محكمة، وآيات محكمة: متقنة مقنعة واضحة، وقيل: محكمة غير منسوخة (mansukhah: abrogated, i.e., not superseded by later ruling) أو محكمة غير متشابهة (mutashabihah: ambiguous) فلا تحتاج إلى تأويل (ta'wil: interpretation beyond its apparent meaning)، قال تعالى: ﴿منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات (٧)﴾ [آل عمران]، وقال تعالى: ﴿فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة (٢٠)﴾ [محمد] أي: متقنة. [القاموس القويم]..

١٥ قال القرطبي في تفسيره (٤/٣٣٢٠): "أحسن ما قيل في معنى: ﴿أحكمت آياته (١)﴾ [هود] قول قتادة، أي: جعلت محكمة كلها لا خلل فيها ولا باطل، والإحكام منع القول من الفساد، أي: نظمت نظما محكما، لا يلحقها تناقض ولا خلل"..

١٦ فصل الشيء: جعله أقساما متميزة واضحة، قال تعالى: ﴿.. وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا (١٢)﴾ [الإسراء]، وقال تعالى: ﴿آيات مفصلات (١٣٣)﴾ [الأعراف] أي: معجزات مبينات واضحات، وقال تعالى: ﴿ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم (٥٢)﴾ [الأعراف]..

١٧ الفرائض (al-fara'id: the prescribed shares of inheritance): المعنى بها علم المواريث (mawarith: the science of inheritance)، أخذا مما فرضه الله لكل واحد من أصحاب الفروض (ashab al-furud: the sharers entitled to fixed portions)..

١٨ قرئت هذه الكلمة بقراءتين: فرقناه، فرّقناه (بتشديد الراء). فعلى القراءة الأولى فمعناه: فصلناه من اللوح المحفوظ (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz: the Preserved Tablet) إلى بيت العزة (Bayt al-Izzah: the House of Honour) من السماء الدنيا، ثم نزل مفرقا منجما على الوقائع إلى رسول الله ﷺ في ثلاث وعشرين سنة، قاله عكرمة عن ابن عباس.
وعلى القراءة الثانية فمعناه: أنزلناه آية مبينا مفسرا، قال ابن عباس أيضا. ولهذا قال: ﴿لتقرأه على الناس (١٠٦)﴾ أي: لتبلغه الناس وتتلوه عليهم: ﴿على مكث﴾ أي: مهل. ﴿ونزلناه تنزيلا﴾ أي: شيئا بعد شيء. تفسير ابن كثير (٣/٦٨)..

١٩ مكث: أقام في مكانه، وتفيد التأني وعدم العجلة. وقوله تعالى: ﴿لتقرأه على الناس على مكث (١٠٦)﴾ [الإسراء] أي: على مهل وتأن بغير عجلة في أزمنة متطاولة. وقال تعالى: ﴿فمكث غير بعيد فقال أحطت بما لم تحط به (٢٢)﴾ [النمل] أي: استمر الهدهد في غيبته مدة طويلة. وقال تعالى: ﴿وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض (١٧)﴾ [الرعد] أي: يبقى مدة طويلة فيها فيزيدها خصبا. وقال تعالى: ﴿امكثوا إني آنست نارا (١٠)﴾ [طه] أي: أقيموا في مكانكم منتظرين. [القاموس القويم]..

٢٠ منجما: مفرقا؛ لأن القرآن أنزل على سماء الدنيا جملة واحدة، ثم أنزل على النبي ﷺ آية آية، وكان بين أول ما نزل منه وآخره عشرون سنة. [لسان العرب، مادة: نجم] فنزول القرآن كان منجما حسب مقتضى حال الدعوة، فالآيات المكية تناولت العقيدة وتقويم العادات، وإعلاء القيم والتمهيد لعبادة الله، والآيات المدنية تناولت العبادات والمعاملات لإقامة صرح العدالة في المجتمع..

٢١ رتلناه ترتيلا: أنزلناه مرتلا منسقا مجودا حسن التأليف. [القاموس القومي] قال ابن منظور في اللسان: "أي: أنزلناه على الترتيل، وهو ضد العجلة والتمكث فيه"..

Therefore: the verses of the Book have been made firm and then made detailed, for a purpose, namely: that we worship none but Allah.

Worship (ʿibadah) is the worshipper's obedience to the one worshipped in what He commands and in what He forbids.

Thus we find that worship requires that there be an object of worship who has a command and has a prohibition. An object of worship that has no command and no prohibition does not deserve worship. Has anyone who worshipped an idol received from it a command or a prohibition?

Has anyone who worshipped the sun received from it a command or a prohibition?

Therefore, the word "worship" applied to anything other than Allah is false worship, because such objects of worship have no command and no prohibition, and beyond that there is no reward from them for an action that conforms to them or opposes them.

Worship without a method of "do" and "do not" does not exist, and worship for which there is no reward is not worship.

Here we must note that the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Do not worship except Allah...﴾ [Hud: 2] differs from His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Worship Allah...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 72].

Had the messengers come to people who were not attentive to a power they worship and sanctify, the messengers would have had to say to the people: ﴿Worship Allah...﴾ [al-A'raf: 59]. But here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Do not worship except Allah...﴾ [Hud: 2]. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is confronting a people who have a worship directed to other than the one who deserves worship; so He, glory be to Him, first wants to put an end to this matter, and then establishes worship for Allah.

Therefore, here there is negation and affirmation, like our saying: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah." Here we first negate that there is any god other than Allah, and we affirm divinity for Allah, glory be to Him.

You do not bear this testimony unless there is a people who testify that there is a god other than Allah, the Exalted. Were they to testify to the divinity of the One, the Unique, glory be to Him, the mind would be free of the necessity for us to say this testimony.(1)

But the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Do not worship except Allah...﴾ [Hud: 2] means first the negation of falsehood, and when falsehood is negated, the affirmation of truth must come, so that everything stands on a sound foundation.

For this reason it is said: "Warding off corruption (dar'(2)) always takes precedence over acquiring benefit." So the beginning is that one does not worship idols, and then worship is directed to Allah, glory be to Him.

Since worship is obedience to command and obedience to prohibition, it therefore includes everything in which there is a command and everything in which there is a prohibition.

If you look at the commands and prohibitions, you will find that they encompass all the affairs of life, from the summit of the testimony that there is no god but Allah down to the removal of harm from the road.(3)(4)

And every movement that life requires, to preserve the good in its goodness or to increase the good so that it becomes better, this is worship. Thus Islam does not recognize what is called "lowly works" and "noble works," but it recognizes that there is a lowly agent and a noble agent.

Every agent who performs a work that life requires, for the preservation of the good or its advancement, and who repels corruption, this is a noble agent; and the worth of every person lies in what he does well.

Thus we find that the word worship encompasses all the affairs of life, because there is a command concerning what must be, and there is a prohibition concerning what must not be; and what has no prohibition in it is left to your choice whether to do it or not. If you look at the proportion of what you are commanded, and look at what you are forbidden, in relation to the works of life, you will find that this proportion does not exceed five percent of all the works of life, yet it is the foundation upon which all aspects of life rest.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakah, the pilgrimage to the House, and the fasting of Ramadan."(5)

The enemies of Islam try to confine religion to these five pillars, but these pillars are the columns upon which the edifice of Islam stands.

The pillars of Islam are the declaration of the continuous allegiance to Allah, the Exalted, and every matter of life is required by religion, because it sets life in order.

Thus we find that knowledge of religion is a necessity for every human being on earth. As for other sciences, they are required of those who specialize in them and advance in them so as to benefit all people, and whenever a Muslim excels, that is a reinforcement of the elevation of Islam.

Therefore, the common denominator in life is knowledge of religion. But this matter must be understood in its proper measure, so that no one who does not know the correct religion speaks about the awl(6) and the radd(7), because a Muslim may spend his whole life without needing an opinion on a question of inheritance, or needing to learn the entitled heirs and their shares, and other such matters.

If a Muslim encounters such a question, we say to him: if you encounter such a question, go to the specialists in this science, namely the people of jurisprudence and fatwa, because when you encounter a health matter you go to the doctor, when you encounter an engineering matter you go to the engineer, and if you encounter an accounting operation you go to the accountant; so if you encounter any religious matter, you ask about it the people of remembrance.(8)

And if you look at worship, you find that it requires every movement in life. I have previously given an example of this and said: suppose a man prays and does nothing in life except prayer. From where will he get the money to buy a garment with which to cover his nakedness, since he is doing no work other than prayer? If he wants to buy a garment, he must have work for which he takes a wage, and he buys the garment from the retailer, who bought the garments from the wholesaler, and the wholesaler bought them from the factory, in religion; for knowledge of religion requires resorting to the people of remembrance.

If it is said: religion is for everyone, we say: you have spoken truly, in the sense that adherence to religion is for everyone; but as for knowledge of religion, it requires study and jurisprudence.

The people of remembrance in other sciences also spend years developing their studies, as in medicine or engineering or other fields, and likewise professional works require of the one who specializes in them time and effort. So what of the one who sets right the foundations of people's establishment in life, which is the understanding of religion?

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...Why did not a group from every faction of them go forth, that they might gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122].

We do not ask every Muslim, for example, to study inheritance so that he knows the 'asabah(10), the sharers(11), and the kin by blood(12). The factory tailored the garments after another factory had woven them, and the other factory wove the garments from cotton yarn or wool. The cotton came from agriculture, and the wool came from shearing(13) the hair of sheep.

Thus you find that merely standing before your Creator to pray requires that you be covered in your prayer, and this covering requires you to interact with life through work.

Look at yourself and ask: what did you break your fast with today?

The least answer is: I broke my fast with a loaf of bread and a little salt. You will find that you bought the loaf from the grocer, the grocer brought the loaf from the bakery, the bakery brought the flour from the mill, and the mill produced the flour after grinding the grain that came from the field. Likewise the grinding machines were manufactured in other factories that may be foreign.

Thus the making of the loaf was accomplished through an immense chain of processes: there is the farmer who ploughed; there is the designer of the milling machine who studied engineering; there is the geologist who studied the layers of the earth to extract the raw iron from beneath it; and there is the iron factory that smelted the raw iron to extract from it pure iron suitable for manufacture.

Thus you find that every movement in life serves the matter of your religion and serves your standing before your Creator to pray. So do not say: "I will devote myself to worship," meaning that you confine your life to prayer alone, for every useful movement in life is worship. And if you wish not to work in life, you will not benefit from the movement of any worker in life. And if you do not benefit from the movement of any worker in life, you will not be able to pray, nor will you be able to have the strength to pray.

Therefore worship is every movement that life requires within the light of "do" and "do not."(14)

Here the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿Do not worship except Allah. Indeed I am to you from Him a warner(15) and a bringer of good tidings(16)﴾ [Hud: 2]. The warner (nadhir)(17) is one who informs of an evil that has not yet come, so that there is an opportunity to avoid the action that leads to evil; and the bringer of good tidings (bashir) is one who gives good news of a good that will come if a person follows the path to that good.

Therefore, warning and good tidings are reports concerning a matter that has not yet come.

In warning there is intimidation and a kind of teaching. When you want to make your son diligent in his studies, you say to him: if you do not study, you will be like the son of so-and-so, who became a vagabond and a worthless person in life.

Thus you warn your son so that he may avoid from now on the action that would lead him to academic failure.

Likewise a person gives good news to his son or to any other person of the good that awaits him when he follows the straight path.

Therefore worship is every movement of life so long as the person follows what came with the true method, within the light of "do" and "do not"; and what has no "do" or "do not" in it is permissible.

The Muslim must make himself and those around him understand that carrying out any act in light of "do" is permissible action, and that he must refrain from any act in light of "do not," since Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden such an act; and the Muslim must be careful to be precise in the meaning of every conduct.

We know that the obligations of faith may be hard on the self, and it is necessary to explain to a person that hardship on the self will bring him great good.

An example of this is when we see the farmer carrying organic manure from the animal shed to put it on the back of the donkey and go with it to the field to mix it with the soil, performing this work with all its hardship, in anticipation of the day of harvest.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes clear here, through the tongue of His Messenger, that the command not to worship any being other than Allah is a command from Allah, glory be to Him, and that the Messenger (ﷺ) is a warner and bringer of good tidings from Allah.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿Do not worship except Allah...﴾ [Hud: 2] contains a negation of worship of other than Allah and an affirmation of servitude to Allah, exalted is He.

This is consistent and in harmony with warning and good tidings(18), because worship of other than Allah requires a warner, and worship of Allah in Islam requires a bringer of good tidings.

And because the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Creator of man and knows man's weakness, the meaning of this weakness is that he may be overcome by immediate benefit, so that it diverts him from a greater and longer-lasting good, and he falls into some heedlessness of the self.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, has explained that whoever falls into some heedlessness of the self should seek Allah's forgiveness, because Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, does not withhold His mercy from any of His creatures.

If the sinning servant seeks Allah's forgiveness, He, glory be to Him, has legislated repentance, which is the return from disobedience to the obedience of Allah, exalted is He.

No servant falls into disobedience except because he has rebelled against the method of his Lord; so if he repents and seeks forgiveness, he returns to the method of Allah, glory be to Him, and strives not to fall into a new sin.

1 Because testimony is given on a matter and about a matter. The one who testifies that there is no god but Allah has negated divinity from other than Allah and affirmed it for Him, because the context requires that; this is firmness in both structure and meaning. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not worship except Allah...(2)﴾ [Hud], it restricts worship to Allah. As for testimony about the matter, the existence with what it contains and whoever is in it establishes the divinity of the One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal, in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things Powerful.

2 Dar': repelling and removing. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment that she testify four testimonies by Allah...(8)﴾ [al-Nur], meaning: it averts from her the punishment of the prescribed penalty by her giving this testimony; the rest of the ruling is in Surat al-Nur in verses (8, 9). [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

3 Removing harm from the road: moving it and removing it away from people's path so that it does not harm them. The harm may be stones or anything that may injure people or obstruct their passage on the road.

4 On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Faith has seventy-some or sixty-some branches; the best of them is the saying 'there is no god but Allah,' and the least of them is removing harm from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith." Related by Muslim in his Sahih, Book of Faith (35); and likewise related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (9), without "the best of them" and "the least of them."

5 Agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (8) and Muslim (16), from the narration of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

6 Awl linguistically means rising. Among the jurists: an increase in the shares of those with fixed portions and a reduction in the amounts of their shares in inheritance. It is a question that appears when calculating the shares, so the one dividing the estate is compelled to increase on one side and decrease on the other.

7 Radd: that is, returning what remains of the estate to the sharers according to the proportion of their fixed portions, when there is no entitlement of others; this is realized through three pillars:
1- The existence of a sharer with a fixed portion.
2- The remaining of a surplus of the estate.
3- The absence of an 'asib.
Consult the detailed treatment of these questions and their applications in the book Fiqh by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq, and other books of jurisprudence.

8 The Lord of Majesty, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know(7)﴾ [al-Anbiya'].

9 Fiqh: understanding. Faqiha, yafqahu, faqih: became a scholar who understands. In terminology, fiqh is the knowledge of the rulings of acts of worship and transactions, and it is a branch of the religious sciences. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿...What is the matter with these people that they hardly understand any statement?(78)﴾ [al-Nisa']. And He, exalted, said: ﴿Why did not a group from every faction of them go forth, that they might gain understanding of the religion...(122)﴾ [al-Tawbah], meaning: that they might study the rulings of religion and learn them. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

10 'Asabah: they are a man's sons and his paternal relatives. What is meant by them in inheritance are those to whom the remainder of the estate is paid after the sharers have taken their prescribed portions. Examples are the brother, the paternal uncle, and the father, when something remains after dividing the estate, he takes it by 'asabah in addition to the fixed portion that Allah has assigned him.

11 Ashab al-furud (sharers) are those who have a fixed portion, namely a share, and they are twelve: four males: the father, the true grandfather however high, the maternal brother, and the husband. And eight females: the wife, the daughter, the full sister, the paternal sister, the maternal sister, the son's daughter, the mother, and the true grandmother however high; and each of them has a fixed portion mentioned in the Noble Qur'an.

12 Ulu al-arham are every relative who is neither a sharer nor an 'asib. Malik and al-Shafi'i held that they do not inherit, and the property goes to the public treasury (bayt al-mal); Abu Hanifah and Ahmad held that they inherit in the case of the absence of sharers and 'asabat.

13 Shearing hair and wool: cutting it.

14 Do: a command from the Commander, who is Allah. Do not: a prohibition from Allah. The command gives rise to obligation (fard), the sunnah, and the recommended (mustahabb). The prohibition gives rise to the forbidden (haram), and the disliked (makruh); silence about something is permissible. This is the legal obligation (taklif shar'i), and it is the principle of choice; this legal obligation includes the command to do good, whether it is devotional or worldly, and from here the balances of social justice are balanced.

15 Nadhir: the one who warns the disbelievers, polytheists, and sinners of Allah's punishment. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner...(119)﴾ [al-Baqarah], and He, exalted, said: ﴿So Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners...(213)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

16 Bashir: one who gives the people good news, and here it means the Messenger who gives the believers good tidings of Allah's reward, His Paradise, and its bliss, as recompense for their faith and worship. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people contentious(97)﴾ [Maryam], meaning: people of great hostility. And He, exalted, said: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds, that for them are gardens...(25)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

17 Nadhir: warning and the one who warns, its plural being nudhur. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner...(19)﴾ [al-Ma'idah], and nadhir here is the Messenger who warns of punishment. His saying: ﴿So how was My punishment and warning?(16)﴾ [al-Qamar] may mean My warnings, and may mean the consequences of My warnings, that is, the punishments with which they were warned; the letter ya of the first person has been dropped for lightness. See al-Qamus al-Qawim, pp. 258-259, vol. 2.

18 [Note: the source reads "wa-al-bashara" at this point; rendered as "good tidings".]

18. Al-bushra (good news) and al-bushara: that which is given to the one who brings joyful news. The bashir (bearer of good news) is one who gives a people news they love, and the Messenger is a bashir, because he gives the believers good news of Paradise and of Allah's reward. The Truth says: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner﴾ [al-Fath: 8], and the Truth says: ﴿And give good news to the believers that for them is a great bounty from Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47]. Al-Qamus al-Qawim, briefly..

And here the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term, and will give every person of merit his merit. But if you turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ (3)

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear that the servant must seek forgiveness for his past sins into which he fell, must repent from now on, and must return to the method of God, Exalted is He, so that he may attain grace from the Truth, glory be to Him.

What is required, then, from the servant is that he seek forgiveness from God, Exalted is He, and turn to Him in repentance.

This is what God requires from the disobedient, because warding off harm (dar' al-mafsada) takes precedence over securing benefit (jalb al-maslaha). When the servant hastens to repent to God, Exalted is He, he knows that a sin has occurred and has been committed by him, and he should not postpone repentance to some future time, because he does not know whether he will remain alive or not.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term...﴾ [Hud] (3). The Truth, glory be to Him, sums up the matter of following His method in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿...So whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, nor will he be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha] (123). And He says in another place: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life...﴾ [an-Nahl] (97). So a good life in this world, and the absence of misguidance and distress, are realized for whoever follows the method of God, Exalted is He.

Some scholars thought that this statement appears, on its surface, to contradict the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever" (4), and: "The people most severely tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then those most like them, then those most like them" (6).

Some scholars said: How, then, can we say: ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision...﴾ [Hud] (3)? Here we say: What is the meaning of "enjoyment" (matā')?

Matā': it is that which you enjoy and receive with joy and delight.

The believer knows that every calamity in this world is only something for which God rewards him with the best reward, and this believer receives the decree of God with a contented soul, because what befalls him has been written for him by God, and He will bring him something better than it.

There are some believers who even ask for an increase in trials.

So the believer's whole affair is good. Beware of looking upon anyone whom life has afflicted with some calamity as truly afflicted, for the truly afflicted is the one who has been deprived of reward.

In the Qur'an we find the story of the righteous servant who killed a boy whose parents were believers. The righteous servant feared that the boy would burden them with rebellion and disbelief, for this boy was a trial, and perhaps he would have driven his parents to every forbidden thing and brought them misery (7).

So the true believer is the one who calls to mind the reward of a calamity at the moment it occurs.

And among us is one who read the story of the righteous believer who walked the road from Medina to Damascus. His foot was wounded and the wound became infected and filled with pus, what is called in modern terminology "gangrene." The doctors decided that his leg must be amputated, and they tried to give him a "murdi'" (sedative), that is, a substance that numbs him and makes him lose consciousness so that he could bear the pain of the amputation. But the righteous servant refused and said: "Indeed I do not like to be heedless of my Lord for the blink of an eye."

Such a servant, God, glory be to Him and exalted, gives him strength to bear pain, because he constantly keeps in mind his presence in the company of God, and he is endowed with the power and strength of God, Exalted is He.

When the doctors amputated his leg and wished to shroud it and bury it, he asked to see it before they did so. He held it and said: "O God, if You have tested me in one limb, indeed You have granted me well-being in (my other) limbs."

So the one who suffers a calamity, when he calls to mind the reward for it, lives in enjoyment. For this reason, do not be surprised when some people praise their Creator for calamities, because praise is due for a blessing, and a calamity may bring a person a blessing wider than what it has taken from him.

For this reason we find two of the knowers of God, each wanting to show superiority over the other. One of them said: "How are you in your lands, O poor ones?" – by "the poor" are meant the ascetic worshippers who spend most of their time in the worship of God, Exalted is He. The second servant said: "Our condition in our lands is this: if we are given, we thank; and if we are deprived, we are patient."

The first servant laughed and said: "This is the condition of dogs in Balkh" (9), meaning that a dog, if you give it something, wags its tail, and if anyone withholds from it, it remains patient.

The second servant asked the first: "And how are you?" He said: "We, if we are given, we give preference (to others); and if we are deprived, we give thanks."

So every believer who lives by the method of God, glory be to Him and exalted, calls to mind, in every painful matter and every wearying matter, that he has a reward for what he has endured of hardship: a great, everlasting reward from God, glory be to Him and exalted. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision...﴾ [Hud] (3). The word "good" (hasan) here has measures by which the consideration of the goal is gauged; when the goal is joined to the action, you come to know the meaning of "good."

An example of this is the student who does not leave his books, but when mealtime comes, he eats while his eyes never leave the book.

This student keeps in mind the enjoyment of success, its goodness, and the bliss of excellence, and he is a student who feels the goal at the time he performs the action.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says in the same verse: ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit...﴾ [Hud] (3). That is: He gives every person of merit abundant (jazl) reward to one who has no merit, so it is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, multiplies merit for the servant.

An example of this is the farmer who takes from his granary an ardab of wheat to sow in the earth, so that God, glory be to Him and exalted, may increase it by the planting of this ardab, and its yield becomes fifteen ardabs.

Merit (fadl) is the surplus over what is needed. For example, there is the surplus of wealth you may have, that is, beyond your need, while another has no wealth sufficient for him. If you graciously give some of your surplus to one who has no wealth, you are investing this giving with God, Exalted is He.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, may give you strength, and you give the excess of it to a weak servant.

And God, glory be to Him, may have bestowed upon you a surplus of forbearance, so you give some of it to one who has been struck by folly and narrowness of character.

So every good trait that a person has, which others do not have, and which he bestows upon them, increases with him, because it grows (yarbū) with God; and if he does not bestow it on others, it diminishes.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And whatever you give in interest to increase within the wealth of people – it does not increase with God. But what you give in charity, seeking the countenance of God – those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward)﴾ [ar-Rum] (39).

And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says in the verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit...﴾ [Hud] (3).

Some people of knowledge understand this noble statement to mean that the person who bestows upon others from what God has given him, God, glory be to Him, gives him, by way of increase, what compensates for what was diminished; or that He, glory be to Him and exalted, gives every possessor of merit the merit of his Lord, and the merit of God is above every merit. Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...But if they turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ [Hud] (3). That is: if they turn away from you, then inform them that you fear for them the punishment of the Last Day. The punishment is described once as "great," once as "mighty," and once as "humiliating," because it is a punishment that does not end, and it varies according to what suits the one being punished. Moreover, the punishment that exists in the world of changing things is a punishment that proceeds under the presumption that it will come to an end, whereas the punishment of the Last Day does not end, for those who associate partners with God, forever.

1 Matā' (enjoyment, provision): it is applied to much and little, being a verbal noun (maṣdar), and its plural is amti'a, according to what is benefited from and what is enjoyed. God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿...seeking ornaments or enjoyment...﴾ [ar-Ra'd] (17), meaning: and making things from which benefit is derived. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until the truth came to them...﴾ [az-Zukhruf] (29), meaning: I prolonged the period of their benefiting from life and its blessings. Matta'a and mattaʿa have the same meaning. And He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿We made it a reminder and a provision for the travelers﴾ [al-Waqi'ah] (73), meaning: a provision for travelers who leave their homes desolate, or a provision for the hungry. (See: Ibn Kathir 4/297).
2 Dar' (warding off): repelling and removing.
3 Jalb (bringing): driving a thing from one place to another; and jalb al-shay': seeking and acquiring it. [Lisan al-Arab: root j-l-b].
4 Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2956) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4113), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. An-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim (18/305): "Its meaning is that every believer is imprisoned, restricted in this world from forbidden and disliked desires, obligated to perform arduous acts of obedience. When he dies, he finds rest from this, and passes over to what God, Exalted is He, has prepared for him of everlasting bliss and pure rest free from deficiency. As for the disbeliever, he has of that only what he attains in this world, together with his being killed and troubled by its disturbances; when he dies, he passes to everlasting punishment and the misery of eternity."
5 Al-amthal fa-al-mithal: that is, the most noble, then the most noble, and the highest in rank and station. It is said: "This is more excellent than that," meaning better and closer to good. And amathil al-nas: their best.
6 Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/172), at-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2398), and Ibn Majah (4023), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan sahih hadith." The complete hadith reads: "A man is tested according to his religion, and the trial continues upon the servant until he walks upon the earth with no sin upon him."
7 The Lord of Glory, glory be to Him, says in Surat al-Kahf concerning Musa, peace be upon him, and the righteous servant who accompanied Musa so that he might learn from him: ﴿So they set out until, when they met a boy, he killed him. [Musa] said: "Have you killed an innocent soul without [its having killed] another? You have certainly done a terrible thing." He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ [al-Kahf] (74-75). And He, glory be to Him, says on the tongue of the righteous servant: ﴿...I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people working on the sea, and I wished to damage it, for behind them was a king who seizes every ship by force. And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with rebellion and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy﴾ [al-Kahf] (78-81).
8 The shaykh said: "The humiliation of trial is better than the honor of blessing."
9 Balkh: a city of the cities of Khurasan, in the lands beyond the river (Transoxiana).
10 That is: if we receive a gift, we give it preference over ourselves to others; that is, we prefer them over ourselves.
11 Al-jazl: the abundant, great thing of every kind; and al-jazl means generous, bountiful. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root j-z-l].
12 Asbagha: he bestowed and abundantly gave. The sububgh of a thing is its completeness and extensiveness. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root s-b-gh, adapted]. And God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And He has completed upon you His blessings, apparent and hidden...﴾ [Luqman] (20).
13 Rabā al-shay' yarbū: it increased and grew; and arbaytuhu: I made it grow.
14 Ad'afa al-rajul: his wealth grew, increased and expanded, becoming multiplied. The active participle is mudʿif: ﴿...then those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward)﴾ [ar-Rum] (39), meaning: those who take the reward of their deeds multiplied manyfold. Ibn Kathir said in his commentary on this verse (3/434): "That is: whoever gives a gift seeking that people return more than what he gave them, for him there is no reward with God. This is how Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and ash-Sha'bi explained it. This practice is permissible, though there is no reward in it; however, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) specifically forbade it, as ad-Dahhak said, and he cited the saying of God, Exalted is He: ﴿and do not give, seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir] (6), meaning: do not give a gift desiring more than it." Ibn Abbas said: "Usury is of two kinds: the usury that is not valid, namely the usury of sale; and the usury that is not objectionable, which is a man's gift seeking its excess and its multiples; then he recited this verse: ﴿And whatever you give in interest to increase within the wealth of people – it does not increase with God.﴾ [ar-Rum] (39). The reward with God is only in zakah."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 4:

And the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿To Allah is your return, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ (4):

That is: to Allah is your return (1) in origination and provision, and in beginning and end, and the beginning of the end that has no end after it, which is the Hereafter. So He rewards the doer of good for his good, and punishes the doer of evil for his evil. Thus He gives every possessor of righteous deeds in this world his reward, and his recompense in the Hereafter.

Whoever's good deeds outweigh his evil deeds enters Paradise, and whoever's evil deeds outweigh his good deeds enters the Fire.

And in this world, whoever's good deeds outweigh his evil deeds lives between contraction (qabd) and expansion (bast).

Contraction and expansion are a turning toward Allah through repentance and an acknowledgment of sin, and acknowledging sin is the beginning of repentance.

And whoever's evil deeds outweigh his good deeds, for him there is a narrow (dank) life (2) and anxiety of the soul.

The Truth, glory be to Him, gives every possessor of grace his grace. So whoever acts for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will grant him success in what he faces afterward in obedience to Him, while those who turn away will fear for them the punishment of a great day.

﴿...and He is over all things Competent.﴾ [Hud]: because He, glory be to Him, is the One Able to originate and to provide, and to begin and end within limits, and the beginning of eternal abode, either to a Garden or to a Fire. So He is Competent over all things.

(1) Al-marji' (the return): it is the act of returning, or a noun of time, or a noun of place. The Truth says: ﴿Then to Me is your return...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 55], meaning your returning, or the time of your returning, or the place of returning. Similarly His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then to Us is your return...﴾ [Yunus: 23]...

(2) Al-dank: narrowness of living. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 124]. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/168): "He has no tranquility, nor expansion of his breast, but rather his breast is constricted and tight due to his misguidance, even if his outward appearance is pleasant, and he eats what he wishes, and dwells where he wishes; for his heart, as long as it has not reached certainty and guidance, is in anxiety, bewilderment and doubt, so he is always in suspicion, wavering. This is the constriction of living."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 5:

The Truthful (Glorified be He) says after that:

﴿Verily they fold their breasts (1) to hide themselves from Him (2). Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments (3), He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed He is Knower of what is in the breasts (4).﴾ (11:5)

When you find "alā" (ألا, "Indeed/Truly") at the beginning of a speech, you know that it is for alerting (tanbih), and the meaning of alerting is an attention-grabber that wakes the listener if he is heedless, because you want that no word of what you are saying be missed by him.

When you alert someone without the style you want from him, here the alerting has taken its due, and after that comes the speech you are saying, and the listener's mind has been prepared to receive what you say.

So "alā," then, is a particle of alerting, because speech is a screen between the speaker and the addressee. The addressee does not know the subject you are going to speak to him about, while the speaker is the one who holds the reins of the situation and prepares his mind to arrange the words he will say. As for the listener, he will be surprised by the subject; so that he is not surprised and the opportunity is not lost on him, so that he may catch the speaker's words from their beginning, he alerts him with a particle of alerting in order to listen (5).

The Truthful (Glorified be He) says here: ﴿Verily they fold their breasts to hide themselves from Him..﴾ (11:5).

It is said: "thaniytu al-shay'" meaning "I folded the thing," that is, I folded it and made it two connected parts one upon the other.

When a person folds his breast, he folds it forward toward his belly, and thereby screens his face, and the purpose here of screening the face is to hide the features, because the agitation of the feelings of the human soul (6) shows on the faces.

They were hateful toward the Messenger (ﷺ) and full of spite against him, and they did not want the Messenger (ﷺ) to notice the emotions on their features that expose their hateful feelings.

A similar thing came from the people of Noah (peace be upon him), when the Truthful (Glorified be He) said on the tongue of Noah: ﴿And indeed, whenever I call them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments, and persist, and are arrogantly proud, with great arrogance (7).﴾ (71:7). It is obvious that we know that a finger does not enter the ear entirely; rather, the fingertip (8) only blocks the opening of hearing. The noble Qur'an corrected that with an exaggeration that reveals Noah's position (peace be upon him): each of them wanted to put his finger in his ear so that he would hear no call at all, and this is a sign of hatred, and this is testimony against them, because they understood that if they heard, their hearts might incline toward what is said.

For this reason, we find the noble Qur'an, as it relays what the polytheists of Mecca said to one another:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise (9) during it..﴾ (41:26).

It is as if they coordinated to create noise over the Qur'an, being confident that if the Qur'an reached the ear, it might affect the listener's soul, because the human soul is changeable, and there may come to the soul what makes it incline without its owner being aware.

And if this Qur'an were false, why did they fear hearing it?

But it is the stupidity of obstinacy and disbelief.

And here the Truthful (Glorified be He) says: ﴿Indeed they fold their breasts to hide themselves from Him; unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal..﴾ (11:5). They covered their garments to conceal their faces, to screen the feelings these faces carry, and these are feelings of hatred, or they may be other feelings: when one of them hears the Qur'an, he may be moved by what he hears, and he does not want to show the emotion.

So then: emotion may be involuntary (qasriyyan) (12), and the Quraysh disbelievers, despite their scheming and warfare against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), used to sneak toward the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) to hear the Qur'an, and they would catch one another there, and each of them would claim that he had only passed by the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) by chance.

On this the poet says:

Remember them, when each one slipped away after the gathering of night-talkers had dispersed,

Stealthily heading for the chamber of Ta-Ha, to hear the Revelation at the dawns,

Their excuse was fine; but when they met, they justified it with prominent excuses.

And the Truthful (Glorified be He) came here, in the same verse, with "alā" in His saying: ﴿..Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed He is Knower of what is in the breasts (5).﴾ (11:5).

So if they conceal themselves from Muhammad (ﷺ), are they able to conceal themselves from the Lord of Muhammad? What the sight of Muhammad does not perceive, the Lord of Muhammad will know it.

And since the Truthful (Glorified be He) knows what they conceal, it is all the more so that He (Glorified and Exalted be He) knows what they reveal.

The Truthful (Glorified and Exalted be He) is unseen, and perhaps someone may suppose that something might escape Him, but the Truthful counts all things and nothing is hidden from Him. If someone supposes that the Truthful knows only the unseen because He is unseen, this is a mistaken supposition, because He knows the secret and the open; He is Knower of what is in the breasts, and the word "ʿalīm" (Knower) is an intensive form (16), meaning one whose knowledge is in its essence knowledge.

And the saying of the Truthful: ﴿..Knower of what is in the breasts (17) (50).﴾ (11:50?) We find in it the word ﴿dhāt﴾ ("possessor of"), which indicates companionship, and "dhāt al-ṣudūr" means the matters accompanying the breasts.

We know that the breast is the seat of the heart and the seat of the lungs, and the heart is the seat of the beliefs that one has arrived at and that have become firm realities, and upon them the movement of life turns.

What is meant by ﴿dhāt al-ṣudūr﴾ is the meanings that do not leave the breasts; they are constant companions in those breasts, whether they are hatred or aversion, or they are the sentiments that do not appear in ordinary movement, whether they are good intentions or bad intentions.

All the matters they call "dhāt al-ṣudūr," that is, the companions of the breasts, which are the hearts, and as if the very substance (18) of the heart itself is known to the Truthful (Glorified be He), so its thoughts are all the more known.

1 Yathnūna ṣudūrahum: they fold them over enmity toward the Muslims, and harbor for them hatred and aversion.
2 Al-istikhfāʾ: seeking concealment and hiding. Out of their ignorance they wish to hide from God Almighty, while He (Glorified be He) nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven. God Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven (5)﴾ (Āl ʿImrān). And God Almighty said: ﴿Whether you show a thing or conceal it, indeed God is ever Knower of all things (54)﴾ (al-Aḥzāb).
3 Yastaghshūna thiyābahum: they cover themselves with them, in exaggeration of concealment. [Kalimāt al-Qurʾān].
4 Al-Wāḥidī mentioned in "Asbāb al-Nuzūl" (p. 153) that this verse was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who was a man sweet of speech and pleasant in appearance, who would meet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with what he loved, and would fold in his heart what he hated.
And al-Kalbī said: he used to sit with the Prophet (ﷺ), showing him a matter that pleased him, and concealing in his heart the opposite of what he showed.
5 "Alā" occurs in the Qur'an in several ways:
The first: alerting, indicating the certainty of what follows it, and it enters both nominal and verbal sentences, as in ﴿..Indeed they are the foolish, but they do not know (13)﴾ (al-Baqara), and {Unquestionably, the day when it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them.. (8)} (Hūd).
The second and third: ḥaḍḍ (urging) and ʿarḍ (proposing), meaning the request for something, but the first is a request of inquiry and the second is a request of gentleness, and in both they specifically enter upon a verbal sentence, as in: {Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths.. (13)} (al-Tawba), ﴿..Do you not love that God forgive you? (22)﴾ (al-Nūr).
6 Mawājīd: plural of mawjida. Fulān wajada wajdan: he grieved or became angry. The meaning: the emotions of the human soul [al-Muʿjam al-Wasīṭ: root (w j d)], adapted.
7 Istaghshū thiyābahum: they covered themselves with them so that they would not see Noah nor hear his speech. Said by Ibn ʿAbbās; mentioned by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr (8/289), Dār al-Fikr edition.
8 Al-anmala: the joint of the finger or its palm. It is also the upper joint of the finger where the nail is. Plural: anāmil. [al-Muʿjam al-Wasīṭ, root (n m l)].
9 Al-laghw: what is not regarded as valuable of speech or otherwise, and from which no benefit or profit is obtained [al-Muʿjam al-Wasīṭ]. And alghaw fīhi: bring idle talk and falsehood while it is recited [Kalimāt al-Qurʾān]. Ibn ʿAbbās said: by whistling and confusion upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited the Qur'an. Mentioned by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr (7/321) and attributed to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
10 Tanāhā: reached and arrived. Al-inhāʾ: informing. Anhaytu ilayhi al-khabar: I informed him of the news. [Lisān al-ʿArab, root: n h y].
11 Qatāda said: the servant is most concealed when he bends his back, covers himself with his garment, and conceals his concern within himself. Mentioned by al-Qurṭubī in his tafsir (4/3324).
12 Qasriyyan: that is, outside the will of the person.
13 He said: that Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, and al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq went out one night to listen to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was praying at night in his house. Each man of them took a place where he could listen, and none knew the location of his companion. They spent the night listening to him, until the dawn broke and they dispersed. Then the road gathered them, and they blamed one another. Some of them said to others: "Do not return; if some of your foolish ones saw you, you would have made an impression on his mind." Then they went away. When the second night came, each man returned to his place, and they spent the night listening to him, until the dawn broke and they dispersed. And so on until a third night, when some of them said to others: "We will not leave until we pledge not to return," and they pledged to that, then dispersed. [Sīrat Ibn Hishām 1/315].
14 Al-sammār: people who converse at night, and this is customary in moonlight.
15 Al-asḥār: plural of saḥar, which is the last third of the night until the rising of dawn. God Almighty said: ﴿And at the dawns they seek forgiveness (18)﴾ (al-Dhāriyāt).
16 ʿAlīm: an intensive form of knowledge, meaning: one whose knowledge is utmost, having no limit to His knowledge (Glorified be He).
17 Al-ṣadr: the front and beginning of everything, and the human chest is known, and inside it are its ribs, its heart, and its lungs. In the chest the effects of emotion appear: constriction in sorrow and expansion in joy. The Truthful (Glorified be He) said: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you? (1)﴾ (al-Sharḥ), and He said: ﴿..Indeed God is Knower of what is in the breasts (119)﴾ (Āl ʿImrān), that is, of the secrets accompanying the breasts [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm, abridged].
18 Jirm of everything: its body. The intended meaning is the human heart itself.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 6:

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.﴾

When the Noble Qur'an presents a scene that clarifies a certain attribute, it brings what relates to that attribute. Since the Truthful One, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, this is knowledge of the negative matters that are not apparent. The Truthful One, glorified is He, also knows the positive matters; He knows good intention as well. But the speech here concerns a group who fold their breasts (in concealment).

It came in the verse on which we are reflecting, and it made clear that He is All-Knowing of everything.

He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage.. (6).﴾

When the Noble Qur'an presents a scene that clarifies a certain attribute, it brings what relates to that attribute. Since the Truthful One, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, this is knowledge of the negative matters that are not apparent. The Truthful One, glorified is He, also knows the positive matters; He knows good intention as well. But the speech here concerns a group who fold their breasts (in concealment).

It came in the verse on which we are reflecting, and it made clear that He is All-Knowing of everything. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And there is no creature (dābba) on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage.. (6)﴾ [Hud]. The dābba (creature): everything that crawls on the earth. In common usage it is specially used to denote any living being on the earth other than man.

In another verse the Truthful One, glorified is He, says: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you.. (38)﴾ [al-An'am].

The Truthful One, glorified is He, mentions about Moses, peace be upon him, that when he was charged (with the mission), his mind was occupied with thoughts of his family, and he asked: How can I go to perform the message and leave my family?

So Allah, glorified is He, inspired him to strike a stone, and the stone split to reveal a rock. The Truthful One, glorified is He, commanded him to strike the rock, and he struck it, and it split to bring forth for him a stone. He struck the stone, and it cleft for him to reveal a worm chewing (talūk) something, as though it were feeding on it. He said: The One who provides for this (creature) in the darknesses of those stones, all of them, will not forget my family upon the surface of the earth. And Moses, peace be upon him, went on to his mission.

This is a natural matter, because the Truthful One, glorified is He, is the Creator of all creation, and He must guarantee for it the preservation of life and the preservation of kind. The preservation of life is by sustenance (qūt), and the preservation of kind is by marriage and affinity.

So, among the arrangements of creation is that the Truthful One, glorified is He, provides the preservation of life by sustenance and the preservation of kind by mating.

Therefore we always say: one must distinguish between the giving of the Deity (ulūhiyya) and the giving of the Lord (rubūbiyya). Allah, glorified is He, is the Lord of all, but He is the Deity of those who believe in Him.

Since the Truthful One, glorified is He, is the Lord of all, all are dependent upon Him. The sun shines upon the believer and the disbeliever, and the disbeliever may extract solar energy from the sun and benefit from it; so why does the believer not take the means? The air exists for the believer and the disbeliever, because it is a gift of lordship (rubūbiyya). If the disbeliever benefits from the air and studies it, and uses its properties more than the believer, then the believer must strive and exert himself in taking the means.

So there is a giving of lordship in which all share, but the giving of deity is only in worship, and it takes you out of your own desires to the desires of your Lord. When your appetites ask you to do something, the method says to you: No.

In this there is your control over appetites and your elevation in choices. As for worldly life matters, the giving of lordship is to every creature so that it preserves its life.

Here the Truthful One, glorified is He, says: The word "upon" (ʿalā) indicates that the provision is a right of the creature, yet the creature has not imposed it upon Allah, glorified and exalted is He; rather He has obligated Himself to this right.

And He says: ﴿and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage.. (6)﴾ [Hud]: Since He is the One who provides for the creature, He knows its place of settlement and where it lives, so that He may deliver this provision to it.

"Mustaqarr" is the place of settling, and "mustawdaʿ" is the place of deposit.

The Truthful One, glorified is He, informs us of this so that every person may be reassured that his provision knows its address, whereas a person does not know the address of provision.

Provision comes to you from where you do not expect, but striving for provision is another matter; you may strive for a provision that is not yours, but is the provision of another.

For example: you may sow your land with wheat, then a journey abroad comes up and you leave your wheat for someone else to eat, and you eat from another's wheat.

Therefore the Truthful One, glorified is He, says: ﴿.. and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage, all in a clear register (6)﴾ [Hud]: that is, every matter is written. There is a difference between doing what you wish, while no written plan governs your wish, and what you do when its steps have been set in a clear written plan, and then your actions come in accordance with what you have written.

And from the greatness of the Creator, glorified is He, is that He has written everything, and then everything in life comes in accordance with what was written.

The proof of this, by way of example, is that Allah, glorified is He, used to reveal to the Messenger a surah of the Noble Qur'an; then after that the revelation would be lifted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (a state of tasriya), and he would recite the surah to his companions; whoever could write, wrote it, and whoever could memorize, memorized it.

Then the Messenger (ﷺ) would come to prayer and recite the surah as it had been written, and each portion of the Qur'an would come in its place which the Prophet (ﷺ) had stated to his companions. How did this happen?

It happened by what the Truthful One, glorified is He, brought and conveyed to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget (6).﴾ [al-A'la]

1 "Dābba" is an active participle, which came to be used predominantly for non-rational beings; masculine and feminine are alike in it, and it may include rational beings and others, as in His saying: {And He spread therein every creature (dābba)… (164)} [al-Baqarah], which includes man and others; likewise His saying: {And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has spread therein of creatures (dābba)… (29)} [al-Shura], where dābba includes living beings in the earth and the heaven, and there is in it evidence that the heavens contain living, rational beings. As for His saying: {And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you… (60)} [al-ʿAnkabut], the dābba here is every animal other than man, by the evidence of "and you".
2 Mustaqarr: the place of its settling in the loins or the wombs and the like. Mustawdaʿ: the place of its being deposited in the wombs and the like, or in the loins. [Kalimat al-Qur'an] of Shaykh Husayn Muhammad Makhlouf.
3 "Lāka al-shayʾ yalūkuhu lawkan": he chewed it. [Lisan al-Arab: root l-w-k].
4 Qūt: that which holds the breath of provision. In al-Sihah: it is what sustains the human body of food. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root q-w-t].
5 And the people of the method who stood by it and upon it; Allah says concerning them: {Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you request, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful (32)."} [Fussilat].
6 Tasriya: the lifting of revelation from him (ﷺ), with what it contains of intensity that causes the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to sweat profusely.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 7:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:
