For example, if meat is offered at a high price, the pride of the self in human nature pushes one who cannot afford it to say, "Eating meat harms my health," and he turns to other foods whose price he can afford, because the commodity is what governs. But if someone intervenes in pricing the goods by hoarding money and not bringing it to the market for investment, then the capacity for movement of the owner of wealth disappears, and the owner of talent finds no room to perfect his craft.

As for the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, in this verse: ﴿...Why has no treasure been sent down to him, or an angel come with him...(12)﴾ [Hud]. The word "why" (lawla(10)), as we know, expresses wishing. They first wished for a treasure, then they asked for an angel to come. How could an angel descend? Would he descend in his own form or in a form other than his, by embodying himself as a man?

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man... (9)﴾ [al-An'am]. And if the angel descended in the form of a man, how would they recognize his origin as an angel? This is folly in the request.

Also the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has God sent a human as a messenger?" (94) Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger." (95)﴾ [al-Isra']. If God sent down an angel, he would be of their own human nature, he would meet them and speak with them, they would not be able to distinguish him from the rest of the people, and they would also deny him.

Here, in the verse we are reflecting upon, the Truth, glorified is He, says, turning them away from this request: ﴿You are only a warner.(11) (12)﴾ [Hud]. This speech is addressed by God, glorified is He, to the Messenger, peace be upon him, to teach him the argument with which he answers them. The Messenger, peace be upon him, had told them about himself that he is a warner and a bringer of good tidings. Others besides you have asked for signs, and when the signs they asked for came, they did not believe but persisted in their denial, so God punished them severely.

Thus, obstinacy in disbelief does not turn into faith merely by the descent of signs. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We withhold not from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them... (59)﴾ [al-Isra']. That is: the signs the disbelievers asked for were not brought by God, because the earlier peoples denied them. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, informs His Messenger, peace be upon him, here with His saying: ﴿You are only a warner... (12)﴾ [Hud]. He, peace be upon him, had the Qur'an sent down to him with warning and good tidings.(12)

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿...And God is Guardian over all things (12)﴾ [Hud]. When you appoint a person as your agent in buying, selling, giving and transporting, and he has freedom to dispose of everything that concerns you, and you observe his conduct: if you are pleased, you remain committed to his agency; if his conduct does not please you, you cancel the agency. This is in the human sphere. But the guardianship of God, glorified and exalted is He, over creation(13) remains forever, even if the disbelievers among them refuse.

Notes from the commentary (translated):

1. Wakil (وكيل): one who stands in charge of a thing and guards it. Al-Wakil: the trustworthy guardian and the helpful supporter. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿...They said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian" (173)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿...Say, "I am not over you a guardian" (66)﴾ [al-An'am], meaning a protector.

2. Fahwa al-qawl: its content and the goal toward which the speaker directs it. Its plural is fahawin and fahawa. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

3. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, emphasized this meaning in many noble hadiths:
- Among them is the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: The Prophet of God, peace be upon him, came to Madinah, and the people were pollinating the palms, saying "they fertilize the palms." He said, "What are you doing?" They said, "We used to do it." He said, "Perhaps you would not do it, and it would be better." So they left it, and the crop fell short. They mentioned that to him, and he said, "I am only a human being. When I order you something of your religion, take it; and when I order you something from my own opinion, then I am only a human being." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2362), Book of Virtues.
- And from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, who said: "I am only a human being. I am pleased as humans are pleased, and I am angry as humans are angry. Whichever one of my community I curse with a curse that is not worthy of him, let it be for him a purification, a charity, and a means of drawing him near to Me on the Day of Resurrection." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2603).

4. Nawamis: the divine laws to which the cosmos is subject.

5. Al-Diyq (with the dad vowelled as kasra or fatha and the ba' sukun) is the opposite of spaciousness, in material and immaterial things. The active participle is ḍā'iq. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and your breast is constricted by it (12)﴾ [Hud], and: ﴿and he was distressed on their account (77)﴾ [Hud], meaning he found constriction in his breast. From it: ﴿We know that you are distressed by what they say (97)﴾ [al-Hijr], and: ﴿...And do not be in distress over what they plan (127)﴾ [al-Nahl]. It was read with fatha and with kasra on the dad. The meaning: your breast should not be constricted because of their plotting. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged].

6. The two towns are Makkah and al-Ta'if. The scholars differed on identifying the great man intended. From Makkah: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah or 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah. From al-Ta'if: 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud or 'Umayr ibn 'Abd Yalil. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/127): "The apparent meaning is that they meant a great man from whichever of the two towns he was."

7. That 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, who was a leader, said one day while he was sitting in the assembly of Quraysh, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was sitting alone in the mosque: "O assembly of Quraysh, shall I not go to Muhammad, talk with him, and offer him matters, perhaps he will accept some of them, and we will give him whichever he wants, and he will refrain from us?" They said, "Yes, O Abu al-Walid, go to him and speak with him." So 'Utbah went to him and sat beside the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: "O son of my brother, you are among us in the position you know, in lineage and standing in the tribe. You have come to your people with a great matter, by which you have split their community, mocked their wisdom, reviled their gods and their religion, and disbelieved those of their forefathers who passed away. Listen to me, I will offer you matters, consider them, perhaps you will accept some of them." The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to him: "Speak, O Abu al-Walid, I am listening." He said: "O son of my brother, if you intend by what you have brought wealth, we will gather for you some of our wealth until you become the richest of us; if you intend nobility, we will make you lord over us so that we decide nothing without you; if you intend kingship, we will make you king over us..." When 'Utbah had finished, he said to him, peace be upon him: "Have you finished, O Abu al-Walid?" He said, "Yes." He said: "Then listen to me." He said, "I will." So he recited: ﴿Ha Mim (1). A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy (2). A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know (3)﴾ [Fussilat]. Then he, peace be upon him, went on reciting it to him. When 'Utbah heard it from him, he listened attentively, placed his hands behind his back, leaning on them, and listened to him. When he returned to his people, he said to them: "Leave this man alone with what he is in, and withdraw from him. By God, the word that I heard from him will surely have a great outcome. If the Arabs overcome him, you will have been spared him by others; and if he prevails over the Arabs, his kingdom will be your kingdom, his honour your honour, and you will be the happiest of people through him." [From the Sirah of the Prophet by Ibn Hisham 1/293-294, with adaptation].

8. Kanaza al-mal yaknizuhu kanzan: he gathered and stored it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿...This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard (35)﴾ [al-Tawbah], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿...And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God, give them tidings of a painful punishment (34)﴾ [al-Tawbah]. The pronoun refers to silver because it is closer in mention and because it is of lesser value, so whoever is stingy with it is stingy with gold a fortiori. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

9. Direct sustenance is what needs are met by with fluid continuity; indirect sustenance is what needs are met by with difficulty of need and necessity.

10. Qanatir: plural of qintar, a measure that varies among people. In our time in Egypt it is one hundred rotls, which is 44,928 kilograms. The qintar may also be meant to denote a large amount of wealth. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

11. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3051): "The scholars differed about wealth whose zakat has been paid: is it called a treasure or not? Some said yes, and this was narrated by Abu al-Duha from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him: 'Four thousand and less is expenditure, and what is more than that is a treasure even if its zakat has been paid.' But this is not sound. Ibn 'Umar said: 'What has had its zakat paid is not a treasure, even if it is under seven earths, and whatever has not had its zakat paid is a treasure even if it is above the earth.' Similarly from Jabir, and this is the sound view."

12. Qasada fi amrihi yaqsudu qasdan (like daraba): he was moderate in it and took a middle course, as in His saying: ﴿And be moderate in your walk (19)﴾ [Luqman], meaning be balanced and middling in it. He said: ﴿Among them is a moderate group (32)﴾ [Luqman], meaning balanced, not deviating. The Truth says: ﴿...Among them is a moderate community (66)﴾ [al-Ma'idah]. Economics has now become a discipline with its own methods, and it is the art of managing wealth. The modern definition does not depart from what the language indicates, and what the noble Qur'an pointed to (al-Qamus al-Qawim, with addition required by the context).

13. Lawla: a conditional particle that does not govern, indicating the negation of the response due to the existence of the condition. It may also be used as a particle of urging and specification, like "hallā," so that it enters upon the present-tense verb, as in His saying: ﴿...Why do you not seek forgiveness from God, so that you may receive mercy? (46)﴾ [al-Naml], and it enters upon the past-tense verb that has the sense of the present, as in His saying: ﴿Why has no treasure been sent down to him...(12)﴾ [Hud], meaning: why does no treasure descend upon him. And His saying: ﴿Why did You not delay me to a near term...(10)﴾ [al-Munafiqun], meaning: why do You not delay me. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

14. Nadhir: the messenger who warns of punishment. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you to warn you...(63)﴾ [al-A'raf].

15. In this He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, "Signs are only with God." And what would make you aware that when they come, they will not believe? (109) And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly (110)﴾ [al-An'am].

16. The Lord of Honour, glorified is He, says to His Messenger, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner...(119)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

17 Al-Wakil (the Trustee, the One entrusted with affairs): the Trustworthy Guardian, the Helper and the Supporter. He, Exalted, says: ﴿...And they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ [Al 'Imran (3:173)]. So Allah's wikala (trusteeship) over His creation means His care for them through provision, protection and support...

Allah, the Exalted, says after that:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ (13)

In the words of the Exalted Lord here there is an explanation of another form of the disbelievers' opposition to the method of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to belief in him, for they said: "Muhammad has invented the Qur'an."

Iftira' (invention): it is deliberate lying, and the meaning of deliberate lying is speech that contradicts a reality in the universe.

So if the reality is a negation and you state an affirmation, you have contradicted reality. For example, if there exists in the universe a certain evil, and then you say, "There is no evil in this place," and so the reality is an existence while the speech is a negation.

Likewise, if there is a negation in reality and an affirmation in speech, this too is a lie, because truthfulness is that the verbal proposition agrees with the cosmic reality; if it differs from the cosmic reality, the speech becomes a lie.

Lying is of two kinds: deliberate and non-deliberate. Lying (kadhib) is breaking a reality and fabricating what does not exist. It is said: "kharaqtu al-shay'" (I tore the thing), meaning you came to a reality and altered it.

The Exalted Lord says: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾ (100) [al-An'am], and ﴿And you fabricate a falsehood﴾ (17) [al-'Ankabut]: that is, you bring something out of nothing, and it is from you alone.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿... they only conjecture﴾ (116) [al-An'am].

When they accused Muhammad (ﷺ) falsely of having invented the Qur'an, the reply came from the Noble Qur'an with utmost simplicity: you, O Arabs, are people of eloquence and rhetoric, and the Noble Qur'an has come of the same kind and type as your genius. Since you have said that Muhammad invented the Qur'an, and that the verses of the Qur'an are not from Allah, then why do you not invent the like of it?

Since inventing is easy for you, why do you not bring the like of the Qur'an, even ten surahs of it? You have lived with Muhammad since his childhood, and he had no poetry, no prose, no oratory, and no connection to your linguistic exercises; he did not practise poetry or oratory, and did not take part in the markets of eloquence and poetry that were held in the Jahiliyyah, such as the market of 'Ukaz.

If one who had no training in speech or eloquence has brought this Qur'an, then let it be within your power, you who have capacity, practice and training in eloquence, to bring something like it; and if he invented the Qur'an, then why do you not invent the like of it?

You know the competitions held in your markets of eloquence, when one poet recites a qasidah, another poet enters into a contest with him to recite a qasidah better than the first poet's, and then judging committees are formed to show the aspects of beauty and the aspects of defect in any qasidah.

And if Muhammad (ﷺ) had invented the Qur'an, as you say, then where are you? Did you not know him from his childhood? Therefore the Exalted Lord commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to say: ﴿Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I have remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?"﴾ (16) [Yunus].

Was it reported from Muhammad (ﷺ) that he composed poetry, delivered a sermon, or competed at 'Ukaz, al-Mirbad, Dhu al-Majaz or al-Majannah, and those were the markets of eloquence and their festivals in those days?

He did not go to those places to compete or to recite.

Then: were not those who competed there more capable than him of inventing? Was not Imru' al-Qays a mighty poet? He was, and he had a counterpart who opposed him.

Likewise 'Amr ibn Kulthum and al-Harith ibn Hilliza al-Yashkuri, and in later eras others such as Jarir and al-Farazdaq came.

Then: you know those who composed poetry and those who opposed them from among their like among the poets.

So bring forth someone who can invent the like of the surahs of the Qur'an. If you cannot invent, then that means the Qur'an is not an invention.

Therefore the Exalted Lord says here: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented..."﴾ (13) [Hud]. Were they able to accept the challenge, by bringing ten surahs like the Noble Qur'an in its captivating expression, the power of its eloquence and the secrets of its meanings?

He challenged them first to bring the like of the Qur'an, and they could not; then He challenged them to bring ten surahs, and they could not; He challenged them to bring a single surah, and then challenged them to bring even a speech like it, and they could not.

Here the Exalted came with the second stage of the challenge, which is to bring ten surahs. The Exalted did not suffice with that, but asked them to call upon an assembly of the eloquent, saying: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides Allah...﴾ (13) [Hud]: that is, bring all your partners and all the eloquent, besides Allah the Exalted.

The Exalted Lord here cuts off from them the opportunity of making claims against Him, lest they say: "We shall call upon Allah"; therefore the Exalted commanded them to set Him aside: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful﴾ (13) [Hud]: that is, if you are truthful that Muhammad (ﷺ) invented the Qur'an; and since you are people of excellence in eloquence, then invent ten surahs like the Qur'an, you and whomever you can call upon from among the partners.

Therefore the wise reply from Allah is in the words of the Exalted that follows:

﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no deity except Him. Will you then be Muslims?﴾ (14)

1 Iftira' (invention): fabricating falsehood. ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"...﴾ (13) [Hud], i.e., he composed the Qur'an and fabricated it from himself. And He said: ﴿Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented..."﴾ (13) [Hud], i.e., fabricated, as you claim. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]

2 Kharq al-amr or al-kalam: lying about it and inventing it. He said: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters without knowledge...﴾ (100) [al-An'am], i.e., they ascribed to Him sons and daughters falsely and by invention, without knowledge. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]

3 Ifk: lying and false invention. He said: ﴿...That was their falsehood, and what they used to invent﴾ (28) [al-Ahqaf]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the falsehood are a band among you...﴾ (11) [al-Nur].

4 Yakhrusun: they lie. Khars in the Qur'an is used in the sense of lying or mistaken assumption. He said: ﴿... They only conjecture﴾ (116) [al-An'am], i.e., they lie or guess and assume, not knowing the reality with certainty. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/191]

5 Labatha: he remained and settled. The Exalted said about Yunus (peace be upon him): ﴿Then had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained inside it until the Day they are resurrected﴾ (143-144) [al-Saffat]. He said about Nuh (peace be upon him): ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years...﴾ (14) [al-'Ankabut]. And He said: ﴿...Then you stayed years among the people of Madyan; then you came at the appointed time, O Musa﴾ (40) [Ta-Ha].

6 Tabari: competition and racing.

7 Suq 'Ukaz: a market near Makkah where the Arabs gathered every year, staying for a month, buying, boasting and reciting poetry to one another. It was named 'Ukaz for this, and it is said: ta'akaza al-qawm, meaning they fought and boasted. [See Lisan al-'Arab, root '-k-z]

8 Dhu al-Majaz: a place in Mina, and it is said near 'Arafat, where a market used to be held in the Jahiliyyah. [Al-Lisan, root j-w-z]

9 Al-Majannah: a place a few miles from Makkah, where there was a market among the markets of the Arabs.

10 Al-Asir: that which captivates people's hearts and minds.

11 This is in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants"﴾ (88) [al-Isra'], i.e., helpers.

12 The Lord of Might, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it...﴾ (23) [al-Baqarah]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful"﴾ (38) [Yunus].

13 Qur'an: applied to the inimitable Book of Allah, written in the mushafs, which was sent down upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it is applied metaphorically by a relation of part to whole to the prayer, as in His saying: ﴿And the recitation of dawn...﴾ (78) [al-Isra'], i.e., the dawn prayer. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged)

The address here is directed to those who claimed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had fabricated the Qur'an, or the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); because the Exalted and Glorified Lord said in the preceding verse: ﴿Say: "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿13﴾ ﴿And if they do not respond to you...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. That is: if they do not respond to the challenge, then let them know and be certain that this Qur'an is from Allah, the Exalted, by the testimony of their own adversaries.¹

Why did the Exalted and Glorified Lord change the address here? It says: ﴿And if they do not respond to you²...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud], meaning: those whom you call upon. Then He said: ﴿then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. The Exalted Lord said that because the Messenger (ﷺ) is charged with conveying, and what the Messenger (ﷺ) conveys to the believers is required of them to convey, even if those addressed do not respond to the Messenger (ﷺ) or to the believers, and no one among those who accuse the Qur'an of being fabricated by Muhammad has come forward.

It may be that these so-called gifted ones are afraid of the challenge, because they know that the Qur'an is true, and if they came to fabricate its like, they would not be able to. Therefore, know—O you who do not believe in the Qur'an—that the Qur'an: ﴿was revealed only with the knowledge of Allah...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. Thus, the address is at one time directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his community.

For this reason, the Exalted Lord shifted from the singular pronoun to the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. That is: increase in knowledge, O believers, that the Qur'an was revealed only from Allah.

Knowledge, as we know, has three stages: the knowledge of certainty, the eye of certainty, and the truth of certainty.³

Or the address is directed to the disbelievers, whom the Qur'an asked to call upon whomever they could to help them in opposing the Qur'an: ﴿then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah...﴾ [Hud].

The highest level of knowledge belongs to the Exalted Lord, who knows all knowledge from eternity. It is different from our knowledge, which changes according to what Allah, the Exalted, permits us to know. You may be knowledgeable in one thing and ignorant of others, or you may have learned something while other things have escaped you.

This is why you find that doctors, practitioners of delicate crafts, and other researchers and scholars correct one another. When a patient goes to a doctor, for example, and he prescribes a medicine that does not work for him, the patient goes to another doctor, who corrects the first one and prescribes a medicine; and the patient may not respond to it a second time. At that point the doctors gather into a "medical council" that decides what is or is not suitable for the patient.

Each of them corrects the other until they reach a decision, and the one who corrects is the more knowledgeable, because the first doctor wrote a prescription that exhausted the patient or did not work for him, and he judged only by what he had of knowledge. The same applies to the rest of the researchers and scholars.

And since "above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing," the second doctor corrects the first doctor... and so on.

But is there anyone who corrects Allah, the Exalted and Glorified? No, there is none.

And since the noble Qur'an has come with the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, no human knowledge can produce its like: ﴿So know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no god but Him...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. The Exalted Lord mentions here "there is no god but Him" so that no one may claim that there is another god besides Allah.

The Exalted Lord mentions here that this Qur'an was revealed within the scope of: ﴿There is no god but Him...﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud]. Since the Exalted Lord has issued this judgment, let us trust this judgment. An example of that: the Exalted Lord's judgment concerning Abu Lahab⁴ and his wife⁵ that they would enter the Fire⁶. Could Abu Lahab have declared his Islam, even hypocritically? Certainly not, because the One who created him knew how Abu Lahab would behave.

Therefore, after Surah al-Masad⁷, which decided that Abu Lahab would enter the Fire, comes the saying of the Exalted Lord: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One.﴾ ﴿1﴾ [al-Ikhlas]. That is: since the Exalted Lord has issued His judgment that Abu Lahab and his wife will enter the Fire, no one will be able to change His judgment, the Exalted. There is no god but Him.

The Exalted Lord concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿...So will you be Muslims?﴾ ﴿14﴾ [Hud].

This is a question, meaning a request for understanding, but not every question is a request for understanding. This question here issues from a real will able to impose Islam upon those addressed by it.

Yet He, glory be to Him, willed that this question come on the tongue of His Messenger so that it would be met with an answer; and if the questioner were not confident that nothing exists except Islam, he would not have said it; and if the questioner were not confident that the only answer is for the listener to submit, he would not have made the listener's answer a proof against the listener.

The speaker of these words is the Creator, the Exalted, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, and He is exalted above every likeness. You find a person narrating to you an affair in its details, then asking you: "Am I truthful in what I told you?" He asks this question because he is confident that you will say to him: "Yes, you are truthful."

If we look at the verse on the prohibition of wine and gambling, for example, we find the Exalted and Glorified Lord saying: ﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you desist?﴾ ﴿91﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

This question carries the form of a command: "Desist from wine and gambling, and be ashamed of what you do."

So the saying of the Exalted Lord at the end of the noble verse: ﴿...So will you be Muslims?﴾ [Hud] means: submit, and abandon obstinacy⁸ in claiming that the Qur'an came from Muhammad, or that he fabricated it. Rather, it is from Allah, the Exalted, there is no god but Him.

¹ Muftariyat: invented, falsely fabricated, as you claim.

[Sirat Ibn Hisham 1/294].

[Said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir: 4/3331].
⁴ This division was adopted by the people of reality and spiritual knowledge, from the inspiration of scientific, spiritual and observational training.

The occasion of revelation of this surah, as al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih (4971) from Ibn 'Abbas: the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Batha, climbed the mountain, and called out "Ya sabahah!" Quraysh gathered around him, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that an enemy would attack you in the morning or in the evening, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Is it for this that you gathered us? Ruin to you!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Ruined are the hands of Abu Lahab, and ruined is he﴾ [al-Masad] to its end.
⁸ Masad al-habl (kanasr) masadan: he twisted it well. And al-masad is fiber; the Exalted said: ﴿around her neck a rope of masad﴾ [al-Masad 5]: of coarse fiber. ["al-Qamus al-Qawim"].
⁹ Shaytan: every rebellious transgressor among humans or jinn; the shaytan among the jinn is a wicked creature, created from among the jinn, and he is an enemy of the human who incites him to evil, except for one whom Allah protects through faith. The Truth says: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed shaytan﴾ [al-Hijr 17], and likewise everyone who seeks refuge in Allah, Allah protects him from the plots of Shaytan. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

So will you desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 91]. So I came to my companions and recited to them up to His saying "So will you desist?" He said: Some of the people had a cup in their hand which they had struck, and some remained in the vessel; he put the vessel under his upper lip, as the cupper does, then they poured out what was in their jug, and they said: "We have desisted, our Lord." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/95).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 15:

The Truthful (exalted is He) then says:

﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be shortchanged therein.﴾(1) (15)

The disbelievers had spoken with what Allah, exalted is He, placed upon their tongues, and they said:

﴿Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?...﴾ [Hud] (12): So they, then, are preoccupied with the bounties of this world and its adornment.

Life requires the natural necessities of existence: covering one's nakedness, a morsel of food, and a house that shields and shelters a person. As for adornment, its matter is different. Instead of a person wearing what covers his nakedness, he seeks for himself soft wool in winter and smooth silk in summer; and instead of seeking a modest room that protects him from cold or heat, he seeks for himself a palace.

Concerning this, Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women and sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilth...﴾ [Al 'Imran] (14): All of these are things that fall within the enjoyment of the life of this world. And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...That is the enjoyment of the life of this world, and with Allah is the best return.﴾ [Al 'Imran] (14). So then: what is the meaning of the word "zinah" (adornment)?

The meaning of the word "zinah" is that it is an embellishment or beautification that comes upon the essence from outside, and there is a difference between intrinsic beauty and beauty that comes from another.

A woman, for example, when she adorns herself, wears beautiful, eye-catching garments and decks herself with shining gold, which is the metal that takes its preciousness (nafasah) from the abundance of its glitter that dazzles the eyes. She does not do so excessively except one who doubts her own beauty.

As for the woman who is beautiful by nature, she refuses to adorn herself; for this reason they call her in the language "al-ghaniyah" (the self-sufficient) (8), i.e., she who has become independent of adornment through her natural beauty, and does not need to conceal the largeness of her ears with a large earring (qurt) (9), nor does she need to conceal her neck with a large necklace, nor does she try to conceal her lush wrist with a bracelet (siwar) (10), and she refuses to hide the beauty of her fingers with rings. When a woman exaggerates in such adornment, she gives the opposite impression.

The example I am giving now may be far from this field, but it clarifies how an exaggerated thing gives the opposite of what it is meant to show.

Concerning this, al-Mutanabbi (11) says: "The perfume is you, when its scent reaches you; and the water is you, when you bathe — the washer."

He here means: if perfume touches that described person, it is the perfume that becomes scented, just as water is what washes when it touches this person. Likewise, the beautiful woman disdains to adorn her throat (nahr) (12) with a necklace (qiladah) (13), because her throat without a necklace is more beautiful. Such a woman is called "ghaniyah" because she has become self-sufficient through her beauty.

The beauty of urban women is described as beauty made with cosmetics, as if those cosmetics were fixed upon the face with a paste like the paste of wall paints, and as if each one who does this had brought a knife of paste to fill the wrinkled cracks in her face.

At the moment this paste melts, she becomes flustered, and the sight of her face is disordered by the mixture of colors; for this reason it is said:

"The beauty of the city is brought by refinement, while in the desert there is a beauty that is not brought by adornment."

So then: adornment is the beautifying of a thing by other than itself, and the thing that is self-sufficient needs no adornment.

Here Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be shortchanged therein.﴾ (14) (15) [Hud]. That is: if you disbelieve in Allah, He, exalted is He, does not withhold from you that He should give you the necessities of life along with its adornment, because He is Lord, and He is the One who created you and brought you into existence; and Allah, exalted is He, has obligated Himself to give you what you desire of the necessities of life and its adornment, because He, exalted is He, is able to fulfil what He has promised.

He, exalted is He, says here: ﴿We will repay them for their deeds...﴾ (15) [Hud]. That is: if they take the means, then Allah, exalted is He, obligates Himself to give the thing in full, without diminution.

And they, in this lower world, will not be shortchanged in their rights; whoever perfects his work takes the fruit of his work.

This noble statement resolves for us a great difficulty from which we suffer. There are those who say: these Muslims who say "there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," who establish prayer and build mosques, while there are peoples who are backward and lag behind the caravan of civilization, while we find the disbelievers reveling in the bounties of civilization.

We say: Allah, exalted is He, has a lordly giving to the means; whoever takes the best means, even if he is a disbeliever, the means give him, but he has no share in the Hereafter, because Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ [Al-Furqan] (23). Allah, exalted is He, repays the disbeliever who gives good to people with good in this world, and repays the truthful disbeliever who does not lie with the truthfulness of others toward him in this world, and repays one who extends his hand in help among the disbelievers with help to him in this world.

These are all deeds that are demanded in religion, but the disbeliever may do them, and Allah, exalted is He, returns to him what he did in this world, even if he did it so that it would be said: "So-and-so did such-and-such," or "So-and-so was courageous in such-and-such," and it is said to him: "You acted so that it would be said, and it has been said."

And if the disbelievers take the means, then Allah, exalted is He, gives them the fruit of what they took by way of means.

We must say to whoever accuses the Muslims of backwardness: the Muslims in the early part of their history were advanced, and they were masters when they applied their religion, outwardly and inwardly, in form and in substance.

Accordingly, backwardness is neither necessary nor concomitant with Islam; rather, backwardness came because we abandoned the spirit of Islam and its application.

If we make a comparison between the condition of Europe when the Church was dominant, we find that every creative intellectual was sentenced to death as punishment for creativity, and those days in Europe were called "the Dark Ages."

When the Crusades came and Europe recognised the strength of Islam and Muslims, and the Muslims repelled them (18), they began trying to break out of the authority of the Pope and the Church, and when they did so, they advanced.

They, then, when they left the authority of the Pope, advanced, and we, when we left off acting upon the teachings of Islam, fell behind. So then: which of the two doses is better?

The reality of life has proven the advancement of the Muslims when they took the teachings of Islam, and their backwardness when they abandoned them.

And thus: the criterion of progress is taking the means. Whoever takes the means while he is a believer attains the goodness of the world's good and the goodness of the Hereafter's reward; and whoever does not believe but takes the means attains the good of the world and does not attain the reward of the Hereafter.

And Allah, exalted is He, is the One who says: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him...﴾ [An-Nur] (39).

Thus he is surprised by the God whom he denied.

And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes, upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they earned...﴾ [Ibrahim] (18).

So then: whoever desires the world and its adornment, the Most High Truth, exalted is He, pays him his account and does not diminish any of his right. Hatim al-Ta'i, for example, took the quality of generosity, and 'Antarah took the quality of bravery, and every person who did good work received his wage; but the gift of the Hereafter belongs to whoever worked his work for the sake of Allah, exalted is He, and believed in Him.

Even those who entered Islam hypocritically and fought alongside the Muslims took their share of the spoils, but they have no share in the Hereafter.

So then: fulfilment means the existence of a contract, and as long as there is a contract between the worker and the work, and the worker perfects the work, he must take his wage without diminution; because "bakhs" is the diminishing of a right.

(1) "Bakhasahu haqqahu": he diminished his right and did not pay it to him in full. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And do not diminish people's things...﴾ [Al-A'raf] (85). And "a price that is bakhs" is a small price that falls short of its equivalent: ﴿And they sold him for a bakhs price...﴾ [Yusuf] (20).

(2) The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. It was said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers, as said by al-Dahhak, and chosen by al-Nahhas, on the evidence of the following verse: ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire...﴾ [Hud] (16); that is, whoever among them performs an act of kinship or charity, he is rewarded for it in this world with bodily health and abundant provision, but there is no good for him in the Hereafter. It was also said: the verse means believers, i.e., whoever intends by his deed the reward of this world, it is hastened to him and nothing is diminished for him in this world, but for him in the Hereafter is punishment, because he stripped his intention for the world. It was also said: it refers to showing off, and a report says that it will be said to the people of showing off: "You fasted, prayed, gave charity, fought, and recited so that it would be said, and it has been said," then: "These are the first by whom the Fire will be kindled." It was also said: the verse is general to everyone who intends by his knowledge other than Allah, exalted is He, whether he had the root of faith or not. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3331].

(3) "Qanatir" is the plural of "qintar", a measure of differing quantity among people; in our time in Egypt it is one hundred pounds, which is 44,928 kilograms, and it may be meant to denote great wealth, as in the noble verse. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you...﴾ [Al 'Imran] (75). "Al-qanatir al-muqantarah" means: the multiplied, or the firmly fortified.

(4) "Al-khayl al-musawwamah": those sent out to pasture, or those marked with marks.

(5) "Al-an'am": camels, cattle, sheep and goats. "Al-harth": cultivated crops.

(6) "Al-ma'ab": the place of return. "Husn al-ma'ab": the good place of return.

(7) "Nafisa al-shay' nafasah": it was of great value, so it is precious (nafis). It was said: from it comes "tanafus" (competition): each wants to be more precious than another, or to attain what is more precious and of greater value. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...For this let the competitors compete﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin] (26), i.e., let them race to attain it for themselves.

(8) "Al-ghaniyah min al-nisa'": she who is made independent by a husband. It is also said: she who has become independent through her beauty and loveliness from jewellery. It was also said: she is one who is sought and does not seek. It was said: "al-ghaniyah" is the beautiful young woman, whether or not she has a husband. She was named "ghaniyah" because she became independent of adornment through her beauty. [Lisan al-'Arab, root gh-n-y].

(9) "Al-qurt": what hangs from the lobe of the ear, of pearl, gold, silver or the like. Plural: "aqrat" and "qurut". [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

(10) "Al-siwar": an ornament of gold, round like a ring, worn on the wrist. Plural: "asawir" and "asawir". [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

(11) He is Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, a wise poet, born in Kufa in a quarter called "Kindah" in the year 303 AH; he grew up in Syria and claimed prophethood in the desert of al-Samawah (between Kufa and Syria). For this he was called al-Mutanabbi. Then he retracted his claim after being captured. He died in the year 354 AH at the age of 52.

(12) "Al-nahr": the upper chest, the place of the necklace.

(13) "Al-qiladah": everything placed around the neck, of strings, jewellery, gold and other things. Sacrificial animals were called "qala'id" metaphorically by metonymy of association, because sacrificial animals were marked with necklaces on their necks. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Nor the sacrificial offering, nor the garlanded ones...﴾ [Al-Ma'idah] (2), i.e., the sacrificial animals adorned with garlands.

(14) "Al-bakhs": diminution. "Bakhasahu bakhsan": he diminished his right and did not pay it to him in full. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And do not diminish people's things...﴾ [Al-A'raf] (85). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

(15) "Rafala": he dragged the hem of his garment and strutted in his walk. "Yarfulun fi al-na'im": they live in luxury, joyful with the bounties they have. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, slightly adapted].

(16) "Al-habaa' al-mansur": dust scattered in the air. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿...and We made it scattered dust﴾ [Al-Furqan] (23), i.e., every deed they did is like scattered dust, not counted and of no value. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

(17) On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought forward, and Allah will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will be asked: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I fought for You until I was martyred.' He will be told: 'You lie; rather, you fought so that it would be said: "He is brave." And it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. And a man who learned knowledge and taught it, and recited the Qur'an, will be brought forward, and Allah will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will be asked: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I learned knowledge and taught it, and recited the Qur'an for You.' He will be told: 'You lie; rather, you learned knowledge so that it would be said: "He is a scholar," and you recited the Qur'an so that it would be said: "He is a reciter." And it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. And a man whom Allah made wealthy and gave all kinds of wealth, will be brought forward, and Allah will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will be asked: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I left no path in which You love spending except that I spent in it for You.' He will be told: 'You lie; rather, you did it so that it would be said: "He is generous." And it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face, and then cast into the Fire." [Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1905), Book of Leadership].

(18) "Dahrahu yadharuhu dahran wa duhuran": he repelled him, drove him away and banished him in humiliation. "Dahrahu fi al-harb": he defeated him in war. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...And they are pelted from every side, repelled, and for them is a constant punishment﴾ [As-Saffat] (8-9). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

(19) "Al-sarab": what you see at midday on open ground, looking like water but not water. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and become a mirage﴾ [An-Naba'] (20), i.e., they will have no reality, resembling a mirage in having no reality, or like a flat ground in which a mirage appears. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

(20) "Al-qa' and al-qay'ah": level ground that is lower than the mountains and hills surrounding it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains; say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast, and leave them a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation﴾ [Ta-Ha] (105-107). "Qa'an safsafan": a low, level, even place with no elevation or unevenness. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a qay'ah [An-Nur] (39), i.e., in a low, level place where a mirage usually appears. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

(21) "'Asafat al-rih, ta'sifu 'asfan wa 'usufan": its blowing became violent. "Al-rih 'asif" and "'asifah": it is both masculine and feminine. Sometimes the violent wind destroys everything it passes over. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to Solomon the wind, violently blowing﴾ [Al-Anbiya'] (81); and He says: ﴿A violent wind came upon them﴾ [Yunus] (22); and He says: ﴿By those that blow violently, blast upon blast﴾ [Al-Mursalat] (2), meaning the strong winds. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. What they did there is rendered void, and what they used to do is nullified.﴾

So: the Fire is the abode of those who worked for the sake of this world without faith in Allah. They have already received their reckoning in this world, while their deeds have come to nothing (ḥabaṭa) in the Hereafter. Ḥabaṭ is the swelling of livestock when it eats something green that has not yet ripened. In the countryside this is described as: "the animal has swelled up," meaning that there are gases in its belly. The ignorant person may think it is fatness, but this swelling disappears when its cause disappears.

The deeds of the disbelievers are indeed rendered void in the Hereafter, because they are false (bāṭil).

1 Ḥabiṭa al-ʿamal: it became void and did not achieve its fruit. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deed has become void...﴾ [al-Mā'idah 5], and Allah nullified his deed: He made it void and scattered it as dust. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿...So He rendered their deeds void﴾ [Muhammad 9] [al-Qamus al-Qawim]...

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy? Those believe in it. And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾ (17)

The bayyinah (clear proof) is the insight of the sound fitrah (innate disposition), which draws a person's attention to the existence of the Necessary Existent (wajib al-wujud), and makes clear to him that this beautiful, wondrous universe must have a Creator. Thus guidance comes through insight and fitrah.

The ancient Arab, when he traversed the desert and found dung lying in the wilderness and saw a footprint, would say: "Dung indicates the camel, and a track indicates the one who passed by. Heaven with its constellations, earth with its wide paths, and seas with their waves: does not all of this indicate the All-Subtle, the All-Aware?" (6) Thus the man was guided by fitrah, which is a clear proof from God.

God, glorified is He, has placed fitrah in every human being, and by this fitrah we bore witness in the realm of atoms (ʿalam al-dhurr). Concerning this, the Almighty says: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify..."﴾ (172) [al-A'raf]. Therefore, the bayyinah is the faith of fitrah embedded in the essences of things.

Desires may cloud this faith, so that a person does not compel himself to the method. So God, in His mercy, sends messengers who remind us of the first clear proofs and guide us to the causes and rulings, so that the clear proof from the messengers joins the clear proof of the fitrah within the creature.

Thus the Almighty explains the basis for being convinced of God's religion. This matter may be unknown to people, so He wishes to show us that this ignorance is unnatural, because the sound fitrah is guided even before a messenger comes to draw our attention to the supreme power that governs the movement of this universe.

I have previously given an example of this: a man whose plane crashed in the desert, with no water, no food, no companion, and no shelter. Then sleep overcame him and he slept, and when he woke he found a table set with the finest food and the finest drink, and found a tent erected for him to shelter in. This person must inevitably turn over in his mind the question: Who made this?

He will ask himself this question before he enjoys any of it, especially since he has found no one to say to him, "You are my guest." Therefore, he must think with his intellect.

Likewise the human being who came into existence. No created being has claimed to have created this existence, no one has claimed to have created the heavens and the earth, and no one has claimed to have subjected everything in the universe to serve man.

Before enjoying all this, a person was obliged to think: Who made all of this for him? Then, if a messenger from the human race came and said to him, "I have come to solve for you the riddle that is posed to you"...

Here the person must lend his ear to that messenger, because he has come to resolve a matter that occupies the human mind.

Among God's kindnesses toward us is that He did not require us to reflect on this beforehand, but left us for a long period without obligation in this world, so that a person might enjoy his Lord's bounty. Then, when maturity and full discernment arrive, and he is not compelled, the Almighty obliges him with the duties of faith.

A person must ask himself: everything, however trivial, must have a maker. The lamp that illuminates a circle of twenty meters in diameter: we know its maker, we have studied the factories that produced it, the capabilities used, and the materials from which it was made. Shall we not know the history of this sun, and who made it need no maintenance, no fuel, no spare parts, and illuminates half the terrestrial globe?

This is a matter we ought to investigate, so that we may see the horizons of that proof, a proof of light, strength and fitrah, which God bestows upon the thinking human being, so that he may be guided to realize that behind this universe there is a Creator who governs.

When a human being like him comes and says, "The Creator of this world is God, the Exalted, and He requires of you such and such," it is logical and natural for us to listen to this person and to test what he says against the sense of fitrah and the sight of clear proofs.

Thus, we reach the unknown first through fitrah, and we may reach it through self-evident knowledge (badihah) which is not tainted with the slightest doubt. When you see smoke, you believe by self-evident knowledge that there is fire. When you walk in the desert and see greenery, do you not believe that there is water that irrigates it?

These, then, are matters you know by self-evident knowledge, and they require no investigation or effort.

There are other matters that may require intellectual effort, by which you seek what lies beyond the premises, such as the intellectual effort by which the Arab reasoned that there is a Creator God who governs this universe. From the dung you infer the existence of the camel, and that the track indicates the one who passed. From this he concluded that the constellations with their orbits, the earth with its wide paths, and the seas with their waves are all indications of the existence of the All-Subtle, the All-Aware.

Reason was only able to pass a general judgment on all of these, even though it did not know the details.

Reason has known that behind this universe is a Creator, a Maker, a Wise One, but it did not know His name. This is something a person cannot know by reason alone, nor can he know what method is required by this Creator, with what He rewards the one who obeys Him, or with what He punishes the one who disobeys Him.

Therefore, there must be a communication (balagh) from God, the Exalted, that indicates the power in which one has generally become convinced.

Those who think by reason about the universe know that behind this universe is a Creator, but they do not know His name or what He requires.

Therefore, you know God's name only from Him, through revelation to His messenger, and you know what God requires only from the messenger to whom the communication was sent.

Among God's mercies toward the human being is that He sent a messenger, and with this messenger is a miracle (mu'jizah), which is the Qur'an. Because reason, until it is guided to the power of the Supreme Able One, He, glory be to Him, will remain obscure to it. When the Almighty sent down the noble Qur'an, He sent it down as a mercy to His servants and as a clear proof for them.

﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it...﴾ (17) [Hud]. So the Qur'an is a proof and a light. It guides the innate insight of fitrah present in the human being, ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, and this is the one to whom revelation was sent. It informs us about the Almighty, that the Supreme Creator and absolute Power is God, glory be to Him, and it clarifies for us what God the Exalted requires of the witness. Here we are before three witnesses:

The first witness: is the proof and the clear evidence.

The second witness: is the demonstration and insight that the intellect is guided to, and the messenger is the one who explains the method after the general outline.

And this messenger came after the Book of Moses: ﴿and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy﴾ (17) [Hud]. This is the third witness.

Whoever does not pay attention to what is indicated by these three proofs is negligent: the one who has that clear proof within him, the one who heard the witness from the messenger, and the witness who is the heart, namely the Book of Moses, peace be upon him, and the witness that followed it among the people of Moses. This must lead him to faith.

The Almighty's words: ﴿Those believe in it﴾ (17) [Hud]: an indication of those who turned to the evidences: the clear proof, the witness, and the witness before it.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ (17) [Hud]. Disbelief (kufr), as we have known, is concealment, and disbelief in itself is a proof of faith, since no one disbelieves in something non-existent.

The existence of the object disbelieved in precedes the disbelief, and disbelief is something that occurs subsequently to it. Therefore, disbelief is an accident upon faith, because faith is the origin of fitrah.

﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ (17) [Hud]. The word "factions" (ahzab) is the plural of hizb (party). A hizb is a group gathered upon a principle, to whose implementation they are zealous, such as the parties one sees in political life. These are human parties that contend over methods and aims, and they are free in that, because they contend with human thought.

As for the first creed, it comes from the highest plan, which is the Almighty, so the method comes from Him, because this method leads to Him. Therefore God, glory be to Him, said about those who follow His method: ﴿Those are the party of God...﴾ (22) [al-Mujadila]. That is, they enter a party that differs from the human parties, which differ or agree according to human thought.

Here the Almighty says: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ (17) [Hud]. What is meant by them are the Quraysh polytheists, worshippers of idols, the Sabians, the Jews and the Christians who did not believe in the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Each of them is a group representing a party. Concerning them the Almighty says: ﴿...each party, with what they have, rejoicing﴾ (53) [al-Mu'minun]. Whoever among these disbelieves in the message of the Messenger of God and in the Messenger of God, the recompense is the Fire. Thus God, the Exalted, has shown us that there are two parties: the party of God and the other factions, and they are two groups each facing the other.

The Almighty says to His Messenger, and also meaning the community of Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾ (17) [Hud]. That is: do not be, O Messenger of God, in doubt about that, because your message and your mission rest upon the proofs of clear evidence, fitrah, guidance and the light sought from God, and the witness is with you, just as the one who came before you testified that you came with the true method: ﴿Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord﴾ (17) [Hud].

The truth, as we have known before, is the established thing that is not subject to change, and this truth can come only from a God whose acts do not change.

The Almighty concludes the verse with His words: ﴿...but most people do not believe﴾ (17) [Hud]. These do not believe out of obstinacy, because the proofs are set up with the strongest arguments, and whoever refuses them is merely stubborn.

The Almighty says concerning such obstinate people: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ (14) [al-Naml]. That is: despite their disbelief, they know the truth of the proofs for the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the truth of his mission. Thus their disbelief is then disbelief out of obstinacy, because the proofs are set up with the strongest arguments, so whoever refuses to believe in these proofs is an obstinate person.

1 Murya: disputation and doubt; likewise tamari, imtira', mira' and mumaraha. God the Exalted said: ﴿So do not argue about them except with outward argument...﴾ (22) [al-Kahf]; and He said: ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ (147) [al-Baqarah]; and He said: ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you dispute?﴾ (55) [al-Najm]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.

2 Bana al-shay' yabinu bayanan: it became manifest and clear; so it is bayyin and it is bayyinah, that is, evident and apparent. Bayyin and bayyinah are used in the sense of manifest and manifested, and clarifying and clarified. God the Exalted said: ﴿How many a clear sign We have given them...﴾ (211) [al-Baqarah], meaning clear and free of doubt, or it clarifies the truth, supports it, and makes its matter manifest. Likewise God the Exalted said: ﴿Why do they not bring a clear authority for them?﴾ (15) [al-Kahf], meaning evident and clear, or clarifying and making the truth manifest. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

3 Al-bi'rah: the singular of al-ba'r, which is the droppings of hoofed and cloven-hoofed animals.

4 Al-abraj: plural of burj, which are the stations of the celestial spheres in the sky, or they are the stars. It was said: they are the stars. [Lisan al-Arab, root b-r-j].

5 Al-fijaj: plural of fajj, which is a wide road between two mountains. From it is God's saying: ﴿And God has made the earth for you a spread-out carpet, that you may traverse therein broad roads﴾ (19–20) [Nuh]. And He said: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with them, and We placed therein broad pathways that they may be guided﴾ (31) [al-Anbiya'].

6 These phrases are from a sermon delivered by Qass ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi in the pre-Islamic period. Its beginning was: "O people, listen and take heed. Whoever lives dies, whoever dies is gone, and whatever is to come, will come." See al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin by al-Jahiz (1/308).

7 On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/233), al-Tayalisi (2433), and al-Tirmidhi (2138).

8 Al-dabb and al-tadbib: covering a thing and one part entering into another. Al-dababah is a cloud that covers the earth like smoke; it was said: al-dabab and al-dababah are dew like dust that covers the earth in the mornings. [Lisan al-Arab, root d-b-b].

9 Manat al-shay': everything to which a matter is attached. Naata bihi al-shay': he connected it with it. [Lisan, root n-w-t, adapted].

10 Al-sawan: the container in which garments are preserved or in which food is placed. See [Lisan, root s-w-n].

11 God the Exalted says in Surat al-Nahl: ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. And what He has created for you on the earth of varied colours. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember. And it is He who subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh meat and extract from it ornaments you wear, and you see the ships plowing through it, and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (12–14) [al-Nahl].

12 That is, no doubt mixes with it, meaning thought free from desires. Shawb is that which is mixed with other things, especially liquids. God the Exalted said: ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of scalding water﴾ (67) [al-Saffat]. It is said: he gave him to drink dhawb with shawb: honey mixed with water or milk. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

13 Al-bi'rah: droppings of hoofed and cloven-hoofed animals. Al-ba'ir: that which is fit for riding and carrying among camels, when it has completed four years. The camel and the she-camel are called ba'ir. The plural is a'bir, a'abir, and ba'ran. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

14 Because there are many opinions regarding the interpretation of this witness, which al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (4/3334):
That it is Muhammad (ﷺ).
That it is Jibril, peace be upon him.
That it is Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The Qur'an in its arrangement and eloquence, with its many meanings in a single word.
The Gospel, for it recites the Qur'an in confirmation, though his heart is [...].
The intellect, which recites knowledge of God, by which hearts have been illuminated.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/440), after mentioning the first three opinions: "The first and second are the truth, and both are close in meaning, because both Jibril and Muhammad, may the blessings of God be upon them, conveyed the message of God: Jibril to Muhammad, and Muhammad to the community. It was also said that it is Ali, but this is weak, and no one holds it. The believer has within his fitrah what testifies to the Shari'ah in general, and the details are taken from the Shari'ah, and the fitrah confirms it and believes in it."

15 What is meant here is the Gospel with which Jesus, peace be upon him, was sent to the Children of Israel.

16 Ahzab: plural of hizb, which is a group of people who have gathered upon one matter, whether good or evil. God says concerning the party of good: ﴿...Those are the party of God. Unquestionably, the party of God are the successful﴾ (22) [al-Mujadila]. And He said concerning the party of evil: ﴿Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of God. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ (19) [al-Mujadila].
What is meant by the factions here is the people of all religions other than the religion of Islam. Said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3335).

17 On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, no one from this community hears of me, be he Jew or Christian, and then dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, Book of Faith, hadith (240).

18 The Sabians: they claim to be upon the religion of Noah, peace be upon him. It was said: they are worshippers of angels, or worshippers of the stars and planets, or worshippers of fire. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Christians and the Sabians...﴾ (62) [al-Baqarah]. So they are other than the Jews and Christians. [See al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/365].

19 Murya: disputation and doubt. There is also a reading with a damma on the mim. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

20 What is meant is denying the truth, yajhaduhu juhudan: he denied it while knowing it. Jahada al-ni'mah: he denied the blessing and did not give thanks for it. Jahada bi-al-ayah: he disbelieved in the sign.
God the Exalted said: ﴿And those were 'Ad, who denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers...﴾ (59) [Hud]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Istayqana al-amr wa-istayqana bihi: mithl ayqanahu wa-ayqana bihi, min al-yaqin (certainty) wa-huwa al-shay' al-thabit al-wadih alladhi la shakk fihi. Wa-istayqanatha anfusuhum: ay: ʿalimat-hā nufusuhum ʿilman wadihan.[al-Qamus al-Qawim]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 18:

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates(1) a lie against Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses(2) will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ (11:18)

This verse begins with a certain statement in the form of a question, so that the admission comes from those who fabricated lies against Allah, and admission is the master of proofs.

When one of these fabricators hears the question and turns his mind over the wrongdoers, he will find no injustice more grievous or more evil than one who fabricates a lie against Allah and admits to it.

Thus the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted willed that this statement come in the form of a question, so that the answer would come as an acknowledgment of this terrible injustice.

These deniers will be presented (ya'ruduna) before Allah, in confirmation of the saying of the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord…﴾ (11:18). Al-'ard (presentation) is the display of a hidden thing so that we may stand upon its condition.

An example of this in our lives is the military parade, through which the army displays its strength before its adversaries, and through which the state conveys to other states the measure of its power.

Likewise, we find the officer reviewing his unit in order to stand upon the condition of its members, to measure the degree of discipline of each individual, the neatness of his appearance, and the soldiers' readiness to obey orders.

Another example from our lives: we find the school principal reviewing his pupils at the moment the examination results are announced, and the principal and the pupils see the disgrace of those among them who fell short or who did not perform their duty fully.

So what of being presented before Allah, the Exalted, when the deniers see their own state of disgrace?

That is because they will be surprised by the existence of Allah, whom they denied by fabrication; for the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain (biqi'a(3)), which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him…﴾ (24:39). So what disgrace, then, will they feel?!

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted reveals what was hidden of them when all are presented before Allah, the Exalted, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in ranks…﴾ (18:48). Likewise they will be presented before the Fire, for the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted is the One who says: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening…﴾ (40:46). Thus disgrace, shame and humiliation appear upon those who fabricated lies against Allah, the Exalted.

He, glorified is He, knows everything from eternity, but He willed by this to reveal people before one another and before themselves, so that when a person in Paradise sees a person in the Fire, this sight does not stir the pity of the believer, because he knows that the recompense of the fabricator is the Fire.

Would that the matter were limited to this disgrace! Rather, there is the testimony of the witnesses, for the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says in the same verse: ﴿And the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord…"﴾ (11:18). Al-ashhad (the witnesses) is the plural of a broken plural whose singular is sometimes "shahid," like "sahib" and "ashab," and sometimes the singular is "shahid," like "sharif" and "ashraf."

Among the witnesses are the angels, for the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready (raqib 'atid(6))﴾ (50:18).

Likewise the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians(7), noble writers, who know whatever you do﴾ (82:10–12).

Or they are witnesses from among the prophets who conveyed to them the method of Allah, for the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ (4:41). Also, the witness against these is the believer from the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, who conveys it to others, in confirmation of the saying of the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿And thus We have made you a median community that you may be witnesses over mankind…﴾ (2:143). The word "testimony" (shahada) means recording what they did, and it also records that they were conveyed the method, opposed it and rebelled against it, thus committing the crime that requires punishment, because punishment is not imposed except for a crime, and there is no criminalization except by text, and no text except by notification.

Therefore we find the laws issued by the state always bearing the phrase: "The law takes effect from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette."

So the function of the witnesses is to declare that those who denied the message and the Messenger have been conveyed the method, and that they were told that denial of this method and denial of this Messenger is the greatest crime, and that the punishment for this denial is eternal abiding in the Fire.

And because the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted is justice itself, there is no punishment except after certainty of the commission of the crime; therefore multiple testimonies are necessary. Thus a witness comes from the angels, who are of a kind other than that of those presented, and a witness comes from the prophets, who are of the human kind but are infallible.

Likewise a witness comes from the believing brethren who testify that they have conveyed the method of faith. Then comes a testimony which is the chief of all testimonies: the testimony of the parts upon the whole.

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿And on the Day the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in groups. Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."﴾ (41:19–21). So the limbs speak to establish the proof against those sinners.

Asking the sinners about how the speech came about is pointless; therefore the question here is "why" (lima), because the limbs were the tools of the sinners in committing their crimes: the hand is what reached out to steal, the tongue is what uttered false speech, the heart is what harboured spite, and the leg is what walked toward disobedience.

The human being, as we know, is composed of limbs, and these limbs have systems that make up the whole human being, and the director of the whole body is the intellect. It is the one that orders the hand to reach out and steal, or to reach out to pat the orphan; and the eye takes its orders from the intellect: either it commands it to look upon the beauty of the universe and take lessons from what it sees of events, or it commands it to look upon the unlawful.

Therefore the limbs are obedient servants, subjected to that human being and his will; but the matter differs in the Hereafter, where no one has command except Allah.

And the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿…"To whom belongs the dominion today?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer."﴾ (40:16). So the limbs will say on the Day of Resurrection to their owners: "We used to do what you commanded us of disobedience against our will, because we were subjected to you in the world; and now your will has been released from us, so we say what you did not compel us to do."

Thus the witnesses acknowledge, in confirmation of the saying of the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿…And the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ (11:18). And since they lied against their Lord, the one lied against is Allah, and He must expel them from mercy; and they have committed the utmost injustice, which is associating partners with Him, atheism (ilhad(10)), and denying the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and the message.

1 Iftara al-qawl: he invented and devised it. Iftara 'alayhi al-kadhib: he invented the lie. The Exalted says: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it…"﴾ (10:38), meaning: he composed the Qur'an and fabricated it from himself.

2 Al-ashhad: that is, the witnesses to the truth. Ashhad is the plural of shahid, like aytam, the plural of yatim. The shahid is an adjective of the attributive form. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]. Regarding the identification of the witnesses in this verse there are opinions: the guardian angels; the prophets and messengers. Qatada said: all creation together. Reported by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3336).

3 Al-saraab: what is seen at midday on open ground as if it were water, though it is not water; it is a phenomenon connected with deception of the sight. Al-biqi'a: level ground lower than what surrounds it of heights; likewise al-qa'. The Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about the mountains; say, "My Lord will blow them away with blasting. And He will leave them a level plain (qa'an safsafa), in which you will see no crookedness or elevation"﴾ (20:105–107) [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]. The safsaf earth is level smooth ground, i.e., the mountains will vanish so that no trace of them remains, and in their place you will see no elevation, no descent, and no crookedness.

4 Al-ghuduww: entering at the beginning of the day. Al-'ashiyy: the end of the day. This verse was said concerning Pharaoh and his household. Its completion: ﴿…And on the Day the Hour is established, "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ (40:46). This verse is a foundation for affirming the punishment of the grave according to the People of the Sunnah. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/81).

5 Al-lafz: bringing a thing out of the mouth, and the intended meaning is speech. Al-lafz also means casting and throwing in general. From it is the hadith of Ibn 'Umar that he was asked about what the sea casts up (lafaza), and he was forbidden from it, meaning what the sea throws to its shore of fish without hunting. [Lisan al-'Arab: root l-f-z].

6 Al-raqib al-'atid: the present one, prepared to record what the human being says in the book of good and evil deeds. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

7 Al-hafizun: that is, the watching angels and those who guard you. The Exalted says: ﴿There is over every soul a guardian (hafiz)﴾ (86:4), meaning a guarding angel watching over it. The Exalted says: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians…﴾ (6:61), meaning angels who guard you and observe your deeds. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

8 On the authority of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: "Recite the Qur'an to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "I like to hear it from others." So I recited Surat al-Nisa until I reached: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ (4:41). I raised my head, or a man nudged me on my side, so I raised my head and saw his tears flowing. Reported by Muslim in his Sahih (800) and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5055).

9 Yuza'un: they are prevented from scattering and gathered into one place. Al-wazᶜ: restraint and prevention. It is said: I arranged the army (wazza'tu al-jaysh), when I held back its first from its last, so that they are prevented from dispersing and spreading out. [See Lisan al-'Arab, root w-z-' ].

10 Al-mulhid: one who is unjust, deviating from the truth, introducing into it what is not part of it. It is said: he has deviated in religion, i.e., turned away from it. Ilhad is injustice in the sacred precinct, and it is also doubt about Allah and inclination away from belief in Him. [See Lisan al-'Arab, root l-h-d].

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), commentary on surah 11, verse 19:

Then the Exalted Lord says:
