﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, of the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾

Here the Qur'an tells us about those who disbelieved in Allah, His signs and His Messenger (ﷺ), and who were not content with their own disbelief. Rather, they went to excess and wanted to bar others from faith.

Thus they transgressed in crime: having committed the crime against themselves, they then wanted others to commit it too.

Allah, the Exalted, had earlier sent a specific address to the People of the Scripture, who had previously believed in a messenger before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But greed for temporal authority blinded them, so they obliterated the verses announcing the Messenger of Allah in their books. In doing so, they were barring from the way of Allah, and they wanted life to proceed in a crooked manner.

The Exalted Lord says: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ [Al 'Imran]

Allah, the Exalted, sent His Messenger (ﷺ) to straighten what is crooked in matters of the method. Crookedness (al-'awaj) is the absence of straightness and evenness, and it may exist in values, which are what is hidden in non-material matters. So you say: "Morals that have crookedness in them," and "the trustworthiness of so-and-so has crookedness in it."

The Exalted Lord says: ﴿Praise be to Allah who sent down upon His servant the Book and did not make in it any crookedness﴾ [Al-Kahf]. Here, in the verse we are reflecting upon, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and seek to make it crooked...﴾ [Hud]. With tangible matters, one does not say "'iwaj" (with a kasra) but "'awaj" (with a fatha). So if you see something crooked among tangible things, you say: 'awaj.

Yet we read in the Qur'an the saying of the Exalted Lord: ﴿They ask you about the mountains; say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast. And He will leave them as level plains, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha]. Allah has presented it in this form for the precision of the Qur'anic expression, because there is a tangible crookedness that a person perceives, such as when a person walks in the desert and finds the path flat, then it rises over a hillock, then flattens again, then a mountain stands in the path, then he descends into a valley. Anyone who sees such a path finds crookedness in it.

But if you see the land spread out and level, like farmland, you may think it is level, but it is not so. Evidence of this is that when the farmer floods the land with water, he finds a patch of ground submerged in water and another piece of the same land untouched by the water. Thus we know that the land had crookedness at the moment the water came, and water, as we know, is the measure of all flat things.

Therefore, when we want to judge whether a wall or a piece of ground is level, we bring a water level, because it prevents any crookedness, however subtle and fine it may be, which the naked eye may not see.

On the Day of Resurrection, the people of crookedness in belief will come, and the Exalted Lord depicts them in His saying: ﴿On that Day they will follow the caller, with no crookedness toward him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ [Ta-Ha]. They, then, line up without deviation, as criminals line up following the orders of those who lead them to prison, in humiliation and abasement, and they speak only in whispers.

Here the Exalted Lord says: ﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, of the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾ [Hud]. The reason for their barring from the way of Allah is that they want the situation to be crooked and deviant, and that they frighten people away from faith so that they may secure temporal authority for themselves and spread corruption in the land, because the coming of reform through faith is something that utterly disturbs them and deprives them of what they profit from through corruption.

1 'Iwaj (عوج): it inclined and bent and was not upright. One says 'aja 'iwajan (with fatha on the 'ayn and waw) and 'awajan (with kasra on the 'ayn and fatha on the waw). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness...﴾ [Az-Zumar 39:28], meaning a Qur'an straight in its principles and rulings. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and seek to make it crooked...﴾ [Hud 11:19], meaning that the wrongdoers who bar from the way of Allah want the way of Allah to be crooked. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]
2 ﴿and did not make in it any crookedness﴾: meaning it is a straight, sound Qur'an in its rulings and principles, with no crookedness in it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
3 Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-'Arab (root 'wj): "With a fatha on the 'ayn, it is specific to any visible person, like bodies; with a kasra, to what is not visible, like opinion and speech. It is said that the kasra is used for both, but the first is more common."
4 ﴿fa-yadharuha qa'an safsafa﴾: al-qa' is land level and lower than what surrounds it. As-safsaf is smooth, level land. Meaning: the mountains will be removed, so no trace of them remains. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]. Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir that Allah removes the mountains from their places, annihilates them and sets them in motion, making the earth a qa' safsaf, i.e., a single flat expanse. Al-qa' is the level ground, and as-safsaf emphasizes the evenness of the earth on that day. It was also said: the land with no vegetation, though the first is more appropriate, even if the latter is also intended by implication. This is why He said: ﴿you will see in it no crookedness or unevenness﴾, meaning on that day you will see in the earth no valley, no hillock, no low place or high place. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah and others. [Ibn Kathir 3/165]
5 ﴿you will see in it no crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:107]: meaning it is smooth and level, with no deviation to the right or left, no inclination at all, and no depression or elevation. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]
6 ﴿On that Day they will follow the caller, with no crookedness toward him﴾: meaning on the Day of Resurrection, in which they see these states and terrors, they hasten to respond to the caller, and wherever they are commanded, they rush to it; had this been in the world, it would have been more beneficial for them. Qatadah said: "no crookedness toward him" means they do not turn away from him. "Khashat" means became still. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/165]
7 Khashat al-aswat: they were subdued and quieted, a metaphor for the intensity of awe and fear on the Day of Resurrection. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/194]
8 As-sighar (with a shadda on the sad): submission in humiliation and abasement. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: sghr]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 20:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Those were not able to escape¹ in the earth, and they had no protectors besides Allah. The punishment will be doubled for them. They could not bear to hear, nor did they see.﴾ (11:20)

I'jaz (ʿijāz) is inability (imtinaʿ). One says aʿjaztu fulānan, meaning: I proved that he is unable to do the matter and incapable of it.

The inimitability (iʿjaz) has become manifest, for example, in the inability of those who denied that the Qur'an is a miracle to bring forth a verse like it. And the one who is "unescapable" in the earth is the one whom you cannot overpower.

In this verse the Truthful, glorified is He, makes clear to us that these disbelievers cannot escape Allah in the earth, as evidenced by the examples of nations that came before and disbelieved: some of them were seized by the wind, some were swallowed up by the earth by Allah, and some were drowned. And when they move on to the Hereafter, they have no protector or helper besides Allah; for the walī (protector) is the one close to you, and none draws close to you except the one you love and from whom you hope for good.

If a person who has gifts above your gifts comes close to you, his gifts overflow onto you. If the one who is close to you is strong while you are weak, then in his strength there is a shield for you; if he is wealthy, his wealth overflows onto you; if he is knowledgeable, he benefits you with his knowledge; if he is forbearing, he benefits you with his forbearance at the moment of your anger. Every person of talent whose talent exceeds yours, while you are near him, will benefit you from his talent.

The walī is also the helper (naṣīr), because the moment you cry out for help, the one close to you will come to you.

As for those who turn people away from the way of Allah, they will not find a protector or helper in the Hereafter, even if they found one in this world, because every human being in the Hereafter will be preoccupied with himself:

﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed, and every pregnant female will drop her burden, and you will see people as drunk, though they are not drunk, but the punishment of Allah is severe.﴾ (22:2)

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail anything for his son, nor a son who will avail anything for his father.…﴾ (31:33)

Likewise the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children, each one of them, that Day, will have a matter that suffices him.﴾ (80:34–37)

So then: those who disbelieved and turned away from the way of Allah are not able to escape Allah in the earth, and they do not find a protector or helper in the Hereafter. Rather: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for them…﴾ (11:20).

We understand "ḍaʿf" (weakness) to mean that a thing becomes two-fold, and we think that this is strength; we say: no, because the one who comes to support the first thing and to intercede for it, the first was weak in relation to him.

So then: doubling (muḍāʿafa) is what manifests the weakness of the thing that needs what supports it. And the doubling of the punishment is a logical matter for those who sought to make the matter crooked, turned away from the way of Allah the Exalted, and wanted by that to lead others astray.

The saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for them…﴾ (11:20) does not contradict His saying, the Truthful: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another…﴾ (6:164). For those who turn people away from the way of Allah do not have one burden only; rather they have two burdens: the burden of their own misguidance, and the burden of misguiding others.

There is a verse that says: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery—and whoever does that will meet a penalty (athām).﴾ (25:68) ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him…﴾ (25:69). That is: whoever does that will meet the doubling of punishment. Why?

Because he became an example for others to commit the same crime.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, does not want sins to spread, and therefore we find the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, urging that believers witness the one who committed the crime at the moment of punishment, just as He says regarding adultery: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (24:2) When the believers see a punishment fall upon a crime, there is in that a warning against committing the crime, and a restraint on the occurrence of crimes.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the punishment is doubled for those who turned away from the way of Allah and wanted to lead others astray, so they committed two crimes:

The first of them: their own misguidance.

The second: their misguiding of others. Therefore you find some of those who led others astray saying on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿…Our Lord, show us those who misled us from the jinn and mankind, that we may place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.﴾ (41:29)

They also say: ﴿…Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ (33:67–68)

So then: calling to deviation is misguidance, and doing a thing in deviation is misguidance, because it becomes an example before others.

The doubling of punishment does not mean burning once in the Fire; for if the Truthful, glorified is He, had left us to the Fire to burn us once, the pain would have ended. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, willed that there be punishment after punishment. He says: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment…﴾ (4:56) So it is a punishment that is constant.

Or the punishment that is doubled for them is of another kind: there is punishment for disbelief, and there is punishment for corruption.

He says: ﴿…We will increase them in punishment above the punishment because of what they used to corrupt.﴾ (16:88) So the punishment for disbelief does not cancel the punishment for the sins that the disbeliever commits.

If the horned sheep is to be avenged on behalf of the hornless sheep, that is, the sheep that has horns and butts the sheep that has no horns, then on the Day of Resurrection retribution will be carried out against it, although there is no reckoning for animals, because they do not possess choice; but they will be used as a means of illustrating the balance of justice.

He says: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for them, what they used to bear (istiṭāʿa) of hearing¹¹ and what they used to see.﴾ (11:20) That is: they were not able to benefit from hearing despite the existence of the organ of hearing, so they did not listen to the message of the Messenger (ﷺ), nor were they able to benefit from their sight to see the signs of Allah the Exalted in the universe. It is as if they were deaf and blind. Or the punishment will be doubled for them for the duration during which they were able to hear and see.

In another verse the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿Hear them and see (on the Day they come to Us)!…﴾ (19:38) That is: their hearing and sight will be sound and good in the Hereafter.

Footnotes (as in the source):

1. aʿjazahu: he made him incapable of reaching him and he escaped from him, so that he could not overpower him. Allah says: ﴿…indeed they cannot escape (lā yuʿjizūn)﴾ (8:59), meaning they cannot escape Allah's reckoning, punishment and seizing them for their sins; they will not get away. Allah also says: ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape in the earth; their refuge is the Fire…﴾ (24:57) [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/7].

2. tadhhal: to be heedless of what one nurses, a metaphor for intense terror and dread. Dhuhul from a thing: leaving it deliberately or being heedless of it and forgetting it due to preoccupation. [Lisan al-Arab, root dh-h-l].

3. jāz: active participle of the verb jazā. Jazā ʿanhu: settled the right on his behalf, or sufficed as a substitute for him in a matter. Allah says: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul anything…﴾ (2:48). Meaning: it neither suffices nor settles. What is meant by His saying: ﴿and dread a Day when no father will avail anything for his son, nor a son who will avail anything for his father﴾ (31:33) is that each of them does not repel from the other any of the punishment [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.

4. wazara al-shayʾ yazuruhu wazran: he carried it. It is used for heavy loads, and is figuratively applied to sins. What is meant by His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another…﴾ (6:164): no soul bears the sin of another soul [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

5. "And whoever does that will meet a penalty": that is, whoever commits those sins and transgressions will receive the requital of his sin and be punished for it. Ithm: doing what Allah the Exalted has forbidden [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

6. ṭāʾifa: a group or company of people. Imam Malik held that a ṭāʾifa is four men or more, since testimony for adultery is not sufficient unless by four witnesses or more. Al-Shafiʿi said likewise; Rabiʿa said five; al-Hasan al-Basri said ten. See [Ibn Kathir (3/262)].

7. al-sādāt wa'l-kubarāʾ: Tawus said: the sādāt are the noble and great ones of the people, and the kubarāʾ are the scholars. Said by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/519) and attributed by him to Ibn Abi Hatim.

8. nadaja al-laḥm: it became tender and fit to be eaten. And "the skins were burned through" (in the sense of being charred).

9. Because he did not believe in the religion that he must believe in, for this reason he was not saved from the punishment, and he is also punished for opposing the method of Allah, if he believed in a messenger, or if he did not believe in the messengers but was opposed to the natural disposition (fiṭra).

10. From Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You will surely render the rights to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2582), Book of Virtue and Kinship. al-Jalhaʾ: the sheep whose hair on the front of its head has gone, and here it is in the position of the jamāʾ, which has no horn.

11. al-samʿ: the goodness of the ear; it is applied to the ear and to the ears, in its own wording because it is a verbal noun. Allah says: ﴿Allah has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their sight is a covering…﴾ (2:7), meaning He sealed their ears so that they do not hear; and it is said: they hear but do not understand [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

12. "Hear them and see!": an exclamation from "heard" and from "saw", meaning: how precise their hearing and sight are, and how wondrous their condition on the Day of Resurrection, when they see all their deeds in this world and hear everything they said, in moments, so as to bear witness against themselves. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 21:

Then the Truthful, Glorified is He, says:

﴿Those are the ones who have lost their souls, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them.﴾ (11:21)

Therefore: they have lost their souls, because by wronging the soul and giving it a fleeting desire whose time is short, they took a delayed punishment whose time is everlasting.

In this there is wronging of the soul, and this is the peak of loss, and it indicates the disruption of the balances.

You may wrong another, taking from him some good so that you benefit from it, and thereby you wrong the other for the sake of your own self's benefit.

Wronging the soul means that you give it immediate pleasure and neglect the delayed punishment for it, and immediate pleasure has a limited duration, whereas punishment has no duration that defines it.

For this reason the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted is He says: ﴿…and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ (Hud). That is: what they used to worship besides Allah did not come to them. Even if those they worshipped had power on the Day of Resurrection, they would have rushed to them to rescue them from the punishment, but they are without strength or power, because the Truthful, Glorified is He has decreed against these disbelievers, and said: ﴿…and they have no protector or helper in the earth﴾ (al-Tawbah 74). Likewise, these deities worshipped besides Allah the Exalted, or partners with Allah, do not come to them, even on the assumption that they were capable of giving aid. Those deities or partners do not reach them, nor do they know any place for them.

The saying of the Truthful, Glorified is He: ﴿…and [it] has gone astray from them…﴾ (21) (Hud): that is, it vanished and wandered away from them.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿…what they used to fabricate﴾ (21) (Hud): that is, what they used to claim falsely.

(1) Ḍalla al-kāfir (ضل الكافر): he went astray from the convincing proof, deviated from the straight path, and did not recognise the truth.
Al-ḍalāl (الضلال): forgetting and losing; ḍalla al-shay' (ضل الشيء): it became hidden and vanished, and it is an intransitive verb.
Ḍalla al-musāfir al-ṭarīq (ضل المسافر الطريق): he did not know the road, so it is transitive [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 22:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Undoubtedly(1) they are, in the Hereafter, the greatest losers.﴾

The scholars differed over the meaning of the phrase ﴿lā jaram﴾, and the general meaning, whenever you hear the phrase ﴿lā jaram﴾, is: it is true and established, or: there must be the occurrence of a specific thing.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Undoubtedly for them is the Fire﴾ [al-Nahl 16:62], that means: it is true and established that for them is the Fire, as a result of what they did of deeds, and those deeds are a precursor before their punishment. So when you hear ﴿lā jaram﴾ and with it the deed they committed, you are confident that it is due upon Allah, glorified is He, to punish them.

Some scholars said: the meaning of ﴿lā jaram﴾ is "true and established." Others said: the meaning of ﴿lā jaram﴾ is "there must be, and there is no escape."

The two meanings converge, because the negation of "al-badd" (alternative, escape)(4) indicates that it is established. The scholars should have examined the root of the word, and the root of the word is "al-jaram," and "al-jaram" is "cutting,"(5) and it is said: "jarama yadahu," meaning he cut his hand.

The saying of the Truth, here: ﴿Undoubtedly they are, in the Hereafter, the greatest losers﴾ [Hud 11:22] means: there is no cutting of Allah's word concerning them that for them is the Fire, nor anything that can stand between that and them ever, and they must receive this threat. And thus the meaning converges with "there must be."

So, when you hear the phrase "lā jaram," it means: it is established, or there must be the occurrence of the threat.

Also, you find the word "al-jarīmah" (crime) derived from "al-jaram," and it is the cutting of a straight law. When we establish that no one should steal from another, this is a straight law. If one person steals from another, he has cut the security and peace of people, and every crime is a cutting of the familiar order by which people live.

Also it is said: "jarama al-shay'" meaning he acquired its evil, and from it comes "al-jarīmah"; for this reason it is said: among people is one who is "jārim," which is the active participle of the verb "jarama," like the word "kātib" from the verb "kataba," and "majrūm 'alayhi," which is the passive participle, just like "maktūb."

If "al-jarīmah" is taken from cutting the order prevailing in the system, then those who fabricated against Allah, wronged, and barred from the way of Allah, there is no crime in Allah punishing them with the Fire.

Such a punishment is not a crime, because the punishment for a crime is not a crime, rather it is a deterrence to crime.(7) Thus all the meanings converge. When we say ﴿lā jaram﴾, that means there is no crime in the recompense, because the crime is the great sins they committed.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ [al-Shura 42:40].

The Truth has called it an evil because it harms society, or it harms the individual himself.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished...﴾ [al-Nahl 16:126]. Thus we find that there are multiple meanings for the interpretation of the Truth's saying ﴿lā jaram﴾: it means: there is no cutting of Allah's word that the polytheists will enter the Fire; or they must enter the Fire; or it is true and established that they will enter the Fire; or there is no crime on the part of the Truth, glorified is He, in doing to them thus, because they are the ones who did what merits their punishment.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Undoubtedly they are, in the Hereafter, the greatest losers﴾ [Hud 11:22]. The word ﴿al-akhsarūn﴾ (the greatest losers) is the plural of "akhsar"(8), which is the elative form of "khāsir," and "khāsir" is an active participle derived from "al-khasārah" (loss).

Loss in worldly affairs is when an exchange is a great injustice to one party, such as one who buys something for five piasters, and it was necessary that he sell it for more than five piasters, but he sold it for only three piasters. So, after he had desired an increase, he sold the thing for less than its original value.

Whoever does this is called "khāsir" (a loser), and worldly loss is limited to the world, and whoever loses in one transaction may profit in another transaction. Let us suppose that he has lost in all the transactions of the world: how short the time of the world is! For everything that ends is short, but the loss of the Hereafter has no end.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you(10) of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work.﴾ [al-Kahf 18:103-104]

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, described them once as "the greatest losers," and once He described the judgment upon them, saying: ﴿...Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.﴾ [al-Zumar 39:15]. It is an all-encompassing loss that covers every place. Then the Truth, glorified is He, willed to bring the counterpart of these, and in that is an overflow of spiritual comfort, because the soul, when it sees a judgment upon something, is comforted to take the opposite judgment upon the opposite thing.

So when a person hears the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous are in bliss﴾ [al-Infitar 82:13], there must come to mind a question about the fate of the wicked, so the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And indeed, the wicked are in Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar 82:14]. This contrast gives the first expansion of the soul and the second constriction, and between expansion and constriction there is admonition and lesson.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, brings the counterpart to the polytheists who barred from the way of Allah and so went to the Fire: the counterpart is the believers, the people of righteous deeds.

So the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves(14) before their Lord — those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ [Hud 11:23]

1 "Lā jaram": "no doubt" and "necessarily"; it has changed into the sense of an oath, so that it is like our saying "truly." Here it means "truly." It occurs in the Qur'an in five places:
First: Surah Hud, verse 22, which is the one under discussion here.
Second: ﴿Undoubtedly Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal; indeed, He does not love the arrogant.﴾ [al-Nahl 16:23]
Third: ﴿...Undoubtedly for them is the Fire, and they are the neglected.﴾ [al-Nahl 16:62]
Fourth: ﴿Undoubtedly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [al-Nahl 16:109]
Fifth: ﴿Undoubtedly, what you call me to has no call in this world or the Hereafter...﴾ [Ghafir 40:43]...
2 Said by al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi and Sibawayh. For them, "lā" and "jaram" are one word, and "anna" is in the place of nominative case. This is the view of al-Farra' and Muhammad ibn Yazid. See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (4/3338).
3 Al-Mahdawi said: It is also related from al-Khalil that its meaning is "there must be and no escape." This is also the view of al-Farra'. Mentioned by al-Tha'labi. See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (4/3338).
4 "Al-badd": the share of every thing. "Lā budda minhu": there is no escape. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]
5 "Al-jurmah": what is cut from the unripe dates (tamr). [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]
6 "Jarama al-shay', jarman": he cut it, and it came to be used for doing evil. One says: "jarama": he committed a sin and perpetrated an offense; "jarama al-māl": he acquired wealth from whatever source he found it; "jarramahu": he moved him to do an evil or a sin or a crime. The Most High said: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people prompt you to not be just...﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:8], meaning: let not the hatred of a people move you to not do justice.
7 Therefore the Most High said: ﴿And in retribution there is life for you, O people of understanding, that you may become righteous.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:179] Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (1/211): "When the killer knows that he will be killed, he refrains from his action, and in that is life for souls. Abu al-'Aliyah said: Allah made retribution a life; how many a man wants to kill, but fear of being killed restrains him."
8 "Akhsar": the form of the elative, which conveys intensification of the meaning, i.e., more and more severe loss. [See: Lisan al-'Arab, root kh-s-r]
9 "Al-ijhaf" and "al-mujahafah": taking a thing and sweeping it away. "Al-juhf": the severity of the sweeping. "Al-ijhaf": severe injustice. [See: Lisan al-'Arab, root j-h-f]
10 "Anba'ahu bi-l-shay'", and "nabba'ahu bihi": he informed him of it and mentioned to him its story. "Al-naba'": news, or news of importance and a matter of weight. "Al-inba'" also: to speak, and from it the saying of the Most High: ﴿And inform them of the guests of Abraham﴾ [al-Hijr 15:51], meaning: tell them. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/250]
11 The verse is general for everyone who worships Allah in a way that is not accepted, thinking he is correct in it and that his deed is accepted, while he is mistaken and his deed is rejected. So you find them believing that they are upon something and that they are accepted and beloved. This is like the saying of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He repays him his account; and Allah is swift in account.﴾ [al-Nur 24:39] [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/107], adapted.
12 "Al-abrar": plural of "barr," the truthful, righteous man, possessor of obedience and goodness. And "al-barr" is one who is dutiful to his parents, treating them well. [Lisan al-'Arab, root b-r-r], adapted.
13 "Al-fujjar": plural of "fājir," one who is immersed in sins, not restrained and not concerned, and also one who exceeds in disobedience and openly declares it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/73], adapted.
14 "Akhbatu ila rabbihim": they humbled themselves, feared, and walked the straight, tranquil, wide path. The Most High said: ﴿...And give good tidings to the humble(34)﴾ [al-Hajj 22:34], meaning: the submissive. "Al-khabt": a wide, low-lying, tranquil place on the earth. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]

Faith, as we know, is a matter of creed (ʿaqdi)¹, in which a person declares his belief in one existing God and commits himself to the method that Allah the Exalted sent down to the Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever believes in Allah the Exalted but does not perform righteous deeds will receive punishment, because the benefit of faith is only realized through righteous action.

Therefore we find the Truthful One, glorified and exalted, saying to us: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'..." (14)﴾ [al-Hujurat]: that is, you have followed the outward form of Islam.

Thus we know that there exists one who is certain, by correct belief, that the One, the Unique God exists, and that the Messenger (ﷺ) is a conveyer from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But the action that a person performs is the criterion distinguishing the rank of the believer from the rank of the one who merely knows.

So the one who performs deeds well is a believer; as for the one who performs deeds lazily and follows only the outward forms of religion, he is a Muslim. Both differ from the hypocrite, who claims zeal for performing acts of worship, yet plots and secretly harbours enmity toward Islam, which he does not believe in.

The hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were the first of people to fill the rows for prayer, yet they were concealing their treachery and devising plots against the Prophet (ﷺ).

Here the Truthful One, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord... (23)﴾ [Hud]. This statement shows us that the criterion of faith depends on monotheism, perfecting the performance of what the method of Allah requires, and that all of this be with humility and submission. Hence it is said: "An act of disobedience that produces humiliation and brokenness is better than an act of worship that produces pride and arrogance." That is, the believer must not take worship as a means to arrogance².

The word ﴿akhbatu﴾ means: they submitted, out of fear of Allah the Exalted. They do not perform the obligations of faith merely out of desire that Allah not punish them; rather, they perform the obligations of faith and righteous deeds out of fear of Allah.

The root of the word is "al-khabt," which is level, calm, lowly ground, and likewise humility (khabt) in faith.

The Truthful One describes the believers who are humble (al-mukhbitin) as: ﴿...Those are the companions of Paradise, therein abiding forever (23)﴾ [Hud]: that is, they remain in it permanently. Their eternity in Paradise means that they dwell in bliss forever, and the bliss of Paradise is lasting and enduring, unlike the bliss of this world, which a person may lose through death, or which may be taken from him by deprivation³; for a person in this world is subject to change. As for the Hereafter, the people of faith, who are doers of righteous deeds and humble before their Lord, are the people of everlasting bliss.

Thus the Truthful One has presented the condition of the two groups: the group that wronged itself by fabricating lies against Allah, barred from the way of Allah, and sought to make it crooked. These will not escape Allah, and they have no protectors to shield them from the doubled punishment.

These are the ones who have lost themselves, and they will find no help from the deities they worshipped besides Allah, nor anything able to separate them from the punishment; they are the greatest losers.

As for the second group, they are those who believed and performed righteous deeds with humility, fear, and love for Allah the Exalted; they are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein forever.

So, for each group is its path and its end.

¹ Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-ʿArab (root ʿ-q-d): "He believed something in his heart, and it has no 'maʿqud' (firm binding), i.e., a firm opinion." In a hadith: a man used to trade and in his ʿuqda (judgment) there was weakness, i.e., in his opinion and his consideration of his own interests. Thus faith is a matter that the heart believes..

² Faith is the firm conviction of the heart that admits no doubt concerning unseen matters, such as belief in Allah, the Last Day, the books and the messengers, things people do not see. As for Islam, it is the outward commitment to the rulings of religion, such as prayer, fasting and other acts, even if there is no faith in the heart. Faith and its excellence is a matter that Allah produces in the heart of every servant..

³ Ibn Manzur cited for "bayyata": he planned it secretly, as if he planned it at night to conceal it. The Exalted says: ﴿They say, "Obedience," but when they leave you, a faction of them plans by night other than what you say. And Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs (81)﴾ [an-Nisa'].[al-Qamus al-Qawmi – 1/89]..

⁴ Istikbar: exaltation and tyranny over people and wronging them without right; the form "istaf'ala" conveys affectation and pretension to a quality, so the arrogant one claims or supposes in himself that he is great..

⁵ Salb: the removal of blessing from a person..

⁶ Aʿjazahu: he made him unable to attain it, and he escaped from him so that he could not be seized. The Exalted says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think they have outrun [Us]; indeed, they cannot escape (59)﴾ [al-Anfal], i.e., they cannot escape Allah's reckoning, His punishment, and His seizing them for their sins; they will not get away..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 24:

Therefore, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says:

﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in likeness? Will you not then be mindful?﴾ (24)

The two groups are those we have spoken about before.

The word "firq" (group) means a company of people who gather around one aim and one goal, just as we say "the football team" or other teams. They are groups, and each group has a goal that unites it.

We find that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿...a group in the Garden and a group in the Blaze (al-sa'ir)(1)﴾ (7) [al-Shura]. The word ﴿the two groups﴾ came in the verse we are now reflecting upon, because each group comprises a community different from the other community, and these have their partisans and the others have their partisans.

In this verse, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, strikes the example with the two chief perceptive senses of man, namely hearing and sight. They are the two basic sources for man to acquire information, either heard or seen. Then in man there develops the capacity for deduction (istinbat)(2) and generation from what he has heard with the ear and seen with the eye.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, has told us: ﴿And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing and sights and hearts, that perhaps you may give thanks﴾ (78) [al-Nahl].

So then: since the Truth, glory be to Him, has made hearing, sights and hearts sources from which fruit comes, namely information and its scrutiny(3), the Truth, glory be to Him, deserves thanks(4) for it.

We know that the civilizational leaps (tafrat)(5) and the advancements of knowledge come only through the one who hears and the one who sees; then from deduction there come applied ideas that benefit mankind.

An example of this: a man saw a cooking pot with a lid, and in the pot there was boiling water, and the lid rose off the pot.

This man discovered the power of steam, and deduced that steam requires a larger space than the liquid in the pot; therefore the lid rose off the pot, and this discovery advanced to develop many aspects of life.

Had every person stopped at what he hears or sees and deduced nothing from it, life would not have developed with all those civilizational advancements.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in likeness...?﴾ (24) [Hud]. No one, whether blind or deaf, would doubt that one who sees or hears is better than him, and the blind cannot be equal to the seeing, nor the deaf to one who hears.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has brought together contrasting things, so that the human being who hears or reads this verse may judge, and decide by a ruling that reminds him of the difference between one who sees and one who is blind, and likewise between one who hears and one who is deaf; and it is natural that they are not equal.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ meaning: will you not take heed of the existence of these things?

We know that God, glory be to Him, has said to us: ﴿...for indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]. That is: a person may be sighted, or have an ear that hears, yet he does not use the faculty of sight or hearing for what they were created for, namely the grasping of unknown things.

After the Truth, glory be to Him, has made clear the description of each side and its conflict with the other, and the difference of each in aim, the conflict between them is explained by the stories of the Messengers, peace be upon them.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says in some places of the Noble Qur'an, and in each place there are snapshots of the story of a particular Messenger; the snapshot found in one surah may differ from the snapshot found in another surah.

An example of this: the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke in Surah Yunus about Noah, Moses, Aaron and Jonah, peace be upon them; and here, in Surah Hud, the story of Noah, peace be upon him, comes again, and He, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed I am to you a clear warner"﴾ (25)

1 al-sa'ir: the kindled, blazing, flaming fire. The Exalted says: ﴿And when the Hellfire is kindled (12)﴾ [al-Takwir], meaning: set ablaze intensely. By al-sa'ir is meant the fire of Hell. The Exalted says: ﴿...Their abode is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze (sa'ir)(97)﴾ [al-Isra'], meaning: We increase for them a raging, kindled, flaming fire...
2 istinbat: extracting water from the inner part of the earth. Figuratively: "istanbata al-ra'y al-sahih" means he extracted the correct opinion by his inquiry and thought, like one who extracts water from a well. The Exalted says: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who seek to draw it out (yastanbitunahu) among them would have known it...(83)﴾ [al-Nisa'].
3 tamhis al-shay': testing and examining a thing precisely. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted. The Exalted says: ﴿And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers (141)﴾ [Al 'Imran], meaning: purify them and free them from defects and from the hypocrites, and bring the disbelievers to an end. And He says: ﴿And that He may test what is in your hearts...(154)﴾ [Al 'Imran], meaning: purify the faith in their hearts from whisperings and doubts. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]...
4 shukr: meeting a blessing with speech, action and intention, so that one praises the Benefactor with his tongue, gives himself over to obedience to Him, and believes that all blessings come from Him...
5 tafrat: plural of tafra, which is a leap upward. One says "tafara yatfuru": he leapt upward. [See Lisan al-'Arab]...
6 nadhir: a messenger who warns of punishment. "Anzarahu": he warned him, made him wary of it; "anzarahu shay'an": informed him of it and made him aware of it and of the harm that follows from it within a period sufficient to guard against it. That is, he frightened him of it so that he would keep away from it. The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed We have warned you of a near punishment...(40)﴾ [al-Naba'], and He says: ﴿And he had certainly warned them of Our seizure...(36)﴾ [al-Qamar], and He says: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am to you only a clear warner (49)﴾ [al-Hajj]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/258], adapted...

The verse clarifies the matter of Noah's (peace be upon him) being sent as a messenger to his people, and the messenger's duty is to convey the message, so he says: ﴿...Indeed I am to you a clear warner﴾ [Hud]. We note that the hamza of (inna) in one of the two readings of the verse is kasra, and in another reading it is fatha(1). As for the reading with kasra, it means that Noah (peace be upon him) brought the message, conveyed it to his people, and said: ﴿...Indeed I am to you a clear warner﴾ [Hud]. As for the other reading with fatha, it means that the message is: ﴿that I am to you a clear warner﴾ [Hud].

So the first reading conveys the report about the act of conveying the message, and the second reading specifies the content of the message: ﴿...that I am to you a clear warner﴾ [Hud].

The first reading involves an elision of the verb of saying (al-hadhf al-qawl), and the elision of the verb of saying is frequent in the Qur'an, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them(2) from every gate. (23) Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured...(24)﴾ [al-Ra'd].

This means that the angels enter upon the believers in Paradise from every gate(3), and at the moment of entry the angels say: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured...(24)﴾ [al-Ra'd]. And from Noah's (peace be upon him) saying: ﴿...Indeed I am to you a clear warner (25)﴾ [Hud], we know that the warner — as we said before — is one who informs of an evil that has not yet come, so that the listener may prepare to meet it. Since the Prophet of God Noah came as a warner, the context continues, because the Truth, glory be to Him, said in the verse before it: ﴿The likeness of the two groups...(24)﴾ [Hud]: that is, there is a disobedient and disbelieving group to whom there is a warner, while the other group has a bringer of good tidings, of good approaching, so that the listener also prepares to receive it with a tranquil soul.

As for the disbelieving group that deserves warning, the Truth, glory be to Him, brings to them the text of the warning in His saying:

﴿That you worship none but God(4). Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a painful day. (26)﴾:

1 The reading with fatha was recited by Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i. Said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3340), i.e.: We sent him with "that I am to you a clear warner..."
2 The pronoun in (upon them) refers to the people of understanding (ulu al-albab) whom their Lord described with attributes by which they deserved entry into the gardens of Eden. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only the people of understanding will be reminded. (19) Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract (20) And those who join what God has commanded to be joined and fear their Lord and dread the terrible account (21) And those who patiently seek the countenance of their Lord, establish prayer, spend from what We have provided them secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good — those will have the good outcome of the home (22)﴾ [al-Ra'd]..
3 Paradise has gates, which some scholars counted as eight, citing the hadith of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "None of you performs ablution and completes (or perfects) the ablution, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, he enters by whichever he wishes." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (234) from the hadith of 'Uqba ibn 'Amir..
4 This is because they used to worship idols alongside God, glory be to Him, and these are the ones mentioned in Surah Nuh, verse 23: ﴿And they said: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth or Ya'uq or Nasr (23)﴾ [Nuh]. They are names of righteous men; when they died, people made images of their likeness as idols to remind them of their deeds, then time passed and they came to worship them besides God. [See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/426]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 26:

We know that Nuh (peace be upon him) is reckoned among his people, and they are reckoned among him; therefore we find him concerned for them, because the bond that ties him to them is a strong, comprehensive bond.

Likewise, we find that Allah, glorified is He, softens the hearts of those sent to them, so that they may receive the Messenger well.

An example of this is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾ [al-A'raf: 65]. Because the Messenger is their brother, he will not deceive them or cheat them.

The chiefs (al-mala') of the people of Nuh received the matter as Allah, glorified is He, reports of them: {The chiefs who disbelieved among his people said, "We see you only as a human like ourselves, and we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us in judgment at first glance (bади al-ra'y), and we see no virtue in you over us; rather, we think you are liars."} [Hud: 27]

1 al-mala' (الملأ): the nobles of the people, or all of them.
2 "Those who are the lowest of us" (الذين هم أراذلنا): that is, the poorest and the most contemptible of people in our view.
bādi' al-ra'y (بادي الرأي): its outward appearance, without reflection, i.e., a superficial opinion, not deeply considered.
It is also read bādi'a al-ra'y (بادئ الرأي): meaning the beginning and first part of the opinion, likewise without reflection [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 27:

The chiefs (al-mala'), as we know, are the notables of the people, those leaders who fill the eyes with awe and occupy every assembly.

There is a popular saying in our country that expresses this meaning when one says: "So-and-so fills the eye."

That is: when the eye looks at him, it is not empty, and no part of the eye sees anything else.

It is also said: "So-and-so has fettered the gazes" (qayyada al-nawaZir), meaning that when he appears, all gazes are bound to him, so they do not turn to anyone else. This cannot be the case unless he has qualities that draw the eyes to him such that they do not turn away from him.

What is meant by this is the close entourage, or the first circle around the center. Around every center there are circles: the al-mala' are the first circle, then a second circle follows them, then a third, and so on. Confusion arises only when a circle has more than one center, so the circles scatter.

Those who make up the al-mala' responded to Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), saying: ﴿We see you only as a human being like us..﴾ [Hud: 27]. That is: you have no distinction that makes you superior to us, so what has made you a master over us, that you should be the Messenger?

Their saying this is evidence of foolishness, because once the Messenger comes from among humans, his conduct serves as a model, and his words are fit to be followed. Had the Messenger been of a kind other than human, the people would have had the right to object, for they would be unable to take angels as a model for themselves.

For this reason, the Truthful, Glorified One clarified this matter in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94]

The response from Him, Glorified is He, came: say to them: ﴿If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 95]. Thus: "The Messenger comes only as a conveyer of a method and a model of conduct. If he is not of the kind of humans, the model will not be suitable, and he will be able to do nothing but convey (the message)."

An example of this: when you see a lion in any zoo, roaming and prowling, eating the raw meat presented to it by the keeper, does your soul tell you to do as it does? Of course not. But if you see a horseman on a steed with his sword, your soul may tell you to be like him.

Thus we find that being a model requires unity of kind. That is why we have said: a model is the proof that refutes whoever claims divinity for 'Uzayr or for 'Isa, peace be upon them both.

Then the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted, mentions what was said on the tongue of the disbelieving chiefs of the people of Nuh:

﴿And we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us..﴾ [Hud: 27]. Al-arādhil (the lowest) is the plural of "aradhil," like our saying "afādil qawm" (the best of a people), which is the plural of "afdal." The arādhil is the base and despised in the eyes of people. "Radhāl al-māl" means its worst part, and "radhl" of everything is its refuse.

In the countryside, during the cotton harvest season, we see the process of "sorting" the cotton, carried out by young boys and girls, who separate the clean cotton from the bolls that have not opened properly, because a diseased boll usually suffers from shriveling and has not ripened correctly.

Likewise, farmers do during the date harvest, separating good dates from defective dates. So: the radhāl of everything is its refuse.

The chiefs among the disbelievers of the people of Nuh said: ﴿And we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us..﴾ [Hud: 27]. That is: they described those who believed in Nuh, peace be upon him, as the refuse of society.

The Truth, through their tongues, said in another place: ﴿..and the lowest have followed you?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]. Nuh, peace be upon him, did not deny this, because those who followed him may have been among the weak, and they are the victims of corruption, for the strong in society is not approached by anyone, and therefore he does not suffer the pressures of the corrupters. As for the weak, they are the ones who suffer from the corrupters. So when a deliverer appears to them from among the corrupters, they must cling to him.

But this does not mean that faith does not touch the hearts of the powerful, as evidenced by some of the masters and wealthy of Makkah who responded to the Muhammadan call, such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with them.

But the general rule in reform movements is that those who respond to them are the ones crushed by corruption, those who feel the seething in the cauldrons of pain caused by corruption. Once a caller to reform appears and wants to dislodge corruption, they rally around him and sympathize with him. Even if they are not slaves, but are ruled by others, they believe openly in the man of reform; and if they are slaves owned by masters, they believe in secret, and the strong among them endure persecution and torture.

So: every messenger who comes, comes in a time of corruption, and this corruption benefits some people, and tyranny afflicts the many upon whom corruption and tyranny fall.

The Messenger comes as if he were a revolution against tyranny and corruption; therefore the weak cling to him and rejoice in him, and their hearts incline toward him.

As for those who profit from corruption, they say: "Your followers are our lowest." It is as if this saying were a slander against the Messenger, but they are foolish, because this saying is evidence of the necessity of the Messenger's coming, to deliver these weak people, and the Messenger comes to lead an outrage against the corruption of the earth and to end this corruption.

This outrage differs from the outrage of the ordinary rebel among people, for the rebel among people sees those who applaud him from among the crushed by corruption.

But the affliction of the human rebel is one thing: he wants to remain a rebel. The true rebel, however, rebels in order to demolish corruption, then calms down in order to build glories. He does not turn the sword on everyone, nor does he favor one people over another, nor does he pamper those who oppressed them, nor wrong those who were oppressors.

Rather, he must judge among people with justice and mercy, so that affairs are set right, resentments depart, and all people know that the rebel did not come against a specific group, but against one group's oppression of another. So if he takes from the oppressor and gives to the oppressed, he must make the two equal before his eyes.

From here comes calm and stability in society.

So: the saying of the disbelievers from the chiefs of the people of Nuh: ﴿And we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us..﴾ [Hud: 27] is a saying that confirms the existence of corruption in this society, and that the weak crushed by corruption had followed Nuh, peace be upon him.

The Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿at first sight..﴾ [Hud: 27]. Al-bādi is the apparent, as opposed to the hidden.

There is another reading: ﴿bādi' al-ra'y..﴾, meaning: after the beginning of opinion.

The verse here says: ﴿bādī al-ra'y..﴾ [Hud: 27], that is: the apparent matter. Whenever anything is presented to a person, he looks at it with a superficial glance, then thinks deeply about that thing.

Whenever a person hears a claim or a case, he must not judge it by its outward appearance, but must examine the case or claim with deliberation and calm.

They said to Nuh, peace be upon him: "You are a human like us, and our lowest have followed you," because they looked at your call with a superficial glance. Had they examined your call, pondered it, and considered its consequences with reflection, they would not have believed in it.

The Truthful, Glorified One exposes this foolishness in them. The chiefs' claim that the weak should have reflected on the matter and hesitated before believing in Nuh's call is refuted by the insistence of the weak on faith, because it confirms that the essence of judgment among them was sound. For each of these weak individuals did not measure the matter by the standard of one who owns wealth, nor by the standard of one who owns status, nor by the standard of one who has lordship. Rather, the weak measured the matter with the heart, which understood and perceived, and with the tongue, which declared faith, for a person is by his two smallest things: his heart and his tongue.

So: this disbelieving chiefs' council of the people of Nuh, peace be upon him, has judged the weak to be "lowest" by degraded standards, not by correct standards.

Had those called "lowest" refrained from serving those called "masters," the masters would have tasted bitterness, for it is they who provide service. If the carpenter did not make the household furniture, there would be no furnished houses.

If the laborers refrained from digging and building, there would be no erected palaces.

If the cook refrained from cooking food, there would be no extended tables. All the services of these weak people flow to the rich, the owner of wealth, or the owner of status.

Thus we see that the universe needs someone who owns wealth, even through inheritance, to spend on those whom society also needs, namely the weak, who give good from their toil and production.

So: the weak are the completion of lordship.

Looking closely, we find that the mastery of the wealthy or the man of status comes only as a result of the efforts of those called "lowest."

If they abandoned the wealthy or the man of status, he would not be able to be a master.

The Truthful, Glorified One mentions the rest of what the disbelieving chiefs of the people of Nuh said: ﴿..and we do not see for you any virtue over us, but we think you are liars﴾ [Hud: 27]. By this saying they denied that your mastery arose from the effort of those they called "lowest," and denied the merit of these people.

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted draws our attention to the affliction that afflicts some societies when He mentions what the disbelievers said: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of the two cities, a great one?" [31] "Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in rank, that some of them may take others in service..﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31-32]. So: the Truthful, Glorified One is the One who apportions livelihood, and the affliction of judgment is to look at the one who is raised as being the one who is wealthy. No, the one who is raised is not the wealthy, but rather everyone who has a talent that others do not have.

As long as he is raised in one field, he will serve others in it, and others will serve him in what they are raised in, for the matter is founded on complementarity.

Therefore Allah, Glorified is He, does not perpetuate anyone's wealth forever, but has made the world a rotation (duwal) among people.

So: had this disbelieving council of the people of Nuh, peace be upon him, known the meaning of the word "virtue" (fadl), they would not have said it, for virtue is the excess over what is required of a thing, in tangible things or in meanings, and virtue requires the existence of a superior and an inferior.

Let every tyrant look in his life to see what the superior in it is.

It is some of the wealth or status, and everyone who serves this tyrant are the people of virtue, for the tyrant's mastery is built on their giving.

They are the people of virtue, since virtue is the matter that exceeds what is necessary.

So: the reality of the connection of the world, one part to another, is a connection of need, not a connection of domination. Therefore, when we see a dominator who tyrannizes, we say to him: "Reflect on the matter, for you have dominated only by means of people from the lowest. Displaying your strength is done through those who are skilled at aiming weapons, or those trained to harm humans. He builds his mastery with some of the base, as instruments to achieve his domination."

The saying of the disbeliever from the council of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿And we do not see for you any virtue over us..﴾ [Hud: 27] reveals that they understood virtue to be wealth, status and positions, and they had misunderstood. The Truthful, Glorified One concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿..but we think you are liars﴾ [Hud: 27]. Ẓann (supposition) is what is inclined to be true, while the less probable is wahm (doubt). This proves that in man there is a nature (fitra) that awakens in the soul like flashes, so the arrogant one continues in his arrogance until a flash from his nature comes to him, and he knows that truth is truth and falsehood is falsehood.

When this flash came into the souls of this disbelieving council, they said: ﴿..but we think you are liars﴾ [Hud: 27]. They did not say: "We believe that you are liars."

1 Sawwadaka 'alaynā: made for you mastery and leadership over us, so that you command us and forbid us.
2 How could they take angels as a model for themselves, when angels are of a kind other than theirs, with rulings and capacities that differ from theirs? So the argument from the actions of angels cannot be applied to other kinds. This is why, when the idolaters of Makkah said: ﴿...why was not an angel sent down to him?﴾ and it was said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved. And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and would have covered for them what they cover﴾ [al-An'am: 8-9]. [Adapted from Ibn Kathir's tafsir, 2/124].
3 Uswa (model): capacity. Here it means the good capacity that everyone should emulate. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, there has been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21].
4 'Uzayr: a righteous man from the Children of Israel whom the Jews made a son of Allah and worshipped because of his knowledge of the Torah and his preservation of it letter by letter, as in the books [al-Qamus al-Qawmi 2/18], and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/348]. He is the one mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿Or like one who passed by a town while it was fallen upon its roofs. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years and then revived him. He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; they have not spoiled. And look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259].
5 Radhala al-shay', radhala and radhala: it became base and inferior, so he is radhal. Al-arādhil: an elative form indicating intensity of the attribute. Allah says in Surat al-Nahl: ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most abject age..﴾ [al-Nahl: 70], meaning to senility and weakness. And He says: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111], meaning the basest of people in our view. And He says: ﴿Those who are our lowest..﴾ [Hud: 27], meaning the poorest and most contemptible of people in our view. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
6 Al-marājil: plural of mirjal, which is any vessel in which something is cooked, such as a pot or other. It is said: it is specifically a pot made of copper. [See: Lisan, root rajal].
7 Āfat al-shay': the error in it, or its deficiency or defect. [See: Lisan al-'Arab, root afa].
8 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3342): "It is permissible for 'bādī al-ra'y' to derive from bada'a yabda' with the hamza dropped. Abu 'Amr realized the hamza and read 'bādī al-ra'y,' meaning the first opinion, i.e., they followed you when they first began to look, and had they examined and reflected thoroughly they would not have followed you. The meaning here does not differ by hamzing or not hamzing."
9 This is one of the proverbs of the Arabs: "A man is by his two smallest things," and the two smallest are his heart and his tongue. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-'Arab: "Its meaning: a man surmounts matters and controls them with his mind (janan) and his tongue."
10 What is meant by the two cities is Makkah and al-Ta'if. Scholars differed about what is meant by the two men. Ibn Kathir mentioned this difference, then said: "The apparent meaning is that they meant a great man from whichever of the two towns." Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/127).
11 Sukhriyyan: that is, some of them make others serve in works, because this one needs that one and that one needs this one. Said by al-Suddi and others. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/127)]. Ibn Manzur quoted in al-Lisan: "Sukhriyyan: slaves, female slaves, and hired workers."
Reviewed against the original by His Eminence Shaykh Muhammad al-Sanrawi, adviser at al-Azhar, and Ustadh Adel Abu al-Mu'ati.
12 - Dawla: a name for a thing that circulates; dawla: the action and transition from one state to another [adapted from Lisan al-'Arab, root: dwl].
13 - Fadl in the concept of the disbelievers differs from fadl in the concept of the believer: fadl for the disbeliever is wealth and authority, while in the concept of the believer it is election, gifts and divine bestowals with which Allah, Glorified is He, chooses His messengers, prophets and sincere servants.
14 - Zann: what arises in the soul from an indication; it is a probable doubt, and its verb is among the verbs of probability. Zann is a verbal noun, and zann is also a name for that thought that arises in the soul. Allah says: ﴿...They follow only assumption, and indeed assumption avails not against the truth at all﴾ [al-Najm: 28]. Its plural is zunun. Allah says: ﴿...and you assume about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10], "al-zununa" with an alif in pause and in connection, and without an alif a reading [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me: if I am upon clear evidence (1) from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, yet it has been obscured from you, shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?"﴾ (11:28)

The words of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿Tell me﴾ means: inform me. If I am upon a clear proof bestowed by Allah, a light, insight, and a natural disposition toward guidance, and Allah the Glorified has given me ﴿mercy﴾, meaning prophethood, while this matter has been hidden from you, would I then compel you to it? No. Faith must come by free choice after convincing, tangible proof, a moved and tranquil disposition, and a choice made with certainty (2).

When we consider His words ﴿...shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾ (11:28):

We find the interrogative hamza, then the verb "nulzim" (we compel), then the pronoun of address (the kaf). Here we have an interrogation, a verb, and a hidden subject within the verb, and the first object is the kaf of address, and the second object is the mercy.

So there is no compulsion from the Messenger upon his people to believe, because faith requires hearts (3), not mere forms, and compelling forms does not plant faith in hearts.

Allah the Glorified desires from His creation hearts that humble themselves, not forms that submit. Had He willed, He would have forced and subdued them (4), just as He subdued the entire universe to Himself. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the sky...﴾ (79:27). Allah the Exalted subdued the sky, the sun, the moon (5), and the whole cosmos, and He says to us: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ (40:57). The entire universe submits to the will of Allah, the Exalted.

Allah created the angels, a kind higher than humans, and He said of them: ﴿...They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (66:6).

So: had Allah the Exalted desired mere forms, He would have subjected all creation to His worship. But He, the Exalted, desires hearts that humble themselves; therefore He says, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself [with grief] that they will not be believers. If We willed, We could send down upon them from the sky a sign, so their necks would remain bowed to it﴾ (26:3–4).

Thus we know that Allah the Glorified is exalted above desiring to compel human forms; rather, He willed that man be free to choose. Therefore Allah does not compel anyone to faith.

Religion is not by compulsion, but by willing acceptance and contentment.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become distinct from error...﴾ (2:256). Thus Allah asks of creation that they present the matter of faith to the intellect; the intellect, through perception, is moved in wonder at the Originator's creativity, and upon admiration it inclines toward choosing certain belief.

Allah says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding﴾ (3:190).

Compulsion occurs only regarding a matter that is not clear, whereas religion is a matter in which right guidance is distinct. For when the method asks you not to steal from others, it guarantees that others will not steal from you; when it commands you not to look upon others' women, it protects your women; and when it commands you not to backbite anyone or harbor resentment toward anyone, in all of this there is comfort for the human being.

So what the method requires is everything that brings ease to a person. If you examine the requirements of the method, you will not find them required of you alone, but required of people toward you as well. It is a reciprocal exchange willed by Allah for the building up of the universe, by taking and giving.

Therefore such guidance does not need compulsion; rather, you find in it clear evidence distinguishing it from error.

The calamity is that some people misuse this verse in the wrong place: when you ask a Muslim to pray, he tells you: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion...﴾ (2:256).

You may say to him: there is no compulsion in bringing people to religion and faith in it, but if you have believed in the religion, beware of breaking it, by neglecting its method or turning away from it.

For this reason Allah the Exalted makes the penalty for leaving the religion severe, because Allah did not compel anyone to enter the religion; rather, a person may reflect and contemplate. But if he enters the religion and commits a sin, he will meet the punishment of the sin, because he entered by his own desire and chose it with certainty. Violation has its consequence. Thus entry into faith has no compulsion, but leaving the religion requires the establishment of the prescribed punishment upon the apostate (8) and the punishment of the disobedient for his disobedience.

When everyone knows this matter, they know that Allah the Exalted has made entry into religion difficult by making the consequences of leaving it severe.

1 - Al-bayyina: the clear proof that makes the truth evident. Al-bayyina is the manifest, obvious evidence about which there is no doubt, or that which clarifies the truth, supports it, and makes its matter apparent. Allah says: ﴿How many clear signs did We give them...﴾ (2:211). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], with adaptation.
2 - Allah says: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ (41:53).
3 - Hearts have a special governance. Allah says: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ (47:24), and He says: ﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned...﴾ (8:2). The faith of hearts is the faith of worshippers, while the faith of forms is the faith of the compelled, the hypocrites, and the sycophants. There is a difference between accepting certainty and the logic of the compelled.
4 - The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Had your Lord willed, all those on earth would have believed together. Would you then compel people until they become believers?﴾ (10:99), and He also says: ﴿...Had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant﴾ (6:35).
5 - Allah says: ﴿The sun and the moon [follow] a calculation, and the stars and the trees prostrate, and the sky He raised and imposed the balance﴾ (55:5–7). And Allah says: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their exalting. Indeed He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ (17:44).
6 - Bakha'a nafsahu, bakhan and bukhuwan: he killed himself with worry, rage, and grief. Allah says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps, if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow﴾ (18:6).
7 - Al-ghayy: misguidance and immersion in ignorance.
8 - The prescribed punishment for an apostate in the law of Islam is execution. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih (12/267, Fath) from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him." And from Ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man may not be shed except for one of three: disbelief after faith, adultery after marriage, and killing a soul without a soul [in retribution]." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1676).
But it must be noted that no one is judged an apostate except after the issuance of something that clearly indicates his disbelief, admitting no interpretation. It is reported of Imam Malik that he said: "If there proceeds from a person what may indicate disbelief in ninety-nine aspects and indicates faith in one aspect, his matter is to be read as faith."
The apostasy punishment is not applied except after requesting repentance for a period of three days.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 29:

Then, after that, the Truth, glory be to Him, says on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it. My reward is only from Allah. And I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾

A similar statement with the same meaning came with every messenger. In other places the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward..."﴾ [al-An'am: 90]. This is because the compensation in an exchange may not be money, but may be dates, barley, cotton, or other things. And "ajr" (reward, wage), as we know, is more general than being money or not being money. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿I do not ask you for it any wealth. My reward is only from Allah...﴾ [Hud: 29]. Thus we find that the Truth, glory be to Him, has elevated the matter.

The words of the Messenger: ﴿My reward is only from Allah...﴾ [Hud: 29] are a statement indicating that the matter which the messenger brought is a beneficial matter, because a wage is deserved only in exchange for a benefit.

We know that exchanging a thing for itself or for its equivalent is called purchase (shira'). As for a person taking the benefit of an object while the object remains the property of its owner, whoever takes this benefit pays a rent (ijar) for it. So it is as if Noah, peace be upon him, is saying: "I would have deserved a wage because I offer you a benefit, but I will not take anything from you, not out of disinterest in the wage, but because I hope for the wage from One who is better than you, greater and more magnificent."

Because this disbelieving council described those who followed Noah as "the lowly" (aradhil), the response comes from Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed...﴾ [Hud: 29]. This response makes clear that Noah, peace be upon him, cannot drive a person out of the enclosure of faith because he is poor, for certainty of faith has no connection to wealth, rank, or poverty and need. A messenger does not vacate a place of his poor followers so that the rich may come; rather, all are equal before Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so if you drive them away you would be among the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-An'am: 52]. The Truth, glory be to Him, has made these, whom they call "the lowly," a trial. Whoever becomes arrogant because of the poverty and weakness of the followers of the messengers, let him drown in his arrogance.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

Also, the Truth, glory be to Him, commands His Messenger to fix his eye upon these weak ones, and not to turn away from them or from any one of them, saying: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face, and let not your eyes pass beyond them...﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. This statement came so that no corruption or enmity would arise among the believers in the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and so that no one would say, "So-and-so is close to him." Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sat, he distributed his gaze over all his companions, so that every sitter thought that his gaze would not turn away from him.

In this noble verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says on the tongue of our master Noah, peace be upon him, describing these weak believers:

﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord...﴾ [Hud: 29]. In this is a clarification that Noah, peace be upon him, will not drive away these weak believers. For if he drove them away, when they are the ones who will meet Allah, Most High, would Noah, peace be upon him, permit it to be said about him before the Truth, blessed and exalted, that he drove away a people who believed in his message? Certainly not.

We know that the Truth, glory be to Him, holds His messengers and those to whom they were sent to account, for He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6].
