Thus, Noah, peace be upon him, knows that he is accountable before his Lord, but this disbelieving council of his people are ignorant; therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, at the end of this noble verse, says on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿...but I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾ [Hud: 29]. That is: they do not understand the mission of Noah, peace be upon him, and that he is accountable before his Lord.

1 - That is: I do not ask you, for conveying the message and calling to Allah and faith in Him, for wealth or anything else.
2 - "In" here is negating, meaning "ma" or "laysa," i.e., "my reward is only from Allah."
3 - ajjara yu'ajjiru ijaran: ajjara min fulan al-dar wa ghayriha: he rented it from him; and ajarahu yu'ajiruhu mu'ajara: he hired him, took him as a hired worker. Al-ijara: the wage for work; a contract transferring the usufruct of a specific object for a consideration. Al-ujra: the compensation for work and benefit. Al-ajr that suffices the worker for living, and the real ajr is the purchasing power of the currency the worker receives. Al-ujra: al-ajr. Al-ajir is one who works for a wage, and the greatest ajr is Allah's giving. Al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, with adaptation.
4 - Al-aradhil is the plural of radhl; it is said the singular is aradhal and the plural aradhil, and the noun form has come to predominate over it even though it is an adjective [al-Tibyan fi I'rab al-Qur'an].
5 - That is, by day and by night. What is meant is that they constantly call upon Allah, Lord of the worlds.
6 - This verse was revealed concerning a few of the poor and weak Muslims, among them Ibn Mas'ud, Suhayb, 'Ammar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal. Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "We do not accept to be followers of these; drive them away." What Allah willed to enter the heart of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered it, so Allah revealed the verse. Recorded by al-Naysaburi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 124).
7 - Fatanna: We tested; al-fitna: testing by fire, and it is borrowed for any severe testing. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿You cannot lead astray [anyone] except one destined for Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 162 (as cited)].
8 - Mann 'alayhi: he bestowed favor upon him and did good to him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164] [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
9 - 'Adat 'aynuhu 'anhu: his eye passed beyond it and he neglected to look at it and preferred others; a metaphor for turning away and lack of concern. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And let not your eyes pass beyond them...﴾ [al-Kahf: 28], i.e., do not abandon them or neglect them. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
10 - The verse ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6] is like His saying: ﴿And the day He calls them and says, "What did you answer the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65], and like His saying: ﴿The day Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge; indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. So Allah asks about the response to the messengers, and asks the messengers about the delivery.
And from the Qur'anic text we take the hadith of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock." [Ibn Kathir, with adaptation, p. 206, vol. 2].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 30:

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then take heed?﴾ (30):

Here Noah (peace be upon him) makes clear that he cannot confront Allah if he drives away these weak ones; for no one will help Noah against Allah, may He be exalted, on the moment of reckoning. On that Day there is no sovereignty for anyone except Allah, and no one intercedes except by His permission, glory be to Him, and no one is able to help anyone against Allah, may He be exalted, for He is the Subduer above all His creation.

Help, as we know, comes through overpowering, whereas intercession comes through submission, and Allah, glory be to Him, does not permit anyone to intercede for the expulsion of a believer from the enclosure of faith.

In this statement there is a reminder from Noah (peace be upon him) to his people; therefore Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿... Will you not then take heed? (30)﴾ [Hud]: That is, you must not be overtaken by heedlessness, and let there not cause you to forget what you must remember.

Just as Allah, glory be to Him, has enjoined remembrance (tadhakkur), which by its constancy keeps a person far from heedlessness, He has also enjoined reflection (tafakkur), which is contemplation aimed at deducing something new through the employment of the intellect by reflecting, which leads a person into a contemplation that guides him to sanctifying and glorifying the Creator; and by this a person reaches the truths that reveal to him the landmarks of the way.

Allah, glory be to Him, has also enjoined contemplation (tadabbur), that is: that a person should not take matters at their outward appearances, nor be deceived by those appearances(1), but there must be investigation into the realities of things.

Therefore Allah, may He be exalted, says:

﴿Will they not contemplate (tadabbur)(2) the Qur'an...? (82)﴾ [al-Nisa'] That is: will they not search for the treasures present in the inner meanings of the Qur'an?

Contemplation (tadabbur) is what uncovers the hidden meanings behind the outward appearances of the verses, and people differ in their access to the secrets of Allah's Book according to whether they look beyond the outward meanings.

Accordingly, we find 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: "Thawwiru the Qur'an" (3), that is: turn over the meanings of the verses so that you may find the treasures within them, and do not take the verses at their outward appearances, for the wonders of the Qur'an never end.

1 - Allah, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿Allah's promise—Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, while of the Hereafter they are heedless﴾ [al-Rum] This was a comment from Him, glory be to Him, on the story of the Romans and that they would defeat the Persians within a few years; the people were astonished at that time, because of their preoccupation with the outward appearances of worldly life without looking to the consequences of affairs, the course of earlier nations, and the decrees of Allah in directing the affairs of His creation.
2 - Tadabbur: reflection upon the backs (adbar) of affairs, their consequences and their ends, or reflection in order to know the realities of affairs. Allah, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿Will they not contemplate the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? (24)﴾ [Muhammad], meaning: have they been incapable and blind so that they do not reflect upon the meanings of the Qur'an and perceive the profound wisdom in it so that they believe in it? Between the interrogative hamza and the conjunctive fa' there is always an omitted verb, and the meaning is: "Have they been incapable, so that they do not contemplate?" [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
3 - Ibn Manzur mentioned it in al-Lisan (entry: th-w-r), saying: "In the hadith of 'Abd Allah: Athirů al-Qur'an, for in it is the news of the first and the last," and in another narration: "the knowledge of the first and the last." Shamir said: tathwir al-Qur'an is reciting it and discussing it with scholars regarding its tafsir and its meanings. It was said: to examine it and reflect upon its meanings, its tafsir and its recitation.

Almighty God continues what was said on the tongue of our master Noah: ﴿And I do not say to you that I have with me the treasuries of God, nor do I know the unseen (1), nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise (2) that God will never give them any good. God knows best what is in their souls. Indeed, if I did so, I would be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (31):

Thus Noah, peace be upon him, closes off to this disbelieving chieftainry every means by which they might turn away from faith. If they think that faith requires wealth, then Noah does not possess the treasuries of God, and he owns no more than this chieftainry does. If they demand that the unseen be disclosed to them, then the unseen belongs to God alone.

Noah did not claim to be of another kind, nor to be other than human. Rather, he is a human being like them, who possesses nothing with which to compel them to obedience: neither wealth, nor status, nor knowledge of the unseen.

Noah, peace be upon him, will not drive away the weak believers whom the eyes of this disbelieving chieftainry despise, belittle and mock, because Noah fears being called to account by God, Mighty and Majestic, for barring the doors of faith before the weak.

Here we must pause at the word of Almighty God: ﴿And I do not say to you that I have with me the treasuries of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise (2) that God will never give them any good...﴾ [Hud] (31). We notice here that the address has been turned into the third person (3). Noah, peace be upon him, did not address the weak and say to them that God will withhold good from them. That is because God, Glorified and Exalted, is the One who knows what is in their souls; and had Noah said such a thing to them, he would have been among the wrongdoers.

The "lam" in the word ﴿for those﴾ (lillatheena) signifies speaking about the weak, not speaking to the weak.

The use of "lam" in the sense of "about" ('an) has parallels (4), such as the saying of Almighty God: ﴿... And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, "This is nothing but evident magic." (43)﴾ [Saba']. They here do not say "to the truth," but they say "about the truth," and thus the "lam" came in the sense of "about" (5).

Thus Noah, peace be upon him, made clear that if he were to drive away those who are called "the lowly," that would mean he knows the intentions, whereas Noah, peace be upon him, knows with certainty that God is the Most Knowing of what is in souls; therefore Noah does not place himself in a position of wronging, neither himself nor others.

1 - "Ghaba al-shay' yaghibu ghayban wa ghaybatan wa ghiyaban wa ghuyuban": the thing became hidden; it is "ghaib" (absent), and its plural is "ghayb" and "ghiyab". "Al-ghayb" is everything hidden from you, and its plural is "ghuyub". In the revelation: ﴿...Knower of the unseen [ghuyub]﴾ [al-Ma'ida, 109]. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear record (59)﴾ [al-An'am].
2 - "Tazdari": to belittle. "Al-izdira'": belittling, disparaging and finding fault [Lisan al-'Arab].
3 - In the rhetorical sciences this is known as "iltifat" (shift), which is moving speech from one style to another, i.e. from first person, or second person, to the third person of it, after expression in the former. (See al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Suyuti) (3/253).
4 - Another example of "lam" in the sense of "'an" is the saying of Almighty God: ﴿And those who disbelieved said of those who believed, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it..."(11)﴾ [al-Ahqaf]. That is, about them and concerning them, not that they addressed it to the believers; otherwise it would have said "you did not precede us."
5 - "Lam": a particle that governs both nouns and pronouns, and carries several meanings, among them: end of purpose, possession, resemblance to possession, indication of ownership, indication of resemblance to ownership, indication of lineage, bare transitivity, causation (ta'lil), pure emphasis, reinforcement, indication of oath and wonder together, indication of wonder without oath, indication of an expected outcome, indication of conveying (tabligh), indication of explanation, being in the sense of "ba'd" (after), being in the sense of "qabl" (before), being in the sense of "min al-bayaniyya", being for transgression (in the sense of "'an"), being for emphasizing negation, being in the sense of "ma'a" (with), and being in the sense of "'inda" (at)... For the detailed treatment of this, see [al-Nahw al-Wafi: 2/472-481].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 32:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They said, "O Nuh, you have argued with us and multiplied our arguments, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾

Jidal (argument, debate) is the utterance of a speech that confronts another speech. The aim of each speaking party is to shift the other party from its position, by proof or by insinuation, with the goal of overturning that position.

So, jidal is a discussion between two parties who share speech, with the aim that one of them persuade the other to turn away from his position toward the position of the speaker.

The word "jidal" is derived from "al-jadl" (الجدل), meaning twisting. The twisting of a rope comes from taking strands of flax, silk, or some similar material, joining two strands together, then twisting each pair of further strands, and so on until the rope is complete.

A strong man is described as "mafttul al-adal" (مفتول العضلات), meaning that his muscles are not slack or weak but twisted, that is, interlaced and taut.

When you look at the muscular system, you are amazed at the power of the Truth, glory be to Him, who created each muscle in a specific form and manner, which enables it to act in concert and cooperate with other muscles to perform the movements required of them.

When a person raises his head, he needs the movement of more than one muscle, and when the hand works, it moves more than one muscle. If the movement of a single muscle were disabled, the movement corresponding to it would be impossible.

They said to Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿You have argued with us and multiplied our arguments...﴾ [Hud]. We know that Nuh, peace be upon him, lived a thousand years less fifty years, which means that his argument with them took a long time.

Jidal differs from mira' (dispute, contention), because jidal is for the sake of the truth, whereas mira' occurs after the truth has become manifest.

Jidal, then, is required, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is the one who says: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner...﴾ [An-Nahl: 125]. Likewise, glory be to Him, He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the speech of she who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah...﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 1]. So jidal is required in order that we reach the truth, on condition that it is good argument, with no friction and no harm.

There is a difference between ihtikak of opinions (rubbing against one another) and tahakkuk of opinions (contrived irritation). Tahakkuk is like tallukk, which is the desire not to reach the truth. But ihtikak is what leads to the truth, just as we strike the flint with a piece of iron so that sparks are produced and we see the truth. As for tahakkuk, it conceals and obscures the reality.

Mira' is argument after the truth has become manifest. It is derived from "mara al-dar'" (مرى الضرع), the milking of the udder. When milk is drawn from the udder of a she-camel or cow, the udder is full, and the milk comes out forcefully and strongly. After the udder has been emptied, the milker continues to hold the teats of the she-camel or buffalo and draws out what milk remains. This last part is called "al-muraa" (المريى).

For this reason they took from this process the word "al-mira'", which is the stage after the truth has become manifest.

Alongside jidal, mira', ihtikak and tahakkuk, there is also hijaj (argumentation), and what is meant by hijaj is demonstrating the opponent's proof against the opponent.

1 - Jadala: to dispute with truth and falsehood. It is used for falsehood in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Here you are, arguing on their behalf in the life of this world...﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], and used for truth in His words: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner...﴾ [An-Nahl: 125]. Allah, glory be to Him, forbade the pilgrims to His Sacred House from all kinds of jidal, to preserve the bond of love among them. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There shall be no obscenity, no transgression, and no disputing during the pilgrimage...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 197]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Mira': contention and jidal. The root meaning of mira' in the language is that a man draws out from his interlocutor speech and the meanings of enmity and other things. From: "maraytu al-shah" when I milked the sheep and drew out its milk. [See Lisan]. Mira' and mumarah carry the meanings of doubt and suspicion regarding a matter, which calls for more, deeper and longer jidal, and this is forbidden.
3 - She is a woman called Khawlah bint Tha'labah, who complained of her husband to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, he has consumed my wealth, worn out my youth, and I have spread out my belly for him; now that my age has grown old and my children have ended, he has divorced me by zihar. O Allah, I complain to You." Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "She had not yet left when Jibril brought down this verse: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah...﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 1]." Her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/318) and Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi (p. 231).
4 - The Exalted says: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner...﴾ [An-Nahl: 125], meaning: whoever among them needs debate and argument, let it be in the best manner, with gentleness, softness and good speech, as in His words: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except for those of them who commit wrongdoing...﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 46]. See Ibn Kathir (2/591).
5 - Tahakkuk: provocation and confrontation. "He provokes you" (innahu layatahakkaku bika), i.e., he confronts your associate [Lisan, root: h-k-k].
6 - Al-Mari': wiping the udder of a she-camel so that she releases milk; al-mara: a she-camel that yields milk to whoever wipes her udders. It was also said: it is the she-camel abundant in milk. [Lisan, root: m-r-y].
It is stated in al-Misbah al-Munir: "Maraytuhu umarihi mumarah wa mira'": I argued with him. The earlier discussion stands whether jidal is intended as truth or falsehood. It is said: "Maraytuhu" when you attack his statement to discredit the statement and belittle the speaker; and mira' is only objection, unlike jidal, which may be initiation and objection. "Imtara fi amr": he doubted it. Adapted, p. 570.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 33:

After the people had grown weary of Noah's (peace be upon him) debating with them, they asked that the punishment he had warned them of descend upon them, for they were slow to see this punishment arrive, since Noah (peace be upon him) had lived among them for a thousand years less fifty. They said: ﴿...then bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.﴾ [Hud 32]. With this statement, it is as though they had placed Noah in the position of one who holds in his hand the power to bring the punishment or to prevent it. But this is a matter that Noah does not possess; rather, it belongs to God, glorified and exalted.

For this reason, Noah (peace be upon him) alerts them. ﴿He said: "Only God will bring it upon you, if He wills, and you will not be able to escape."﴾ [Hud 33]

This is because the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who decrees a time for the punishment, and decrees a moment of appearance for every chastisement, and God does not hasten by the haste of His servants, until affairs reach what He intends.

They will not be able to frustrate God, the Exalted, nor will they escape from Him, because there is no power in the universe that can prevent the will of God, the Exalted, or that can refuse Him.

1 - Tata'abba (تتأبى): to resist and refuse to submit and obey. The Lord of Might, glorified is He, says: ﴿Every one who is in the heavens and the earth comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.﴾ [Maryam 93].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 34:

Then, after that, Allah the Glorified says on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him:

﴿And my counsel will not benefit you, if I wished to counsel you, if Allah wills to lead you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ (1) (2) (3)

The meaning here: if Allah the Glorified wills to lead you astray, then you will not benefit from the counsel, even if I wish to advise you; for the verse contains two conditions.

An example of this from our own lives: when the school principal expels a student as a punishment for a certain mistake, the student may plead with the principal, and the principal says: "If you come to me tomorrow, I will accept your apology, provided your father is with you."

The principal's words "provided your father is with you" are a later condition, yet it ought to have come first.

In the noble verse we are discussing, the first condition came later. But does Allah the Glorified lead His servants astray?

No. He guides them. Al-ghiwaya (misguidance) is ḍalāl (going astray) and deviation from the straight path.

Allah the Glorified says about Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾ (4) [al-Najm].

And He the Glorified said about Adam, peace be upon him, when he ate from the tree: ﴿...And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred﴾ (121) [Ṭā-Hā].

We must not fall into the error that some people fall into, when they understand the terms of belief according to the meaning for which the word is famous; for words have multiple meanings.

Therefore we must set out all the meanings of a word so that we may take the meaning that suits the context.

An example of this is the saying of Allah the Glorified: ﴿So there succeeded them a generation who neglected prayer and followed desires; so they will meet ghayy (5)﴾ (59) [Maryam]. His saying here, ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, means: they will meet punishment, because their error was the cause of their being punished, so the punishment was named after its cause.

Like the saying of Allah the Glorified: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ (40) [al-Shūrā]. Allah the Glorified does not do evil to His servants, but they are the ones who do evil to themselves, so what reaches them of punishment is called an evil (6).

Likewise, al-ghayy comes with the meaning of "al-ighwā'" (leading astray), and comes with the meaning of the effect that results from error, namely punishment.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted has presented in His Book various images of leading astray. Adam, peace be upon him, when he deviated (7) from the path and ate from the forbidden tree, despite Allah's warning him not to approach it, Allah the Glorified and Exalted said regarding this situation: ﴿...And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred﴾ (121) [Ṭā-Hā]. Adam, peace be upon him, did this according to his human nature, so Allah the Exalted wished to teach him that if he opposes the method in "do" and "do not do," his nakedness will appear and his private parts (8) will become visible to him. Thus Adam, peace be upon him, took the experience so that he would be prepared to receive the method and the revelation.

Allah the Glorified has related to us the words of Satan by His saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, because You led me astray, I will surely make [evil] attractive to them on earth and mislead them all"﴾ (39) [al-Ḥijr]. But did Allah, the Glorified, lead Satan astray?

Allah the Glorified does not lead astray; rather He leaves the choice to the responsible person: if he wills, he obeys, and if he wills, he disobeys.

Had He the Glorified and Exalted made us believers, we would have had no choice (9). If a person obeys, he attains Allah's bounty; and if he goes astray, Allah has given him choice and turned him toward what is not intended, while he remains capable of what is intended.

Thus: choice is not confined to misguidance; rather it includes guidance as well, and a human being is able to be guided, and able to go astray (10).

Notes (translator's rendering of the footnotes):

1 - Naṣaḥa lahu wa naṣaḥahu naṣḥan wa naṣīḥatan: he sought what would benefit him, wished him good and gain, and guided him to it. Naṣaḥa lahu al-wudd: he made it pure. Naṣaḥa lillāh: he obeyed Him and was sincere to His religion. Naṣaḥa lil-rasūl: he was truthful to him and sincere toward him, and did not oppose his command, secretly or openly. From naṣḥ in the sense of guidance and pointing to good, the Exalted says: ﴿...I counselled you, but you do not love counsellors﴾ (79) [al-A'rāf], and He says: ﴿...I am a trustworthy counsellor to you﴾ (68) [al-A'rāf]. [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm].

2 - Aghwāh: he led him astray and caused him to fall into error and misguidance. The Exalted says: ﴿So We led you astray; indeed, we were astray﴾ (32) [al-Ṣāffāt].

3 - Ḍalla: the proof was hidden from him and he turned away from the truth. Ḍalāl: forgetting and loss. Ḍalla al-shay': it was hidden and vanished; it comes intransitive as in the previous example. It also comes transitive, as in: ḍalla al-musāfir al-ṭarīq (the traveller lost the way). Allah has negated misguidance and error from His Messenger and affirmed that he speaks from Him, by Him and for Him, as the Exalted says: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ (3-4) [al-Najm]. [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm with the Burhān commentary, abridged].

4 - Ghawā: yaghwī ghayyan, and ghawā yaghwā ghiwāyatan: he immersed himself in ignorance, and it is the opposite of right guidance. Ghawā also means he failed and erred, because he immersed himself in ignorance.

5 - Al-ghayy: a valley in Hell was named by it, and the Exalted's saying ﴿...so they will meet ghayy﴾ (59) [Maryam] was explained accordingly: that is, the recompense of error, or they will enter the valley of ghayy in Hell. [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm].

6 - This is known as al-mushākala, which is mentioning a thing by the word of something else because it occurs in its company. Its example is the Exalted's saying: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ (40) [al-Shūrā], since recompense, being just, is not described as evil. Similarly the Exalted's saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed...﴾ (54) [Āl ʿImrān], where the application of makr to the Creator is only by mushākala with what is alongside it. See al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān (3/281).

7 - Nakaba ʿan al-shay' and ʿan al-ṭarīq: he deviated. Tanakkaba fulān ʿannā: he inclined away from us. Tanakkabahu: he avoided it. [See Lisān al-ʿArab]. The Exalted says: ﴿And indeed those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾ (74) [al-Mu'minūn], meaning: inclining and turning away from it.

8 - Sawāʾāt, plural of sawʾa: everything whose disclosure is shameful and which ought to be concealed. The Exalted says: ﴿Then Allah sent a crow searching in the earth to show him how to conceal the body of his brother. He said, "Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's body?" And he became of the regretful﴾ (31) [al-Mā'ida].

9 - The Exalted says: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ (99) [Yūnus]. He also says: {There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from error...} (256) [al-Baqara]. Man is free to choose among alternatives, whereas matters he cannot change are the specific attribute of the Creator. It is understood from the words of the Shaykh that Iblīs is of the jinn, in order to establish for him the right of choice.

10 - The Exalted says of man: {Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or be he ungrateful} (3) [al-Insān]. Allah has made man prepared to follow one of two paths: the path of guidance and the path of misguidance. Then He the Glorified guided him to the right, straight way, and left him free to choose: either grateful for the blessing of being guided to good, and so he is a believer, or ungrateful, and so he is a disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 35:

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾

This statement came within the story of Nuh (peace be upon him). It may be something Allah, glorified is He, revealed to Nuh (peace be upon him), or it may be that what is meant is that they said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) words similar to this.

Iftira' (invention) — as we know — is deliberate lying that contradicts reality.

Look at everything that came in the methodology (manhaj) so that the individual may abide by it: you will find that it binds everyone, and the benefit that returns to you from everyone's adherence — including yourself — is a great benefit. If the methodology tells you, "Do not steal," this is a safeguard for you from people stealing from you.

For this reason, when you listen to the methodology, do not look at what is taken from you; rather, turn your attention to what is taken for you.

On this basis, the methodology cannot be an invention (iftira').

We know that the methodology establishes just standards of uprightness in societies, and when Allah, glorified is He, legislates a law, it may seem to you that it restricts your freedom, but in reality it achieves for you many benefits and protects you from others transgressing against you.

The response to the accusation of invention was embodied in two things: either that they invent the like of it, or that he bears the burden of the crime of invention.

And if he had not invented it, then upon them falls the burden of their crime (2) in accusing him that he had invented it.

The style of the noble verse removes innocence from them in its first half. Had it come with the statement without ihtibak, He, glorified is He, would have said: "Say: If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and you are innocent of it; and if I have not invented it, then upon you is your crime, and I am innocent."

The omission came from one side corresponding to the other side, and this is what is called in the language "al-ihtibak" (3).

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah...﴾ (2:249). The small company is small in its individuals and equipment and all requirements of war, and the large company shows its largeness in its numbers, its number and all requirements of war. The small company is only overcome by the permission of Allah, the Exalted.

Thus Allah, glorified is He, clarifies that the causes decree the victory of the large company, but His will, glorified is He, overrides the causes and reaches what Allah, the Exalted, has willed.

For this reason, Allah, glorified is He, says in another verse: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two companies which met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving...﴾ (3:13). He, glorified is He, omitted the attribute of faith from the first company, just as He omitted from the second company the attribute that it fights in the way of the taghut (4) and Satan, and this is called "al-ihtibak."

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit﴾ (11:35).

But Allah, the Exalted, willed to show us the words of the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ) when he addressed his people, so He, glorified is He, said: ﴿...Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do."﴾ (34:25). He did not say, "what you commit," so he did not answer their verbal and physical harm to him with verbal harm.

Likewise, Allah, glorified is He, mentioned what came on the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿...And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ (34:24). This is an elevation in disputation that befits the mercy of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which Allah sent down to the whole world.

1 - Iftara al-qawl: he fabricated and invented it. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"...﴾ (11:35), meaning: they say, "He invented the Qur'an and fabricated it from himself." And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated..."﴾ (11:13), meaning: fabricated lies, as you claim. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - The sins of crimes in what they invented.
3 - Al-ihtibak: one of the methods of Arabic eloquence, which is that the first part omits what its counterpart in the second part establishes, and the second part omits what its counterpart in the first establishes, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And put your hand into your pocket; it will come out white...﴾ (27:12). The estimation: "you put it in, not white, and bring it out, it comes out white"; so he omitted from the first "not white" and from the second "and bring it out." Al-Zarkashi said: it is that two opposites come together in the speech, so from each of them is omitted a counterpart, the other indicating it, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit"﴾ (11:35). The estimation: "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and you are innocent of it, and upon you is your crime, and I am innocent of what you commit." [al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an: 3/182, 183].
4 - Taghut: a noun denoting exaggeration, applied to Satan, an idol, and everything worshipped besides Allah, and everything that incites to evil and calls to misguidance and strife.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 36:

After a thousand years less fifty of Noah's (peace be upon him) argument with his people, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said to him: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing."﴾ (36)

The coming of "illa" (إلا) here is not for exception (istithna'), but it is a noun with the meaning of "ghayr" (other than). That is: none of your people will believe other than the one who has already believed.

There is a parallel to this in the foremost of beliefs, when the Truth, glorified be He, said: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined.﴾ (21:22). Here too "illa" carries the meaning of "ghayr", and if "illa" were for exception, it would mean that Allah, glorified be He, - God forbid - would be among other gods. Therefore "illa" cannot here be for exception, but rather it means "ghayr", and it conveys the meaning of Allah's oneness and His singularity in divinity, may He be mighty and majestic.

The verse we are contemplating affirms that there is no one among his people who will believe other than those who have already believed in Noah (peace be upon him); for Allah has concluded the matter.

This gives us justification for Noah's (peace be upon him) boldness in invoking destruction upon those among his people who did not believe, when he said: ﴿"My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except a wicked disbeliever."﴾ (71:26-27). The justification for this was that he (peace be upon him) had invited them to faith for a long time, and they did not respond, and Allah the Exalted revealed to him that they would not believe. And He, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿"...so do not be distressed by what they have been doing."﴾ (11:36). Ibtu's (ابتئاس) is the distress that causes despair, and they had disbelieved, and there is no sin after disbelief.

1 - From Ibn 'Abbas: they were eighty souls, including their women. From Ka'b al-Ahbar: they were seventy-two souls. It was said: they were ten. It was also said: it was only Noah and his three sons Sam, Ham and Japheth, and his four daughters-in-law, the wives of these three, and the wife of Yam. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/445).

2 - Ibtaasa al-rajul (ابتأس الرجل): he was dejected and grieved. "La tabta'is" (لا تبتئس): do not grieve. It is said: "ibta'asa al-rajul" when something he dislikes reaches him. Al-ibtu'as (الابتئاس) is grief with submissiveness. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: b-a-s]

3 - Yadharuh (يذره): he leaves it and abandons it. This verb is used in the Noble Qur'an only in the imperfect and the imperative. From the imperfect is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land...?﴾ (7:127), and His saying: ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods..."﴾ (71:23), meaning: do not abandon your gods. From the imperative is His saying: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone.﴾ (74:11), meaning: leave me, I will take revenge upon him and punish him for his crimes against the religion and the Qur'an, and this is a style of threat and warning. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]

4 - Al-diyar (الديار): one who inhabits the house, or one who moves and roams in it freely. It is said: "ma bil-dar diyar" (there is no one in the house), meaning: there is no one in it. And His saying, on the tongue of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿"My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant."﴾ (71:26), meaning: do not leave any one of them alive. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 37:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And build the ark(1) under Our eyes(2) and by Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed they are to be drowned.﴾ (37)

Thus Noah learned of the matter of the drowning through the revelation to him concerning the building of the ship. The meaning of "build" (isna') is: perform the craft (san'ah). There is a difference between sun'ah (craft/manufacture) and hirfah (trade/skilled work). Sun'ah is bringing into existence something that did not exist, like the maker of cups, the maker of shoes, the maker of chandeliers, or the maker of chairs. The one who maintains and keeps up a craft is the artisan (hirfi).

There is another kind of production, like the occupation of the farmer who ploughs the land, sows the seed in it and waters it so that plants grow from it. The one with this occupation is called a "zari'" (farmer) or "fallah" (cultivator), because the direct sustenance of life comes from agriculture.

As for the manufacturer, he brings some of the necessities of life as they develop; he creates a tool or makes a device that did not exist. The artisan is the one who maintains that tool. As for the merchant, he is the one who carries out an operation that gathers all of that together, and he is the intermediary between the producer of a thing and the consumer. The merchant exists to display goods for the purpose of buying and selling.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And build the ark... (37)﴾ [Hud]. That is: bring into existence something from nothing. However, this thing will be made from another thing that already exists, because Noah, peace be upon him, had earlier planted a tree, and it lived with him all this long period and grew large in trunk and branches.

Noah, peace be upon him, began the process of splitting the tree to make from it the ship, whose length, as it is said(3), was three hundred cubits(4), whose breadth was fifty cubits, and whose height was thirty cubits, consisting of three decks, to hold the believers and a pair of every kind of the animals of the earth, its beasts, its creeping things and its predators and wild beasts.

We know that the tree Noah planted grew very large because of the long period that Noah spent in calling his people; and we also know that the trunk of a tree grows circularly by the measure of one circle each year. When we cut the trunk of a tree, we find that the diameter of the trunk is made of circles, and each circle represents a year of its life.

Thus the size of the tree reached what would help Noah, peace be upon him, to build the ship.

The Truth, glorified is He, taught him by revelation and by the inspiration of thoughts how to build the ship. Did God, glorified is He, not inspire His prophet David, peace be upon him, in the matter of iron? He told us, glorified and exalted is He, that He commanded the mountains to return (in glorification) with him, and likewise the birds, and He made iron soft for him without fire:

﴿O mountains, repeat the praises with him, and the birds; and We made iron soft for him (10), [saying], "Make full coats of mail(11)...﴾ [Saba']

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, informed us that iron became soft without fire, by His permission, so that David could make from it large coats of mail covering the back and the chest, to protect the vulnerable parts(7) of a man.

The Truth, glorified is He, inspired David, peace be upon him, to make those coats of mail in a wondrous way, by making them complete(8).

Complete (sabighah) is that which is woven like a mat, where one strand is placed beside another and all the strands are tied in a way that makes it easy to unroll or roll up the mat.

In the same verse the Truth, glorified is He, explains to us how the revelation came to David, peace be upon him, concerning this precise craft, and He says: ﴿And measure well in the weaving(9)...(11)﴾ [Saba']. That is: O David, when you weave(10) the soft iron, by God's permission, to make it into coats of mail for yourself, you must make those coats of mail with precise measurement, so that the coat is not tight on the chest of the warrior, which would restrict his movement and reduce his capacity to breathe, so that he pants quickly and cannot continue fighting.

Likewise the coat of mail must not be loose on the chest of the warrior, so that the looseness of the coat does not help the opponent's sword; the blow would then strike the warrior's chest through the coat itself, and the strength of the coat would add to the strength of the opponent's sword. Rather, when the coat is able to encompass the body without binding its movement, this is the coat suitable for fighting.

David, peace be upon him, perfected the making of those coats of mail with that precise geometry which the Truth, glorified is He, revealed to him. He made them by the command of the Most High, glorified is He, when He said to him: ﴿And measure well... (11)﴾; and the word qadara gives the meaning of measuring and perfecting.

So those who make things must know that the Noble Qur'an, at the very moment it directs toward excellence in performance and work, teaches us the method of measurement and perfection in work and in creative effort, so that we take this guidance as a lamp by which we walk, so that the work may be righteous. You see the one who perfects his craft saying: "Allah," as if this saying is the primordial nature's acknowledgment of the power of the Truth, glorified is He, to grant man the capacity for perfection and creativity.

The Truth, glorified is He, also says, in His teaching to David, peace be upon him:

﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail(12)...(80)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. Thus God, exalted is He, casts the thought into the heart of the Messenger or prophet that "do such-and-such," and he does it.

When we look at the civilization of ancient Egypt, we find that all its sciences and arts in embalming, colours and sculpture were the specialty of the priests, who represented the religious authority, and these priests did not write down the secrets of those sciences, so none of the contemporaries was able to learn about them. Thus we find that every matter in its origins has its source in heaven.

In the story of Noah, peace be upon him, we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying: ﴿And build the ark(13) under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed they are to be drowned. (37)﴾

The meaning of "under Our eyes" is under Our protection and Our care. The phrase "under Our eyes" indicates comprehensive protection and complete care.

Did the Truth, glorified is He, not say, in a matter concerning the Messenger of God Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:

﴿So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes(14)...(48)﴾ [al-Tur].

Likewise He, glorified is He, said in the story of our master Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿...and that you may be brought up under My eye (39)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. The Truth, glorified is He, rescued Moses, peace be upon him, from Pharaoh, who used to kill the children of the Children of Israel, and God cast love for Moses into the heart of Pharaoh's wife, and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me... (39)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. This is because Moses, peace be upon him, when he was a nursing infant, was cast into the river(15), and Pharaoh's people picked him up; but Pharaoh's wife said to her husband, seeking life for Moses: ﴿A coolness of the eye for me and for you...(9)﴾ [al-Qasas]. We find that the enemy of Moses and his people picks Moses up so that he may live under their protection and care, as if God, glorified is He, were saying to them: "I will make you raise the one who will take charge of your subjugation."

As for the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And build the ark under Our eyes... (37)﴾ [Hud]. That is: if you stop at any obstacle, We will inspire you with how to confront that obstacle.

When Noah, peace be upon him, built the ark, he needed wooden planks, and those planks had to hold together; nails had not yet been invented, so God inspired him to bind the planks with twisted ropes. One of the discoverers of America in the modern age did this too, when he built a ship from papyrus plants and bound it with strong twisted ropes.

The Truth, glorified is He, said about the manner of building Noah's ship, peace be upon him:

﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails(13)﴾ [al-Qamar]. That is: Noah, peace be upon him, brought planks of wood and bound them with twisted ropes, and made the binding firm with a powerful Determiner, in a way that did not allow water to seep into the ship.

Just as wooden barrels are made in our age, where the craftsman makes them from long wooden pieces, arranges them and binds them firmly with a strong frame; when any liquid is placed in them, the wood soaks up that liquid and swells to close the pores, so the liquid does not seep out of the barrel, because wood is the only material that expands with cold, unlike all other materials that expand with heat.

For this reason we find that the skilled carpenter in his craft is the one who makes furniture, doors or windows in the temperate seasons(19), because if he makes them in summer, we will find the wood shrunk; when winter comes the wood expands and causes the doors and windows not to close tightly. Likewise, if he makes them in winter while the wood is swollen, summer will come and the doors will shrink, and they will have their troubles, so it is not easy to control the closing of doors or to control any chest or window tightly.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed they are to be drowned(20). (37)﴾ [Hud]. That is: do not speak to Me about forgiving those who have wronged themselves by disbelief, those who committed the great wrong, which is disbelief at the summit of creed, namely belief in God, one, unique, with no partner. Therefore they deserved punishment, which is drowning.

Thus Noah, peace be upon him, learned that building the ship was linked to the kind of punishment that would fall upon those who disbelieved in his message; he and those who believed with him would be saved, but whoever disbelieved would surely drown.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes this clear when He says:

﴿And he began building the ark, and whenever a company of his people passed by him they mocked him. He said, "If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock. (38)"﴾

1 - Sun' (making): its meaning is bringing into being and creating, and it occurs with intention, will and planning; therefore one does not say "the animal made such-and-such." The Almighty said: ﴿They only made the plot of a magician...(69)﴾ [Ta-Ha], meaning that what they made and brought into being was a plot and magic. The Almighty said in the story of Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿...and that you may be brought up under My eye (39)﴾, meaning: raised under My watchful care. His saying: {And build the ark under Our eyes...(37)} [Hud] means: under Our care and Our protection. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], with adaptation.

2 - Fulk (ark): the ship, for masculine and feminine, singular and plural. The Truth says: {And you see the ships ploughing through it...(14)} [al-Nahl]; and fulk also means the orbit in which the heavenly stars swim: ﴿...each in an orbit they swim (33)﴾ [al-Anbiya'] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged].

3 - Qatadah mentioned it. There are other opinions. The view that agreed upon is that its height in the sky was thirty cubits, three levels, each level ten cubits: the lowest for the animals and beasts, the middle for humans, and the top for the birds; its door was in its side, and it had a covering over it sealed. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/444).

4 - Dhira' (cubit): a measure of length estimated at 75 centimetres or less. The cubit of a human is from the elbow to the fingertips.

5 - Ta'wib: to glorify along with Him and return the glorification. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/527): "Ta'wib in the language is repetition/return; so the mountains and birds were commanded to return with him with their voices."

6 - Al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-A'mash and others said: David did not need to put it into fire or strike it with a hammer; rather he would twist it with his hand like threads. Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/527).

7 - Ma'atib: places of ruin. Its singular is ma'tab. 'Atab is ruin, which occurs among people and others. 'Atiba (with a kasra on the ta') 'ataban and a'tabahu: destroyed him. [Lisan al-Arab, root '-t-b]. The meaning: the places where, if a fighter is stabbed, he may be destroyed.

8 - Complete coat of mail (al-dir' al-sabighah): the wide one that extends down to the ground, covering the ankles. [Lisan al-Arab, root sabagh].

9 - Sard: weaving the rings of the coat of mail and perfecting its making. Sarada al-adim and al-jild yasrudu sardan: he punctured and pierced it with an awl in succession and consistency; for this reason weaving coats of mail is called sard, because of its precision, succession and consistency. "And measure well in the weaving" means: perfect the work in the sard of the coats, that is, during their weaving; i.e., perfect the sard and make the weaving excellent. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

10 - Nasj (weaving): joining one thing to another. Nasaja al-shay' yansijuhu nasjan: to join. The wind weaves dust: it draws some of it to others; and the wind weaves water when it strikes its surface so that it forms lines like ripples; and the wind weaves dry leaves: it gathers some to others. Among the meanings of nasj: weaving of cloth, and sometimes a maker of coats of mail is called "nassaj" (weaver). [Lisan al-Arab, root n-s-j, adapted].

11 - Nibras: a lamp, or a luminous thing. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted.

12 - Libus: what is worn. Here it means: the coats of mail worn in war. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

13 - Fulk: the ship. The word fulk applies to masculine and feminine, singular and plural. The Almighty said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship (119)﴾ [al-Shu'ara'], making it singular masculine. He said: ﴿And you see the ships ploughing through it...(14)﴾ [al-Nahl], making fulk plural and describing it as "mawakhir", i.e., ships.

14 - That is: be patient with their harm and do not heed them, for you are in full view of Us and under Our protection, and God will keep you from people. Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/245).

15 - Yamm: a large gathering of water, whether sweet or salty; both meanings occur in the Qur'an. The Almighty said: ﴿When We inspired to your mother what is inspired (38), [saying], "Put him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank...(39)"﴾ [Ta-Ha], where it means sweet water, intended as the Nile of Egypt. He also said: ﴿So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the yamm...(136)﴾ [al-A'raf], where it means salt water, intended as the Gulf of Suez, an extension of the Red Sea.

16 - "A coolness of the eye for me and for you": that is, a cause of joy for me and for you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

17 - Dusur: al-dassar in a thing: pushing into it with force. Al-dassar is a nail, or a rope of palm fibre with which the planks of a ship are tied; its plural is dusur. The Almighty said: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and dusur (13)﴾ [al-Qamar], a metonymy for the described thing, the ship. Mujahid said: al-dusur are the ribs of the ship. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: it is its chest, which strikes the waves. al-Dahhak said: al-dusur are its two ends and its base. Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/264).

18 - Hudhdhaq: skilled in his work. Hadhaqa al-shay': excelled at it. [See Lisan].

19 - Rateebah: the stable one that is not described as cold or hot.

20 - Drowning is when water covers a person until he dies; the Almighty said: ﴿...until when drowning overtakes him (90)﴾ [Yunus]. It means it overcomes him. Gharaqa, like fariha, so he is gharq, gharig, and ghareeq. The plural of the last is gharqa, and its passive participle is mughraq. The Almighty said: ﴿...so he was among the drowned (43)﴾ [Hud]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, p. 51, vol. 2].

21 - Mala': a group of them.

22 - Sakhira minhu wa bihi (from the pattern of fariha): sakhran, sukhran, sukhran, sukhriyyatan, and sukhriyyan: he mocked him. The Almighty said: ﴿...He said, "If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock (38)"﴾ [Hud]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

The chiefs and nobles among the people of Noah would pass by him while he was building the ship, and they would mock him, meaning: here he is, after claiming prophethood, turning into a carpenter. Then they would ask: how will this ship reach the sea from "Mosul"?

They had not known what Noah (peace be upon him) knew, namely that it was the water that would come to carry the ship.

And we observe in the words of the Truthful One, glorified is He: ﴿And he was constructing the ship﴾ [Hud 11:38]: the carrying out of the command that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had issued to Noah (peace be upon him) when He said: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ [Hud 11:37].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 39:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him (1) and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment (2).﴾ (39)

We note in the words of the Truth, glorified is He, ﴿So you will come to know﴾ that the matter which Noah, peace be upon him, is informing them of, namely the event of the drowning, will take place in the future. This is because any event, as we know, has more than one form. If the speech about the event comes after it has occurred, the verb is in the past tense; and if the speech comes at the time the event is occurring, the verb is in the present tense.

If the speech concerns an event whose time has not yet come, then the matter requires that we precede the speech about the event with the particle "sin" (sa-, the future prefix), as when we say "sa-yaʿlamūn" (they will know). This indicates the near future. As for the distant future, the word "sawfa" is used.

We know that Noah, peace be upon him, spent many years building the ship(3). Therefore He said "sawfa" to indicate the widest span of time.

And what is it that they will come to know? It is the punishment. Will it come to Noah and those with him, or will it come to those who disbelieved from the chiefs of Noah's people?

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him...﴾ (39). In this statement there is what confirms that Noah, peace be upon him, knew that the punishment would come to them, because they disbelieved, mocked, and said: ﴿...So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful.﴾ (32)

As for the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿...and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment (39)﴾: we find in it the word ﴿yaḥilla﴾ (will descend), which is the opposite of departure. It indicates coming down from a height to a place of settling. One says "ḥalla bi-l-makān," meaning he descended to dwell in the place; its opposite is departure or travelling.

As for the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿muqīm﴾ (lasting) means that the punishment which will descend upon them is a constant punishment(4).

1 - Khaziya (خزي), yakhza: to be humiliated, exposed and ashamed. Akhzāhu fulān, yukhzīhi: he humiliated him and exposed him. The Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him...﴾ (192) [Āl ʿImrān].
2 - Yaḥilla: it descends upon them. The Exalted said: ﴿...and do not transgress therein, lest My anger descend upon you; and whoever has My anger descend upon him has certainly fallen﴾ (81) [Ṭāhā] [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm].
3 - Zayd ibn Aslam said: Noah, peace be upon him, remained one hundred years planting trees, cutting them, and drying them, and one hundred years building it. Mentioned by al-Qurṭubī in his tafsir (4/3349).
4 - What is stated in the explanation of the verse in al-Qurṭubī (4/3351) indicates that there are two types of punishment here.
- The first: ﴿a punishment that disgraces him﴾, which is in this world.
- The second: ﴿a lasting punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 40:

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Until when Our command came and the oven gushed forth, We said: Load into it two of each kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe. But none believed with him except a few.﴾ (40):

The word ﴿until﴾ indicates a limit (ghaya), and the word ﴿Our command﴾ indicates the flood. Then the command from Allah, glorified is He, that he should load into it two of each kind, and those who believed with him, who were a small handful.

So in the story of Noah, peace be upon him, there is more than one stage. There was a command from Allah, exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿And construct the ark...﴾ (37) [Hud], and an action by Noah, peace be upon him, which was to build. This act took a long time on the part of Noah, peace be upon him, until the command of the flood came, which is indicated by the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And the oven gushed forth...﴾ (40) [Hud]. The meaning of the word ﴿gushed forth﴾ is that the water had reached the point of boiling.

Water contains air, as evidenced by the fact that fish breathe from the water. When we boil water we see bubbles of air coming out of the water. Then the water grows heavier until the heat of boiling intensifies, and the water surges out, scattered beyond the vessel of boiling.

The "tannur" is the place where baking takes place, and the emergence of water from the tannur was a distinctive sign that Noah, peace be upon him, knew, so that he would carry those he wished to save, from the believers, and from all the goods of the world.

The sign was the emergence of water from an unexpected place, which is the tannur.

The scholars differed in interpreting the word "tannur". Some of them said: the tannur is the place where Adam, peace be upon him, used to bake, or it is the place where Eve used to work, or it is the house of Noah, or it is the house of an old woman.

All these interpretations neither benefit nor harm; the important point is that the gushing of the tannur was a sign between Noah, peace be upon him, and his Lord, and that when the tannur gushed forth, Noah was to load two of each kind.

The saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿Load into it two of each kind...﴾ (40) [Hud] means: that he should load from all creatures. This is indicated by the word ﴿kull﴾ (each/every), with tanwin, which conveys generality, i.e., load into the ark from every thing that the life of the survivors requires, from all categories of plants and animals, even the pig was among what Noah, peace be upon him, carried.

As for those who say that the prohibition of the pig came because Noah, peace be upon him, did not carry it with him, they did not perceive the importance of the pig as an animal that eats filth and cleans the earth of it, because every creature has a function, and the function of creatures is not only that man eats them.

The saying ﴿two of each kind, two...﴾ (40) [Hud] indicates that the word "zawj" (pair) (4) is singular; as evidenced by the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And created from it its mate...﴾ (1) [An-Nisa'].

So: the word "zawj" means a single one with its like, like a pair of shoes, for example.

I say this so that we do not take the word "zawj" to mean two; therefore we find the Truthful, glorified is He, saying in another verse:

﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. (143) And of camels two, and of cattle two...﴾ (144) [Al-An'am]. When we add up the number we find it is eight; and if the word "zawj" were applied to two, the number in that noble verse would be sixteen.

The Noble Qur'an also clarifies that the word "zawj" is singular in the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? (37) Then he was a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned, and made of him two mates, the male and the female (39)﴾ [Al-Qiyamah]. So: the male is a zawj, and the female is also a zawj.

Noah, peace be upon him, continued carrying out the command of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿...Load into it two of each kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.. (40)﴾ [Hud].

Thus Allah, glorified is He, willed to preserve life by saving everything that life needs in the ark. And it is said that they lived in that ark for two years. (9)

1 - Tannur: a place where water gushes forth, and the oven in which bread is baked. The Exalted said: ﴿And the oven gushed forth (40)﴾ [Hud], meaning: the earth burst forth with abundant water, or it burst forth in a manner resembling the surging of fire in an oven. The tannur is also the gathering place of a valley's water, and all of this indicates the abundance of water and the strength of its rush. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

2 - "Ahl" (family/people), from the forms fariha, daraba and nasara, ahlan and ahwalan: to marry; and "ahl al-makan" means to populate a place with its people. "Al-ahl" means relatives, the clan, and the wife; "ahl al-dar" are its owners; "ahl al-nabi" are his followers; and "ahl al-Kitab" are the people of the heavenly religions. The Exalted said: ﴿...O People of the Book, do not commit excess in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray, and strayed from the right way (77)﴾ [Al-Ma'idah]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged]..

3 - Al-Qurtubi mentioned these differences in his tafsir as seven opinions, so refer to them there (1/3351, 3352), then he said: "Al-Nahhas said: these opinions are not contradictory; they all agree that this was a sign." End of quote, with adaptation. As for Ibn Kathir, he preferred the opinion of Ibn 'Abbas that the tannur is the surface of the earth, meaning the earth became springs gushing forth until water erupted from the tannurs which are the places of fire; they became gushing water. Ibn Kathir said: "This is the opinion of the majority of the early scholars and the scholars of later generations," and he mentioned the rest of the opinions but described them as strange. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/445]..

4 - Zawj: each one together with another of its kind, with a difference of function, because in the difference of function is the completion of purpose; it is applied to the male and the female, so a man is a zawj for a woman, and a woman is a zawj for a man. In arithmetic, zawj is the opposite of fard (odd), and it is whatever divides into two equal parts. Zawj also means a form or category that has a counterpart or opposite, like moist and dry, male and female. The Exalted said: {Load into it two of each kind...(40)} [Hud], meaning: load into the ark a male and a female of every species. And the Exalted said: {And other things of similar kinds in pairs (58)} [Sad], meaning: categories that are paired, male and female, or opposites, everything and its opposite. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted..

5 - Nutfah: the water flowed and dripped. And "nutfah" is clear water, and in the Qur'an it is applied to the semen of a man or a woman from which the child is created. The Exalted said: ﴿He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once he is an open adversary (4)﴾ [An-Nahl]..

6 - Yumna: it is poured into the womb. [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Makhluf]..

7 - 'Alaqah: thick congealed blood that clings to whatever it touches. Its plural is 'alaq. The Exalted said: ﴿Then We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot...(5)﴾ [Al-Hajj], and the Exalted said: ﴿Then We made the sperm-drop a clinging clot, then We made the clot a lump of flesh, then We made the lump bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh, then We produced it as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators (14)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun], and the Exalted said: ﴿He created man from a clinging clot (2)﴾ [Al-'Alaq]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]..

8 - Fasawwa: He made it proportionate, completed it, and breathed into it the soul. [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Makhluf].

9 - 'Ikrimah said: Noah, peace be upon him, boarded the ark on the tenth of Rajab, and it settled on al-Judi on the tenth of Muharram. That is six months. Al-Tabari mentioned from Ibn Ishaq what implies that he remained on the water for about a year. This was stated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3354). Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/447) mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that they remained in the ark one hundred and fifty days, i.e., about five months. And Allah knows best.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿And he said, "Embark upon it; in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful." (41)﴾

This is the final stage in the story of the ship. The story began with a command from Allah, may He be exalted, to Noah, peace be upon him, to build the ark (al-fulk). Then came Noah's preliminary address to his people. Then he kept building the ark until the sign of the beginning came: ﴿...and the oven gushed forth...(40)﴾ [Hud]. Noah, peace be upon him, then carried aboard the ark, by the command of Allah, a pair of every kind, along with his family and those who believed with him.

Noah, peace be upon him, said to those who believed: {Embark upon it; in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring...(41)} [Hud]. This statement is attributed to Noah, peace be upon him, because he added: {...Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful (41)} [Hud]. Riding (al-rukub) requires that the rider be upon the ridden object and above it.

Being above requires that the thing one is above be at the service of the one above it. It is as though Allah's subjection of the ship came only to serve the one who rides it.

But Allah, may He be exalted, says here: ﴿Embark upon it...(41)﴾ [Hud], and He did not say, "Embark upon it" with "ala" (on it).

Allah, may He be exalted, said this to give us a glimpse of the way the ship was made. Noah, peace be upon him, built it by revelation from Allah, may He be exalted, in the best arrangement of ships, and did not build it in a primitive way. Thus they did not ride on its deck; rather, it was constructed so as to allow them to dwell within it, especially since that ship carried wild beasts, reptiles and animals alongside humans, so it had to be built in the form of levels and decks.

The statement of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its mooring...(41)﴾ [Hud] shows us that it was made to save from drowning. Therefore it must sail with those riding in it to a place the water does not reach, and this place must be high, to allow mooring, just as the flood enabled the process of flowing.

Thus its course was in the name of Allah, and its mooring by His permission, may He be exalted.

Noah, peace be upon him, said: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its mooring...(41)﴾ [Hud]. This teaches us that its movement is accomplished only by the will of Allah, may He be exalted, and that they ride in it not because of their personal status, but because of their faith in Allah, may He be exalted.

An example of this from our own lives, and to Allah belongs the highest example: we find a judge who, opening a ruling, says, "In the name of the Constitution and the Law." That is, he does not judge by his own essence as a judge, but judges in the name of the Constitution and the Law.

Noah, peace be upon him, says: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its mooring...(41)﴾ [Hud], because the ship belongs to Allah in command, and to His messenger in making.

For this reason it is said: "Every matter not begun with the name of Allah is cut off (abtar)" (3).

Because when you set about doing something, actions or events require many kinds of energy. If the action is physical, it requires strength; if it is mental, it requires thought, deliberation and patience; if it is an action that involves confronting people of rank, it requires courage; and if it is for the purification of souls, it requires forbearance.

So the needs of events are many and varied. In order to obtain strength you may say, "In the name of the Strong, the Capable"; to obtain knowledge, you say, "In the name of the All-Knowing"; and if you want wealth, you say, "In the name of the Rich"; when you need forbearance, you say, "In the name of the Forbearing"; and when you need courage, you say, "In the name of the Subduer (al-Qahhar)."

A single action may require many things, and what suffices for all of that is that you call upon your Lord and seek blessing by the name of the One who gives existence to existence, which is Allah, may He be exalted, in whom all the attributes of perfection and majesty are gathered.

Beware of being timid or shy; rather, enter upon every matter in the name of Allah, even if you are a sinner, for Allah, may He be exalted, is Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.

The statement of Allah, may He be exalted, on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿...Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful (41)﴾ [Hud] intends only that these believers in Noah's message were human beings, and, like the majority of humankind, did not fully observe all the obligations, because they were not angels.

Therefore Allah, may He be exalted, accepted their faith, pardoned some of the sins they had committed, and did not hold them to account for them.

This is the distinctive feature in the saying: "In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful."

1 - Al-majra (with a fatha on the ra and inclined toward a kasra): a noun of place/time meaning "the running/course." Allah says: ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its mooring...(41)﴾ [Hud], meaning its sailing and its anchoring by the blessing of the name of Allah and His care and protection. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Al-sun' (ṣun‘): means bringing into being and creating, done with intention, will and planning; it is also applied to a craft as "ṣinā‘a." As in Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, they have only contrived the plot of a magician...(69)﴾ [Ta-Ha], and: ﴿...Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do (8)﴾ [Fatir]. It also comes after training and teaching under My watch and care, as in His words: ﴿...and that you may be raised under My eye (39)﴾ [Ta-Ha], and it is applied to lofty buildings and sturdy palaces, as in His words: ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever (129)﴾ [al-Shu‘ara’]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].
3 - Abtar: that is, cut off from blessing, with no good in it.

Almighty Allah then goes on to describe the ship and those aboard it:

﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called out to his son, who was apart: "My son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ (42)

The ship sailed with them not merely amid a towering wave, but the waves were like mountains, and this indicates that it was moving with high power, so the waves had no effect upon it.

(1) Al-jary (الجري): swift movement. "Jarā al-mā' yajrī" means the water flowed; "jarat al-safīnah" means the ship moved and sped along. Allah says: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs (50)﴾ [al-Rahman], and He says: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains... (42)﴾ [Hud], referring to the ship of Noah, peace be upon him. And He says: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship (11)﴾ [al-Haqqah], meaning: in the well-known ship. The plural of al-jāriyah is al-jawārī. And He says: ﴿And among His signs are the ships in the sea like landmarks (32)﴾ [al-Shura], where the yā' was dropped for lightness in the orthography of the Mushaf. And His saying: ﴿And by those that run with ease (3)﴾ [al-Dhariyat] — it is said they are ships, it is said they are winds, and it is said they are the stars and planets. And He says: ﴿And the ships that run in the sea with that which benefits people... (164)﴾ [al-Baqarah] [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Then the discussion turns to the tenderness of fatherhood, when Noah calls out to his son:

﴿...And Noah called out to his son, who was apart [from them], "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers." (42)﴾ [Hud]: The son rejected his father's request, relying on the mountain to protect him.

On this, the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, explains the son's intention in opposing his father's wish: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy." And the waves came between them, so he was among the drowned. (43)﴾

Thus the son of Noah thought that he would be saved if he took refuge on a mountain, perhaps the height of the mountain would protect him from drowning. But Noah, peace be upon him, knew that there is no salvation for a disbeliever; rather, salvation is only for the one whom Allah has shown mercy through faith.

And so the waves separated Noah from his son, and the son drowned.

Allah, glory be to Him, wished to conclude the account concerning Noah, peace be upon him, so He brought the image of the ship settling on al-Judi.

It is said that Mount al-Judi is located in Mosul, and it is said that it is in the region of Kufa. Yet this statement is mere knowledge that does not benefit, and ignorance of it does not harm.

1 - Al-Ma'zil (المعزل): a noun of place. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿...was apart...(42)﴾ [Hud], meaning: in a place where he isolated himself to one side, and did not join the passengers of the ship with his father Noah, peace be upon him. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..
2 - Ya'simuni (يعصمني): it prevents me and protects me from the water so that I do not drown, and al-'isma (العصمة) means prevention and preservation..
3 - Hala bayna-huma yahulu hawalan (حال بينهما يحول حولا): it blocked and separated. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿...And the waves came between them, so he was among the drowned (43)﴾ [Hud], meaning: the waves blocked and separated between Noah, peace be upon him, and his son, so he was among the drowned. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], with adaptation..
4 - Awa (أوى): sought refuge at a mountain and clung to it, seeking protection from the abundant water. And awa ila al-makan, awa ilayhi ya'wi awban: he alighted there and took refuge in it. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave...(10)﴾ [al-Kahf], meaning: they alighted in it and took refuge in it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..

The Lord, glorified is He, says:

﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]!" And the water subsided, and the matter was decided, and it came to rest upon al-Judi. And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people!"﴾ :

Al-bal' (swallowing) is the passage of a thing through the throat so that it falls into the belly. Whenever a command from Allah, may He be exalted, comes in the Qur'an, such as ﴿And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water..."﴾ [Hud], understand that the one who speaks is one to whom the earth submits.

Allah, glorified is He, did not say, "Allah said, 'O earth, swallow your water'," because there is an underlying helper even though it is not stated. The Lord, glorified is He, wants to cultivate in us the instinct and insight of faith, because no one other than Allah, may He be exalted, is capable of commanding the earth to swallow water.

His command, glorified is He, to the sky is ﴿and O sky, withhold [your rain]﴾, meaning: let the rain stop.

Thus the Lord, glorified is He, ends the deluge that had drowned the world by stopping the outflow and giving the command to the drainage system to draw off the water.

We observe, when rain falls, that the sewage network overflows if something blocks the drainage of the water, because the land of cities nowadays has become asphalt that does not absorb water. Therefore we find the competent authorities mobilising their resources to repair the sewage pipes so that they absorb the rainwater and the movement of life is not disrupted.

I say here: good use of water is part of good faith, because I notice that when people perform wudu' they open the water taps far beyond their need for the lawful wudu'. So we must not commit the sin of wasting pure water so that it is lost without benefit (5).

People should save water and not misuse it, because when water is abundant it gives life to dead land. We need water to cultivate deserts, and we need to lighten the burden on the sewage networks.

In short, we need to receive the blessings of Allah, may He be exalted, well and to deal with them well, so that we may enjoy them and be happy with their goodness.
