The saying of the Lord, glorified is He: ﴿And O sky, withhold... (44)﴾ [Hud]: meaning, stop the rain. From this we take the word qal' (ṣail, sail), which is placed atop small sailing boats, and it is the sail.

It is said: "uqli'at al-markab" (the ship set sail), meaning it left the stillness it had been in while standing on the shore.

The saying of the Lord, glorified is He: ﴿And the water subsided... (44)﴾ [Hud]: He has put this verb here in the passive so that we know that Allah, may He be exalted, is the one who commanded the water to subside.

The root gh-y-d (ghāḍa) is used intransitively and is used transitively (6).

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And it came to rest upon al-Judi... (44)﴾ [Hud]: meaning, the ship settled on the mountain of al-Judi.

The Lord, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿...And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people!" (44)﴾ [Hud]. This is a final distance until the Day of Resurrection.

1 - Aqli'i (withhold): refrain (desist) from sending down rain [Kalimat al-Qur'an]. Al-iqlā' 'an al-amr is to cease from it, and aqla'a 'an al-shay' is to desist from it. Uqli'at al-sama' means it stopped raining [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Ghuyida al-ma': decreased and went away into the earth [Kalimat al-Qur'an]. Ghāḍa al-ma' yaghīḍu ghayḍan: it went away and the earth swallowed it [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
3 - Istawat 'ala al-Judi: settled upon a mountain near Mosul [Kalimat al-Qur'an]. It is said that this was on the day of 'Ashura', and Noah fasted it, together with those who were with him of the beasts and creatures, in thanks to Allah, mighty and majestic [Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari].
4 - Bu'dan: that is, destruction and perdition [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
5 - It is narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by Sa'd while he was performing wudu'. He said: "What is this extravagance?" He said: "Is there extravagance in wudu'?" He said: "Yes, even if you are beside a flowing river." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/221) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (425). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "Its chain is weak, due to the weakness of Hayy ibn 'Abd Allah and Ibn Lahi'a."
6 - Ghāḍa is used intransitively, meaning it is satisfied with its subject and needs no object, as in ghāḍa al-ma' (the water decreased). It is also used transitively, passing from its subject to an object, so one says: aghāḍa Allah mā'ahu [lil-bi'r] or ghāḍahu or ghayyaḍahu.

The compassion of fatherhood stirs in Noah, peace be upon him, and the words of the Truth, glory be to Him, manifest it:

﴿And Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾

The compassion of fatherhood is a praiseworthy compassion, and the Truth, glory be to Him, charges the father's heart with it in proportion to the child's need. Had that compassion not existed, no father or mother would have borne the hardships of raising children.

So that we know that prophets have no offspring except the offspring of following, we find the example in Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, upon him and upon our Prophet be the best of prayers and peace, when the Truth, glory be to Him, said of him:

﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them...﴾ [al-Baqarah]: That is, Abraham, peace be upon him, performed the obligation in its complete form. Just as he wanted to raise the foundations of the House, and he raised them above his stature by means of a stratagem, bringing a stone and standing upon it to raise the wall of the Ka'bah.

Allah, exalted is He, said to him: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people...﴾ [al-Baqarah], because you are trusted with the way of Allah and capable of carrying it out precisely. Abraham, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And from my descendants...﴾ [al-Baqarah].

The Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿"My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Baqarah]. From this we know that prophethood has no lineage of blood; rather, prophethood has followers.

This is also made clear in the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, after the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, had settled in his mind: ﴿"...My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Baqarah].

Abraham said to his Lord, glory be to Him, seeking provision for Makkah and its people: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day..."﴾ [al-Baqarah].

Thus Abraham, peace be upon him, asked for provision for the believers, but the Truth, glory be to Him, explains to him that the matter has been moved from its proper place: provision is a gift of lordship (rubūbiyyah) to the believer and the disbeliever alike, whereas the obligations of divinity (ulūhiyyah) are for the believer only. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿"And whoever disbelieves..."﴾ [al-Baqarah]. That is, provision includes the believer and the disbeliever; it is a gift from lordship.

We want to say that the compassion of fatherhood and motherhood is in inverse proportion to the child's need: if the child is strong, the compassion of fatherhood and motherhood decreases.

An example of this: we find two brothers, one of them wealthy, who attends to the parents and takes care of them, while the other son is poor and cannot care for the parents.

We will observe that the hearts of the father and mother are with the poor one, not with the rich one. The compassion of fatherhood and motherhood is with the weak, the sick, and the absent, and whenever the child is in greater need, the compassion is with him.

In Noah's, peace be upon him, call to his Lord, glory be to Him, we observe that Noah had a justification for requesting the deliverance of his son, because the Truth, glory be to Him, had commanded him to carry into the ship two of every kind, and likewise his family. So Noah, peace be upon him, wished to request deliverance for his son because he was of his family, and he said: ﴿"My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾ [Hud, 45].

So then: Noah, peace be upon him, has the right of supplication, because he asks for the fulfillment of Allah's promise that his family would be with him for deliverance.

When Noah says: ﴿"...and You are the most just of judges"﴾, it is an acknowledgment that Allah, glory be to Him, does not err, because the son drowned; rather, that drowning must have been for a wisdom.

1 - Aḥkam (most just): a superlative form indicating intensification of the attribute, that is, He, glory be to Him and exalted, is the best of judges. And aḥkama al-amr means he perfected it. Allah says: ﴿Then Allah establishes His verses...﴾ [al-Ḥajj, 52], that is, He clarifies them and makes them precise, convincing, and firm. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

2 - Ibtalā (tested): examined and tried. Bi-kalimāt (with words): with commands and prohibitions. Fa-atammahunna (and he fulfilled them): he performed them for Allah completely. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
The words by which Allah tested Abraham, peace be upon him, have been differently identified. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah tested him with the rites (manāsik). And also from him: He tested him with purification: five in the head and five in the body. In the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. In the body: clipping the nails...

3 - ʿAhd (covenant): time, charge, pledge, guarantee, and security. Allah says: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification...﴾ [al-Baqarah, 27]...

Al-Sha'rawi says, may Allah have mercy on him:

Almighty Allah says:

﴿He said: "O Noah, he is not of your family; he is one whose conduct is unrighteous. So do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant."(1) (46)﴾

Almighty Allah here intends to draw the attention of His Prophet Noah to the fact that the family of the prophets is not a family of blood and flesh, but a family of method and following. If Noah, peace be upon him, measured his son by this rule, he would not find him to be his son.

Did not our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say about Salman al-Farisi: "Salman is one of us, the Family of the House"?(2)

So, sonship with regard to the prophets is sonship of following, not sonship of lineage.

Look at the precision of expression in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He is not of your family...﴾ (46) [Hud].

Then He, glory be to Him, gives the cause and the basis for that with His words: ﴿He is one whose conduct is unrighteous...﴾ (46) [Hud].

It is as if sonship here is an action, not an essence. The essence is indefinite here, and what is mentioned is the action. The action of Noah's son made him unfit to be Noah's son.

Thus we find that what is judged regarding sonship of the prophets is not blood, nor fat, nor flesh, but following. This is shown by the fact that Almighty Allah described the son of Noah with His words: ﴿he is one whose conduct is unrighteous﴾, and had he been one of righteous conduct, he would have been his son.

Almighty Allah says:

﴿...So do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant (46)﴾ [Hud]:

Almighty Allah here asks Noah to think carefully before he asks, and there is no fault in the prophets when their Lord trains them.

1 - {Verily he is not of your family...(46)}: i.e., he is not of the people of your guardianship and your religion, nor of those whom I promised you I would save with you. {Verily he is one whose conduct is unrighteous...(46)}: It was said: its meaning is that your asking Me about your son, who opposes you, is an action that is not righteous. ﴿...I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant (46)﴾: in your asking Me about that. [Abridged Tafsir al-Tabari].
Wa'aza yaʿizuhu wa'zan wa'itan (وعظ): he advised him to obey and to do righteous deeds, and guided him to good. Al-mawʿizah (admonition): that with which one is admonished, whether words or deeds. Allah says: ﴿...and an admonition for the God-fearing (66)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Narrated by al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak (3/598) from the hadith of Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani. al-Dhahabi and al-Ajluni said: its chain is weak.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 47:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿He said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers."﴾ (47)

Here Noah (peace be upon him) calls upon his Lord, glorified and exalted is He, to forgive him for what he said. He acknowledges that when he wished to ask for the salvation of his son, he could not restrain his request. But Allah, the Truthful, glorified is He, alone is able to prevent such a request from his heart, and this is the pinnacle of submission to Allah, exalted is He.

Noah's statement (peace be upon him), ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in You...﴾ (47) [Hud], makes clear to us that a person does not seek refuge from something with something unless his own strength is unable to keep him from it.

Therefore Noah (peace be upon him) seeks refuge from asking about that of which he has no knowledge, and hopes for the forgiveness and mercy of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, so that he will not be among the losers.

1 - ʿādha yaʿūdhu ʿawdhan: laadha wa-lajaʾa (he sought refuge and took shelter). Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind"﴾ (al-Nas, 1), meaning: I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, and shelter under His safeguard [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 48:

Then the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him, says:

﴿It was said: "O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations (descended) from those who are with you. And (there will be) nations whom We will provide for, then a painful punishment from Us will touch them."﴾ (48):

The saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him:

﴿Descend with peace from Us... (48)﴾ [Hud]:

It indicates that Noah, peace be upon him, received the command to disembark from the ship in order to undertake his mission of faith in a land that possesses the means of life, after the ship had carried from every pair two, and those believers with him whom God Most High saved, and drowned those whom they had called "the lowly" (ar-arādhil)[3].

The saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him: ﴿nations who are with you... (48)﴾ [Hud]: includes the family (ahl)[4] of Noah, peace be upon him, and those who believed in him, and likewise the nations of wild beasts, birds, animals and cattle.

That is: it is an indication of the core community, which is the community of humankind, and of the communities that serve humankind. Thus the means of life were made available to the believers, and Noah and his people are free for the mission of faith on earth.

The saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him: ﴿Descend(5) with peace from Us... (48)﴾ [Hud]: The intended meaning of peace (salām) is security and tranquility, for there remains among the disbelievers none who would trouble Noah, peace be upon him, in his affair, and he will not find anyone who would vex him with the words: ﴿You have disputed with us and multiplied your disputation... (32)﴾ [Hud], nor will he find anyone who accuses him of fabrication.

And those who remained with Noah were all believers, and they had witnessed that their deliverance from drowning had been accomplished by virtue of the method which Noah conveyed to them from God Most High.

The saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him: {and blessings... (48)} [Hud]: meaning that the Truthful Lord blesses the little so as to make it abundant.

It is said: "This thing is blessed," like the food that a person brings to suffice two, but he is surprised by five guests, so this food suffices all of them.

So then: the blessed thing is the little that performs what much performs, while there is an expectation that it will not suffice.

The word ﴿blessings﴾ should have come here, because what Noah, peace be upon him, carried of every pair of two needs the blessings of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him, in order to multiply and suffice.

The saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him:

﴿...and upon nations from those who are with you, and nations whom We will provide for, then a painful punishment from Us will touch them (48)﴾ [Hud]:

This statement suits human nature. The believers with Noah, peace be upon him, were the elite, but with the passage of time heedlessness came upon some of them, and a generation comes after them that finds no model or exemplar, and then influences surround the following generations and separate them entirely from the method.

On this the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ("A man sleeps a sleep and the trust is taken from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a *waktah*; then he sleeps another sleep and the trust is taken from his heart, and its trace remains like the trace of a *majl*, like a pebble you roll over your foot so that it blisters, and you see it swollen (*munTabiran*), and there is nothing in it. Then he took a pebble and rolled it over his foot. In the morning people trade with one another, and hardly anyone fulfils the trust, until it is said: 'In the tribe of so-and-so there is a trustworthy man,' until it is said of a man: 'How strong he is! How refined he is! How intelligent he is!' and there is not in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith.")[10]

Thus heedlessness comes upon the people of the method. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ("Trials are presented to hearts like a mat, strand by strand. Whichever heart absorbs them, a black spot is marked upon it, and whichever heart rejects them, a white spot is marked upon it, until hearts become of two kinds: one white like smooth stone, which no trial harms as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and the other black and dusky like an inverted pitcher, knowing no good and rejecting no evil except what its desire has soaked up.")[15]

I seek refuge in God, the Exalted, from the onset of the trial of heedlessness upon hearts.

In this verse the Truthful Lord speaks of those who remained with Noah, peace be upon him, and they were an elite of believers, but among them are some upon whom heedlessness will come, and God, glory be to Him and exalted, will also provide them with the enjoyment of worldly life, and He will not withhold it from them, but punishment will overtake them.

When a generation comes upon the heedless, it is subject to two influences:

The first influence: his own heedlessness.

The second influence: the example of the heedless among those who came before him.

We know that among the descendants of Noah, peace be upon him, is the "people of 'Ad," to whom the Truthful Lord sent Hud, peace be upon him, and likewise the "people of Thamud," to whom He sent their brother Salih, peace be upon him, and the people of Lot; all of these had heedlessness settle upon their hearts.

1 - *al-Barakah*: increase of good, growth and happiness. God the Exalted said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn (96)﴾ [al-A'raf] [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/65].
2 - *yamassuhum al-'adhab*: it reaches them and harms them. God the Exalted said: ﴿...And when harm touches him, he is despairing (83)﴾ [al-Isra'], and God the Exalted said: ﴿And do not incline toward those who wronged, lest the Fire touch you... (113)﴾ [Hud]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
3 - *al-Arādhil*: plural of *arhal*, meaning the lowest of people; it is said: the lowest in appearance and condition; it is said: the worst of everything. They regarded them as lowly because they attributed them to their trades, such as weaving and cupping. Said by al-Zajjaj [see: Lisan al-Arab, root r-dh-l].
4 - God the Mighty and Majestic has excepted from them the wife of Noah, of whom the Lord of Might said: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot; they were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against God, and it was said: "Enter the Fire with those who enter."(10)﴾ [al-Tahrim]. Their betrayal of Noah was in matters of faith. Ibn 'Abbas said: Noah's wife did not commit fornication; her betrayal was that she used to tell that he was a madman, and she would inform upon his secret, so when anyone believed with Noah, she informed the tyrants of Noah's people. [See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/393].
5 - *habata yahbituhu habtan*, from the pattern of *daraba*: he descended from a height to a lower place, or went down from a height; in a rare dialect, *habata yahbutu* from the pattern of *qa'ada*, *hubutan*. God the Exalted said: ﴿And among them is that which splits and water flows from it, and among them is that which descends out of fear of God...(74)﴾ [al-Baqarah], as the mountain crumbled when God manifested Himself to it [al-Qamus, adapted].
6 - *al-Waktah*: a slight trace; al-Harawi said so, and others said: it is a slight darkness; it is said: it is a colour that appears, differing from the colour that was before it [Sharh al-Nawawi li-Sahih Muslim, 2/528].
7 - *al-Majl*: that there be water between the skin and the flesh. *al-Majlah* is a thin layer in which water gathers from the trace of work. *Majilat al-yad*: the hand blistered from work, then grew hard and firm, its skin thickened and roughened, and there appeared in it something like a pustule from work with hard, rough objects [Lisan al-Arab, root m-j-l].
8 - *munTabiran*: raised. Everything you raise, you have *nabarta*. *Intabara al-jurh*: the wound rose and swelled. [Lisan al-Arab, root n-b-r]. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim [2/528]: "From it comes *al-minbar*, because of its height and the height of the preacher upon it."
9 - *al-Khardal*: a kind of spice grain, used as a proverb for smallness. God the Exalted said: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or within the earth, God will bring it forth. Indeed, God is Subtle and Acquainted (16)﴾ [Luqman].
10 - Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [7086] and Muslim in his Sahih [143], from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him.
11 - i.e., the love of trials mixed into his heart, as if he had given it to drink. From it is God's saying concerning the Jews: {and they were made to drink the calf into their hearts because of their disbelief...(93)} [al-Baqarah], i.e., the love of worshipping the calf instead of God mixed into their hearts. [See also: Lisan al-Arab, root sh-r-b].
12 - *al-Nakt*: that one strike the ground with a rod and it leaves an impression; i.e., the trial leaves a trace upon the heart. [See: Mukhtar al-Qamus, root n-k-t].
13 - *Murbadan*: black with a dusty tint; the intended meaning is in sense, not in appearance, as mentioned by Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-Arab. *Al-tarabbud*: changing of colour; it is said: when he saw me his colour changed (*tarabbada*), i.e., you see him red at one time, green at another, yellow at another [al-Lisan].
14 - *al-Kawz al-mujakhkhi*: i.e., the leaning pitcher that is tipped and pours out what is in it. Here *al-mujakhkhi* is the one that deviates from uprightness and moderation, so the heart that understands no good is likened to a leaning pitcher in which nothing remains, because when a pitcher leans, what is in it pours out [al-Lisan, root j-kh-y].
15 - Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/386, 405) and Muslim in his Sahih (104), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.
16 - *ran al-shay' rayna*: it became rusty, derived from *al-sada'*, the rust that covers a sword and takes away its polish; it is borrowed for the veil that covers the heart because of sins. *Ran al-sada' 'alayhi*: it prevailed over it and covered it entirely. God the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, rather, what they used to earn has rusted upon their hearts (14)﴾ [al-Mutaffifin], i.e., the veil of sins covered their hearts [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 49:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says:

﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this. So be patient; indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous.(49)﴾

The word "tilka" (that) is a demonstrative and an address, and the one addressed is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The "ta'" (in tilka) refers to the ship and what followed it of the news of the unseen. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not a contemporary of these events, and he did not know them himself, nor did anyone among his people know them.

And you, O Messenger of Allah, it was not known of you that you sat with a teacher (mu'allim)(1), nor was it reported of you that you read in a book. That is why the Qur'an says: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Moses...(44)﴾ [al-Qasas].

And it came: ﴿...And you were not with them when they cast their pens (aqlam)(3) to see which of them would take charge (yakfulu)(4) of Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed(44)﴾ [Ali 'Imran].

So then: since you, O Muhammad, did not read and did not learn from a teacher, from whom did you learn? It was none other than Allah, glorified is He, who taught you.

It is as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, taught His Messenger (ﷺ) the story of Nuh (peace be upon him), intending by it to provide an example and a lesson for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that he would be certain that every messenger carries out his faithful, methodical movement under the watchful eye of Allah, and that He, glorified is He, will never hand him over to his adversaries or enemies.

Therefore the noble statement comes: ﴿So be patient﴾, because you have now come to know the outcome of the patience of Nuh (peace be upon him), who persisted for a thousand years less fifty. Then comes His statement, glorified is He: ﴿...indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous(49)﴾ [Hud].

1 - The idolaters of Quraysh tried to discredit the claim that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah. Concerning them He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue(103)﴾ [al-Nahl]. So they accused him of learning from a foreign Christian youth, who was a seller who sold near al-Safa. Ibn Kathir says in his tafsir (2/586): "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with him and speak with him somewhat, and that man was foreign-tongued and did not know Arabic, or he knew only a little, enough to answer the address in what was necessary."
2 - ﴿And you were not﴾: an address from Allah, the Exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). [On the western side]: that is, on the side of the mountain, the valley, or the western place relative to Moses at the time of the communion. ﴿When We decreed the command to Moses(44)﴾ [al-Qasas]: that is, We revealed to Moses (peace be upon him) the command to deliver the message to Pharaoh and his people. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, and Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari], with adaptation.
3 - "Al-aqlam" here is the plural of "qalam," meaning an arrow or a piece of wood resembling it, on which a sign indicating an amount is written, given to whoever comes out with his name. They used it in gambling, which Islam prohibited, and they also used it in casting lots. Among its use in casting lots is His statement, glorified is He: ﴿When they cast their pens to see which of them would take charge of Maryam...(44)﴾ [Ali 'Imran]. So "al-aqlam" here means the lottery arrows; the lot was drawn and the arrow of Zakariyya (peace be upon him) won, so he took charge of Maryam. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
4 - Kafala, yakfulu, kafalan wa kafala: to undertake the nurturing and care of the one he sponsors. His statement, glorified is He: [yakfulu Maryam]: that is, he cares for her and raises her. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her...(37)﴾ [Ali 'Imran], that is, He made him her guardian (kafil). [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 50:

After the story of Noah comes the story of the people of ʿAd, and we know that Allah, glory be to Him, does not send a messenger except when corruption has become widespread.

So, heedlessness set in after Noah, and the imitation of children of their fathers was added to it, so the method (manhaj) was effaced, and it became difficult for those present to establish it.

Allah, glory be to Him, does not send new messengers except when there is no one left in the nation who raises the word of Allah. For we know that faith-based immunity (al-mana'a al-imaniyya) in the human soul may be a self-immunity, meaning that a person may be tempted by his soul to deviate from the method of Allah, but the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama) restrains him and returns him to faith.

But if his self becomes hardened and there is no self-reproaching soul in him, self-immunity disappears, though the surrounding society may then rebuke him.

But if self-immunity disappears, and immunity from society, then the Lord of Might, glory be to Him, must send a new messenger, a new clear sign, and a new proof.

This is what happened after Noah, peace be upon him.

Therefore comes the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And to ʿAd (1) their brother Hud. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. You are but inventors of falsehood (2).﴾ (50)

Allah, glory be to Him, opens the verse by endearing them to him and making them comfortable with the one sent to them: He tells them that he is their brother, and a brother cannot want hardship for them; rather, he is a sincere adviser, trusted by them and regarding what he conveys to them.

When he says to them, ﴿O my people...﴾ (50) [Hud], this is also for making them feel at ease.

Then he calls them to worship Allah alone, because they had taken other than Allah as a god, and this is the peak of fabrication.

Allah, glory be to Him, only said ﴿...you are but inventors of falsehood﴾ (50) [Hud] because corruption had overwhelmed (3) [everything].

1 - Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/224): "These are the first ʿAd whom Allah mentioned, the children of ʿAd ibn Iram, whose dwellings were in Yemen, in al-Ahqaf, which are sand dunes." Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3369): "It is said there were two ʿAds: the first ʿAd and the second ʿAd. These are the first, and the second is Shaddad and Luqman, mentioned in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Iram, of the pillars (7)﴾ [al-Fajr]."

2 - In ﴿...in antum illa muftarun (50)﴾ [Hud], the word "in" here is negating, with the meaning of "ma" (not), i.e., "you are nothing but inventors of falsehood."

3 - Something that increases until it rises above is called "qad tamma" (it has overflowed). It is said: "tamma al-ma'" when the water increases. Tamma means: it overwhelmed; for this reason the Day of Resurrection is called: ﴿Then when the Greatest Overwhelming (34) comes﴾ [al-Nazi'at]. [See: Lisan al-Arab, and al-Qamus al-Qawim.]

Then He, glorified is He, says, after that, what came on the tongue of Hud:

﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it(1). My reward is only from the One who originated me(2). Will you not then reason?﴾ (11:51)

It is as if Hud (peace be upon him) were saying to them: What is it that burdens you in what I command you and call you to? I present to you this message from Allah, the Exalted, and I do not ask you for any reward for it. It is not reasonable that I should move you away from what you are accustomed to and then take from you money in return for that. Nor can I impose on you the hardship of abandoning what you have become used to, and likewise the wage for that call.

Since I will not take any reward from you, then there is no burden I impose on you by it, just as I am free of need for that reward, because my reward is with the One who sent me.

﴿... My reward is only from the One who originated me(3). Will you not then reason? (11:51)﴾: That is, my reward is from the One who created me, prepared for this mission, because fitrah (fitrah: the basic natural constitution of a human being) means the fundamental formation of the human being.

Allah, the Exalted, has prepared Hud (peace be upon him) to be a messenger, and we also know that a reward is usually given in return for a benefit.

We have previously given the example of someone who buys a house: he pays the price of the house to its owner, and this transaction is called sale and purchase.

As for when a person rents a house, he pays rent in return for the benefit of living in it.

The statement of Hud (peace be upon him): ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it... (11:51)﴾ indicates that it was obligatory for them to pay a great reward in return for the benefit of what he called them to; because the reward you pay for the public services available to you is only in return for temporary benefits, but what Hud (peace be upon him) offers them is a benefit that is not temporary!

Therefore Hud (peace be upon him) left the reward to the one who is able to give it, namely Allah, the Exalted. He is the One who is capable of everything.

We have already explained that all the messengers came with this phrase(4): ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it... (11:51)﴾, except Abraham and Moses (peace be upon them both). Our master Abraham did not say it because of his father, and our master Moses did not say it(5) because Pharaoh said to him: ﴿Did we not raise you among us as a child... (26:18)﴾. So: it was incumbent upon the people of Hud to reflect on the great benefit, which is the messenger's method that Hud (peace be upon him) brought.

1 - The word [in] in this noble verse is a negation meaning [ma] (not); i.e., "my reward is not but from the One who originated me," or "is not my reward but from the One who originated me," and He is Allah, the Exalted. Ajara fulan falanan (from the patterns daraba and nasara) ajran: he rewarded him for a deed, or he became his hired worker; and with both meanings His saying is explained: ﴿on condition that you hire me for eight years...(28:27)﴾ [al-Qasas]. The dowry is called ajr (wage) metaphorically—He says: ﴿So give them their wages...(65:6)﴾ [al-Talaq], meaning their dowries—and His saying: ﴿then for him is his reward with his Lord...(2:112)﴾ [al-Baqarah], meaning his reward [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

2 - Fatara Allah al-khalq: He created them and originated them; so He is Fatir. He says: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth...(6:14)﴾ [al-An'am], meaning: their Creator. And His saying: ﴿He originated you the first time...(17:51)﴾ [al-Isra'], meaning: He created you the first time in this world. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

3 - Fatara Allah al-khalq, like nasara: He created them and originated them, so He is Fatir. He says: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth...(6:14)﴾ [al-An'am], its Creator. Fatara al-shay' means he split it, fatran; its plural is futur, and the noun is fitrah. He says: ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind...(30:30)﴾ [al-Rum] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged].

4 - Noah (peace be upon him) said it: [Surah Yunus, verse 72], [Surah Hud, verse 29], [al-Shu'ara' verse 109]. Hud (peace be upon him) said it: [Hud: 51], [al-Shu'ara': 127]. Salih (peace be upon him) said it to his people Thamud: [al-Shu'ara': 145]. Lut (peace be upon him) said it: [al-Shu'ara': 164]. Shu'ayb said it: [al-Shu'ara': 180].

5 - This is because Pharaoh reproached Moses (peace be upon him) with this when he asked for the departure of the Children of Israel with him. Pharaoh said: ﴿...Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life? (26:18) And you did your deed that you did, and you were among the disbelievers (26:19)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. So it was not possible for Moses, after this, to say what his brothers the messengers said.

Then the Exalted says, relating what Hud (peace be upon him) said to his people, addressing them:

﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain, and add strength to your strength. And do not turn away as criminals (52).﴾

Thus we know that seeking forgiveness (istighfar) is an acknowledgment of shortcoming and of having committed sins, so we say: "O Lord, forgive us."

When you ask Allah the Exalted for forgiveness, this is a declaration from you of faith, and an acknowledgment that the obligation Allah has placed upon you is a true obligation.

As long as a person has asked Allah the Exalted to forgive him for the sins that have passed, he must not commit new sins, and after repentance the servant must be keen to avoid acts of disobedience.

A person must remember that whatever blessing he has is from Allah, and that the created things that have been subjected (to us) are subjected by the command of Allah the Exalted; the routine of life should not make you forget the One who causes it and the Bestower of all blessings.

When the Truth, glorified is He, sends a messenger, the first thing the messenger brings to the nation is to correct the creed at its summit, and to call them to belief in one God, from whom they receive "do" and "do not do."

Here the speech is from Hud (peace be upon him) to his people, the people of 'Ad, and the call to believe in one God, worship Him, and adopt His method cannot be confined to rituals alone, such as testifying to the Oneness of Allah, prayer, fasting, zakat, and hajj.

Rather, worshipping Allah the Exalted means performing the rites and acts of worship, and perfecting every deed in the light of Allah's method, so you do not isolate religion from the movement of life.

As for those who fear the entry of Islam into the movement of life, they want us to limit religion to rituals. We say to them: when Islam entered the movement of life, it conquered the whole world, and it fought two ancient civilizations: the civilization of the Persians in the East and the civilization of the Romans in the West.

These were nations with ancient and powerful civilizations, cultures and laws. Nevertheless, a people of Bedouin unlettered folk came, led in their creed by an unlettered man sent by Allah the Exalted, and he overthrew all of them: their systems, their cultures, and their advancement of life to the level of the aspirations of minds.

These people, then, want to confine Islam to the five pillars alone, so as to isolate it from the movement of life.

We say to them: No, you cannot restrict worship to the five pillars alone, because worship means that there is a worshipper of a true object of worship, and that the worshipper obeys the commands of the one worshipped; and the commands of the one worshipped are embodied in "do" and "do not do." What has no "do" or "do not do" attached to it is permissible: if you wish, you do it, and if you wish, you do not do it, and doing or not doing it does not corrupt the universe.

So, worship is every command issued by Allah the Exalted. Do not confine it to rituals, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us and made clear to us that the five pillars of Islam are those upon which Islam is built, and they are not the whole of Islam.

So, Islam is a structure that stands on pillars; therefore we cannot confine Islam to its pillars alone. Islam is every movement in life, and human movements must be regulated according to the method of Allah, so that life is regulated just as the universe around us is regulated.

Worship encompasses every movement in life. Some have mistakenly understood that worship is confined to the section of acts of worship in the jurists' division, and have overlooked that the section of transactions is also part of worship. The uprightness of people in their transactions leads to the regulation of people's lives. In the noble verse about which we are sharing our reflections, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord...(52)﴾ [Hud]. Seeking forgiveness (istighfar) is only for sins that have already occurred. If this is the first thing Hud (peace be upon him) said to his people, then the seeking of forgiveness here is for the sins they committed in opposition to the method of the messenger who came before him, or the sins they committed by their natural disposition.

Then he calls them with His words: ﴿Then turn to Him in repentance...(52)﴾ [Hud]. Repentance requires the resolve not to initiate new sins.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says in the same verse:

﴿He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain and add strength to your strength...(52)﴾ [Hud]:

One might ask: what is the connection of seeking forgiveness to this cosmic matter?

We say: the universe has an owner of everything in it, its inanimate matter, its plants and its animals; He, glorified is He, is capable, and no creature can disobey Him in any command; He is able to take things out of their nature. If a cloud comes that you think will rain, Allah the Exalted may command it, and it will not rain.

Just as He said, glorified is He, in another place in His Noble Book:

﴿So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is what you were impatient for: a wind wherein is a painful punishment (24).﴾ [Al-Ahqaf]: So do not take causes as mere routine; rather, the Lord of causes owns them, and if He wills, He does what He wills.

When you worship Allah the Exalted with the worship that regulates every movement in life, you turn to the cultivation of the earth and secure your sustenance by extracting it through the causes that Allah the Exalted has buried in the earth.

Sustenance, as we know, is of the same kind as the earth, so we must cultivate the earth; the seeds send their humble roots, glorifying and prostrating to Allah the Exalted; then Allah the Truth sends rain from the sky, the seeds take their need of water that seeps to them through the earth, and we too take our need of this water.

The sky is everything that rises above you and shades you; as for the highest heaven, that is another subject, and all things are beneath it.

Consider the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Whoever thought that Allah would not give victory to His messenger in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch a rope to the sky and then cut it off, and see whether his scheming removes what enrages him (15).﴾ [Al-Hajj]: That is, whoever thought that Allah the Exalted would not help His messenger, let him bring a rope or anything, tie it to what is above him, and hang himself by it; he will die, and his rage will not leave him.

﴿And He sends down the sky upon you in abundant rain... (52)﴾ [Hud]: Midrar (abundant) is one that pours forth in succession without harm, because rain may fall in a harmful excess, as Allah opened the gates of the sky with pouring water.

So, midrar is rain that follows in succession in a beneficial way, not a destructive one.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say when rain fell: "O Allah, around us and not upon us."

When rain is sent abundantly, in succession, beneficially, the earth turns green, the world flourishes, and we are increased in strength upon our strength.

As for one who turns away, he commits a crime against himself, because the criminality of a servant returns only upon himself; so do not think that my sin, as any servant by disobedience, harms others.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...But people wrong only themselves (44).﴾ [Yunus]

1 - Midrar: an intensive form, meaning abundant, copious, and successive. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We sent down upon them the sky in abundant rain...(6)﴾ [Al-An'am], meaning it pours upon them heavy rain. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim] The word "midrar" occurs in the Qur'an three times: in verse 6 of Surah al-An'am, in verse 52 of Surah Hud, and in verse 11 of Surah Nuh.
2 - Routine of life: its movement according to one unchanging system, which does not deviate, so that it appears to you to move by itself and of its own essence, and you forget its mover and its causer. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan [entry: r-t-b]: "al-rahib: the constant, enduring thing, and al-rutab: the established, abiding thing."
3 - He is the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), and the unlettered status (ummiyya) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a matter emphasized by the Lord of Glory in the Qur'an, when He said: ﴿Those who follow the messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel...(157)﴾ [Al-A'raf].
"Ummi" is related to "umm" (mother), as if he remains in the state in which he was born, created with the nature of Allah, receiving from Him by inspiration and revelation, so he does not speak from desire: ﴿It is not but a revelation revealed (4)﴾ [An-Najm]. This description is one of the special characteristics of the Prophet, and it is an honor for him, because if he was unlettered and Allah sent down to him the inimitable Book, there is no doubt that it is from Allah, and his unlettered state is evidence that his knowledge is from Allah directly, not from humans; and had he not been unlettered, it would have been said that he read and transmitted from others. ["From the sayings of Shaykh al-Sha'rawi" m. s.]
4 - On the authority of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, paying zakat, hajj, and fasting in Ramadan." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [8] and Muslim in his Sahih [16].
5 - Ghafara al-dhanb (yaghfiruhu, like daraba) ghafran and maghfiratan: he covered it, pardoned it, and did not punish its doer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will forgive you your errors...(58)﴾ [Al-Baqarah]. Al-ghafir is an active participle; ghafur and ghaffar are intensive forms, and all of them are among the Beautiful Names of Allah; ghufran is a verbal noun, and maghfira is a noun of place/manner. Istaghfara means he sought forgiveness for himself, as Allah said: ﴿And the Messenger asked forgiveness for them...(64)﴾ [An-Nisa'], meaning he asked Allah to forgive them. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged].
6 - That is, when they saw the punishment approaching them, they thought it was a cloud bringing rain, so they rejoiced and were glad, though they had been in drought and in need of rain. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/160].
7 - Because they said to their messenger Hud (peace be upon him): ﴿...Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful (22).﴾ [Al-Ahqaf].
8 - Qut: food that preserves the body's life; its plural is "aqwat." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He measured therein its sustenance in four days...(10)﴾ [Fussilat], meaning the sustenance of all the inhabitants of the earth, human and animal and every living thing, until the end of time. "Aqata" a plant or animal: he supplied it with its strength that preserves its life. "Aqata 'alayhi": he preserved him and preserved his survival. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿...And Allah is ever over all things Maqit (85)﴾ [An-Nisa'], meaning dominant and capable, or a guardian preserving his life. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
9 - Tamara: buried it, deposited it, and hid it in the depths of the earth. Al-matmura: a hidden pit under the earth, or a place under the earth prepared secretly where food and wealth are stored, i.e., hidden. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: t-m-r].
10 - Al-Zajjaj said: "al-sama'" in language: it is said of everything that is raised and elevated: "qad sama yasmu." Every ceiling is a sama'. "Al-sama'": everything that rises above you and shades you, and from this the roof of a house is called sama'. [Lisan, entry: s-m-w].
11 - Related by Muslim in his Sahih (897), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (933), on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: People were struck by drought in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). While the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the Friday sermon, a Bedouin stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, property has perished and dependents are hungry, so pray to Allah for us." He raised his hands, and we did not see a cloud in the sky. By Him in whose hand is my soul, he did not lower them until clouds rose like mountains. Then he did not descend from his pulpit until I saw the rain pouring down on his beard (ﷺ). We were rained upon that day, and the next day, and the day after, and the one following, until the next Friday. That Bedouin stood again and said: "O Messenger of Allah, buildings have collapsed and property has drowned; so pray to Allah for us." He raised his hands and said: "O Allah, around us and not upon us."
12 - Yatawalla: turns away. Al-tawalli: turning away and retreating. From it is His saying: ﴿Whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient (82).﴾ [Al 'Imran].
13 - And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise (111).﴾ [An-Nisa'] Ithm is sin, and its consequence returns only upon himself.

Then, after that, the Truth (Allah, glory be to Him) brings the reply given by the people of ʿAd:

﴿They said: "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof (1), and we will not abandon our gods on your word, nor will we believe you." (53)﴾

Here they deny that Hud came to them with any proof (bayyinah) or miracle.

The bayyinah, as we know, is the sign that indicates the truthfulness of the Messenger.

It is true that Hud did not mention his miracle; but they overlooked that the essence of any miracle is the challenge. The miracle of Noah, peace be upon him, was the flood, and the miracle of Abraham, peace be upon him, was that the fire became coolness (2) and safety for him when they threw him into it.

We observe that the general miracle of every Messenger is represented by the words of Noah, peace be upon him:

﴿"O my people, if my standing (3) among you and my reminding you of the signs of Allah is grievous to you, then in Allah I have put my trust. So resolve upon your affair, you and your partners, then let not your affair be obscure (4) to you; then carry it out against me and give me no respite." (71)﴾ [Yunus]. That is: if you are fit for the challenge, here I am before you, fighting corruption, while you are people of domination, strength, tyranny and oppression.

Plot your scheme, but you will never be able to kill the divine method, because no one can extinguish the light of Allah in the hand of one of His messengers, nor can they rid the world of him by killing him... This never happened.

Thus: the proof (bayyinah) (5) that Hud, peace be upon him, brought was that he stood before them and called them to abandon disbelief; and this is a challenge to those capable of it, since they were people of tyranny and brutality; yet they were unable to do it, just as the disbelievers of Quraysh were unable to do it against our Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

We know that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, came with the all-encompassing miracle, which is the Noble Qur'an; and the Qur'an will remain a miracle until the Hour comes.

We know that the majority of the Messengers, peace be upon them all, came with sensory, cosmic miracles whose time ended with their occurrence; and were it not for the Qur'an informing us of them, we would not have believed them, their likeness being that of a match that flares once and then goes out.

For example, Jesus, peace be upon him, healed the blind from birth (6) and the leper (7), by the permission of his Lord; whoever saw him believed in him, and whoever did not see him may not believe. Likewise Moses, peace be upon him, struck the sea with his staff and it split before him; whoever saw it believed in him, and those miracles ended. But the Noble Qur'an remains until the Hour comes.

Any individual of the Ummah of Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, before the Hour comes, can say: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and his miracle is the Qur'an; because Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, came as a universal Messenger, and there is no messenger after him; therefore his miracle had to be of the enduring kind. Nevertheless they said to him:

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth (8) (90), or you have a garden of palms and grapes, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly (91), or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces (9) as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group (10) (92)." [al-Isra']﴾. All that they asked for were sensory matters; therefore the reply comes: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them...﴾ (51) [al-ʿAnkabut].

Yet they denied.

And the people of ʿAd added: ﴿"...and we will not abandon our gods on your word, nor will we believe you." (53)﴾ [Hud].

They, then, deceived themselves by calling those idols "gods"; for the god (ilah) is the one who sends down a method through which it is determined how he is to be worshipped; and the idols did not speak to them, nor did they convey to them any method.

Thus: logical reasoning (al-qiyas al-mantiqi) cancels the conception of those idols as gods. So why did they worship them? They worshipped them because human nature (fitrah) calls every person to have a power to which he devotes worship; and if that power has commands that restrict the desires of the soul, those commands may be difficult for the soul; but if those gods have no commands or prohibitions, then these are comfortable gods for whoever deceives himself with them, worshipping them presuming that they benefit or harm.

This is the argument of every claim to prophethood or claim to being the Mahdi in this age: the false prophet claims prophethood, calls to mixing with women, drinking wine, and committing destructive sins (12), and calls that a religion.

You find such claims in the Baha'iyya (13) and the Qadiyaniyya (14), and other false beliefs.

Their words: ﴿"...and we will not abandon our gods on your word..." (53)﴾ [Hud]: meaning: we will not abandon our gods because of your saying.

Their words: ﴿"...nor will we believe you." (53)﴾ [Hud]: that is: nor will we accept you as truthful, because [āmana] has several meanings (15).

If it is transitive by itself, as in the saying of the Truth (Allah, glory be to Him): ﴿"...and He has made them secure from fear" (4)﴾ [Quraysh].

If it is transitive by the particle [bi] (with), as in the saying of the Truth: ﴿"And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds, for them is their reward..." (62)﴾ [al-Baqarah]: the meaning then relates to belief in divinity.

If it is transitive by the particle [li] (for), as in the saying of the Truth: ﴿"But none believed in Moses except some of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs that he would persecute them..." (83)﴾ [Yunus]: it carries the meaning of affirmation (taṣdiq).

1 - bayyinah: that is, a clear proof, evidence and argument that is free of doubt. Allah says: ﴿How many clear signs (ayah bayyinah) We have given them...(211)﴾ [al-Baqarah], and He says: ﴿...until there comes to them a clear proof (1)﴾ [al-Bayyinah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
2 - al-bard: the opposite of heat. Some scholars said: Allah placed in the fire coolness that removes its heat, and heat that removes its coolness, so it became safety for him. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: Had He not said "coolness and safety," its coolness would have been harsher on him than its heat; and had He not said "upon Abraham," its coolness would have remained forever. See Tafsir al-Qurtubi (6/4482).
3 - maqami (with a dammah on the mim): that is, for my residing among you. From it is His saying: ﴿And when a group of them said: "O people of Yathrib, there is no place (muqam) for you, so return..."(13)﴾ [al-Ahzab], meaning there is no residence for you. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir.
4 - al-ghummah: the confusion of a matter and its lack of clarity. Allah says: ﴿And We shaded you with the clouds (57)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
5 - abana al-shay' yubayyinu bayanan: it appeared and became clear, so it is bayyin; and it is bayyinah, meaning manifest; the words bayn and bayyinah are used in the sense of the manifest and the making clear, and by both meanings the verse ﴿How many clear signs We have given them...(211)﴾ [al-Baqarah] is interpreted, meaning clear, free of doubt; and bayyinah means proof and argument. Allah says: ﴿...until there comes to them a clear proof (1), a Messenger from Allah...(2)﴾ [al-Bayyinah]. Tabayyana al-amr: it became clear and manifest. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
6 - kamaha yakmahu kamhan, so he is akmah: he was born blind, or he lost his sight, so he is akmah. Allah says: ﴿And I heal the blind from birth and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission...(49)﴾ [Al ʿImran]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
7 - al-abras: one afflicted with the disease of leprosy (baras), a skin disease that produces white patches on the skin that disfigure it, and it is among the symptoms of leprosy (judham). Allah says: ﴿And you heal the blind from birth and the leper by My permission...(110)﴾ [al-Ma'idah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
8 - nabaʿa al-ma': came out of the spring. Al-yanbuʿ: a spring from which water flows abundantly and easily; plural: yanabiʿ. Allah says: ﴿And He threads them as springs in the earth...(21)﴾ [al-Zumar]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
9 - kisafan: pieces. Al-kisfah: a piece. Allah says: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling...(44)﴾ [al-Tur]. And He says: ﴿If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them or drop upon them pieces from the sky...(9)﴾ [Saba']. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
10 - al-qabil: a group, a clan, or supporting helpers. Allah says: ﴿...or you bring Allah and the angels as a group (qabilan) (92)﴾ [al-Isra'], i.e., with you to support you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
11 - This refers to those who claim to be the awaited Mahdi, mentioned in narrations transmitted by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, that he will come at the end of time and be contemporary with the descent of Jesus son of Mary.
12 - al-mubiqat: the destructive things. Awbaqahu: he destroyed him. Allah says: ﴿...and We made between them a destructive barrier (mawbiqan) (52)﴾ [al-Kahf], meaning: We made their mutual connection in this world a destruction for them in the Hereafter. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root: w-b-q].
13 - al-Baha'iyya: a sect with corrupt beliefs, attributed to "Mirza Husayn ʿAli al-Mazandarani," raised in Tehran, born in 1233 AH; his ideas are a mixture of Buddhism, Mazdakism, Judaism, Islam and Christianity. See: Haqiqat al-Babiyya wa al-Baha'iyya, Dr. Mohsen Abdul Hamid, 1985.
14 - al-Qadiyaniyya: attributed to Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian in the Lahore district of the Punjab region between Pakistan and India, born in 1252 AH, who claimed prophethood. [al-Qadiyaniyya, Nash'atuha wa Tatawwuruha, Dr. Hasan ʿIsa, Dar al-Qalam/Kuwait, 1981].
15 - amana yaʾmanu: he became tranquil and was not afraid; amina minhu: he was safe from him; amina ʿala kadha: he felt assured of it and trusted it, as in His saying: ﴿He said: "Shall I entrust you with him except as I entrusted you with his brother before?..."(64)﴾ [Yusuf]. Amina (active participle): ﴿My Lord, make this city secure...(35)﴾ [Ibrahim], meaning: whoever enters it is safe. Amannahu min khawf: He made him secure, not fearful; and the meanings of the root all return to trust and tranquility. Allah says: ﴿...and He made them secure from fear (4)﴾ [Quraysh], meaning He made them secure and unafraid, since they are neighbors of the Sacred Sanctuary in a secure land. The Mu'min is among the Beautiful Names of Allah, meaning the Giver of security and the One who instills tranquility in the hearts of believers; there is no fear for one who seeks refuge in Him, glory be to Him. Allah says: ﴿The Giver of Security, the Guardian...(23)﴾ [al-Hashr]. Amana lahu: he submitted and yielded out of trust, love and esteem. Allah says: ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut]. Amana bihi: he affirmed it and trusted it from conviction. Allah says: ﴿Indeed I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me (25)﴾ [Ya Sin]. Al-iman: submission and affirmation. Allah says: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith...(158)﴾ [al-An'am]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿They said: "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil." He said: "I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness, that I am free from what you associate."﴾ (54)

The "in" (إن) with which this noble verse begins is a conditional particle (adat shart). After the conditional "in" there normally comes a conditional clause and a response clause. If it is not so, then it carries the sense of negation, as in the words of Allah the Almighty: ﴿Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them...﴾ (58:2) [al-Mujadila].

Here Allah the Almighty says: ﴿They said, "We only say that some of our gods have struck you..." (11:54) [Hud]. That is: "We say nothing except that some of our gods have struck you."

Thus we know that the word "in" here has come in the sense of negation.

And "illa" (إلا) is a particle of exception (adat istithna'), and before it is a verb, which is "naqul" (نقول). When an exception particle is present and the excepted-from element (al-mustathna minhu) is not mentioned explicitly, know that it is one of three things: either it is the verbal noun (masdar) of the verb, or it is the adverb of time or place (zarf) of the verb, or it is the circumstantial state (hal) of the verb.

Accordingly, the meaning of the noble verse is: "And we do not say to you except that our gods have struck you with evil, because you have insulted them and nullified their divinity, and you have come with a new god of your own; so the gods have struck you with evil, meaning madness, and you have begun to talk in confusion, in speech that has no meaning."

Hud, peace be upon him, responds to them with what came in the same verse: ﴿...He said: "I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness, that I am free from what you associate."﴾ (11:54) [Hud]. He calls Allah to witness, the One whom he trusts has sent him, and he protects his own self and his own intellect, because the intellect of the Messenger is what directs the manner of conveying the message from Allah.

And Allah the Almighty and Exalted cannot send a messenger and then not protect him.

The disbelievers also said about our master, the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), that he was mad; so Allah the Almighty revealed His noble saying: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ (68:2-4) [al-Qalam]. We know that a madman has no moral character, and in this is a clarification that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is at the peak of intellect, because he is at the peak of good character.

Here Hud, peace be upon him, calls his people to witness and demands that they return to sound human nature and judge whether he is mad or not, and he also makes them witness that he is free from those gods which they associate in worship with Allah the Exalted.

1 - ʿaraha yaʿruhu: he was afflicted by or overcame him and struck him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They said, "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil..."﴾ (11:54), meaning: has struck you. Al-Farra' said: They had denied him, meaning Hud, peace be upon him, and then made him deranged, and they claimed that their gods had unhinged him because of his insulting them. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is: We say nothing except that some of our idols have seized you with madness because of your reviling them. [Lisan al-'Arab; al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Grammarians call this type of exception construction "al-istithna' al-mufarragh" (the emptied exception), which is when the excepted-from element is omitted and the sentence is non-affirmative [i.e., negated], such as: ma takallama illa wahid (no one spoke except one). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They say not, but we think a thought...﴾ (45:32) [al-Jathiya], meaning: we do not think except a great thought. See the detailed explanation of this in al-Nahw al-Wafi [2/317-337].
3 - His call for witness here is not because they are people fit to bear witness, but the meaning is: "I call you to witness" as a final affirmation, that is, so that you may know that I am free from the worship of the idols which you worship. See the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi [4/3370].
4 - "Ghayr mamnun": meaning, not cut off, but lasting; and it may mean not spoiled by reproach, taunting, or boasting about it. The two meanings do not conflict [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/240].

Then the Exalted Lord says what was spoken on the tongue of Hud, peace be upon him:

﴿Then scheme against me, all of you together, and give me no respite.﴾ (55)

As for His saying ﴿from besides Him﴾, it means: besides Allah. They worshipped idols besides Allah, the Glorified. Hud's demand of them was that they scheme against him all together, and they were a tyrannical multitude while he was a single individual. Even if a tyrannical multitude is arrayed against one man, it is expected that they would overcome him. Yet he, peace be upon him, here challenges them and asks them to employ all their cunning and plotting, and to kill him if they are able. This is the pinnacle of challenge.

This challenge is itself a miracle, because at the moment he challenges them, he knows that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, will grant him victory. He, peace be upon him, is certain of his saying ﴿I call Allah to witness...﴾ (54) [Hud], which he said in the previous verse. A person cannot hurl such a challenge recklessly, for a person does not gamble his life on a word.

He would not have said ﴿Then scheme against me, all of you together, and give me no respite﴾ (55) unless he had taken refuge in a mighty support, and he spoke the word out of faith that Allah, the Glorified, would grant him the power for his word to take effect.

He called Allah the Exalted to witness, and Allah, the Glorified, is the first to bear witness for Himself. The Lord, the Glorified, says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him...﴾ (18) [Aal Imran].

Likewise the angels and the people of knowledge bore witness, and when Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, bears witness for Himself, it assures us that when He decrees a matter, He knows it will certainly be carried out.

Hud, peace be upon him, called his Lord, the Glorified, to witness, while he was confident of His protection for him. Allah, the Glorified, would not send a messenger and then enable a people to remove him from the movement of the message.

1 - "Kāna fulānan kaydahu kaydan": he deceived him, plotted against him, and schemed to inflict harm upon him. Scheming (kayd) from Allah, the Exalted, is the nullifying of the schemes of the disbelievers and punishing them for what they have plotted. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, they are scheming a scheme. And I am scheming a scheme﴾ (15-16) [At-Tariq]. Kayd is a verbal noun and is also applied to the action or means by which the schemer resorts to a stratagem. The Lord says: ﴿So gather your scheme, then come in rows...﴾ (64) [Ta-Ha] [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

2 - The Lord of Might, the Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and the people of knowledge, standing in justice...﴾ (18) [Aal Imran].

Then the Exalted Lord says, relating what was said by the tongue of Hud (peace be upon him):

﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He takes it by its forelock.¹ Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.² (56)﴾

Hud (peace be upon him) declares to them the truth that he relies upon Allah, the Exalted, who is not only above them, and not only the Provider for them, but is the One who takes by the forelock every creature (dābba) that crawls upon the earth and has freedom and movement. The nāṣiya (forelock) is the front part of the head, and on it is a tuft of hair.

When you want to humiliate someone, you seize him by this tuft of hair and pull him by it.

And the Almighty says: ﴿The criminals will be recognized by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet (41)﴾ [al-Rahman].

And in another verse Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock (15)﴾ [al-ʿAlaq].

So how is it that the people of ʿĀd did not dare to set upon Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) a group of snakes, or numbers of savage dogs, for example?

They were unable to do so, and he had declared to them the reason for their inability to harm him when he said to them:

﴿... There is no creature but that He takes it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path (56)﴾ [Hud].

We notice that he (peace be upon him) said at the beginning of the verse: ﴿my Lord and your Lord... (56)﴾, and at the end of the verse he said: ﴿... Indeed, my Lord (56)﴾. The reason for his saying ﴿my Lord and your Lord...(56)﴾ is that they were disparaging the matter of the Lordship (rubūbiyya) of the Exalted Lord.

Therefore he (peace be upon him) said, in the context of control, ﴿my Lord and your Lord﴾, whereas at the end of the verse he said:

﴿... Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path (56)﴾ [Hud]: meaning that the one God, the Exalted, possesses absolute justice. He did not mention here anything specific to their lords, because here he is speaking of the absolute justice of the Exalted Lord.

The Exalted Lord is on a straight path in the utmost of His power, subjugation and control, and nothing escapes Him. And with all of Allah's boundless power, He does not use His subjugation for oppression.

**Notes:**

1. **al-Dābba (dābba):** an active participle, predominantly used for non-rational beings; it applies equally to masculine and feminine, and may include the rational and others. Examples: ﴿And He spread therein from every creature (dābba)...(164)﴾ [al-Baqara], which includes humans and others. ﴿And how many a creature (dābba) does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you...(60)﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt], where the dābba here is every animal other than humans, by the evidence of the words "and you", since conjunction implies difference. ﴿Indeed, the worst of creatures (dawāb) in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason (22)﴾ [al-Anfāl], which includes animals and disbelieving humans. ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed therein of creatures (dābba)...(29)﴾ [al-Shūrā], where the dābba here includes living beings in the earth and the heaven, and in it is evidence that there are living, rational beings in the heavens [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm], adapted.
2. **al-Nāṣiya (nāṣiya):** the hair that projects from the front of the head above the forehead; the place itself is also called "nāṣiya." "Akhadha bi-nāṣiyat fulān" means: he seized him and gained control over him, having power over him. In ﴿There is no creature but that He takes it by its forelock...(56)﴾ [Hud], it means: He controls it, possesses its affair, and disposes of it. In ﴿... they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet (41)﴾ [al-Rahman], it means the criminals are dragged by their forelocks and feet, so the forelock of the criminal is bound with his feet, and he is seized and cast into the Fire, helpless and humiliated. In ﴿a lying, sinful forelock (16)﴾ [al-ʿAlaq] it is a metonymy (majāz mursal) with a partial relation, meaning its owner is a liar and sinner [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm].
3. **al-Ṣirāṭ (al-ṣirāṭ):** a dialectal variant of al-sirāṭ; both have been recited, with ṣ and s. It is the path and road, toward good or evil. Of good: ﴿Guide us to the straight path (6)﴾ [al-Fātiḥa], and ﴿... Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path (56)﴾ [Hud]. Of evil and destruction: ﴿... then guide them to the path of Hellfire (23)﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt], where the expression ﴿then guide them﴾ is said in mockery and derision [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm].
4. **al-Sīmā, al-Sīma, al-Simma:** a mark or sign; "sawwama al-shay'" means to mark it with a sign.
5. **Safaʿa bi-nāṣiyatihi:** he seized it and pulled it; that is, "We will surely drag him by his forelock" in humiliation of him, which is a metaphor for humiliation, subjugation and abasement [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm 1/316].
6. **Al-ṣadr:** the front or beginning of anything. Here it means the beginning of the noble verse.
7. **ʿAjz:** the end or back of anything. Here it means the end of the noble verse.
8. **Al-qadḥ fi al-shay':** finding fault in something and belittling it [see Lisan al-ʿArab, root q-d-ḥ].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And if you turn away (1), then I have indeed conveyed to you what I was sent with to you, and my Lord will bring in place of you another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian (2) over all things.﴾ (11:57)

The verb "tawallaw" (تولوا) originally was "tatawallaw" (تتولوا). In the language, when a verb begins with two taa's, one of them is dropped.

Thus the meaning is: if you turn away, then I have conveyed to you the method with which I was sent to you, and there is no excuse for you before me, because the Truth, glorified is He, does not punish a people while they are heedless; therefore He sent me to you.

Or, the address is from Allah, glorified is He, to Hud, peace be upon him, to clarify for him: "If they turn away, then say to them: 'I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you, and my Lord will bring in place of you another people...'" (11:57) [Hud].

Istikhlaf (الاستخلاف) means that there come into being a people who are successors (3) to a people. Either they are just, so they do not stand against the methods or the messages as the people of 'Ad stood against them.

Or they are not just, like those of whom the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors who neglected prayer and followed desires...﴾ (19:59) [Maryam]. And the Truth, glorified is He, has promised the believers a good promise: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them...﴾ (24:55) [An-Nur].

So, istikhlaf is either that the successor is a person of righteous deed, or that the method is abandoned and not followed, and instead desires are followed.

In another verse the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Here you are, those invited to spend in the way of Allah, but among you are those who withhold. And whoever withholds only withholds from himself. And Allah is the Free of need, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you.﴾ (47:38) [Muhammad].

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they will not harm Him at all...﴾ (11:57) [Hud], because the method that was sent down to creation was sent down by the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, for the goodness of the servants. He, glorified is He, created everything first with all attributes of perfection in Him, and the servants will not add to Him any attribute, nor will anyone take away from Him any attribute (4).

Therefore we say to those who rebel against their servitude to Allah by disbelief, and to those who rebel against the method by disobedience: You have become accustomed to rebellion. Either rebellion at the summit, which is disbelief in Allah, or rebellion against the rulings of Allah by opposing them. So why does not one of you rebel against sickness and say, "I will not fall ill"? And why does not one of you rebel against death and refuse to die?

So then: since you have known rebellion in what is within your choice, can you rebel against the compelling rulings of Allah within you?

You will not be able to, because you are taken by your forelock. If the Truth, glorified is He, wills that the heart stop, you will not be able to command your heart not to stop.

Therefore Hud, peace be upon him, said: ﴿...and they will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾ (11:57) [Hud]: Allah, glorified is He, is the Watchful, because He is the Self-Subsisting, sustaining all the affairs of His existence.

Some philosophers said: Allah created the universe and created the nawamis (5), the laws, and then left them to carry out their work.

To these we say: No. You have affirmed the attributes of the Creator, the Able, so where are the attributes of self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) of Allah, who stands over every soul for what it has earned? He, glorified is He, said about Himself to His servants: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.﴾ (2:255) [Al-Baqarah]. When He, glorified is He, says this, He reassures the servants so that they may sleep and rest, because He, glorified is He, is free from heedlessness or sleep; rather He, glorified is He, is Self-Subsisting.

1 - Wala 'an al-shay' (ولى عن الشيء): he turned away from it, or he turned aside from it. The Exalted said: ﴿...they turned back on their backs in aversion (46)﴾ (17:46) [Al-Isra'], i.e., they turned away. And the Exalted said: ﴿And if they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance...(20)﴾ (3:20) [Al 'Imran] [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..
2 - Hafiz (حفيظ): one of the Beautiful Names of Allah. Al-Hafiz: the trustworthy Guardian who protects His servants and shields them. The Exalted said: ﴿...And your Lord is Guardian over all things (21)﴾ (34:21) [Saba'] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]..
3 - Khalafahu yakhlifuhu (خلفه يخلفه) from the pattern of nasara: he came after him and took his place. Al-khalf is a generation of people, i.e., one generation after another, and al-khalf is also a son. The Exalted said: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors who neglected prayer (59)﴾ (19:59) [Maryam]. And al-khalifah is one who succeeds another, and its plural is khulafa' and khala'if. The Truth says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah...(69)﴾ (7:69) [Al-A'raf], and He said: ﴿It is He who has made you successors upon the earth...(39)﴾ (35:39) [Fatir] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, pp. 203-204, vol. 1]..
4 - The Lord of Honour says in the Hadith Qudsi: "O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, and you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase anything in My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease anything from My dominion." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih [2577], and Ahmad in his Musnad (5/154), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4257), from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him..
5 - Nawamis (النواميس): the divine laws to which the universe is subject..
6 - Sunnah (السنة): drowsiness, which is the beginning of sleep. Drowsiness is what is from the eye; when it reaches the heart it becomes sleep. Al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi distinguished between them, saying: sunnah is from the head, nu'as (drowsiness) is from the eye, and sleep is in the heart. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 2/1196].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 58:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh torment.﴾ (1) (58):

As soon as you hear ﴿And when Our command came﴾, you know that there is a commander and a command that is obeyed, and as soon as the command is issued by the Commander, glorified is He, its execution follows; for He commands one who has the power to execute.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿When the sky is split open (1) and hears and responds to its Lord, and it is right that it should (2)﴾ [al-Inshiqaq]. So, by merely hearing, it carried out the command of the Truth, glorified is He.

When the Truth, glorified is He, willed to save Musa, peace be upon him, from the slaughter that Pharaoh had ordered, Allah, glorified is He, inspired Musa's mother, saying: ﴿...And when you fear for him, then cast him into the river (3), and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [al-Qasas] (7).

And how did his mother act?

Every mother is eager for her son; slaughter for Musa was a presumed danger, while casting him into the sea was a certain death (4). But Musa's mother received the revelation and did not hesitate, which indicates that she did not debate the matter by human measures, but acted upon an inspiration that came to her from Allah, glorified is He, an inspiration that no doubt or devil could contest.
