After that, Allah, glorified is He, commands the sea: ﴿Let the river cast him onto the bank (5)...﴾ [Ta-Ha] (39). The sea received the divine command, because it was a command from One who has the power to enforce it, just as it also carried out the opposite.

In the story of Nuh, peace be upon him, the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven gushed forth...﴾ [Hud] (40). The flood occurred, to drown the disbelievers.

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when Our command came...﴾ [Hud] (58): meaning: the arrival of the command of torment upon those who opposed the call of Hud, peace be upon him. This torment was realized in a particular and precise manner, one that in its precision is commensurate with the greatness of the One who commanded it, glorified and exalted is He.

When a fierce wind (6) or a tyrannical cry comes, this torment is from outside them. Since the torment comes from outside, through a force of nature issued by the direction of Allah, it may encompass those who denied Prophet Hud and, along with them, those who believed in him and his message. How, then, could the cry reach only the ears of the deniers and pierce those ears, while leaving the ears of the believers untouched?

It is the power of determination, not the power of destruction.

The One who directs the cry has determined whom it will strike and whom it will spare. It is a directed cry, like the stones of sijjil (7) which the birds, in flocks (8), threw upon Abraha the Abyssinian and his army, while the army of Quraysh was saved by the same stones. It was not a plague, as some of the self-styled philosophers claimed.

This is among the secrets of the greatness of the Truth, glorified is He: He takes with one thing, yet He saves the believer and punishes the disbeliever. There is no law governing the universe without a dominant power over it.

Al-Mutanabbi (9) says:
"The sun blackens our white faces, but it does not blacken the white of the eye or the hair (?)*
And their state in judgment is one, if we were to submit to the judgment of the world."

Thus al-Mutanabbi gives the example: when one of us sits in the sun, the skin of the fair-skinned person tends toward tanning, but the whiteness of the hair is not darkened; yet if you leave a black object in the sun for a while, you would find it tending toward white. This happens although the agent is one, but the receiver differs.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says here: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us...﴾ [Hud] (58). So do not ask how they were saved from the comprehensive torment and the general torment, for this is mercy.

Mercy, as we know, is that the disease does not touch a person from the very beginning; whereas healing is the treatment of a disease.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And We send down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers...﴾ [al-Isra'] (82).

We observe here that the Truth, glorified is He, mentions in this same noble verse two deliverances:

The first deliverance: from the comprehensive torment, the fierce wind, the cry, the tyrannical one. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿...We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh torment﴾ [Hud] (58).

The second deliverance: deliverance from the harsh torment of the Hereafter. The torment of this world, despite its severity, is limited by the lifespan of this world.

As for the torment of the Hereafter, it is a torment without end, and the Truth, glorified is He, described it as harsh.

The harshness of a thing gives it strength and firmness, and it is a harsh torment in proportion to what the Judgment can contain.

For this reason, when the Truth, glorified is He, lets a man possess a woman (10) through the marriage contract, and describes that as a firm covenant, the benefit here is connected with chastity and honor, and the man does not possess an absolute benefit from the woman he marries; the husband is granted access to the nakedness of his wife through the marriage contract.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...and they have taken from you a firm covenant﴾ [al-Nisa'] (21).

And the deliverance of Hud, peace be upon him, and the believers with him from the first torment was a prelude to deliverance from the harsh torment.

Footnotes:

1. Harsh torment: that is, great, abundant, severe, difficult. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2. Haqqa lahu [passive voice]: it was established for him. Allah said: ﴿And it hears and responds to its Lord, and it is right that it should﴾ [al-Inshiqaq], that is, it was a firm obligation upon it to submit to the command of Allah. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
3. Al-yamm: the sea or sweet river. Both meanings occur in the Qur'an. Allah said: ﴿So We drowned them in the yamm...﴾ [al-A'raf] (136), which is the Gulf of Suez with salty water, an extension of the Red Sea. Allah said to Musa: ﴿When We inspired your mother with what is inspired (38), [saying]: Put him into the chest and cast it into the river, and let the river cast him onto the bank...﴾ [Ta-Ha] (39). Here al-yamm is the sweet river Nile. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
4. Musa's mother lived in a presumed fear accompanied by anxiety: it may happen, or it may not. She also lived in a certain fear, which was casting her son into the sea, and the sea means drowning... But the aspect of inspiration made her receive the certain fear with pious faith. The sea received him, the waves caressed him, the shore embraced him, the enemy raised him, and the eye of Allah watched over him.
5. Al-sahil: the bank of a river, because the waves eat from it, carve it and erode it. Allah said: ﴿Let the river cast him onto the sahil...﴾ [Ta-Ha] (39), that is, onto the riverbank. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
6. Al-sirr: intense cold. Allah said: ﴿Like a wind in which is a sirr...﴾ [Al 'Imran] (117), and Allah said: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a fierce, violent wind﴾ [al-Haqqah] (6). [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
7. Sijjil: hardened clay. Allah said: ﴿...and We rained upon them stones of sijjil, layered﴾ [Hud] (82), and Allah said: ﴿striking them with stones of sijjil﴾ [al-Fil] (4). [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
8. Ababil: scattered groups with no singular from its own form, and it indicates multitude. Allah said: ﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks﴾ [al-Fil] (3). [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
9. He is Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, a wise poet, born in Kufa in a quarter called Kinda in the year 303 AH, raised in Syria. He claimed prophethood in the desert of al-Samawa [between Kufa and Syria], and therefore was called al-Mutanabbi. He later retracted his claim after being captured, and died in the year 354 AH at the age of 52. [al-A'lam by Khair al-Din al-Zirikli].
10. Al-Mutanabbi, although a man of letters with the ability to manage meanings, touched upon a scientific reality from which hidden secrets are derived, which make the intellect choose unity in the power of Allah, glorified is He.
11. Al-bud': intercourse and copulation; al-mubada'ah: sexual union and a man's contact with a woman [Lisan al-Arab, root: b-d-a].
12. Thus the woman, for example, has a separate financial liability of her own; her husband has no right to seize her property or interfere in how it is invested except after her consent given by her free will.
13. Mithaqan ghalidhan: that is, great and important, the covenant of marriage. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 59:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And that was ʿĀd. They denied the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers(٢), and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant(٣).﴾ (59)

"Tilka" (that) is a reference to the place where the people of ʿĀd lived, because the demonstrative here is feminine. Let us remember that the speaker here is Allah, glorified and exalted.

Thus He distinguishes between "ʿĀd" as a place and "ʿĀd" as the people who dwelt in it, namely the people of ʿĀd. For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord...﴾ (59). They have gone, but their traces remain.

"ʿĀd" may be applied either to the place and locality, or to the beings who lived in the place. So when Allah, glorified is He, points with "tilka" (that), it refers to the dwellings, and the dwellings did not deny the signs of Allah. That is why there follows His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord...﴾ (59) [Hud]. And al-judūd (denial) is repudiation together with the strength of proof and evidence.

And the āyāt (signs), as we know, are the plural of āyah, and they are the wondrous matters that strike the attention in a way that suggests belief in what they attest to.

Among the signs are those that point to the summit of creed, which is belief in the Necessary Existent: in Allah, the Lord, the Creator, the Wise, the Capable, glorified and exalted, such as the signs of the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and seeing the earth humbled, and so on through those signs that are at the summit.

Likewise there are other signs that come to confirm for those who report that he came as a messenger from Allah, exalted is He, and these are the miracles.

And other signs that contain the rulings which Allah, glorified is He, wills through His method, to guarantee the soundness of the movement of life among His creatures.

The people of ʿĀd denied all of these signs: they denied faith, they denied confirming the messenger by means of the miracle, and they neglected and abandoned the method of Allah, denying it by turning away(٤).

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And disobeyed His messengers...﴾ (59) [Hud]. Hud, peace be upon him, is the one whom Allah, glorified is He, sent to the people of ʿĀd. So is he the one meant by disobedience here?

We say: No, because Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant(٥) of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and support him..."﴾ (81) [Ali ʿImran].

So every nation has received word from its messenger that it should confirm the reports of every messenger who is sent.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, "We make no distinction between any of His messengers..."﴾ (285) [al-Baqarah]. They then divided into two groups, because the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...and disobeyed His messengers and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾ (59) [Hud]. That is: there is one who follows and one who is followed.

What is meant by "the obstinate tyrant" is the leaders of society, the masters of tyranny, and the second category are those who followed the tyrants.

Among His mercy, glorified is He, is that when He speaks of the misguided groups, He also speaks of the groups that misguide others. There is one who is astray in himself, and there is one who misleads others.

The one who misleads others bears two burdens: the burden of his own error, and the burden of misleading others(٨).

As for those who followed, they have some excuse, because they followed by force and compulsion, not by persuasion and clear proof.

Look at the Noble Qur'an when it treats this matter: it speaks of the group that went astray in itself and says: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who know not the Scripture except wishful beliefs, and they only conjecture﴾ (78) [al-Baqarah].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, speaks of the misleading group and says: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," to trade it for a small price...﴾ (79) [al-Baqarah].

١ - Jaḥada al-ḥaqq yajḥaduhu juḥūdan: he denied it while knowing it. Jaḥada al-niʿmah: he denied the blessing and did not give thanks for it. Jaḥada al-āyah: he disbelieved in it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ (33) [al-Anʿam] [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..
٢ - Here "rusul" (messengers) is in the plural form, not the singular. al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3373): "It means Hud alone, because no other messenger was sent to them besides him. Its parallel is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things...﴾ (51) [al-Muminun]. It means the Prophet ﷺ, because there was no other messenger in his time. This plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was also said: they disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers had been sent to them, they would have denied them all"..
٣ - Jabbār: the arrogant one. ʿAnīd: the tyrant who does not accept the truth and does not submit to it. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3373]..
٤ - Juḥūd does not arise except when the heart is closed, thought wanders, and the soul is weak..
٥ - Al-mīthāq and al-mawthiq: a firm covenant. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And remember the blessing of Allah upon you and His covenant which He made with you...﴾ (7) [al-Ma'idah], meaning the pledge He made with you and obliged you to fulfil. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/319]..
٦ - ʿAnīd: an intensive form. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾ (15) [Ibrahim] [al-Qamus al-Qawim] p. 390, vol. 2..
٧ - Wizr: a heavy load, a sin, the requital and punishment for a sin, and worry and distress. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾ (100) [Taha], meaning a heavy load which is his sin or the requital of his sin. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We relieved you of your burden﴾ (2) [al-Sharh], meaning the worry that wearied you, which was the concern of seeking the true religion. When the message came to him, the worries of his soul vanished, and he began to work for Islam with vigor and resolve, bearing nothing but the concern of his community. Or the wizr may be the sin which you saw as a sin because of the intensity of your love for Allah and your fear of Him, and He removed it from you and forgave it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ (2) [al-Fath]. The Messenger ﷺ regarded small lapses as great sins, so Allah removed them from him by forgiveness [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/333]..
٨ - Allah, exalted is He, says of those who mislead others: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ (25) [al-Nahl]. He also says of the disbelievers: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent﴾ (13) [al-ʿAnkabut]. The "athqal" (burdens) are sins, and they bear the burdens of those whom they misled, who followed them in their error [see: al-Qamus al-Qawim, root th-q-l]..

And then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse(1), and on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud! (60)﴾:

Time, with respect to creation, has three divisions. Their life is the first period; from the moment of death until the Hour rises is the second period, which is the period of the barzakh(2); and the hour when they are raised is the third period.

The first life is where deeds are performed; the life of the barzakh is where the recompense is presented(3), mere presentation; and the third life is the Hereafter, either to Paradise or to Hellfire.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿How do you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He causes you to die, then gives you life, then to Him you will be returned. (28)﴾ [al-Baqarah]: These are the three times: life, barzakh, and resurrection, and each time has its own context. The Qur'an expresses this, saying about the punishment of the family of Pharaoh from the time Allah drowned them in the sea: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening(4), and on the Day the Hour comes: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest punishment." (46)﴾ [Ghafir].

In this is evidence for the presentation of recompense in the barzakh, in confirmation of the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "The grave is either a garden of the gardens of Paradise, or a pit of the pits of Hellfire"(5).

So here there are two periods: the period of their being presented to the Fire morning and evening, and the period of their entering the Fire.

This establishes the punishment of the barzakh, because the disbelieving person sees in it his place in the Fire(6), and sees his share of punishment; then the Hour rises so that he takes his share of punishment.

As for the people of 'Ad, Allah, glory be to Him, made them taste the punishment in this world, and then He will admit them to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says in the same verse: ﴿... Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud! (6)﴾ [Hud]: The word "alā" (7) is a particle of alertness, as we said before, alerting the hearer to the importance of what the speaker is about to deliver, so that the hearer is not confronted with speech while he is heedless. Because the speaker is the one who leads the speech, the hearer must not receive it heedlessly; so the word "alā" comes like a bell alerting to what follows of speech.

The discussion is about the people of 'Ad who received punishment in this world by the barren wind(8), then they were followed by a curse in the barzakh, and they will be met on the Day of Resurrection with curses; so these are three curses.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, gave the reason for these curses, lest the hearer's heart soften from the abundance of cursing that falls upon them; so He explained with the word "alā," meaning: pay attention, that the people of 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord.

Crime has a time, and the punishment for it has a time, and their disbelief in their Lord occurred in this world, and it was disbelief at the summit; therefore they received punishment in this world.

The real danger is that the time of punishment be delayed beyond the time of the crime, so that foolish mercy does not seize you for them, because their disbelief is disbelief in the summit of creed; therefore their cursing continues in the barzakh, and then the curse of the Hereafter comes upon them.

And they did not disbelieve in the blessing of their Lord; rather they disbelieved in their Lord.

The Truth, glory be to Him, did not demand worship from anyone before the age of responsibility, and He provided for them, as He provides for all creation, blessings that cannot be exceeded or counted; therefore they deserve the curses, which is just recompense.

Hud, peace be upon him, had explained to them:

﴿Indeed I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock(9). Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path. (56)﴾ [Hud]: That is, the Truth, glory be to Him, is just.

When you hear their crime, you become agitated and seek the utmost punishment for them; therefore the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, comes: ﴿... Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud! (60)﴾ [Hud]:

So you are not content with cursing them the first time, but you curse them again.

And a questioner may ask: why does the Truth, glory be to Him, say here: ﴿... Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud! (60)﴾ [Hud].

We say: The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿And that He destroyed 'Ad the First (50)﴾ [al-Najm]. This makes clear to us that "'Ad" were two: 'Ad the First, a people who lived and went astray, so Allah destroyed them; and there is 'Ad the Second(10).

1 - al-La'nah (curse): a noun of single occurrence, and it is used in the sense of the verbal noun. The Exalted said: ﴿... Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers (18)﴾ [Hud], meaning: His wrath, His anger, and His expulsion are directed at the wrongdoers. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - al-Barzakh: the barrier between two things. The Exalted said: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting. Between them is a barrier they do not transgress (19-20)﴾ [al-Rahman], meaning: between the two seas is a barrier of land that holds each of them in its course, so that neither oversteps upon the other. And He said: ﴿... And behind them is a barzakh until the Day they are resurrected (100)﴾ [al-Mu'minun], meaning: a barrier that holds them from returning to this world until the Day of Resurrection. The period of the graves is called the barzakh period; whoever dies has entered the barzakh until the Day of Resurrection. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
3 - The Exalted said about the punishment of the family of Pharaoh: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour comes: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest punishment." (46)﴾ [Ghafir]. This is a presentation of recompense upon them, and it is in itself a punishment.
4 - al-Ghadw: entering the morning, or traveling at the beginning of the day. The Exalted said: ﴿Its morning journey is a month's [travel] (12)﴾ [Saba'], meaning the duration of the winds' travel in the morning, which caravans cover in a month. The morning (ghadw) is contrasted with the evening (ʿashiyy) and the asal (late afternoon). The Exalted said: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening...(46)﴾ [Ghafir], and He said: ﴿...glorifying Him therein morning and evening (36)﴾ [al-Nur]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
5 - Related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir from Abu Sa'id, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir from Abu Hurayrah; their chains are weak. See Majma' al-Zawa'id (3/46) and Musnad al-Firdaws by al-Daylami (3/231).
6 - From Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you dies, his seat is presented to him morning and evening. If he is from the people of Paradise, then he is from the people of Paradise; and if he is from the people of the Fire, then he is from the people of the Fire. It is said: 'This is your seat until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection.'" Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [1379] and Muslim in his Sahih [2866].
7 - Alā: an opening particle composed of the interrogative hamza and the negative la. It serves for alertness, indicating the confirmation and affirmation of what follows, as in His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the foolish...(13)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. It also serves for offering, urging, and encouragement, as in His saying: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you...(22)﴾ [al-Nur]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/27].
8 - That was the punishment of the people of 'Ad, as the Exalted said: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind (41)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. The barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim) is that in which there is no good, rather it destroys and annihilates. This is a description by way of metaphor, in brief. [al-Qamus al-Qawim p. 31, vol. 2].
9 - al-Nasiyah: the hair that appears at the front of the head above the forehead; its place is also called nasiyah. To take someone by the forelock means: to seize him and gain control over him, having power over him. The Exalted said: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock...(56)﴾ [Hud], meaning: He has control over it, the owner of its affair, disposing of it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, p. 270, vol. 2].
10 - This agrees with what al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3369] that they are two 'Ads: 'Ad the First and 'Ad the Other. The people of Hud are the First; as for the Other, they are peoples who lived in the Arabian Peninsula, and they are the ones mentioned in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars (7)﴾ [al-Fajr]. He says [3/2752]: "Between Hud and Nuh, as the commentators mention, there were seven fathers. 'Ad, as narrated, were thirteen tribes, dwelling in the sands of 'Alij; they were people of gardens, crops, and construction. As narrated, they were in the regions of Hadramawt to Yemen, and they worshipped idols. Hud, when his people were destroyed, joined those who believed with him in Makkah, and they remained there until they died."

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 61:**

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you upon it, so seek forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive."﴾ (61)

We observe here that Allah, glorified is He, tells us that He sent to Thamud one of their own, Salih, peace be upon him.

Allah, glorified is He, used the expression "their brother" [akhahum] to show the relationship between Salih, peace be upon him, and his people. He had grown up among them, they knew him and had tested him. So when he came to them with a call, and they had perceived his truthfulness, they must believe in the way of life he brought.

Salih, peace be upon him, addressed them with "O my people" [ya qawm]. The word is derived from qiyam (standing up), meaning: O you who stand up to affairs. Those who usually take charge of affairs are men, because the affairs of women are always kept hidden, folded within the man. Thus not every ruling of religion mentions women; rather we find that many rulings are addressed to men, while women are folded in concealment under the shelter of men. The man toils and struggles, while the woman manages the life of the home and the upbringing of the children.

We find among both women and men those who agree at marriage that the woman should not go out to work.

A woman has the right to work if she needs to and has no one to support her. But if there is someone who provides for her, why should she not turn to a work no less important than the man's work, namely the care of the family?

Likewise, we find those who, in the name of freedom, attack the veil. We say to whoever does this: if you have not criticised immodesty in dress and described it as "freedom," then why do you interfere in the matter of the veil and not regard it as "freedom" too?

Returning to the noble verse which is the subject of our reflections: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him...﴾ (61). Worship requires receiving the commands of the deity worshipped, in the form of "do" and "do not do"[^4] in every movement of life.

So the first thing Salih asked of his people Thamud was ﴿worship Allah﴾. The worship of Allah alone is required of everyone, and no one may oppose it.

﴿You have no deity other than Him...﴾ (61) [Hud]: this is a statement of a fact you cannot change. There is no other god besides Allah, however much you may try to claim other gods.

Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿He has produced you from the earth and settled you upon it...﴾ (61) [Hud].

Insha' (producing) is bringing into existence at the outset, without the intermediacy of anything. It is said: anshaa, that is, brought into existence from the beginning, without seeking help from anything else.

Therefore we do not say of an inventor that he "produced" [anshaa], because he used many things to reach his invention. He may have used material taken from the mountains and the experience of experiments made by those who came before him. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who produces from nothing.

Existence from non-existence is of two kinds: one kind you bring into being by means of something already existing, and the other you bring into being from pure nothingness. The latter is production (insha'), and only Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is capable of it.

Allah, whose will is glorified, produces in the way of production: He produces the human being from the union of husband and wife. If you trace this production back to the first beginning in Adam, peace be upon him, you will find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created him from the same material as the earth, and the earth is one of Allah's creatures.

The sperm of the husband and the ovum of the wife are formed from the essence of blood, which is the essence of foods, and foods come from the earth. So whether you take the creation of Adam from earth as a symbol, or you consider it as residing in his offspring, everything returns to the earth.

As for the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿He produced you from the earth and settled you [istamarakum]...﴾ (61) [Hud]: we find the word ﴿istamarakum﴾ in it. Whenever you see the alif, sin and ta' (in a verb form), know that it indicates a request[^6]. Thus the meaning of the word "istamara" is to request settlement (ta'mir).

It is a common mistake to call the countries that occupy other countries "the states of colonisation" [duwal al-isti'mar].

I say: this is an error, because if they were states of "isti'mar" (settlement/cultivation), this would mean that they desired to cultivate the earth; but in reality they were laying waste to the earth. Therefore they should have been called "states of destruction" [duwal al-istikhrab].

﴿Istamarakum fiha﴾ means: He requested you to cultivate it. This requires two things: that people keep a good matter in its goodness, or that they increase its goodness.

As I gave an example earlier of improving the means by which water reaches homes after the discovery of the principle of communicating vessels[^7]: people used to drink water from irrigation channels; then a method of purifying water was invented; then the principle of communicating vessels came, and people exploited it to build high reservoirs and to convey water through pipes that enter every house.

In this way clean water reaches every dwelling, and in this way the good matter increases in goodness.

Likewise, if we reclaim barren land, we increase the area of the earth suitable for producing food, to meet the increase in population.

As long as the population is increasing, it is necessary to increase the area of land by reclamation, because the crisis we suffer from now is the result of the negligence that has passed over us: multiplication outran reclamation. What duty required was that we increase reclamation in proportion to the increase in population.

In this way we understand the meaning of cultivating the earth.

Among the greatness of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is that He manifested Himself to creation through some of His attributes. The strong helps the weak; Allah, glorified is He, possesses absolute strength, bestows wisdom on creatures according to His wisdom, grasps from whom He wills, expands for whom He wills, and enriches whom He wills. Yet all the Most Beautiful Names are essentially His, and are bestowed by Him upon us.

The proof of this is that the strong among us becomes weak, and the rich among us may fall into poverty; so that we do not understand these attributes to be inherent in us, and that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has given us some of His attributes as a capacity to act.

Whoever Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has given the capacity to act must notice that he has benefited from the action of those who came before him. If he eats dates today, for example, he must remember that the one who planted the palm tree for him is one who came before him. So let him who eats fresh dates now plant a palm tree, so that it may benefit him after seven years (the time needed for the palm to bear fresh dates), and so that whoever comes after him may benefit from it.

Allah, glorified is He, says, concerning what was spoken by Salih, peace be upon him, to his people Thamud, in the verse which is the subject of our reflections: ﴿...so seek forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.﴾ (61) [Hud]: if a person seeks forgiveness, then Allah, glorified is He, is near to every servant who seeks forgiveness for sins that do not involve the rights of people, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, responds to the one who seeks forgiveness.

1 - Thamud: an ancient Arab tribe. It is said that they were a remnant of 'Ad, and they were the people of Salih. [See: Lisan al-Arab, root th-m-d.]

2 - Anshaa al-shay': he brought it into existence, created it, and made it. And Allah anshaa the clouds: He formed them and made them appear in the sky. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...and He produces the heavy clouds﴾ (Ra'd, 12), that is, He makes the clouds full of water. "And He produced you from the earth": He created you from it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], with adaptation.

3 - 'Amara fulan al-dar: he built the house; and 'amara al-qawm al-makan: they inhabited the place, so it is ma'mur (inhabited). And 'amarat al-dar bi-ahliha: the house became populated with its people, so it is 'amira (populated). Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah cultivate the mosques of Allah...﴾ (al-Tawbah, 18), that is, they establish prayer in them, sit in them for knowledge, remain in them for seclusion (i'tikaf), build them and maintain them; all of this is their cultivation. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you made the providing of water to the pilgrims and the cultivation of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah...﴾ (al-Tawbah, 19), that is, the cultivation of the mosque without faith has no weight; faith is the foundation for the acceptance of deeds. And ista'marahu fi al-makan: he made him cultivate it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿He produced you from the earth and settled you [istamarakum] in it...﴾ (Hud, 61). [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/35.]

4 - The whole matter of obligation in people's lives does not go beyond command and prohibition. From command we take the obligatory (fard), the sunnah, the recommended (mustahabb), the commendable (mandub), the voluntary (tatawwu'), the required (wajib), and the lawful (halal), and everything that pleases Allah for the happiness of humanity. Prohibition concerns the unlawful (haram) and the disliked (makruh). The movement of life is governed by "do" as a command, and "do not do" as a prohibition; in obeying the prohibition there is happiness, and in opposing it there is misery.

5 - Istamarakunna fiha: He permitted you to cultivate it and to extract your people from it, and made you its cultivators. [See Lisan, root '-m-r.]

6 - The judge Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: the form istaf'ala occurs in the language of the Arabs with several meanings:
- One of them is istaf'ala in the sense of requesting the action, as in your saying: "istahmaltuhu," meaning I asked him for a load (hamlan).
- And in the sense of believing: as in their saying "istashhaltu hadha al-amr," meaning I believed this matter to be easy or found it easy. And "isti'zamtuhu," meaning I believed it to be great or found it great.
- And in the sense of finding: as in their saying "istajdtuhu," meaning I found it good.
- And one of its meanings is the sense of the basic verb (fa'ala), as in his saying: "qarra al-makan wa-istaqarr" (the place settled and became settled). Narrated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir [4/3375].

7 - Communicating vessels (al-awani al-mustatriqa): several tubes of different sizes and shapes, connected to one another by a horizontal tube; when a liquid is placed in one of these tubes, the surface of the liquid rises to one common horizontal level. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit.]

8 - Al-nakhl: the tree of fresh dates, dates and unripe dates; its singular is nakhla, and its plural is nakhil. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates﴾ (Maryam, 25). He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And from the palm trees, from their spathes, clusters hanging low...﴾ (al-An'am, 99). And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Would any of you like to have a garden of palms and grapevines...﴾ (al-Baqarah, 266).

9 - On the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: Allah said: "O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and then you sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if you came to Me with sins as great as the earth, and then you met Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with forgiveness as great as it." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan [3540], and he said: "A gharib hadith which we do not know except through this chain." It was also narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad [5/154] and al-Darimi in his Sunan [2/322], from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 62:

What was the response of the people of Thamud?

The Truth, may He be exalted, says, relating what came from their tongues:

﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this. Do you forbid us from worshipping what our fathers worshipped? Indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾ [Hud 11:62]

They used to look upon Salih, peace be upon him, with estimation and hope before he called them to worship Allah alone, with no god besides Him.

Al-marju (the one in whom hope is placed) is the person in whom good is expected: intelligence, ambition, trustworthiness, and any quality that gives promise of a good future.

But as soon as Salih, peace be upon him, called them to worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, they declared that with that call he was ruining the hope they had placed in him and what they had hoped of him.

Salih, peace be upon him, made clear to them what the messengers before him and after him had made clear: that taking idols, trees, or the sun as gods to be worshipped is a mistaken matter, because worship requires commands and prohibitions revealed through a method (manhaj) that those who worship follow, whereas those beings that are worshipped have no method, and there is no worship without a method.

The people of Thamud added: ﴿...and indeed we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us﴾ [Hud 11:62]. Shakk (doubt) is the equal balance of two sides: negation and affirmation.

Thus, they were not certain that their worship of what their fathers worshipped was true worship, and Salih's call caused them to waver concerning that worship. This shows that the qualities of good in Salih, peace be upon him, made them waver about their worship.(1)

1 - Also, they were in doubt about the call of Salih, peace be upon him, to worship one God, so their address here is directed to Salih: [mimma tad'una] meaning: O Salih. Thamud came after 'Ad, and their dwellings were famous between the Hijaz and the Levant. Their brother Salih was sent to them to call them to worship Allah alone, without partner. They asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they proposed that a she-camel of the pregnant kind come out for them from a solid rock that they had themselves specified, a single rock in a region of al-Hijr called al-Katiba. So Salih took from them covenants and pledges that if Allah answered their request they would surely believe in Him and follow him. He then went to his prayer and called upon Allah, may He be exalted, and the rock moved and split open, bringing forth a she-camel whose unborn young moved between her sides. The she-camel used to drink from the well one day, and leave it for them one day, and they used to drink from her milk and fill whatever containers they wished. But nine men agreed to kill her, and they hamstrung her, so the punishment of Allah descended upon them after three days. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/227-229] Very briefly.

The Exalted says what was spoken by Salih, peace be upon him, to Thamud:

﴿He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Him, then who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him? You would only increase me in loss."﴾ (63)

It is as if Salih had made them the judges, and so he said: Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and certainty that He has sent me and strengthened me, and if I were to deceive all the people, I would not deceive myself. Would I then abandon what my Lord has honoured me with, and what He has sent down to me as a path I call you to? Would I abandon that and listen to your words? Would I abandon my certainty that He has sent me with this message, "and has given me mercy from Him..." (63), which is prophethood?

"Then who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him..." (63) [Hud]: When a person asks a question in such a situation, he asks only about something he is confident the answer will be one that pleases him.

Then the Exalted says on the tongue of Salih, peace be upon him: "...You would only increase me in loss" (63) [Hud]: We know that loss is the opposite of gain, and the meaning of loss is that capital decreases. So is the causing of loss done by him to them, or by them to him?

The richness of the Qur'anic style here makes all these meanings clear to us. If Salih, peace be upon him, obeyed them and disobeyed his Lord, then he would have increased his own loss, or he would be attributing to them greater ruin, because they are not guided and they want him to go astray and follow what they worship besides Allah, the Exalted.

So: the causing of loss is either done to them by Salih, peace be upon him, or it is done by them to Salih.

1 - "Ra'aytum" (رأيتم): i.e., tell me. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
2 - "Bayyina" (بينة): certainty, proof and insight, [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Muhammad Makhluf]. It is the clear proof that makes the truth manifest to the eye.
3 - "Rahma" (رحمة): i.e., prophethood. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn]. The saying of Nuh, peace be upon him, has already preceded: ﴿He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Him..."(28)﴾ [Hud]. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3343]: "That is, prophethood and messagehood. From Ibn Abbas. It is mercy upon creation. It was also said: guidance to God through proofs, and it was said: faith and Islam."
4 - "Khasarahu" (خسره): he made him lose; "khasSarahu takhsiran" means: he distanced him from good, and destroyed him. The Exalted's saying: ﴿...then who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him? You would only increase me in loss (63)﴾ [Hud] means: other than distancing from good, or other than destruction by the punishment of Allah. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim]. In Tafsir al-Jalalayn: [ghayra takhsir] means: other than misguidance. In the abridged Tafsir al-Tabari: "...fa ma tazidunani ghayra takhsir (63)" means: you increase nothing but loss, which deprives you of your portions of the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 64:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that on the tongue of Salih, peace be upon him:

﴿And O my people, this is God's she-camel, a sign for you. So leave her to eat on God's earth, and do not touch her with harm, lest a near punishment seize you.﴾ (1) (2) (3) (4)

The people of Salih had asked for a sign. They said to him: "If you are our prophet, bring forth for us a she-camel from that rock," and they pointed to a certain rock (5). They were a people skilled at hewing their houses in the mountains. Whoever visits the region lying between Syria and Medina can see the dwellings of Salih, which are carved into the mountains.

Concerning them, the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And you hew houses from the mountains, skillfully (farihin)﴾ (6) [al-Shu'ara' 149]. So they had specified the sign, which was the emergence of a she-camel from a rock they had indicated, and the she-camel came forth while pregnant.

After the she-camel was found in accordance with what they had requested, they could not bring themselves to declare their belief. Salih, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿And O my people, this is God's she-camel...﴾ (64) [Hud]. Whenever you hear something attributed to God, the Exalted, know that it has a greatness in proportion to the greatness of the one to whom it is attributed.

Just as we say "the House of God" (Bayt Allah). If this phrase is used absolutely, what is meant is the Sacred Ka'bah. If we specify a location and say of it "the House of God," we build a mosque upon it, and its ground is set aside to be a place of prayer, and no other work is carried on in it.

Thus the Ka'bah is the House of God by the choice of God, the Exalted, and there are other mosques which are houses of God by the choice of the creatures of God.

Therefore, the House of God, by God's choosing, is the qibla for the houses of God chosen by the creatures of God.

So, if something is attributed to God, the Exalted, it takes on the greatness of the Truth, glory be to Him. Salih said to them: ﴿This is God's she-camel...﴾ (64), and she is not the she-camel of Zayd or the she-camel of 'Amr.

The people of Salih did not heed what Salih, peace be upon him, said, and did not notice that a thing attributed to God has a greatness derived from the one to whom it is attributed.

An example of this: the son of Abu Lahab. He had married a daughter of the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him. When the opposition of Abu Lahab to the Messenger, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, intensified, Abu Lahab said to his son: "Divorce the daughter of Muhammad." So he divorced her, and did an act that showed contempt. The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, invoked a curse upon him, saying: (Indeed, I ask God to set his dog upon him.)

Abu Lahab said: "I sense an evil from the supplication of Muhammad."

Then the son of Abu Lahab travelled with some of his people on a journey. Whenever they slept, Abu Lahab would seek a place in the middle of the whole caravan's baggage, out of fear for his son from the supplication of the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him. Then suddenly a lion leapt from among the baggage and devoured the youth. Here the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, attributed the matter to God, saying: (Your devourer is a dog from the dogs of God.) So the dog of God was a lion.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, Salih, peace be upon him, makes clear to them: this she-camel is the sign you requested, and it has come out of the rock.

He could have brought them the higher kind of inanimate thing, which is plant life, but the Truth, glory be to Him, responded to the sign they had requested, which is of the kind of animal life.

We know that earthly beings are either inanimate, or inanimate matter takes on the property of growth and becomes a plant, or it takes on the property of sensation and movement and becomes an animal, or it takes on the property of sensation, movement and thought and becomes a human being.

It would have been possible for Salih, peace be upon him, to bring them a tree out of the rock, and this too is a matter of miracle, but the Truth, glory be to Him, sent the sign as they requested: a she-camel, of the animal kind, and pregnant at the same time.

Salih, peace be upon him, urged them to protect her, because she is a miracle, and they must not molest her. He said to them: ﴿...So leave her to eat on God's earth, and do not touch her with harm, lest a near punishment seize you.﴾ (64) [Hud]. Thus he admonished them, and asked them to let her eat on God's earth, and that if they harmed her, a punishment would seize them, for whoever believes in him must necessarily disbelieve.

So, the near punishment must necessarily come if they touch her.

And indeed they did touch her, as the following noble verse shows:

﴿But they hamstrung her, so he said: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ (65)

(1) Naqah (she-camel): the female of the camel. Salih's she-camel is attributed to God because she is the she-camel of God's poor, whom she gives to drink of her milk; or because she is vowed to God and God is her protector and shepherd; or because she is the she-camel of the Messenger of God, and she is attributed to God as an honour to her. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
(2) Ayah: a miracle indicating the truth of the prophethood of Salih, peace be upon him. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
(3) Dharuha: leave her, or let her be. This verb is used only in the imperfect and imperative. From the imperfect is His saying: ﴿Will you leave Musa and his people to cause corruption in the land...?﴾ (127) [al-A'raf], and His saying: ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods..."﴾ (23) [Nuh], meaning: do not leave your gods. From the imperative is His saying: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ (11) [al-Muddaththir], meaning: leave Me to take vengeance on him and punish him for his crimes against the religion and the Qur'an, and this is a style of threat and warning. And His saying: ﴿...Leave us, we will be with those who sit back﴾ (86) [al-Tawbah], meaning: leave us. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted. And in the abridged Tafsir al-Tabari: ﴿So leave her to eat on God's earth...﴾ (64) means: let her eat from God's earth; her provision and sustenance are not upon you.
(4) ﴿...and do not touch her with harm...﴾ (64) means: do not kill her or reach her by hamstringing. [Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari].
(5) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3378]: "It is said: he brought her forth from a solid rock standing alone in a region of al-Hijr, called al-Kathiyah."
(6) Farih: insolent and haughty, so he is farih; and farih, farahah and farohah: to be skilful, expert, active and nimble, so he is fari. Both readings are attested for His saying: ﴿And you hew houses from the mountains, skillfully (fari-hin)﴾ (149) [al-Shu'ara'], meaning: skilful and active; and it is read fa-rihin, meaning: insolent and haughty. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
(7) Three opinions are reported about his name: Lahab, Utbah, Utaybah. Mentioned by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah [2/338], who also said: Umm Kulthum, daughter of the Messenger of God, was under Utaybah ibn Abi Lahab, and Ruqayyah was under his brother Utbah ibn Abi Lahab.
(8) When God, mighty and majestic, revealed [Perish the hands of Abu Lahab], Abu Lahab said to his two sons Utaybah and Utbah: "My head and your heads are forbidden to me unless you divorce the daughters of Muhammad." He asked the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, to divorce Ruqayyah for Utbah, and Ruqayyah asked him for that too; and Umm Kulthum bint Harb ibn Umayyah, who was the firewood carrier, said to her: "Divorce her, my son, for she has become a sinner." So he divorced her, and Utaybah divorced Umm Kulthum. The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, came when she was separated from him and said: "You have disbelieved in your religion, and you have separated from your daughter; she will not love me, and I will not love you." Then he (Utaybah) attacked the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, and tore his shirt. The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: (Indeed, I ask God to set his dog upon him). [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/338, 339)]. Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id [6/19], and attributed it to al-Tabarani as a mursal report, saying: it contains Zuhayr ibn al-'Ala', who is weak. Al-Hakim also reported it in his Mustadrak [2/539] from the hadith of Abu 'Aqrab and declared it sahih. Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in Fath al-Bari [4/39].
(9) Al-Kalb: every savage predator that tears, including the lion. Ibn Sida said: the term kalb has come to be applied specifically to the barking kind. The term takhlib may apply to the leopard and birds of prey. In the revealed text: ﴿And what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (mukallibin)...﴾ (4) [al-Ma'idah], which includes the leopard, the falcon, the hawk, the shaheen and all types of hunting animals. [See Lisan, root k-l-b, and Fath al-Bari [4/39].]
(10) Al-Mass: madness, on the imagination that a jinn has touched him, as in His saying: ﴿As one whom Satan has confounded by touch...﴾ (275) [al-Baqarah], meaning the one stricken who does not comprehend his touch. Massa and musasa (mutual touching) are reciprocal, and tamassa the spouses means their skins met. Massahu (from the verb of fariha) means to pass one's hand over something without a barrier. Masathu al-nar: the fire struck him. Masahu al-marad: the illness afflicted him. And His saying: ﴿None touches it except the purified (al-mutahharun)﴾ (79) [al-Waqi'ah], meaning none holds the mushaf except those pure from major impurity. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, p. 226, vol. 2].
(11) Al-'Aqr: the root of everything. 'Aqartuhu: I struck its root, as in His saying: ﴿But they hamstrung her...﴾ (65) [Hud], meaning they struck her a fatal blow, i.e., they slaughtered her. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
(12) Tamatta' and istamta' have the same meaning. Mata' bi-al-shay': he benefited from it. Al-mata': a verbal noun that is used as a name for the thing benefited from, and al-mata' is everything one benefits from, such as food, furniture, tools and wealth. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon know﴾ (3) [al-Hijr], and He said: ﴿...And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ (12) [Muhammad]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
(13) "A promise not to be denied": that is, a true promise that will certainly occur; this is of the type of affirming a thing by negating its opposite.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 65:

﴿And they remained in their homes for three days.﴾(1) Then the punishment came upon them.

One may ask: why was the delay set at three days?

We say: when the punishment comes, the physical pain is cut off from the one being punished. God, exalted is He, willed that they should live in that pain throughout that period, so that they would suffer physically. Every day that passed over them increased their pain, because of the nearness of the threat concerning which God, exalted is He, said: ﴿...a promise not to be denied (65)﴾ [Hud]. God, exalted is He, is the One who makes the promise, and He is capable of fulfilling the promise, and no power can stand before Him. Therefore it is a true promise, not one that can be denied.

This is unlike a human being when he makes a promise to something: it may happen that the time for fulfilling the promise comes and he is unable to do it.

Therefore the Real, exalted is He, says to us: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow" (23) Unless [adding], "If Allah wills"(24)﴾ [al-Kahf]. For if you say, "I will do that tomorrow," and you promise a person to meet him at such and such a time, then say, "If Allah wills." This is because God, exalted is He, does not prevent the arranging of matters for a time that is yet to come, but whoever arranges matters must attach to them "the will of the Mighty, the Capable," so that if he does not accomplish what he promised, he will have stepped out of lying, because God, exalted is He, did not will it. For when a human being promises, he does not rely on his own will, but the will of God, exalted is He, rises above everything.

And the act, as we know, requires an agent, an object, a time, a cause, a motive, and a capacity that enables a human being to act. So does anyone own any of all this?

A human being does not own himself to live until tomorrow, and the one he promises does not own that he will exist tomorrow so that he meets him, and he does not own that the cause will remain a cause for the meeting. Perhaps the cause ends, and even when all the causes gather, he does not own the power and strength to bring about the cause.

Therefore, if he says, "I will do that tomorrow with so-and-so," he has gambled and spoken about something of which he does not own a single element. So say, "If Allah wills," meaning: you seek help from the will of the One who owns all these elements.

In every moment of faith, the Real, exalted is He, gives [a demonstration of] His power over His creation. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So they hamstrung her(2), and he said, "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied" (65)﴾ [Hud].

His words ﴿in your homes﴾ [are said] because among these disbelievers there were people in one place who differ from another place where there are also disbelieving people. Among them were travelers and those returning from a journey, so the punishment followed them wherever they were; it did not descend upon one place only, but descended upon those who were settled in whatever place they were.

From this matter there came out only one man, named "Abu Righal"(3), who used to make the pilgrimage to the House of God. The punishment did not follow him into the House of God, because God, exalted is He, asked us, His servants, to grant security to whoever enters His House; He, exalted and majestic is He, is more worthy of granting security to whoever enters the Sacred House(4). The stone with which he was to be struck, or the cry that was to seize him, remained [held back] until he left the Sanctuary, and then it fell upon him. The punishment encompassed the disbelievers of the people of Salih, and it pursued all who were in the dwellings except this man; as soon as he left the Sacred House, the punishment fell upon him.(5)

For this reason, the killer of a father, or a person who bears blood-guilt as a result of having committed a murder, when he enters the Sacred House, is granted security until he leaves. They would restrict him, so that no one would feed him or give him drink, in order to compel him to leave, and then retribution would be carried out against him after he leaves the Sacred House, so that the sanctity of the Sacred House remains preserved.

We know that the Real, exalted is He, intended by the prohibition of fighting in the Sacred House the protection and honouring of human dignity.

We also know that every event requires a time and requires a place.

The Arabs were constantly raiding one another, so the Real, exalted is He, willed that there be a place in which fighting is forbidden; He singled out the Sacred House for this. He, exalted is He, willed that there be a time in which fighting is forbidden, so there were the Sacred Months, because war may be a back-and-forth (sijal)(6) among people, and it awakens among them zeal, pride (al-anfa)(7), and honour.

Each of them, in himself, loves to be finished with war, but he does not like to appear a coward before people. So the Real, exalted is He, willed to give them something behind which they could shelter in terms of time and place, and He forbade fighting in the Sacred Months.

As soon as the Sacred Months come, one of these combatants declares: "Had it not been for the Sacred Months, I would have inflicted a crushing defeat on my opponent," and he says that to conceal his pride, for in his depths he wishes the war would end.

Likewise, when a combatant enters the Sacred House, the one who was fighting him says: "If he had not entered the Sacred [Precinct], I would have made him taste the punishment of defeat."

With the passing of time and the remaining in the place, people enjoy security and peace, and perhaps they come to love it and so they end the war.

1 - Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his Tafsir [4/3379] that the hamstringing was on Wednesday, so they remained Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and the punishment came upon them on Sunday. They remained three days because the young camel cried out three times: on the first day their colours turned yellow, on the second they turned red, and on the third they turned black, and they perished on the fourth. See also the tafsir of Ibn Kathir [2/229].
2 - ʿAqr (عقر): the root of everything; and "ʿaqartuhu" (from the pattern of naṣara) means: you struck its ʿaqr, like the words of the Exalted: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel...(77)﴾ [al-A'raf]; they struck it with a deadly blow, that is, they slaughtered it. "ʿAqirat al-mar'ah" means the woman was afflicted with barrenness, so she does not bear children, and she is ʿaqir; the Exalted said: ﴿And my wife is barren...(5)﴾ [Maryam].
3 - From Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the Hijr, he said: "Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them, and the she-camel would come from this mountain pass and go out from that mountain pass. They rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung her, though she used to drink their water one day and they drank her milk one day. So they hamstrung her, and a cry seized them, by which Allah destroyed them from beneath the expanse of the sky, except for one man who was in the Sanctuary of Allah." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Abu Righal. When he left the Sanctuary, there befell him what befell his people." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad [3/296], and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak [2/320, 567], who declared its chain sound. Al-Haythami said [7/50]: "The men of Ahmad are the men of the sound [collection]." I say: they are also the men of the first chain.
4 - The Lord of Glory, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds (96). In it are clear signs; the standing place of Abraham; and whoever enters it shall be safe...(97)﴾ [Al 'Imran], that is, he will be secure and at peace, not fearing for his self or his property. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched away from around them?...(67)﴾ [al-'Ankabut].
5 - Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir [2/229] "that there was a girl who was paralysed, whose name was Kalbah, daughter of al-Salaq, and she was called al-Dhurayʿah. She was a disbeliever, intensely hostile to Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, her legs were freed, and she got up running as swiftly as anything. She came to one of the tribes and informed them of what she had seen and what had befallen her. Then she asked them for water, and when she drank, she died."
6 - War among them is sijal: that is, its victory is shared among them, at one time for them and at another against them. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted.
7 - Al-anfa: honour, zeal, and dignity. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that Day. Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾ (11:66)

When God willed to send the punishment upon Thamud, after the period had passed which they had been warned would precede the descent of the punishment, God saved Salih, peace be upon him, and those who believed in his message from destruction. The mercy of God preserved them, because they believed in the way (manhaj) revealed to Salih. The believers in Salih's message did not suffer what the people of Thamud suffered of humiliation and disgrace.

This humiliation and that disgrace is what befell (haqat) Thamud.

The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His words: ﴿...Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾ (11:66). This is an address to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as consolation and comfort for him and as strengthening of his resolve. God is all-powerful; He seizes every disbeliever, no one overcomes Him, and nothing can frustrate Him. In this there is also a warning to those who disbelieved in the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

1 - "Haqa bihi al-shay' aw al-'adhab yahiquhu haqqan": it descended upon him, befell him, and encompassed him. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass anyone except its own people...﴾ (35:43).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 67:

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And the cry seized those who did wrong, so they were found in their homes lying prostrate, motionless (1) (67)﴾:

Here the Truthful, glory be to Him, names the punishment that descended upon Thamud "the cry" (al-sayha). In another place He calls it "the tyrannous blast" (al-taghiya), saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the tyrannous blast (5)﴾ [al-Haqqah].

In another place He calls it "the thunderbolt" (sa'iqa), saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud (13)﴾ [Fussilat].

In Surat al-A'raf He calls it "the quake" (al-rajfa). Each of the thunderbolt, the cry and the quake conveys the meaning of a sudden event (al-hadath alladhi yadham(3)) from which there is no escape.

One may ask: why did the Truthful, glory be to Him, not say here, "And the cry seized those who did wrong" (wa-akhadhat alladhina zalamu al-sayha)? Why has the feminine ta' (ta' al-ta'nith) disappeared from the verb, so that He says ﴿And the cry (akhadha) seized those who did wrong...(67)﴾?

We say: the One speaking here is the Lord of the worlds, glory be to Him. It is not correct to understand "al-sayha" as coming to express a single cry. The feminine ta' expresses the cry occurring once, but when it is repeated and becomes many cries (siyah), each cry seizes them from among the outcries.

Here we perceive that "al-sayha" contains the weakness of femininity, while "al-siyah" contains the resolve and strength of masculinity. So the Truthful, glory be to Him, wished to combine both matters, and He said "akhadha" and did not say "akhadhat."

Then He says: ﴿...so they were found in their homes lying prostrate, motionless (67)﴾: that is, fallen upon their knees and their foreheads without movement.

(1) Jatham jutuman (jathama): he remained in his place, clinging to the ground. The Exalted said: ﴿...so they were found in their homes lying prostrate (67)﴾ [Hud], a metaphor for their death in their state, for they were lifeless, clinging to the ground. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
(2) Rajafa yarjifu rajfan wa rajafanan: he moved and was agitated violently. The Exalted said: ﴿On the day when the earth and the mountains quake (14)﴾ [al-Muzzammil]. Al-rajfa is the noun of single occurrence from al-rajf. The Exalted said: ﴿So the quake seized them (78)﴾ [al-A'raf]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
(3) Dahamahu amr dahman: it came upon him suddenly and overwhelmed him. Dahamahu al-qawm: they came upon him gathered together at once. Adhamahu: it grieved him and forced him. Al-dahm: a great number; jaysh dahm: a numerous army. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿As if they had never dwelt therein. Surely Thamud disbelieved their Lord. Away with Thamud!﴾ (68)

The root "ghana" (غنى), and "ghina" (غنى) or "ghina'" (غناء), all share one meaning, because al-ghina' (الغناء) is existence: the existence of one thing that suffices (yughni) in place of another. Thus al-ghina (الغنى) is possessing wealth that makes you independent of others. Al-ghina' (الغناء) is what we hear from singers, and the song that a person admires for its words and melody, so that he settles with it, expelling whatever else he has heard of speech, however much he has heard or read. Al-ghina' is for residing (al-iqamah).

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿Until, when the earth took its adornment and was beautified, and its people thought they had power over it, Our command came to it by night or by day, so We made it a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday...﴾ (24) [Yunus]: that is, as if it had never existed before.

Here the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿As if they had never dwelt therein...﴾ (68) [Hud]: that is, they did not reside in it, because it had become a harvest.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says in the same verse: ﴿Surely Thamud disbelieved their Lord...﴾ (68), and this is the reason (haythiyyah) for the punishment that descended upon them.

The word "kufr" (كفر) usually takes the preposition "bi" (ب), and it is said: "kafaru bi-rabbihim" (they disbelieved in their Lord). But the Truthful, glorified is He, says here: ﴿Surely Thamud disbelieved their Lord...﴾ (68) [Hud]. The difference between the two meanings is great: the meaning of ﴿kafaru rabbahum﴾ is that they concealed His existence, so that for them there is no existence of Him. But the meaning of "kafaru bi-rabbihim" is an acknowledgment of God as existing, yet they did not believe in Him.

The saying of the Truthful, glorified is He, ﴿kafaru rabbahum﴾ refutes the atheists who do not acknowledge the existence of God, for the sin of denying God's existence has no sin beyond it, and nothing greater than it exists among sins.

Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿...Away with Thamud!﴾ (68) [Hud]: that is, they deserve what befell them of destruction and expulsion from God's mercy, and no one will show them compassion because of the enormity of their sin.

1 - Ghanna al-qawm fi diyarihim (غنى القوم في ديارهم): they prolonged their stay therein. God the Exalted says: ﴿So they became prostrate in their homes (67), as if they had never dwelt therein...(68)﴾ [Hud] [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

2 - Ghana yaghna ghina' and ghina (غنى يغني غناء وغنى): his wealth increased, so he is ghan and ghani; al-Ghani is among the Beautiful Names of God. God the Exalted says: ﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy...(133)﴾ [al-An'am]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

3 - Hasada al-zar' yahsaduhu hasadan wa hasadan (حصد الزرع): he cut the crop when it ripened; hasd is used figuratively in the sense of destruction and annihilation. God the Exalted says: ﴿...until We made them a harvest, extinguished (15)﴾ [al-Anbiya']; that is, We made them like cut crops, i.e., We destroyed them. And God the Exalted says: ﴿That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you; of them some are standing and some are harvested (100)﴾ [Hud]; that is, of them some remain and some are destroyed. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

4 - Aghnat al-dar bi-ahliha (أغنيت الدار بأهلها): the house was inhabited by its people, i.e., populated by them. God the Exalted says: ﴿So We made it a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday...(24)﴾ [Yunus]; that is, as if it had not been inhabited. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/21].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 11 (Hud), verse 69

The Truth, glory be to Him, in the following verse brings a new story from the stories of the prophets, which is part of the story of the father of the prophets, Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, the prayer and peace. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Ibrahim with good tidings(1). They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and it was not long before he brought a roasted calf(3).﴾ (69)

The word "rusul" (messengers) is the plural of "rasul" (messenger). The rasul is the one sent from one place to another, and any person whom you dispatch to some place is called a rasul. But the religious meaning of rasul is one who is sent from Allah.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Allah chooses (yastafi(4)) messengers from among the angels and from among mankind...﴾ (75) [al-Hajj]. The choosing of angels as messengers is to facilitate reception from the Creator, glory be to Him, because the power that receives from the Creator, glory be to Him and exalted, must be a high power, and none of us humans can receive directly from the Truth, glory be to Him.

Therefore Allah, majestic and exalted, brings us the messengers: He chooses, from among the angels, those specially qualified to receive, so that they may descend upon the chosen of mankind who is capable of bearing the message.

Thus we know that not all angels are capable of receiving from Allah, exalted be He, and not all humans are capable of receiving from Allah or from the angels.

These links in conveying were intended by the Truth, glory be to Him, so that the weak may take from the stronger; and humans resort to this in their lives.

I have previously given the example that at night we extinguish the light of the house, but we leave a faint light that shows us the features of the house, so that if we get up from sleep at night we do not collide with the furniture of the house, which would break what we collide with if it is weaker than us, or would harm us if we collide with what is stronger than us.

And the faint light allows us to see the place of the switch of the strong light.

So too does Allah, glory be to Him and exalted: He brings a chosen one from among the angels, who receives from the Truth, glory be to Him, and conveys to the chosen messenger from among mankind.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, is the one who says: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation(5), or from behind a veil(6), or that He send a messenger(7) who reveals by His permission what He wills...﴾ (51) [al-Shura].

And here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Ibrahim with good tidings...﴾ (69) [Hud]. Good tidings (al-bushra) is the announcement of something pleasing before its time of occurrence, and it is the opposite of warning (al-indhar), which is the announcement of something grievous before its time.

Before the messengers explained to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, the good tidings for which they had come, the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us the preliminaries necessary for entering places. It is part of the etiquette of entering any place that we greet its people, and the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission(8) and greeted their occupants...﴾ (27) [al-Nur].

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, brings here what the angels said before announcing the good tidings: ﴿They said, "Peace..."﴾ (69) [Hud].

And He, glory be to Him, brings the reply of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿He said, "Peace..."﴾ (69) [Hud]. We observe that the greeting came from their tongues in the accusative (salaman), while the reply with peace came in the nominative (salamun). Their saying "salaman" indicates a verb that expresses renewal, whereas the reply came with the word "salam" in the nominative, to indicate stability and firmness.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it or return it...﴾ (86) [al-Nisa']. Thus did Ibrahim, peace be upon him, receive the messengers of the Truth, glory be to Him.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿...and it was not long before he brought a roasted calf.(69)﴾ [Hud]. The ʿijl (calf) is the young of the cow.

There are many verses in the Qur'an that deal with the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in more than one place in the Qur'an, not for the sake of repetition, but because every snapshot in any place is a deliberate snapshot with its indications and secrets, so if the snapshots are gathered together, the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, will be completed for you in comprehensive totality.

By way of example, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And thus did We show Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (75) [al-An'am].

In another place the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses the certain upbringing He intended for Ibrahim, saying: ﴿So when the night covered(10) him, he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord." But when it set(11), he said, "I do not like those that set." (76) Then when he saw the moon rising(12), he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "If my lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray." (77) Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free of what you associate with Allah." (78) Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who originated(13) the heavens and the earth, inclining(14) toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah." (79)﴾ [al-An'am].

These verses show the function of the senses in perception, the function of feeling in emotion, and the function of choice in monotheism and submission with certainty.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says in another place on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he addressed his uncle respectfully, in keeping with his standing which equals the station of a father:

﴿And mention in the Book Ibrahim. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet. (41) When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which hears not and sees not and avails you not at all? (42) O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path. (43) O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has ever been disobedient to the Most Merciful. (44) O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan." (45)﴾ [Maryam]. This verse shows the gentleness of the caller together with the beauty of the presentation.

The uncle insisted on polytheism, so Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord...﴾ (47) [Maryam]. After that he disassociated himself from him because of his insistence upon disbelief.

Then there is the snapshot of one who disputes with Ibrahim about his Lord: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Ibrahim said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death..."(258)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

That was sophistry in speech, arising from incapacity of expression, for issuing a sentence of death against a man and then pardoning him is not giving life and causing death. So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, took him to a place no one dares to enter, and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west...﴾ (258) [al-Baqarah]. This verse shows the logic of the Truth in the face of the falsehood of falsehood. Then in another place of the Qur'an it comes to present the comparison between the idea of disbelief and the idea of faith, and He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And recite to them the news of Ibrahim (69), when he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?" (70) They said, "We worship idols and remain devoted to them." (71) He said, "Do they hear you when you call? (72) Or do they benefit you or harm you?" (73) They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus." (74)﴾ [al-Shu'ara'].

In this verse there are examples that carry the answer of silencing.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says, on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿He who created me, and it is He who guides me (78). And He who feeds me and gives me drink (79). And when I am ill, it is He who cures me (80). And who causes me to die and then gives me life (81). And who I aspire will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense (82).﴾ [al-Shu'ara'].

The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says in Surah al-Anbiya': ﴿And We had certainly given Ibrahim his sound judgment before, and We were well acquainted with him.
