Thus the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) was entrusted with two duties. It was entrusted with transmitting the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) to the generations, each generation passing it to the one after it.

Here he (ﷺ) says: "May God make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, retains it, and conveys it to one who has not heard it, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who understands it better than he who heard it."[^9]

The community of Muhammad (ﷺ) was also entrusted with standing against the disbelievers in the manner of chastisement, not to impose the religion, but to protect the freedom to choose religion. No sword was ever raised in Islam to compel a religion. Rather, the sword was raised to protect a person's freedom to choose his religion.

He says, glorified is He: ﴿Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve...﴾ [al-Kahf 29]. If he believes, then he is obligated to adhere to faith and must not violate any of its rulings. This makes entering Islam a serious matter. So from where comes the claim that religion is to be imposed on opponents?

Therefore, the believer from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) bears two faiths: the first faith is to believe in Islam, and the second is to convey the call.

For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The scholars of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Israel."[^10]

Does "scholars" mean only those who know knowledge? No. Rather, it refers to everyone who knows an article of faith correctly and soundly, and who travels across the earth spreading the call, to teach those who are not believers and to leave people free to choose their religion.

Likewise, the believers stand with the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) against any force that fights the freedom to choose religion.

Thus the stories of the Qur'an came to strengthen his heart (ﷺ).

We know that God, glorified is He, sent the Chosen One (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca, and he proclaimed the call, not into the ears of the weak tribes on the fringes of the peninsula, but into the ears of the lords of the peninsula, so that it could not be said that he had overlooked a people and called them to believe in him while fearing the masters. The masters were the Quraysh, who had taken leadership by virtue of their residence in the place of the Ancient House. All the Arabs used to make pilgrimage to the Sacred House. If any tribe harmed a member of Quraysh, Quraysh were able to strike the sons of that tribe when they came on pilgrimage to the Sacred House.

Thus Quraysh gained their prestige from their presence around the House.

Therefore, the House itself created the leadership of Quraysh, and it also created leadership for the gods claimed in the form of idols, when each people brought their god of stone and placed it in the House, so that the stone acquired sanctity from the sanctity of the House.

Thus Quraysh took leadership from the Sacred House. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came and announced the call in the hearing of the lords, ridiculed their judgment, and did not care for their tyranny and their dominance over the peninsula.

But God, glorified is He, willed that the victory of Islam should not come at the hands of the lords of Quraysh in Mecca. Rather, the rise of Islam came from Medina, because God, glorified is He, wished to make the whole world know that partisanship for Muhammad did not create faith in Muhammad.

Yet God, exalted is He, willed that the weak from the fringes of the peninsula would be the ones who supported the call. So it was as if faith in Muhammad (ﷺ) was what created partisanship for Muhammad, for the truth represented in the message of Muhammad, and partisanship for Muhammad did not create faith in him and his message.

If God, glorified is He, has described them as wrongdoers, and has shown them that the place whose top He turned to its bottom is not far from them, will they take a lesson from that?

Injustice, as we know, is transgressing the right of another; that is, taking someone's right and giving it to one who has no right to it. If it is injustice in divinity, then this is the great polytheism. If it is injustice in giving a worldly right to another, then it is injustice to humanity. Injustice has degrees according to the offense.

Quraysh wronged themselves greatly, because they associated partners with God and made for Him partners in divinity, and this is the greatest kind of injustice.

God, glorified is He, wants to remind these wrongdoers that when the punishment of God comes, or when the command of God arrives, no one can stand before it to prevent it. So be alert, for you are exposed to God sending down punishment upon you just as He sent it upon these towns, which are not far from you. The distance between Medina and Syria may appear long, but God made them pass by those towns on every journey of the summer trips to Syria.[^12]

Therefore, these are towns that lie on a traveled route. For this reason God, glorified is He, says of their location: ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾ [al-Hijr 76]; that is, on a road you pass through, which no flood carries away and no wind changes its features.

Rather, it is a fixed, enduring road that you pass through when you go on the summer journey to Syria. So it was necessary that you take a lesson and an admonition at every passing, so that you would not fall into another injustice.

God has also warned you by your passing through the dwellings of the people of Salih, whom God, glorified is He, addressed, saying: ﴿Do you build on every height a monument for vanity? And do you take fortresses that perhaps you may live forever? And when you strike, you strike as tyrants﴾ [al-Shuʿara 128–130]. Thus you see the dwellings of Thamud, the dwellings of ʿAd, and the dwellings of Lot, and they are desolate. It was necessary, O assembly of Quraysh, that you not exaggerate in injustice, and that you take heed, by the lesson, of the fate of everyone who associates partners with God, exalted is He.

God also draws their attention to the fact that they not only disbelieved in the right of divinity, but also disbelieved in gratitude for blessings, and they were unjust. God, glorified is He, is the One who bestowed upon them the winter journey to Yemen and the summer journey to Syria. These two journeys were for trade, which brought increase to Quraysh, because they went out with wealth and returned with goods which they sold to the people of Mecca and to the visitors of the Sacred House of God.

Quraysh also gained awe among every people they passed during the two journeys, because they lived around the Sacred House. Therefore God, glorified is He, bestows favor upon Quraysh in His words: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plan into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and He made them like eaten straw﴾ [al-Fil 1–5]. So the people who came to demolish the Sacred House, which was the symbol of their leadership, if it had been destroyed and the pilgrims had turned to San'a, then the prestige of Quraysh would have collapsed. But God, exalted is He, protected the House, sent against them birds in flocks, and made those who intended it harm like eaten straw.

Why did God do that?

The answer comes in the surah that follows the surah of the Elephant, where God, glorified is He, says in surah Quraysh: ﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravans of winter and summer. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh 1–4].

Therefore, when they passed by these dwellings, it was necessary that they take a lesson from them. Even though they passed by these dwellings for the purpose of trade, which was the secret of their livelihood, if they did not take a lesson from these people, they would be committing yet another new injustice.

For this reason God, glorified is He, says: ﴿...and it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 83].

Alternatively: God, glorified is He, wished to warn Quraysh that the destruction which befell those idolatrous people is not far from befalling Quraysh, and that God may send down upon each disbeliever in Him a marked stone that strikes him in the place where he is.

The superficial critics in matters of language make errors, taking objections against the Qur'an which the sound linguistic faculty does not heed. They say: how does God say ﴿...and it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 83]? The word "*hiya*" (it) is feminine, and it would require saying "*baʿidah*" (far, feminine) instead of "*baʿid*" (far, masculine). That is, the statement should be: "and it is not far (feminine) from the wrongdoers." They forget that the speaker is God, exalted is He, and that they have not studied the language correctly, because when the form *faʿil* comes in the sense of *mafʿul*, the masculine and feminine are equal.

An example of this in the Noble Qur'an is also His statement: ﴿...and the angels after that are a supporter﴾ [al-Tahrim 4].

And His statement: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good﴾ [al-Aʿraf 56].

Therefore, their lack of familiarity with the language is what led them to make such an error.

---

**Notes**

1. *Nadad al-shay yanudduhu*: to arrange a thing, placing one part upon another or beside another in order. So it is *manḍud* and *naḍid*, meaning arranged. God says: ﴿And the date palms with ranged spathes﴾ [Qaf 10], meaning arranged in order. Similarly His words: ﴿And acacia trees arranged in layers﴾ [al-Waqiʿah 29]. As for His words: ﴿...of baked clay, layered﴾ [Hud 82], it means successive and falling upon them in an orderly fashion. (Source: *al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

2. *Iram*: the name of a tribe, of which ʿAd was one; it is said to be a great city of theirs. Al-Kindi, in his book *Fada'il Misr*, claimed it was the city of Alexandria. His words: ﴿...of the pillars﴾ [al-Fajr 7] indicate that it was a civilization with lofty buildings. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/18.)

3. *Jaba yajubuhu jawban*: he cut it. His words: ﴿...who carved out the rocks in the valley﴾ [al-Fajr 9] mean they cut, hewed, and fashioned from it their houses and their idols. The letter *ya* of "*al-wadi*" was omitted in the orthography of the Mushaf. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/135.)

4. *Al-awtad*: plural of *watad*. A *watad* is an elongated piece of wood or iron fixed in the ground to which a rope is tied to restrain an animal or to hold the tent cover. Mountains are likened to stakes because they preserve the balance of the earth and fix it. God says: ﴿And the mountains as stakes﴾ [al-Naba 7]. He also says: ﴿And Pharaoh of the stakes﴾ [al-Fajr 10]. It is said they were the soldiers who secured his kingdom. It is also said they were literal stakes to which he tied those whom he wished to torture. Perhaps the intended meaning is the pyramids that Pharaoh built, which resemble mountains. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 2/318.)

5. *Al-sawt*: the whip with which one strikes. It was named *sawt* because it mixes blood with flesh. God says: ﴿So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾ [al-Fajr 13]. He expressed striking with the whip by the verb *ṣabba* ("to pour") to convey the continuity and comprehensiveness of the pain, as if He poured the pain of the blows upon them, drowning them in it, as water is poured over a body and covers it. Or *sawt* may mean mixture, so the punishment is mixed and varied, and He poured upon them mixed and varied punishments. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

6. *Al-mirsad*: a place of watching, like *al-mirsad*. God says: ﴿And sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ [al-Tawbah 5]. He says: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a place of ambush﴾ [al-Naba 21], and: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [al-Fajr 14]. The meaning is that God, glorified is He, watches over them and counts all their sins, however small, in order to punish them for them. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/266, adapted.)

7. *Al-wasat*: a verbal noun, and the middle portion of a thing is also called by it. Because it is a verbal noun, it describes both the singular and the plural with the same form. God says: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation...﴾ [al-Baqarah 143], meaning a virtuous, excellent community, the best of communities. *Al-wasat* is the best of two extremes. This is supported by His words: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind...﴾ [Aʿl ʿImran 110]. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

8. *Bakhaʿa nafsahu bakhʿan wa bukhuʿan*: he killed himself through grief, rage, and sorrow. God says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf 6]. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

9. Narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* (1/437), al-Tirmidhi in his *Sunan* (2657, 2658), Ibn Majah in his *Sunan* (232), and al-Humaydi (1/47), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud.

10. Cited by al-Suyuti in *al-Durar al-Muntathirah* (293), who said: "It has no basis." Al-Shawkani in *al-Fawaʾid al-Majmuʿah* (p. 286) said: Ibn Hajar and al-Zarkashi said: "It has no basis." See also al-ʿAjluni's *Kashf al-Khafa* (2/83).
It may be derived from the hadith that we should honor from the scholars sincerity and trustworthiness in conveying and skill in presentation.

11. *Safahtu al-rajul*: I charged him with foolishness and attributed to him levity and ignorance. *Safiha nafsahu*: he led himself into ignorance and levity, as if he made himself foolish. God says: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes himself foolish?﴾ [al-Baqarah 130]. *Safaha ahlamahum*: he accused them of foolishness and ignorance. *Al-ahlam* here means the intellects. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/317.)

12. On this God says: ﴿And indeed, Lot was among the messengers. When We saved him and his family, all of them, except an old woman among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 133–138].

13. *Al-rayʿ* (with a kasrah on the *ra*): a mountain, or something resembling it of high buildings, or an elevated place. God says: ﴿Do you build on every height a monument...﴾ [al-Shuʿara 128]. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

14. ﴿And take fortresses that perhaps you may live forever﴾ [al-Shuʿara 129]: that is, lofty buildings and sturdy palaces, which you carve, hoping that you will live forever in them, while you are not immortal. (*al-Qamus al-Qawim*.)

15 - Batasha bihi batshan: akhadhahu bi-'unf wa shiddah (he seized him violently and harshly). The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ [al-Buruj 85:12]. Al-jabr means compulsion, and jabarahu means he overpowered him and compelled him to do something. Al-jabbar is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah), and al-jabbar among people is the tyrannical, rebellious, domineering one. The Almighty said: ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of great strength (jabbarin)..."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:22]. And He said: ﴿...And every obstinate tyrant (jabbar 'anid) has failed.﴾ [Ibrahim 14:15] [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/72], with adaptation.

16 - Kaydahum: their scheming, i.e., their effort to ruin the Ka'bah. Tadlil: loss, nullification, and ruin. Tayran ababil: flocks scattered and following one another. Sijjil: clay turned to stone and burnt (ajurr, baked brick). Ka'asfin ma'kul: like straw eaten by animals, which have eaten it and passed it as dung. [Kalimat al-Qur'an, by Shaykh Husayn Makhluf].

17 - Li-ilaf Quraysh: "Marvel at the Quraysh's habit of making the two journeys, and at their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House" [Kalimat al-Qur'an].

18 - Al-zahir: the helper, the assistant, as if he supports the back (zahr) of the one who aids him. The Almighty said: ﴿...and he has no supporter (zahir) among them.﴾ [Saba' 34:22]. He said: {...and if some of them were to others a supporter (zahir).} [al-Isra' 17:88]. And He said: {...and the disbeliever is ever a supporter (zahir) against his Lord.} [al-Furqan 25:55], meaning one who aids the enemies of Allah against Allah, against His Books, and against His Messengers. Exalted is Allah above what they do [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/418].

19 - Qaraba al-shay'u min al-shay'i yaqrubu qurban: it drew near to it, so it is qarib (near) in terms of distance. In this sense the masculine and feminine are alike. The Almighty said: ﴿...Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾ [al-A'raf 7:56], meaning its place is near to them. As for kinship by blood (qarabat al-nasab), it agrees with the noun it describes, so you say: "He is my relative (qarib li) and she is my relative (qariba li) by lineage and kinship." [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/108].

Then the Almighty tells another of the stories that God relates in this surah about the procession of the messengers. He brings the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, and says, Exalted is He:

﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the balance. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day." (84)﴾

"Midian" is the name of the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. This son was not alive at the time of Shu'ayb's mission, but the tribe descended from him was named after him, and likewise the town in which the tribe settled was named after him. If you say that Shu'ayb was sent to the tribe of Midian, that is a sound statement; and if you say he was sent to the town of Midian, that is also a sound statement, because a town must have inhabitants.

The Almighty says, speaking on the tongue of the brothers of Yusuf, peace be upon him:

﴿And ask the town in which we were...(82)﴾ [Yusuf]. The intended meaning is "ask the people of the town" (4).

So, sometimes the name is applied to the place, and sometimes the place is mentioned while the people living in it are meant.

Shu'ayb began his mission with his people from the same point from which all the messengers began the call: to the summit of religion, which is that they worship God alone, with no partner, and that there is no god besides Him. This is the common ground in all the divine messages.

The Almighty says:

﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with God is that to which you invite them. God chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back (to Him)." (13)﴾ [al-Shura].

So, the summit of religion is the matter of the creed of faith, which is the worship of God Most High alone, with no god besides Him. For when the Almighty directs the commands of obligation, "do" and "do not," He addresses them only to those who believe in Him as the one God. As for one who does not believe in Him, God does not direct any ruling to him at all.

That is why you find that the basis of every obligatory ruling in the Qur'an is introduced by the saying of the Most High:

﴿O you who have believed...(178)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Whether the command is fasting (7) or retaliation (8), every obligation that begins with this address must carry the meaning: "O you who have believed in Him as a powerful, wise God, listen to Me regarding this obligation."

That is why it is always said: the reason (ʿilla) for every obligation is faith in the One who imposes it, and there is no need to search for another reason.

For example, when it is said that the reason for wudu' (ablution) is cleanliness, we say: and if water is not available, we touch dust or stone and then wipe our faces in tayammum (9) (dry ablution).

So the objective is that we prepare ourselves for prayer by whatever means achieves the purpose of worship, which is obedience to the Creator, Glorified and Exalted is He.

Beware of delaying the implementation of a ruling until you justify it, for its justification is that it issued from God, Glorified and Exalted is He.

Likewise, everything the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says, we follow, and we do not search for its reason. Otherwise, if we were postponing rulings until their scientific justifications were established, such as the corruption of pork due to the diseases it carries, and the ability of wine to destroy the brain and ruin its cells, as well as destroying liver cells, then if we had postponed those rulings, what would have been our position?

The Muslims implemented these rulings immediately upon their revelation, because of their faith in the method and their love of drawing near to God. Then the days proved the truth of God, Exalted is He, in His obligation.

Here the Almighty says:

﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him...(84)﴾ [Hud].

We have understood that worship is not confined to prayer, fasting, zakah, or hajj, because these are the fundamental pillars (10) upon which Islam stands. Rather, Islam is also the building of the earth through the implementation of all the obligations (11), and whatever the completion of an obligation depends upon is itself obligatory.

So a person's taking up a profession that society needs is an act of worship. If a craft is left without a craftsman, then the ruler of affairs must oblige and compel some people to learn it. Likewise, perfecting the craft is an act of worship.

As for the Almighty's saying on the tongue of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him:

﴿...you have no god other than Him...(84)﴾ [Hud]: meaning, beware of taking a ruling of obligation from anyone other than God, Glorified and Exalted is He, for there is no god but God alone, with no partner.

And beware of correcting (12) a ruling of God by a ruling from human beings, wronging yourself and saying, "God has missed telling us this ruling, so let us come up with a new ruling for ourselves" (13).

Beware of correcting a ruling of God. Understand the ruling first; if it comes as a clear, definitive ruling, then take it, and if it is not definitive, meaning it comes in general or unclear terms, then look, through your own ijtihad (independent reasoning), to which direction it leads.

That is why we find the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking the one whom he sent as a deputy to Yemen. He said: "How will you act if a case comes before you?" He replied: "I will judge by what is in the Book of God." He said: "And if it is not in the Book of God?" He said: "Then by the Sunnah of the Messenger of God." He said: "And if it is not in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God?" He said: "I will exert my opinion and not fall short." Then the Messenger of God struck my chest and said: "Praise be to God, who has guided the messenger of the Messenger of God to what pleases the Messenger of God." (14)

After Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, called the people of Midian to worship God alone, which is the common matter among all the messengers, peace be upon them, the other rulings come. Whoever commits an immorality has its remedy, and whoever cheats in measure and weight, the messenger addresses this matter.

Because the ancient world was a world of isolation, with no connection or communication among its parts; a defect or disease might exist in one place while that defect or disease did not exist in another place.

Each messenger came to treat a specific defect in the place to which God sent him. But the Messenger of God, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and he is the mercy sent to all and the seal of the prophets and messengers. He came, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the world was destined for a union of faith. Then, as the lands drew close through the speed of communications, and what happens in our time in the continent of America we find here on the same day or the next day, the world is now a world of connection. Diseases multiplied within it and became unified because of the speed of connection, through the lack of distinction between the wicked and the good.

That is why God, Glorified and Exalted is He, willed that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, be the seal of the messengers.

The failing of the people of Midian was their not worshipping God alone, and among them was also the base vice of cheating in measure and weight. Therefore the Almighty says on the tongue of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him:

﴿And do not diminish the measure and the balance. Indeed, I see you in prosperity...(84)﴾ [Hud].

When the scholars read this noble statement, they did not take it to mean merely diminishing what is measured or weighed, for had He intended that, He would have said, "And do not diminish the measured or the weighed." This is when we look at the matter from the viewpoint of what the seller wants. But the saying here intends that every person with a right receives his right: the buyer takes his right of the goods, and the seller takes his right of profit.

So this noble statement encompasses both the seller and the buyer together (17).

Measuring (kayl), as we know, is the equalizing of one thing with another. If it concerns lightness and heaviness, the matter requires a balance; and if it concerns the equalizing of one thing with another in quantity, this requires measuring. This is the well-known matter of measure and balance. Any equalizing of one thing with another requires what suits it. Cloth, for example, is equalized by the metre, and land is equalized by area, that is, measuring its length and width. Some things are sold by volume, which means measuring length, width, and height, and extracting the product by multiplying each of them by the others.

So the important matter is that every person takes his right, even if it is the hiring of a worker's strength to accomplish a task. You equalize the time and the strength of the labor with the appropriate wage. The well-known matter is measure and balance, but the other assessments exist too, so that everyone with a right takes his right.

For if a person takes what is not his right, he becomes accustomed to taking people's rights, and if some people devour the rights of others, those whose rights are devoured become disinclined to work.

When you give a person less than he deserves, or take from his effort more than what you pay him in wages, you find him slowing down in his work and not accomplishing what is required of him with full precision. From here the disorder arises.

That is why I say: giving every person his right increases the quality of performance at work.

It is also incumbent upon us to leave the ambitious person to work, rather than letting him hoard or store up his wealth, because the ambitious person, when he establishes a project or a building, benefits the poor and is useful to them, even if he does not intend that. The one who builds a residential building benefits craftsmen, workers, and producers of the materials needed for construction without intending to. The poor worker will benefit, without the employer intending it, and perhaps all the poor will benefit from what the employer produces, before it, in what he does.

So it is important that every person takes his right before his sweat dries, in confirmation of the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Give the hired worker his wage before his sweat dries." (18)

Thus we know that religion, on the surface of the matter, urges altruism (preference of others), but in reality it is keen to affirm a person's reward with his Lord. For the one who prefers another over himself, even though he is in need (19), if he has a little wealth and gives it to another who is in distress, while this other has no wealth, here the giver of the little wealth has, on the surface, preferred the other over himself, but he will receive many times that wealth as reward from God, Exalted is He (21).

Thus religion teaches us refined benefit, which is the benefit with which God treats us. When we leave the law of mutual benefit to govern the movement of people, we secure a flow of benefit in society.

Here, in the noble verse about which we are sharing our reflections, we have understood that Shu'ayb said to the people of Midian:

﴿And do not diminish the measure and the balance. Indeed, I see you in prosperity...(84)﴾ [Hud]: meaning, you, O people of Midian, are not compelled to do that, for among you the seller has goods, and the buyer possesses only money. So be content with the good that you have, and let every person with a right take his right. This is a matter that many people overlook, for the one who sells may sell only one kind of goods, and if he cheats in measure or weight, others will cheat and deceive him in the other kinds of goods that he needs for his life.

If one person begins diminishing measure and weight, others will do the same in everything that concerns his life, for one deceiver will meet many deceivers. Here Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, says: What compels you to that, when you are in prosperity? Then he warns:

﴿...and indeed I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day (84)﴾ [Hud]: because when you diminish something while selling, or add something while buying, you are not deceiving the one you deal with; you are deceiving yourself.

We all know that heedlessness may befall the seller, and may befall the buyer. A seller may try to exploit the buyer's heedlessness by pressing down on the scale with his finger to increase its weight, and a buyer may try to exploit the seller's heedlessness by raising the pan of the scale with his finger without the seller seeing it, and so takes what is not his right. This is a kind of self-deception, for the Almighty only commands uprightness in buying and selling, because the benefit of anything, however abundant, is limited by a person's lifespan in this world, and a person's lifespan is limited. But the one who cheats and deceives only exposes himself to the punishment of God, Glorified and Exalted is He, in the Hereafter, and that punishment has no term and no end.

Thus a person surrenders himself for a small benefit in the passing world, and then meets a punishment that does not end in an everlasting hereafter that does not pass away.

The punishment in the Hereafter is an all-encompassing punishment, meaning that the one being punished cannot escape from it. In this world you can devise ways to escape punishment, and you may resort to someone stronger than you to protect you. But in the Hereafter, you will face a day in which there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession, if you are among the people of the Fire.

1 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3404): "Regarding their being named so, there are two views. One: they are the children of Midian son of Ibrahim, a group; Midian, and the intended meaning is the children of Midian, just as one says Mudar and means the children of Mudar. The second: it is the name of their city, and they were attributed to it. Al-Nahhas said: Madyan is not declined, because it is the name of a city."

2 - He measured the wheat by measure: he assessed it with a measuring vessel, which is a container of known capacity upon which people have agreed for measuring. God Most High says: ﴿And give full measure when you measure...(35)﴾ [al-Isra]. Al-kayl (measure) is a verbal noun of "kala," and it is also applied to the measuring vessel. The measuring vessel is used for measuring grains, and if the vessel is diminished, what is measured with it is diminished. So God, Glorified and Exalted is He, forbids that the believer diminish anything of what he sells to people or what he measures for them. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/182], adapted. The plural of mikyal is makayil, the plural of kayl is akyal, and the kayla is a vessel in which grains are measured, and its current quantity is eight qadah (cups), its plural being kaylat. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

3 - Yawm muhit: a destroying day. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].

4 - The verse contains metaphor by omission (majaz bi-l-hadhf), which is one of the branches of eloquence.

5 - Shara'a al-shay': he explained and clarified it. Al-shir'ah and al-shari'ah: what God has prescribed and explained of creeds and rulings. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.

6 - Al-ijtiba': choosing, extracting, and selecting. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/117].

7 - The Lord of Majesty, glorified is He, says: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous (183)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

8 - God Most High says: ﴿O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retribution for those murdered: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned by his brother [i.e., the victim's heir] – then grant recompense in a reasonable manner and pay him with good conduct. This is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. And whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment (178). And for you in retribution is life, O men of understanding, that you may become righteous (179)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

9 - Tayammum linguistically: intention. Legally: an earthen purification that takes the place of water when water is absent, in reality or in legal judgment. It is valid for nine kinds of people: one who lacks sufficient water, one unable to use it, one who fears that an illness will occur or worsen, one whose recovery is delayed, one suffering thirst that must be respected, one who fears loss of a valuable thing... [Al-Sharh al-Saghir of al-Dardir, vol. 1]. God Most High says: ﴿...And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have contacted women, and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands. Indeed, God is ever Pardoning and Forgiving (43)﴾ [al-Nisa'].

10 - From Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing prayer, giving zakah, fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it." Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (8), and likewise Muslim (16).

11 - Obligations are confined to command and prohibition. From command we derive the obligatory, the required, the recommended, and the desirable, whether it is devotional or social. From prohibition we derive the forbidden and the disliked. Following commands and avoiding prohibitions produces a righteous society, by the evidence of the Most High's saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger has given you, take; and what he has forbidden you, refrain from...(7)﴾ [al-Hashr], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is God," and then remained steadfast...(30)﴾ [Fussilat].

12 - Istadrakma fat: he caught up with what was missed. Istadraka al-shay' bi-l-shay': he compensated for it with it. Istadraka 'alayhi al-qawl: he corrected his error, completed his deficiency, or removed ambiguity from it. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit].

13 - The Truth says: {Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion...(3)} [al-Ma'idah].

14 - Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad [5/230, 236, 242] and Abu Dawud in his Sunan [3592], Kitab al-Aqdiyah, from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal.

15 - Tatfif al-kayl (the fraud of defrauding in measure): he lengthens its upper edge and makes a lip (taff) on top of it. This is done when he places his hand or hands at its side, so that the excess grain does not spill, and then hurries to put it into his container to take more than his due, thereby wronging the one who buys the goods from him. God Almighty said: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss.﴾ So they are defrauders in both situations, because they take more than their due and give others their due short.

16 - Al-mikyal: the passive participle of [kala], meaning everything measured by the measure, whether wheat or something else. The active participle is "kaʼil." Al-mawzun: the passive participle of [wazana], meaning everything weighed on the scale. The active participle is "wazin."

17 - As is understood from the Shaykh's meaning, giving people their rights is the balance of life's scale.

18 - Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan [2443] from a hadith of Ibn Umar. Al-Busiri said in his Zawa'id: its chain is weak, containing two weak narrators. It was also recorded with this wording by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir [1/20] from a hadith of Jabir, and by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya [7/142] from a hadith of Abu Hurayra. Thus, by the combination of these routes and narrations, it rises to the rank of hasan (sound-good), and it has a basis in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayra, in the Book of Sales (Kitab al-Buyu').

19 - Athara: he chose and preferred it. God said: ﴿They said, "By God, God has certainly preferred you over us..."﴾ [Yusuf 12:91]. God said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life﴾ [al-A'la 87:16], meaning you prefer it over the Hereafter. God said: ﴿They prefer others over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ [al-Hashr 59:9], meaning they prefer others over themselves out of generosity, chivalry and piety.

20 - Al-khasasa: poverty, bad condition and need. Its root is from the gap or the lack, because when a thing opens up, it is (wa-hiya wakhnal).

21 - The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain that grows seven ears; in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies for whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:261]

22 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3405]: "Scholars differed regarding that punishment. It was said: it is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. It was said: it is the punishment of annihilation in this world. And it was said: it is high prices."

23 - There is another punishment in this world, brought by the hadiths of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Al-Qurtubi cited in his tafsir [a4/3405] from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "No people have shown fraud in measure and weight except that God has afflicted them with drought and high prices."

24 - Al-khulla: pure, firm friendship that penetrates the heart. Its plural is khilal. God Almighty said: ﴿...before a day comes in which there is no trade and no friendship﴾ [Ibrahim 14:31].

Almighty Allah then says, continuing the words spoken by Shu'ayb to the people of Madyan:

﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice, and do not deprive the people of their things, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.﴾

In the previous verse, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the weight…﴾ [Hud: 84]. Thus we learn that not diminishing in measure and weight is required, and likewise giving full measure and weight is required, because they are one matter. Allah the Exalted speaks of the measured (al-makil) and the weighed (al-mawzun) only in their general sense, which is every transaction in which there is an intermediary between seller and buyer.

In another place in the Noble Qur'an, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they give less.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 1-3]. This is because the seller may say to you: "You are trusted, so weigh for yourself or measure for yourself," and you may deceive the seller and take more than your right; and the seller may do the opposite, and in such a case there is hardship for both.

Here Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, says: ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice…﴾ [Hud: 85]. Allah the Exalted here speaks of both the diminishing and the giving in full.

Then He says: ﴿and do not deprive the people of their things…﴾ [Hud: 85]. This is a general statement that is not confined to what is measured or weighed. A buyer may come to diminish the value of a commodity, or one may take a bribe to get an interest fulfilled, or snatch what is not rightfully his, or usurp, or embezzle, and all of these mean: taking what is not right by various means.

We know that snatching (al-khatf) means that a person reaches out his hand to what another possesses, takes it, and runs off. As for usurpation (al-ghasb), it is that a person reaches out his hand to take something, and the owner of the thing resists him, but the usurper takes the thing by force. As for embezzlement (al-ikhtilas), it is one who is entrusted with a thing and then misappropriates it. And the one who takes a bribe (al-murtashi) is one who takes money or something in exchange for a service which is the right of the one who requests it.

So the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and do not deprive the people of their things…﴾ [Hud: 85] encompass many things.

Depriving (al-bakhs) means that you harm another by causing damage, by diminishing his right, whether that right concerns size, weight, quantity, or quality.

The word "ashya'" (things) is the plural of "shay'" (thing), and they say of the thing that it is "the genus of genera"; a fruit is called "shay'," and all fruit is called "shay'."

Allah the Exalted instructs us not to be deceived by anything, however small it may be.

We notice here that the word "al-nas" (people) is plural, and the word "ashya'uhum" (their things) is also plural, and when a plural is paired with a plural, the division requires singulars; that is, do not deprive the individual of anything, however little it may be.

We find that one of those who know Allah had hired a mount (matiyyah) from a caravanserai (khan) to take it from one place to another. When he mounted the mount, the whip with which he drove it fell from him. He halted the animal where it stood, went back on foot to the place where the whip had fallen to take it, then returned on foot to the animal in order to ride it. One of the people said to him: "Why did you not return with the animal to the place of the whip to take it and come back?" The knower of Allah replied: "I hired it to bring it to a place in a specific direction, and my agreement with its owner did not include that I search with it for the whip."

We find another knower of Allah who sat writing a book. In that era people would dry excess ink by placing a little sand over the written pages, and this knower of Allah found nothing with which to dry what he had written, so he took a handful of earth from beside a wall. Then he went to the owner of the wall and said: "I took earth from the side of your wall, so assess its value for me [that I may buy it from you]." The owner of the wall said: "By Allah, out of your scrupulousness I will not assess it," meaning that he was lenient in this matter.

The Exalted concludes the noble verse with His words: ﴿…and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.﴾ [Hud: 85]

The word ʿathā (ʿathā, ya'thu, and ya'thā, meaning "to act corruptly"; in the Qur'anic sense, to commit corruption in the extreme), all of these mean: to engage in corruption, that is, that a person deliberately goes to what is sound in itself and corrupts it, such as filling in a water well, or digging up a road on which people travel, and it is every matter that takes what is sound in itself out of its soundness.

The whole society, with every individual in it, is commanded not to engage in corruption; if each one applied this, the whole society would become sound. But the calamity is that some people wish that others be free of corruption while they themselves corrupt, and they do not want anyone to object to them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 86:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a watcher over you.﴾ (86)

Meaning: what remains for you of lawful (ḥalāl) wealth is better for you, because whoever takes what is not his right errs, since he removes the blessing from what is lawful by means of what is unlawful. Whoever takes what is not his right, Allah sets upon him gates of loss that plunder from him what exceeds his right.

You hear someone say: "So-and-so lives in blessing," meaning that his income is small, but his condition is good, and he raises his children with ease. This is in contrast to another person who may be wealthy from unlawful means, yet lives in narrowness of life (ḍank al-ʿaysh).

You may find that this person has had the doors of worldly expenditure opened to him, so his wealth does not suffice to dispel his worries, because Allah, glory be to Him, has let loose upon him many evil outlets of expenditure.

A person may be able to deceive other people, but he will never be able to deceive his Lord, ever.

As for the saying of the Truthful One, glory be to Him: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you...(86)﴾ [Hud]: meaning that Allah, exalted is He, removes from those who respect the rights of others the evil outlets of expenditure.

We have said previously, long ago: let us look to the provision of subtraction (al-salb), not the provision of addition (al-ījāb). This is because most people look to the provision of addition, meaning the search for much wealth, and forget that the Truthful One, glory be to Him and exalted, may let loose the evil outlets of expenditure upon the owner of much wealth that he gathered without right, while He strips those evil outlets away from the one who respects people's rights.

Those who raise their children on illicit gain (suḥt) or unlawful wealth will not have Allah bless them, because there is something unlawful in their make-up. For example, we find the son of the one who accepts bribes takes private lessons and fails, while the son of the disciplined person who is committed to earning lawful income is eager for knowledge and succeeds. Or Allah may grant the owner of unlawful wealth a wife with whom nothing satisfies, rather she always covets more,

while Allah, glory be to Him, gives the one who respects people's rights a wife who appreciates everything he does.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers...(86)﴾ [Hud]: meaning, if you are believers that Allah, exalted is He, is a watchful Observer, and that He, glory be to Him, is the Self-Subsisting; then do not take a right that is not yours, because you will only be harming yourself, since Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is watching over you.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿...And I am not a watcher over you (86)﴾ [Hud]: meaning that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, made clear to the people of Madyan: I will not stand over every corrupter to prevent him from corruption, because every person must be a watchman over himself so long as he has believed in Allah, glory be to Him, and so long as he knows that the Truthful One, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿What remains (86)...﴾ [Hud]: meaning that what remains is that in which blessing spreads.

This is the benefit of faith: what it commands and what it forbids.

This matter differs from man-made law (al-qānūn al-waḍʿī), because the eye of man-made law is limited in regard to what is hidden of people's affairs, so it is as though it protects them from falling under its reach. As for the divine law, it encompasses people's conditions, both the apparent and the hidden. Whoever reflects on the three verses:

﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day. (84) And O my people, give full measure and scale in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. (85) What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a watcher over you.(86)﴾ [Hud]: whoever reflects on these verses finds the elements that safeguard the movement of the whole society, and society, if its movement is not safeguarded, becomes corrupt, because the movement of society, as the Truthful One intended it, is a complementary movement, with no repetition in it; for if talents were repeated, no one would need the talents of another.

The public interest requires that each person needs the talent of the other: whoever studies for a doctorate needs someone to sweep the street, and whoever treats people, so that Allah may heal them, is found to need someone who repairs the sewers.

And what was the response of the people of Madyan to the words of Shu'ayb?

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped or that we not do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided." (87)﴾:

1 - al-baqiyya (remainder): what remains of a thing, or what deserves to remain because of the benefit and good it brings to people; the term is applied to what remains. The Exalted said: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you...(86)﴾ [Hud], meaning: what Allah has preserved and stored up for you of reward is better. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/79].
2 - ḥafīẓ (watcher): one who watches over you and recompenses you for your deeds. [Kalimat al-Qur'an], adapted.
3 - ḍank al-shay': it became narrow; al-ḍank is narrowness of anything, and it is a verbal noun described by which the masculine, feminine, singular and other forms are alike. The Exalted said: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life...(124)﴾ [Ṭā-Hā], meaning its narrowness, not expansive. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/395].
4 - The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive only themselves and perceive not (9)﴾ [al-Baqara]; He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them...(142)﴾ [al-Nisa']; and He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah...(62)﴾ [al-Anfal].
5 - The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. (124) He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?" (125) [Allah] will say, "Thus did Our verses come to you, and you forgot them; and similarly, this Day, you are forgotten." (126)﴾ [Ṭā-Hā].
6 - al-suḥt: wealth acquired by an unlawful means, such as bribery and what is taken by deceit and trickery. The Exalted said: ﴿Listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain...(42)﴾ [al-Mā'ida], and the Exalted said: ﴿And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and their consumption of unlawful gain...(62)﴾ [al-Mā'ida]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], adapted.
7 - The "tā'" in [baqiyyat] is written in the Qur'anic orthography with an open tā'. al-Zarkashi said in "al-Burhan 1/413": "its tā' was extended, because it means what remains in their wealth of gain that is perceptible, since the address concerns it from the aspect of ownership."
8 - al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing): one of Allah's Beautiful Names. The Exalted said: ﴿...And know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing (235)﴾ [al-Baqara], and Allah described His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing, grieving, and turning back (75)﴾ [Hud]. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿...Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided (87)﴾ [Hud], it is a description of forbearance and rectitude given in mockery by the disbelievers toward their messenger Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/170].

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 87 (part 1 of 2):**

I.e.: Does your God and your religion command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped?

One may ask: why did they say "your prayer" (ṣalātuka)?

We say: because Islam is built upon five (1). The first of them is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. A person need only say it once in his whole life. Then comes the establishment of the prayer (iqamat al-ṣalah), then the giving of zakat (the obligatory alms), then the fasting of Ramadan, then the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it.

If you look at these pillars, you may find a person who has nothing with which to pay zakat or to perform the pilgrimage. He may be sick, so fasting is not obligatory for him. He utters the testimony only once in his life. Thus, of the pillars of religion, only the prayer remains. That is why it is said of it: "It is the pillar of the religion. Whoever establishes it has established the religion, and whoever abandons it has demolished the religion" (2). This is because it is the one pillar in which the servant declares his allegiance to his Lord every day, five times, a continuous allegiance to Allah.

The prayer never falls from any person, whatever his circumstances. If he is unable to move, he may pray with the eyelids of his eyes. If he is unable to move his eyelids, he should run the prayer over his heart. Even in a time of war and sword-fighting, the Muslim prays the prayer of fear (3).

Therefore, the prayer is the pillar that never falls, and it is repeated five times a day. Allah, glory be to Him, has given it in legislation the importance that befits it.

All the obligations of Islam came by revelation from Allah, glory be to Him. Gabriel, peace be upon him, carries the revelation to the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the Messenger conveys it to us. The prayer alone is distinguished in that Allah, glory be to Him, imposed it upon the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was in the Highest Assembly, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (4), because of its exceeding importance.

An example of this from our own lives, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: we find the director at any workplace receiving the daily mail related to the work. He transfers every letter to the competent employee to study it or to propose a suggestion regarding it. If the director finds an important matter that has come from the highest levels, he summons the competent employee and arranges with him the procedures and arrangements that must be taken. If this happens in human affairs, what then of the obligation from Allah, glory be to Him, to the Messenger?

Allah, glory be to Him, willed that the obligation of prayer, because of its importance, be the only obligation that attained that rank, because it is the pillar that is repeated five times in a single day, and there is no escape (5) from it.

You may utter the testimony only once, but you say it in every prayer.

In zakat you sacrifice part of your wealth, unless you inherited it while you were in your mother's womb. You must give zakat from your property, and property comes only from work, and work is a branch of time. In prayer, you sacrifice that very time, and time is wider than the scope of zakat.

In fasting you abstain from the two desires of the belly and the private parts, from dawn until sunset, yet you engage in all the activities of life. In prayer, you abstain from the two desires of the private parts and food, and you abstain even more from things that were permitted to you during fasting.

In the pilgrimage you turn toward the Sacred House of Allah, and in every prayer you turn toward the Sacred House of Allah.

Thus all the pillars of Islam are gathered in the prayer.

The people of Madyan here, in the noble verse about which we are offering these reflections, mocked their Messenger Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, and his prayer, just as the disbelievers of Quraysh did with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

The people of Madyan said to Shu'ayb, peace be upon him: ﴿Does your prayer command you...﴾ (87) [Hud].

They thought that by this saying they were only ridiculing him, because Shu'ayb used to pray much. They, like the disbelievers of Quraysh, make it as if prayer commands and forbids.

﴿Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing...﴾ (45) [al-'Ankabut]. So prayer has a command, and prayer has a prohibition. Whenever a thing is established with a ruling, it establishes a counterpart to it. You hear someone say to another: "You pray, so I trust your honesty," and you hear another person advise a friend, saying: "How can you allow yourself to commit this sin when you have just come out of prayer?" (10).

Many people overlook the fact that the balancing of directions (opposites) resolves many problems, so they take one direction and leave the other.

Therefore I say: since Allah, glory be to Him, has said that prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing, it must be that it also commands righteousness and goodness (11).

Another example we find in the saying of Allah, glory be to Him, about the drowning of the people of Pharaoh: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them...﴾ (29) [al-Dukhan]. Since Allah, glory be to Him, has negated the weeping of the heavens and the earth over the people of Pharaoh, then by contrast it must be that they weep for other people (12). This is because the heavens and the earth are among the things subjected to glorifying (tasbih). Allah, glory be to Him, said about them: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust (13) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it...﴾ (72) [al-Ahzab]. By this saying, both the heavens and the earth chose the status of beings that glorify, in confirmation of the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿And there is not a thing except that it glorifies [Allah] by His praise...﴾ (44) [al-Isra']. So when the heavens and the earth see a person who glorifies, they must love him, and if they see a disbelieving, obstinate person, they must hate him.

Since the heavens and the earth did not weep over the people of Pharaoh, that is because they were astray, for they weep only over the rightly guided.

The Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah ennoble his face, resolved this question. He said: "When the believer dies, two places weep for him: a place on the earth and a place in the heaven. As for his place on the earth, it is his prayer-place (musalla). As for his place in the heaven, it is the ascent of his deeds (5)."

This is because the place where he used to pray is deprived of one who used to pray in it, and the place from which his deeds used to ascend lacks the fragrance of the passing of righteous deeds.

If by "prayer" you mean the religion, and it is the symbol of the religion, then prayer has a command that is the very command of religion, namely the command to true faith, for blind imitative faith (imitation) has no benefit.

Thus, the people of Madyan intended to mock Shu'ayb's call to them, and they asked: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped...﴾ (87) [Hud]. This saying also carries their rejection of his call to them not to worship other than Allah, for there is no god but Him. They also rejected his call to them not to diminish the measure and the scale, and not to deprive people of their things, and to be certain that what remains with Allah is better for them, and not to spread corruption on the earth.

They said: Do you also forbid us from doing with our wealth what we wish? As if their insight had been blinded, for if they permitted themselves to do with their wealth what they wished, then others would also permit themselves to do with their wealth what they wished, and interests would collide, and everyone would lose.

Their saying: ﴿...Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾ (87) [Hud]: a continuation of the mockery with which they began when they said: ﴿Does your prayer command you that you abandon what your fathers worshipped...﴾ (87) [Hud]. They are like the hypocrites of Medina who said to the Ansar: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse...﴾ (7) [al-Munafiqun]. They wanted to undermine the bond of brotherhood between the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar), and they said "the Messenger of Allah" mockingly, while they were inciting the wealthy of Medina to starve the Emigrants.

They are also like the people of Lot when he forbade them from committing that immorality, and they said, mocking him and those who believed with him: ﴿...Expel them from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ (82) [al-A'raf]. Is their purity a reason for expulsion from the town? But they said this because they did not want anyone among them who would disturb what they were in.

This is like what we hear in our lives from someone who says: "Do not seek help from so-and-so, for he is a Hanbali."

They, then, said: ﴿...Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾ (87) [Hud].

This is the logic of mockery directed at him, for he did not agree with them on worshipping other than Allah, and did not agree with them on diminishing the measure and the scale, and he forbade them from depriving people of their things.

When a true ruling is stated by someone who does not believe in it, he intends by it only ridicule and mockery.

This is a kind of mockery that came in the Noble Qur'an in many places. We find Allah, glory be to Him, saying to the one who was arrogant and tyrannical in this world and who will meet the torment of the Blaze in the Hereafter: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ (49) [al-Dukhan].

Likewise Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces...﴾ (29) [al-Kahf]. In each of these two sayings there is mockery and derision. Likewise is their saying in the verse about which we are offering these reflections: ﴿Does your prayer command you...﴾ (87) [Hud]. This is a saying that carries mockery of his prayer.

Likewise their saying: ﴿...Indeed, you are the forbearing (23), the rightly guided﴾ (87) [Hud]: it means, as a question: how is it proper for you, being wise and forbearing, to become entangled and say to us: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him...﴾ (84) [Hud]? They said that because they had become accustomed to worshipping idols. Likewise they mocked his call to them not to diminish the measure and the scale.

Also they did not accept from him his saying that they should act well in the handling of wealth. The reason they gave to justify all this foolishness was that Shu'ayb is forbearing and rightly guided, so how could he call them to what contradicts their desires?

Then Allah, glory be to Him, relates what Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said. He, exalted be His majesty, says:

﴿He said: "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has provided me from Himself with good provision, and I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from. I intend only reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn back in repentance."﴾ (88)

1. From Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; the establishment of prayer; the giving of zakat; the fasting of Ramadan; and the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it." Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (8) and Muslim in his Sahih (16).

2. Al-Hafiz al-'Iraqi said in his takhrij of the Ihya' [1/147]: "It was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab with a chain that he declared weak, from a hadith of 'Umar." Mulla 'Ali al-Qari said in al-Asrar al-Marfu'a (hadith 578): "Ibn al-Salah said in Mushkil al-Wasit: it is not known. Al-Nawawi said in al-Tanqih: it is munkar (rejected) and false. But al-Daylami narrated it from 'Ali, as al-Suyuti mentioned in al-Durar al-Muntathira (no. 279)."

3. Whoever has an excuse, such as illness or the like, by which he is unable to stand in the obligatory prayer, is permitted to pray seated. If he is unable to sit, he prays on his side, signaling with bowing and prostration. See Fiqh al-Sunnah [1/234].

4. When fear intensifies and the ranks are locked in combat, each one prays according to his ability, on foot or mounted, facing the qibla or not facing it, signaling with bowing and prostration however possible. He makes prostration lower than bowing, and drops from the pillars whatever he is unable to perform. [Fiqh al-Sunnah, 1/210].

5. The prayer of fear is established by the Book of Allah. He said: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group come who have not prayed and let them pray with you, taking their precaution and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings, so they could come upon you in one attack...﴾ (102) [al-Nisa']. Imam Ahmad said: "Six or seven hadiths about the prayer of fear are established; whichever way a person performs it, it is permissible." Shaykh al-Sayyid Sabiq mentioned six modes of the prayer of fear in Fiqh al-Sunnah [1/208-210]. See also Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas [2/322-332].

6. The prayer was obligated directly on the night of the Night Journey and Ascension, because of its nobility, and because it encompasses the acts of worship: in it are the testimony, zakat, fasting, and pilgrimage. Therefore it was not dropped from the one who is accountable. From the understanding in the reflections of Shaykh [al-Sha'rawi].

7. La manas: there is no escape and no flight. Nasa, yanus: he fled running away; nasa min al-makruh: he was saved from the disliked thing and got clear of it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿...And there was no time for escape (3)﴾ [Sad], meaning: this is not a time of flight and escape from the torment that encompasses them, nor a time of rescue and deliverance from the torment. [al-Qamus al-Qawim], with adaptation.

8. Al-fahsha': fahsh is the evil and reprehensible deed. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality...﴾ (268) [al-Baqarah], meaning: he orders you to stinginess or to committing what is ugly in general, and stinginess is among it. Al-fahisha: the ugly act. Al-fawahish: the ugly matters. One says fahusha and fahasha fuhsh, so he is fahish: he exceeded the limit and did the ugly thing [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/73].

9. Because the prayer is performed in response to the command of the One who commands. It includes the verses of the Noble Qur'an, and the verses are either commanding verses or forbidding verses. What is in it of the opening takbir, bowing, and prostration indicates that it is received with a penitent heart in humble response. Everything in it benefits you, whether as command or prohibition. Therefore the prayer is a school that forbids immorality and wrongdoing.

10. From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever his prayer does not forbid immorality and wrongdoing, he has only increased in distance from Allah by it." Recorded by al-Tabarani in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir [11/54]. Ibn Kathir attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim in his tafsir, and al-Haythami mentioned it in al-Majma' [2/258] and said: "In its chain is Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, trustworthy but a mudallis (one who conceals defects in narration)."

11. From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: "So-and-so prays at night, but when he wakes in the morning he steals." He said: "His prayer will forbid him from what you say." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad [2/447], al-Bazzar [1/346, Kashf al-Astar], and Ibn Hibban [p. 167, Mawarid al-Zaman]. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' [2/258]: "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."

12. From Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There is no servant but that in the heaven he has two doors: a door from which his provision comes out, and a door into which his deed and his speech enter. When he dies, they both lack him and weep over him." And he recited this verse: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them...﴾ (29) [al-Dukhan]. And he mentioned that they had not done any righteous deed on the earth that would make them wept over, and no good speech or righteous deed of theirs had ascended to the heaven, so it misses them and weeps over them.

13. Al-amanah: a verbal noun of amina, so he is amin. The term amanah is applied to the deposit itself. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners...﴾ (58) [al-Ahzab]. The trust here is used metaphorically for the legal obligations: commands, prohibitions, rulings, beliefs, acts of worship, and morals. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/35].

14. Inna here is negative, meaning "ma" or "laysa": meaning, there is nothing that Allah created but that it glorifies the praise of Allah, the Exalted.

15. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir [4/142] and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim that 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah said: A man asked 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do the heaven and the earth weep over anyone?" He said to him: "You have asked me about something no one has asked me before you. There is no servant but that he has a place of prayer and an ascent for his deeds from the heaven. And the family of Pharaoh had no righteous deed on the earth nor any deed that would ascend to the heaven." Then 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved (29)﴾ [al-Dukhan].

16. Bakhasahu haqqahu bakhsan: he diminished his right and did not fulfill it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not deprive the people of their things...﴾ (85) [Hud] [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/56].

17. 'Atha ya'thu: he corrupted in the utmost corruption. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿...And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption (60)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Their not giving full measure and full weight, and depriving people of their things, is the pinnacle of corruption on the earth.

18. Those intended are the Emigrants whom the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had made brothers with the Helpers after his arrival in Medina. The leader of this statement was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. It was among the requirements of this brotherhood that the Emigrant share the property and the home of the Helper. Indeed, some of the Helpers went so far as to offer to divorce one of their wives so that the Emigrant could marry her. See the books of biography and the tafsir of Ibn Kathir [4/370].

19. That is: until they disperse from around the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and turn away from him. It is said: *infaḍḍa al-nās*: the people scattered and departed. [See *al-Qamus al-Qawim* 2/84].

20. Mujahid said: That is, they purify themselves from the anuses of men and the anuses of women. They said this as mockery of them. Qatada said: They found fault with them without any fault, and blamed them without any blame. See *al-Durr al-Manthur* of al-Suyuti [3/496].

21. *Dhāqa al-shay' yadhūquhu dhawāqan*: he perceived its taste in his mouth. It is used figuratively for general sensation, as in His words: ﴿That they may taste the punishment﴾ [An-Nisa 56], ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Al 'Imran 185], and His words: ﴿And when they tasted the tree﴾ [Al-A'raf 22]. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* p. 247, vol. 1].

22. *Istaghātha*: to seek relief and help. *Istaghātha fulānan* and *istaghātha bihi*: he asked him for support and sought his aid. Allah says: ﴿So he who was of his party cried out to him against him who was of his enemy﴾ [Al-Qasas 15], i.e., he asked him for support. *Ghāthahu Allāh yaghūthuhu ghawthan*: Allah supported and aided him; *aghāthahu* and *ghāthahu*: he supported and aided him. *Al-mahl* (with a *ḍamma* on the *mīm*): molten metal, tar, the dregs of boiled oil, and pus. Allah says: ﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces﴾ [Al-Kahf 29]. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 2/62].

23. *Al-ḥilm* (forbearance): deliberateness, self-restraint and sound reason. So *ḥalīm* means one who is deliberate, sensible, and in control of himself, far from ignorance, folly and recklessness. *Al-Ḥalīm* is one of the Beautiful Names of Allah. Allah says: ﴿...know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [Al-Baqara 235]. Allah described His friend Ibrahim with His words: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was forbearing, grieving, and turning back in repentance﴾ [Hud 75]. As for His words: ﴿...Indeed you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾ [Hud 87], it is a description of forbearance and rectitude given by way of mockery by the disbelievers toward their messenger Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/169, 170].

24. *Bayyina*: proof and evidence. *Bāna al-shay' yabīnu bayānan*: the thing became manifest and clear, so it is *bayyin*, and she is *bayyina*, i.e., manifest and evident. The words *bayyin* and *bayyina* are used in the sense of that which manifests, clarifies, makes clear, and is made clear. Both meanings are used to explain His words: ﴿How many clear signs (*āya bayyina*) We have given them﴾ [Al-Baqara 211], i.e., clear without any doubt. Or it clarifies the truth, supports it, and makes its matter manifest. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim*].

25. Here *in* is a negating particle, meaning *mā* or *lā*: i.e., "I do not desire, or I do not desire except reform."

26. *Anāba al-'abd ilā rabbihi*: the servant returned to his Lord, repented, and abandoned sins. His words: ﴿...Upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn back﴾ [Hud 88] mean: to Him I repent and return. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim*].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 88:

Here Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) declares to them that he is certain that Allah, glory be to Him, has given him proof (hujjah) and a method (manhaj), and has provided him with good sustenance (al-rizq al-hasan) which means he has no need of anyone; the affairs of his life are made easy (1).

It may be that what is meant by good sustenance is the mercy of prophethood.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says what came on the tongue of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): ﴿And I do not wish to differ from you in that which I forbid you...﴾ (88) [Hud]. That is: I apply to myself what I call you to; so I do not diminish the measure or the scale, nor do I defraud anyone of his things, because I do not worship other than Allah.

The word "akhalifa" (2) indicates two opposing directions. If your speech aims to turn a person away from an act so that you may do it yourself, you have opposed him "ila" (towards) such-and-such; and if you want him to do an act so that you do not do it, you have opposed him "an" (away from) such-and-such.

So Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) makes clear to them that he does not forbid them from acts so that he himself would do them; rather he forbids them from what he does not do, because the Truth, glory be to Him, has commanded him not to do those acts. The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who revealed the method to him and sent down the message to him.

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) does not forbid them from acts that he himself performs, because he does not keep for himself what they would see as good; there is no slightest good in diminishing the measure and the scale, or in associating partners with Allah. All those acts are evil itself.

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) clarifies to them the mission of prophethood, so he says: ﴿I only desire reform as far as I am able...﴾ (88) [Hud]. All prophethoods are such that Allah, may He be exalted, sends them only when corruption has overwhelmed (tamma), and the prophet who is sent comes with a method that guides people to what sets their conditions right, through "do" and "do not do". The sent prophet is the exemplar for applying the method; he does not command a thing from which he is far removed (najwa) (4), and he applies to himself first everything he calls to.

For this reason Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: ﴿I only desire reform as far as I am able...﴾ (88) [Hud], because Allah, glory be to Him, does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, and what falls within its power.

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) then says: ﴿...And my success is only through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn (in repentance).﴾ (88) [Hud]. Thus we know that there is a difference between the work and the success (tawfiq) in the work; for your limbs may be occupied with the work while your intention is not sincere, and then success does not come from Allah.

But if you approach the work with the intention that Allah, glory be to Him, grant you success to perform this work sincerely, you will find Allah correcting for you any error you fall into; you will accomplish the work with excellence and feel the beauty of excellence, and in beauty there is majesty.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says here what came on the tongue of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾; that is, he relies only upon Allah, and it is not right to conjoin anything to this statement; for if you conjoin to this statement and say "I have relied upon Allah and upon you", you should expect that Allah will not grant you success, because you have associated someone other than Allah (5).

In the Qur'an we find the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, on the tongue of Hud (peace be upon him): ﴿I have relied upon Allah...﴾ (56) [Hud]. Here it is permissible for you to conjoin.

And you may remember the saying of one of the knowers (ʿarifun) (6): "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness from every deed by which I intended Your Face but which was mixed with what is not for You."

So do not let anything creep upon your reliance upon Allah, glory be to Him, for to Him you turn and return, as Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: ﴿and to Him I turn﴾.

1 - Al-rizq al-hasan: the wide lawful provision. Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) was wealthy in property, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. It was also said: he meant guidance, success, knowledge and recognition, as al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3408].
2 - Abu Hayyan said regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And I do not wish to differ from you in that which I forbid you...﴾ (88) [Hud], the meaning: I do not wish to do the thing I have forbidden you, of diminishing the measure and the weight and taking more wealth for myself. Ibn 'Atiyyah and Qatadah said: I would not forbid you from a matter and then commit it myself.
