Based on this, the apparent sense is that the words ﴿an akhalifakum...﴾ (88) [Hud] stand in the position of the object of "urid", i.e. "ma urid mukhalafatakum", meaning I am not a successor (khalf) to you, and "khalafa" here carries the sense of "khalafa" as in "jawaza" and "jaza", and "ila" is connected: I would not oppose you towards what I forbid you. Al-Zajjaj said: I do not intend by opposing you to commit what I forbid you [Tafsir al-Bahr al-Muhit 6/198, abridged].
3 - Tamma al-shay': it grew great and rose high. Tamma al-ma': when water increased. When the flood came, it overwhelmed everything, i.e. covered it. The intended meaning is that corruption multiplies, spreads, and becomes general corruption that covers the lands and their people. See [Lisan al-Arab, root: t-m-m].
4 - Al-najwa: that which is raised from the ground so that the flood does not reach it; i.e., an elevated place. The intended meaning: you are far from what you command. See [Lisan, root: n-j-w].
5 - From Huthayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not say 'What Allah wills and what so-and-so wills', but say: 'What Allah wills, then what so-and-so wills.'" Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad [5/384], Abu Dawud in his Sunan [4980], and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak [3/462]. Al-Nawawi said in al-Adhkar [p. 318]: "This is a guidance toward good manners, for the waw denotes joining and association, while thumma denotes sequence and delay; so the Prophet (ﷺ) guided to placing the will of Allah, may He be exalted, before the will of anyone else."
6 - He is Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, who wore wool and sat with the poor. Abu Nu'aym cited this report in Hilyat al-Awliya' [2/207], and Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali in Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam [p. 27]. Both cited it complete, and the conjunction in it is part of the supplication itself, not a separate conjunction.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 89:

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And O my people, let not my opposition (shiqaq) bring upon you the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and the people of Lut are not far from you.﴾ (89)

Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, says to them: I hope that your enmity toward me will not lead you to commit a crime that would be the cause of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sending down punishment upon you, like what befell the peoples who came before you, those who opposed their messengers. So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, sent down upon them punishment such as drowning, the quake, the cry, and the thunderbolt (al-sa'iqa). So beware of that.

Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, advises them here out of his concern for them, despite his knowledge that they harbor enmity toward him, because he had called them to abandon the worship of the idols that their fathers worshipped, and he forbade them from diminishing the measure and the balance, and from depriving people of their goods. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had previously punished those among the earlier nations who opposed the law of God. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, reminds them of those who were nearest to them in time and place among those who were punished, namely the people of Lut.

1 - Jarama (جرم) al-shay' jarman: he cut it; the word became predominantly used for evil conduct. It is said: jarama: he committed a sin and perpetrated an offense. Jarama al-mal: he earned the wealth by any means. Jarramahu: he drove him to commit an evil act, a sin, or a crime. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people lead you to deviate from justice...﴾ (al-Ma'ida 8), meaning: let not the hatred of a people lead you to abandon justice; that is, adhere to justice even toward those you dislike, that is, always be just, for justice is closer to piety.
And ajramahu: he pushed him and drove him to commit a crime and an evil. The reading [wa la yajrimannakum] with a damma on the ya' from the quadriliteral form with the hamza added means: let them not drive you to commit crime and injustice. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Shaqqahu mushaqqatan wa shiqaqan: he opposed him. From it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (al-Anfal 13).
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if they turn away, then they are only in opposition (shiqaq)...﴾ (al-Baqara 137), meaning: in dissension and dispute. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/353].
3 - The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So each We seized for his sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the cry, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (al-'Ankabut 40).

Allah, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿And ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving.(1) (90)﴾

This verse shows us that Allah, glorified be He, does not close the door of repentance before the sinner, even one who persists in some sin.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you who, having lost his camel with his provisions and his belongings in a barren desert, then finds it again."(2)(3)(4)

Let us imagine how the one who lost his camel feels, for that camel carries his provisions and his belongings. Then the man finds this camel.

Surely, then, the owner of the camel must rejoice at finding it.

Allah says here what came on the tongue of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) to his people: ﴿And ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him...(90)﴾ [Hud]. That is: since you will seek His forgiveness for past sins, and turn to Him by not returning to committing them again, then Allah does not turn away one who intends His door. ﴿...Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving (90)﴾, because His forgiveness covers the punishment, and His mercy prevents the punishment.

Allah, the Exalted, has come here with the broadest meanings: forgiveness and mercy, and with them His attribute "al-Wadud" (the Loving). It derives from "wadd," and "wadd" is love. Love requires tenderness toward the one loved in proportion to his need.

To Allah belongs the highest likeness: we see a mother who has two sons: the first is capable and wealthy, who brings her what she wants; and the second is weak and poor. We find the mother's heart is always with this weak, poor one, and the heart of the strong, capable one is moved with compassion toward the poor, weak one.

We find the ancient Arab woman, when asked: "Which of your children do you love most?" answering: "The young one until he grows up; the absent one until he returns; and the sick one until he recovers."

So: love requires tenderness in proportion to need.

Allah says in the Qudsi hadith: "O son of Adam, do not fear any ruler as long as My dominion remains, and My dominion never ends. O son of Adam, do not fear narrowness of provision, for My treasuries are full, and My treasuries never run out. O son of Adam, I created you for worship, so do not play; and I guaranteed your provision, so do not weary yourself. By My might and My majesty, if you are content with what I have apportioned to you, I will ease your heart and body, and you will be honored with Me; and if you are not content with what I have apportioned to you, then by My might and My majesty, I will set the world upon you, and you will run in it like wild beasts run in the wilderness, and nothing from it will come to you except what I have apportioned to you. O son of Adam, I created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation; will a loaf of bread weary Me, which I drive toward you? O son of Adam, do not ask Me for tomorrow's provision as I ask of you tomorrow's deeds. O son of Adam, I love you; so by My right over you, love Me."

This noble hadith shows the extent of Allah's love for His creation, a love that polytheistic hearts cannot comprehend.

1 - Al-Wadud: one of Allah's Beautiful Names, and it is an intensive form, meaning "the Much-Loving." [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/326] And "wadd" means love; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿...The Most Merciful will bring about for them affection (96)﴾ [Maryam], meaning love from Him, and love in the hearts of people...
2 - Saqata 'ala ba'irihi: meaning he came upon it and found it by chance without intending to, and so obtained it. From this is the saying: "Upon the expert you have fallen" (ʿala al-khabir saqatta), said by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in Fath al-Bari [11/108].
3 - Al-Fala: the desert with no water or companion; it is the barren land, because it is cut off ("fulia") from all good or weaned and isolated [Lisan al-Arab].
4 - Agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [6308, 6309] and by Muslim in his Sahih [2744] from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. The wording is al-Bukhari's.
5 - La yanfad: does not end. Nafida, yanfadu, nafadan and nafadan: it was exhausted and cut off, leaving nothing of it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah remains (96)﴾ [al-Nahl]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end (54)﴾ [Sad]. That is, it is a lasting provision with no cessation. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]
6 - Al-Rakd: running and sprinting. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they perceived Our punishment, behold, they fled from it running (12)﴾ [al-Anbiya] meaning they run and flee, a metaphor for fear and extreme terror. And rakd also means striking with the foot, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Strike with your foot... (42)﴾ [Sad], meaning strike with it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]
7 - Al-barriyya: the desert; its plural is al-barari; and al-barr is the opposite of the sea. [See: Mukhtar al-Sihah, root b-r-r]
8 - Lam a'yaa bi-khalqihinna: I was not incapable of it, nor did I find it too hard to perfect; al-i'ya' means fatigue and weariness [from Lisan al-Arab].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 91:

Then, after that, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, relates the words of the people of Madyan in reply to Shu'ayb (peace be upon him):

﴿They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and we see you among us as weak. Were it not for your tribe (ruhț), we would have stoned you, and you are not mighty against us."﴾ (11:91)

This resembles the words of the polytheists of Quraysh to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they said:

﴿"Our hearts are in coverings against what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you there is a barrier..."﴾ (41:5)

Faith requires a heart not filled with falsehood, so that it may receive it well. As for hearts filled with falsehood, they are unable to receive faith, unless the intellects empty those hearts of falsehood, and the intellects weigh both truth and falsehood, and then permit into the hearts what they have been convinced of.

For this reason, we find that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, seals upon hearts filled with disbelief, so that disbelief does not leave them and faith does not enter them.

The people of Madyan were not content with declaring disbelief; rather, they threatened Shu'ayb and said: ﴿"...we see you among us as weak. Were it not for your tribe, we would have stoned you, and you are not mighty against us."﴾ (11:91). This threat carries a challenge, as if they thought they had the power to destroy him, because they hated his life. They put forward a feeble argument, namely that his tribe, i.e., his people and family, since the rahț (ruhț) are the group whose number of members ranges between three and ten, were still worshipping idols, and that this tribe would be angered by any harm that befell Shu'ayb. They forgot that He who sent Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) must protect him, and by this forgetting they fulfilled the will of Allah, glory be to Him, that disbelief be made to serve faith.

An example of this is the remaining of the Prophet's (ﷺ) uncle Abu Talib upon the religion of his people; this matter contributed to protecting Muhammad (ﷺ) in terms of apparent means.

1 - Al-fiqh (understanding): comprehension. Faqiha, yafqahu, fahuwa faqih: he became a learned, understanding person. Fiqh as a technical term (in the sense of al-fiqh): the science of the rulings of acts of worship and transactions, a branch of the religious sciences. Allah says: ﴿You do not understand their glorification...﴾ (17:44), i.e., you do not comprehend it. And He says: ﴿that they may gain understanding of the religion...﴾ (9:122), i.e., that they may study the rulings of the religion and learn them. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/86].

2 - Al-rahț (ruhț): a group of men fewer than ten, and the rahț of a man is his clan and tribe; it has no singular from its own root. Allah says: ﴿Were it not for your tribe, we would have stoned you...﴾ (11:91), i.e., were it not for your clan of men, we would have stoned you. And His saying: ﴿nine men of a company (tis'at rahț)...﴾ (27:48) is an idafa of the thing to what specifies it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/278].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, after that brings the response of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, to his people; so He says:

﴿He said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more esteemed by you than Allah? And you have taken Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do."﴾ (92)

Here Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, asks in disapproval: Have you placed my kinsfolk on one side of the scale and the might of Allah, exalted is He, on the other? Have you given precedence to your fear of my kinsfolk over your fear of Allah?! Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, did not heed their pride in their kinsfolk in the face of his pride in his Lord, because he had already declared his reliance upon Allah, and because he knows that might belongs to Allah, exalted is He, first and last.

Nor were they content with taking pride in their kinsfolk instead of taking pride in Allah; rather, they cast the thought of believing in Allah behind their backs. For Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, says to them: ﴿And you have taken Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded...﴾ (92) [Hud]. That is: they did not make Allah, glory be to Him, before them, so they paid no heed to the might of Allah nor to the protection of Allah; and they gave some of His creation a might above the might of Allah.

And he did not say "ẓihriyyan" (ظهريا) as a relative adjective derived from "al-ẓahr" (الظهر, the back). When we form a nisba (نسب, relative adjective), changes occur: when we form it from "al-Yaman" we say "Yamani" and also "Yamani" [with the variant form]; so the nisba here is to "ẓahr" in the sense of that which is forgotten and abandoned, for when you say, "You threw so-and-so behind your back," meaning you put him far from the scene of events, did not reckon with him, and gave him no account. Thus, changes occur in the field of nisba.

Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, reminds them with his words: ﴿...Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do (92)﴾ [Hud]. That is: everything you say or do is recorded against you, because the Truth, glory be to Him, is not hidden from Him anything. We have already known that speech falls within the scope of deed; every occurrence is called "deed," the deed of the tongue is speech, and the deed of the other limbs is action.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, has honoured speech because it is the first means of making Him known.

1 - Ẓihriyy (ظهري): that which is forgotten and abandoned behind the back. It is said: he made him ẓihriyy, i.e., made him a forgotten, neglected thing. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you have taken Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded...(92)﴾ [Hud], meaning: you forgot Allah and His rights over you [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/419]..
2 - Muhit (المحيط): one of the Beautiful Names of Allah, meaning the one who controls everything. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿...And Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers (19)﴾ [al-Baqarah], meaning: He has control over them, and they cannot escape from Him or flee [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/178]..
3 - Nisba (نسب) is one of the branches of the science of ṣarf (morphology)..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 93:

The Truthful One (Allah, exalted is He) says, after that, what came on the tongue of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him):

﴿And O my people, act according to your station; indeed, I am acting. You will know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. And watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher.﴾ (1):

So Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) is at the point of opposition, because Allah the Exalted is, in his view, mightier than his kinsmen; and by his reliance on his Lord he has taken refuge in a strong pillar. With this faith he declares to them: Do whatever is within your power. What is within your power is what is within the power of humans, and I will act within my power. I am not alone; rather, Allah, glorified and exalted, is with me. Your emerging strength will never rise above the absolute power of Allah.

Whatever you do to oppose this reform to which I call you, He who sent me will not forsake me. And as long as you wish to take the same stand as the earlier nations who confronted the waves of heavenly reform, Allah defeated them with the Cry, with the Quake, with the violent wind (2), and with being struck by any of these things. He said to them: Act according to your station, and beware of imagining that I am seeking your favour. I am upon clear proof from my Lord, but I love good for you, and I want reform for you.

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) did not say this out of weakness; rather, he said it in reply to their words: ﴿And indeed we see you among us as weak, and were it not for your kinsmen we would have stoned you...﴾ (91) [Hud]. He displayed to them his station, derived from the strength of the One who sent him, saying: ﴿O my people, act according to your station; indeed, I am acting...﴾ (93) [Hud].

Thus he made clear to them: I will not stand with folded hands, for I will act according to my station. And ﴿...you will know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. And watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher﴾ (93) [Hud]. That is: the future will show which of us is upon the truth and which of us is upon error, to whom victory and dominance will belong, and upon whom disgrace will come; that is, he will feel the contempt and humiliation of his own self and suffer exposure before creation; and which of us is the liar and which is upon the truth.

The next verse had to come:

﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the Cry seized those who did wrong, so they became, in their homes, prostrate corpses﴾ (94).

1 - Al-makanah (station): elevated rank, dignity and deliberateness. Allah says: ﴿Say, O my people, act according to your station...﴾ (135) [al-An'am], i.e., with dignity, deliberation and insight. It is also read as "ʿalā makānātikum" in the plural. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/232].
2 - Al-rīḥ al-ṣarṣar (the violent wind): al-ṣarr and al-ṣarṣar are extremely cold; it was said also that it is extremely loud. Al-Zajjaj said: al-ṣarr and al-ṣarra are severe cold [as stated by Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-'Arab].
3 - Al-rahṭ (kinsmen): a group fewer than ten men; the rahṭ of a man is his clan and tribe, having no singular from its own root. Allah says: ﴿And were it not for your kinsmen, we would have stoned you...﴾ (91) [Hud], i.e., were it not for your clan of men, we would have stoned you. His saying: ﴿nine kinsmen...﴾ (48) [al-Naml] is an idafah of a thing to what explains it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/278].
4 - Al-ṣayḥah (the Cry): the noun of one instance of ṣiyāḥ, which is intense sound. Al-ṣayḥah is the punishment accompanied by an intense sound. Allah says: ﴿On the day they hear the Cry in truth; that is the day of coming forth﴾ (42) [Qaf]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
5 - Jathama juthūman: he remained in his place, clinging to the ground. Allah says: ﴿...so they became, in their homes, prostrate﴾ (94) [Hud], an allusion to their death in their state, so they are lifeless, clinging to the ground. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 94 (part 1 of 2):

We note that Allah, the Glorified, has presented two expressions in this surah, one with *wa* (و) and the other with *fa* (ف).

The first is ﴿And when Our command came...﴾ (11:94), in the story of two other messengers.

The second is ﴿So when Our command came...﴾ (11:66) [Hud], in the story of two of the messengers.(1)

The story of Shu'ayb is one of the two stories in which ﴿And when Our command came﴾ occurs, and he did not use *fa* (ف), because *fa* (فاء), as we know, requires immediate sequence with no time gap. In the language it is called *fa' al-ta'qib* (the *fa* of immediate sequence), as in the words of Allah, the Glorified: ﴿Then He caused him to die and buried him(2)﴾ (80:21) [Abasa].

As for *thumma* (ثم), it indicates a different sequence, namely sequence after a time gap, as in the words of Allah, the Glorified: ﴿Then, when He wills, He will resurrect him(3)﴾ (80:22) [Abasa]. The *fa* (ف) has come once in the story of the people of Lot, because Allah, the Glorified, specified the appointed time at which the punishment would descend, and said: ﴿...Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾ (11:81) [Hud]. So it was necessary for *fa* to precede the account of their punishment, and He said: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hardened clay, layered(4)﴾ (11:82) [Hud].

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, Allah, the Glorified, said: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him...﴾ (11:94) [Hud]. He did not mention a promise, nor did He specify the time of the punishment.

Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿And when Our command came...﴾ (11:94) [Hud]. Every command requires a commander, a one who is commanded, and a thing commanded.

The commander here is Allah, the Glorified, who is capable of carrying out what He commands. No one commanded dares to oppose what Allah, the Glorified, commands; the whole universe submits to the command of its Creator.

Therefore, when Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, informs us that punishment has come upon a people, this means that the command has been issued, and the punishment cannot fail to arrive. Failure arises only from a command issued to one who may not obey it, whereas punishment cannot disobey, because it is subjugated and has no choice.

The speaker here is Allah, the Glorified, the Possessor of the cosmic command and the legislative command. When Allah, the Glorified, decrees a ruling and records it in the Qur'an, be certain that it will occur without doubt, because the cosmic matter comes from Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, and does not fail or differ with His will, the Glorified. A legislative ruling brings happiness to the one who applies it and misery to the one who opposes it.

Allah, the Glorified, gives us an example of this in the story of the mother of Moses. He, the Majestic, says: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses: Suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river...﴾ (28:7) [al-Qasas]. Human logic says: how can we tell a woman, "If you fear for your son, cast him into the sea"? How can we save him from a probable death to a certain death?

Although this was contrary to customary patterns, the mother of Moses hastened to carry out the command of Allah, the Glorified, because the commands of Allah given by inspiration to those brought near (to Him) do not meet any opposing thought in the mind.

As Allah commanded her to cast her infant into the river, she said(5)... as He says: ﴿When We inspired to your mother what is inspired: Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river...﴾ (20:38-39) [Ta-Ha]. Likewise, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, commanded the river to carry the chest, with Moses inside it, to the shore. Therefore, the certainty of the mother of Moses that Allah's commands do not fail made her hasten to carry out what Allah had commanded her.

Allah, the Glorified, wants to increase faith, that is, to increase it in the hearts of His servants. Suppose that Allah has decreed a matter or commanded a command, and then the universe did not conform to what Allah commanded. What would be the position of people?

Since the Lord of Might, the Glorified, has spoken, what He commanded must happen. So when Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the victorious﴾ (37:173) [al-Saffat],

then victory must belong to the soldiers of Allah. If they are defeated, understand that the condition of being Allah's soldiers has failed, and that an element of soldiering has failed, which is obedience.

An example of this is those who disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to remain on the mountain on the day of Uhud. They disobeyed the command of the Messenger (ﷺ). So what would happen if they had achieved victory despite this disobedience?

Thus, the Muslims who lost a quality of their soldiering to Allah were defeated.

The Qur'anic matter and the cosmic matter must meet, because the speaker of the Qur'an is the Possessor of the laws of the universe, the Glorified, the Exalted.

And because the people of Madyan here have declared disbelief, the punishment must come upon them.

Allah, the Glorified, called the punishment here *al-sayha* (الصيحة, the Cry); He said: ﴿...And the Cry seized those who did wrong, so they became in their homes prostrate, dead﴾ (11:94) [Hud].

In Surat al-A'raf, Allah, the Glorified, called the punishment that befell them *al-rajfa* (الرجفة, the Quake); He said: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became in their home prostrate﴾ (7:91) [al-A'raf].

He called it in the story of the people of 'Ad: ﴿...by a violent, furious wind(6)﴾ (69:6) [al-Haqqa]; and He called it *al-khasf* (الخسف, the sinking into the earth) in the punishment of Qarun.

Among the greatness of the divine direction is that the punishment selected only the disbelieving people and did not strike those who believed, as the words of Allah, the Glorified, show: ﴿We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him...﴾ (11:94) [Hud]. Only a capable, powerful God can do this, one who directs affairs as He wills, the Glorified.

The word *najjayna* (نجينا, "We saved"): it derives from *al-najat* (النجاة, deliverance), meaning that someone reaches a *najwa* (نجوة), which is a high place. The Arabs had long known the violence of water. They used to live in Yemen, then the flood scattered them, in confirmation of the words of Allah, the Glorified: ﴿There was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and the left. "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord." But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of *al-'Arim* (العرم, the dam-burst), and We exchanged for their two gardens two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote trees.﴾ (34:15-16) [Saba']. Thus the Arabs dispersed from Yemen and spread across the Arabian Peninsula. They feared water, although it is the secret of life, and they preferred the hardship of searching for water to drink for themselves and their livestock, rather than living beside water. From this enmity toward water came the word *naja* (نجا), meaning that he climbed to a high place.

The word *naja* is used in every situation in which a person escapes from a sudden danger. One says: "He escaped from the fire," "He escaped from the enemy," "He escaped from the predatory animal." All of these are derived from *al-najwa*, meaning the high place. The verb *naja* is used as: *naja fulan* (نجا فلان, "so-and-so escaped"), when his own strength helps him to save himself from punishment.

But if his strength is unable to save him from punishment, he needs someone to save him, and one says *anjahu* (أنجاه, "he saved him"), when the matter requires effort and difficult treatment in order for success to be achieved, and the act is attributed to Allah; so He said *najjayna* ("We saved").

In such a matter, Allah uses the plural pronoun, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, We revealed it in the Night of Decree(13)﴾ (97:1) [al-Qadr]. So everything in which an act of Allah, the Glorified, occurs, Allah uses the plural pronoun *inna* (إنا, "We").

But if the thing is related to an attribute of the Divine Essence, Allah uses the singular pronoun *ana* (أنا, "I"), as in His words: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah...﴾ (20:14) [Ta-Ha].

Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him, because Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said to his people: ﴿O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting...﴾ (11:93) [Hud]. The action of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, contained sincerity and the determination of reliance on Allah. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, saved him and those who believed with him. He, the Glorified, wants from worship only that one turn to Him with a pure, sincere intention. When the servant turns to Allah with a sincere intention, Allah, the Glorified, gives the servant ease and helps him to feel secure in performing any action.

Mere faith in Allah, the Exalted, and turning to Him with truthfulness and sincerity, opens before the servant horizons of success and elevation. The key is in the hand of the servant, because Allah, the Glorified, has said in the sacred hadith: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it."(14)

So the key is in the hand of the servant.

Allah, the Glorified, is the One who said: "Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit."

Thus Allah, the Glorified, leaves the matter of drawing near to Him to the servant, and when the servant draws near to Allah, the Exalted, He draws nearer to the servant more and more.

Then Allah, the Glorified, says in the sacred hadith: "Whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running,"(15) because walking may tire the servant, but nothing tires Allah, the Glorified, ever, because He is exalted above that.

So Allah, the Glorified, wants us to purify intention in joining the company of Allah, the Exalted, so that our Lord, the Glorified, may bestow upon us some of the attributes of His majesty and the attributes of His beauty.(16)

Look at our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) in the cave. Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us..."﴾ (9:40) [al-Tawba]. That is, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade his companion from grief on the basis of the companionship of Allah, the Glorified. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq must have said something indicating grief, because grief did not come to him from himself, but from a cosmic law, when he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If one of them were to look beneath his feet, he would see us." But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak of the cosmic law; he spoke of the absolute power of the Creator, the Glorified, and said: "What do you think of two whom Allah is the third?"(17)

The companionship of Allah conferred upon them something of His majesty and beauty. Allah, the Glorified, is not perceived by sight, and He perceives the sights.(18)

Allah, the Glorified, saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Him, the Glorified. Mercy means that nothing afflicts you.

An example of this: a person is treated and is healed, and another time Allah protects him from the disease.

Therefore, pay attention to the truth that the Qur'an has come with two things: healing and mercy. If there is a disease and you return to the method of Allah, then Allah, the Glorified, heals it, and the mercy is that the disease does not afflict you from the beginning.

As for those who did wrong, the Cry seized them. In another verse He, the Glorified, says: ﴿And the Cry seized those who did wrong...﴾ (11:67) [Hud].

In this verse Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿And the Cry seized those who did wrong...﴾ (11:94) [Hud].

Because the Qur'an, in its majority, came in the dialect of Quraysh, not to elevate Quraysh, but because the language of Quraysh had been refined from all the Arab tribes; it possesses the choicest language of all the tribes. Yet this does not mean that the other tribes should be erased. Therefore some of the dialects of other tribes came in the Qur'an, so that sovereignty in Islam would not be given to Quraysh as it had sovereignty in the pre-Islamic period. Hence it brings the dialects of other tribes: sometimes it uses the feminine marker *ta'* (تاء التأنيث), and sometimes it does not.

Feminine gender is either real (حقيقي)(19) or metaphorical (مجازي)(20). Real feminine is the counterpart of the masculine, as in *al-mar'a* (المرأة, "the woman"). Metaphorical feminine is like *al-sayha* (الصيحة, "the cry") and *al-hujra* (الحجرة, "the room"). The Arab tribes differed regarding the metaphorical feminine: sometimes the *ta'* appears and sometimes it does not.(21)

If there is a separation between the verb and the subject, then the separation stands in place of the feminine marker. So He, the Glorified, says: ﴿And the Cry seized those who did wrong...﴾ (11:67) [Hud]. It is as if the Cry has the capacity to seize by what the sender of the Cry has deposited in it of the power of seizing; its seizing is painful and severe.

Allah, the Glorified, concludes the noble verse with His words: ﴿...So they became in their homes prostrate﴾ (11:94) [Hud].

We note that for every punishment, Allah, the Glorified, sets a specific time, which is the morning, as in His words: ﴿...Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾ (11:81) [Hud].

And as the words of the Truth: ﴿...Evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾ (37:177) [al-Saffat].

The morning is the time of the attack upon the heedless one whom sleep has not yet left, like the night visitors who seize people just before daytime.

Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿...So they became in their homes prostrate﴾ (11:94) [Hud]. He did not say "in their house" (singular), because some of them may not be in their house, but in another place for a visit or for trade.

An example of this is the story of Abu Righal, who was in Mecca, but the stone that killed him by the will of Allah, the Glorified, fell upon him in the *baq*...

---

1. They are the Prophet Salih and the Prophet Lut, peace be upon them both. Allah says: ﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him...﴾ (11:66) [Hud]. And Allah says: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hardened clay, layered﴾ (11:82) [Hud].
As for [*wa-lamma jaa amrunaa*, "and when Our command came"], it came in the case of the Prophet Hud in His words: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him...﴾ (11:58) [Hud], and likewise the Prophet Shu'ayb in His words: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him...﴾ (11:94) [Hud].

2. *Qabarahu* and *aqbarahu*: he buried him in a grave. This verb is transitive by itself and also transitive with the *hamza*. Allah says: ﴿Then He caused him to die and buried him﴾ (80:21) [Abasa]. The plural of *qabr* (قبر) is *qubur*. Allah says: ﴿And when the graves are scattered﴾ (82:4) [al-Infitar]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/95, adapted].

3. *Ansharahu*: he gave it life and brought it into existence. His words, "Then, when He wills, He will resurrect him" (80:22) [Abasa], mean: He will raise him from his grave. Allah says: ﴿And We revived therewith a dead land﴾ (43:11) [al-Zukhruf], meaning: We gave it life with rain water, because it had been dead before. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

4. *Al-sijjil*: hardened clay. *Al-mandud*: that which falls upon them in succession, regularly ordered. Allah says: ﴿And the palm trees with ranks of fruit﴾ (50:10) [Qaf], meaning arranged in order. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/304].

5. *Al-yamm*: the sea, or the sweet river. Allah says: ﴿So We drowned them in the sea﴾ (7:136) [al-A'raf], and His words: ﴿Cast him into the sea...﴾ (20:39) [Ta-Ha] mean the sweet river. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, p. 372, vol. 2].

6. *Al-sirr* and *al-sarsar*: intense cold. Allah says: ﴿Like a wind in which is a cold...﴾ (3:117) [Al 'Imran]. *Al-rih*: moving air in the atmosphere; its root is *rawh*, the *waw* was changed to *ya'* because of the preceding kasra. Its plural is *riyah*, and it is also pluralized as *arwah*, according to the original form. Allah says: ﴿...By a violent, furious wind﴾ (69:6) [al-Haqqa], meaning: severe and destructive, in the manner of metaphor, as if it were a tyrannical, arrogant, and rebellious man. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

7. Saba': the name of a man from whom several tribes that arose in Yemen descended. A large city in Yemen was named after him, and it was the capital of the king of Yemen. Allah says: ﴿...And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news﴾ (27:22) [al-Naml]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/299].

8. *Al-sayl*: abundant water that flows and runs over the earth. *Sayl al-'Arim* means the flowing of the dam, which were dams in Yemen, or a violent rain flood. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/340].

9. *Al-khamt*: every plant that has bitterness and sourness, which the soul loathes. Allah says: ﴿...Two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote trees﴾ (34:16) [Saba']. When Allah was angry with Saba', He made their food these things, and that is a metaphor for extreme poverty. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/211].

10. *Al-athl*: a tall tree with straight wood and many branches, with fine leaves and a red bitter seed that is not eaten. Allah says: ﴿...Two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote trees﴾ (34:16) [Saba'], a metaphor for narrowness of living and severe poverty. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/7].

11. *Al-sidr*: the nabq tree, a thorny tree that bears fruit with little sweetness; its singular is *sidra*. It is a metaphor for narrowness of living, for Allah restricted their provision because they did not give thanks. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/307].

12. Whatever covers you has overtaken you. One says *yadhhamuhum*, meaning: it surprises them. See Lisan al-'Arab.

13. *Anzalnahu*: We began the sending down of the Great Qur'an. *Laylat al-Qadr*: the Night of Honor and Greatness. [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Husnayn Makhluf].

14. The full text of the hadith: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running." From the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

15. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [7405] and by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad [2/315], from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

16 - The attributes of beauty (jamal) are those that express mercy, forgiveness, security and peace, such as al-Rahim (the Most Merciful), al-Ghafur (the Most Forgiving), al-Salam (the Source of Peace), and al-Mu'min (the Granter of Security). The attributes of majesty (jalal) are those that express domination, overpowering might and harm, such as al-Qahhar (the Subduer), al-Jabbar (the Compeller), al-Darr (the Afflicter), and al-Mumit (the Causer of Death)..

17 - Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [4663] and by Muslim in his Sahih [2381], from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him..

18 - The Lord of Majesty, glorified is He, says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord. There is no god but He, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Guardian over all things. (102) No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware. (103)﴾ [al-An'am]..

19 - The true feminine (al-mu'annath al-haqiqi) is that which gives birth and reproduces, even if its reproduction is by means of eggs and hatching. The word of a true feminine must carry a feminine marker, either apparent or implied, such as Fatimah, Layla, Hind, 'usfurah (a little bird, feminine), baqarah (a cow), etc. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb..."﴾ (35) [Al 'Imran], and His saying: ﴿A female ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings..."﴾ (18) [al-Naml: 18]..

20 - The metaphorical feminine (al-mu'annath al-majazi) is that which neither gives birth nor reproduces. It may end with an apparent feminine marker, such as waraqah (a leaf) and safinah (a ship), etc., or with an implied one, such as dar (house) and shams (sun). There is no way to recognize the metaphorical feminine except through what has been transmitted from the Arabs by hearing (al-sama')..

21 - Feminizing the verb and leaving it unfeminized is permissible when the agent (al-fa'il) is a true feminine and is not directly attached to the governing verb, that is, when a separator has come between the verb and the feminine agent. Such as His saying: ﴿Then one of the two women came to him, walking shyly. She said: "My father invites you..."﴾ (25) [al-Qasas], and His saying: ﴿When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them...﴾ (10) [al-Mumtahanah]. The same applies when the agent is a metaphorical feminine, as in His saying: ﴿Do they await only the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come...﴾ (18) [Muhammad], and when the agent is a broken plural (jam' taksir), as in His saying: ﴿The Bedouins said: "We have believed..."﴾ (14) [al-Hujurat], and His saying: ﴿And women in the city said...﴾ (30) [Yusuf]. There are many other details, which may be consulted in "al-Nahw al-Wafi" by 'Abbas Hasan [4/586, 587], and "al-Nahw al-Musaffa" by Dr. Muhammad 'Id [pp. 402-406]..

22 - Allah, glorified is He, has said: ﴿And an enduring punishment came upon them early in the morning. (38)﴾ [al-Qamar]. Al-bukrah is the early part of the day. It is also used to express hastening to a matter at any time [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Then Allah, glorified is He, says, after that, about the people of Madyan who were seized by the Cry:

﴿As if they had never prospered therein. Yet away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away!﴾ (95)

That is: anyone who passes by the people of Madyan after that will find that it is as if they had never existed.

Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and become beautified, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes upon it...﴾ (24) [Yunus]. So the human being who has advanced until he reached many civilizations, to the point that he may order coffee by pressing a button on a machine, will find that when Allah, glorified is He, wills, He removes all of that in the blink of an eye.

This luxurious life, in which a person enjoys being served, is other than Paradise, where a person obtains whatever he desires the moment the thought occurs to him.

Here Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿As if they had never prospered therein...﴾ (95) [Hud]. The root of the word "ghina" (prosperity/dwelling) includes *ghina'* (with a kasra on the ghayn), which is what singers sing, and *ghina'* (with a fatha on the ghayn), which leads to something that makes you independent of something else. Wealth in money suffices one from what is in people's hands.

Likewise, song: the ear hears a great deal, and the eye reads a great deal, but a person repeats only the words that please him, and the melody in a manner that pleases him. So song is the pleasing melody that makes you independent of others.

And *ghina'*, that is, residing in a place that makes you independent of going to another place, and settling in this place which makes you independent of the rest of the places.

So the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿As if they had never prospered therein...﴾ (95) [Hud] means: as if they had never dwelt here and had never been content with this place instead of any other.

Allah, glorified is He, says in another place of the Noble Qur'an: ﴿...Some of them are still standing and some are harvested﴾ (100) [Hud]. That is: the ruins are still standing with what they contain of stones and traces, like the temples of the ancient Egyptians. When you visit them, you do not find all the temples intact; rather you find a column standing, another lying on the ground, and a door that is not intact. Had they all been harvested, they would have disappeared completely, but these are standing remains, and some of them have been effaced.

This proves to us the truth of the Qur'anic report that there were civilizations, for if they had all gone, we would not have known that civilizations had preceded us.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿...Away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away!﴾ (95) [Hud]. The word *alā* ("ألا"), as we have known before, is an "opening particle" so that the listener turns and listens, so that heedlessness does not take him from the important matter the speaker is speaking about, and so that the listener receives the whole speech as one who benefits from it.

The word *bu'dan* ("بعدا") is not a supplication against the people of Madyan to be removed, because they had already perished. The root of the word *bu'dan* is *b-'-d*, and it is used in two ways: sometimes you mean separation, and separation is a parting that leads to a hoped-for meeting. But if it leads to a certain parting, it does not exist; therefore it is followed by: ﴿...just as Thamud were taken away!﴾ (95) [Hud]. It indicates a distance after which there is no meeting, except when Allah, glorified is He, gathers people on the Day of Resurrection.

The poet says:
*They say: "Do not be far away," while they bury me,*
*And where is the place of distance except my place?*
This is the distance to which a person goes and does not return.

Why did Allah, glorified is He, single out Thamud for mention here, when He had already said about other peoples: "Away with..."?

Because the Cry came upon Thamud, and in that way they agreed in the manner of punishment.

Here the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, with Madyan ends. We note that it has a connection with messengers such as Musa, peace be upon him, just as the people of Lut had a connection with Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

Thus we know that there were messengers who were contemporaries, that is: each of them was sent to a particular environment and a particular place. And since those to whom they were sent are all servants of Allah, He sent to each environment a messenger whose method suits the defects of that environment.

Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was the paternal uncle of Lut, peace be upon him, and Musa, peace be upon him, was the son-in-law of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. Musa went to the people of Madyan before Allah sent him to Pharaoh.

We know that places in ancient times were isolated, and communication between them was difficult; each community lived in its location and might know nothing of the other locations, and each community's disease might differ from the others'.

But when Allah, glorified is He, willed to send Muhammad (ﷺ) as the final messenger, Allah, glorified is He, knew from eternity that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would coincide with the advancement of humanity, and the diseases had become unified.

What happens now in any place in the world is transmitted to us by satellites in a few seconds; therefore there had to be the final Messenger (ﷺ).

As for the multiplicity of messengers and the multiplicity of scenes for each messenger in the Qur'an, it is not repetition, as superficial people imagine, because the basic purpose of Qur'anic narrative is that Allah, glorified is He, sent it to strengthen the Messenger (ﷺ). The verses were descending from the lowest heaven with revelation to suit the situation in which the Messenger (ﷺ) needed the strengthening of the heart.

Allah, glorified is He, shows His Messenger (ﷺ) that he should remember his brothers among the messengers, what happened to them with their peoples, and Allah's victory for them in the end. When Allah, glorified is He, wished to narrate a well-woven story, He brought Surat Yusuf.

Thus there is no repetition in the Qur'an; rather every scene came to suit its place in strengthening the Messenger (ﷺ).

We may note that the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, with his people had to end only with a scene from the story of Musa, peace be upon him, who was Shu'ayb's son-in-law.

It is noticeable that Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned here two scenes from the story of Musa, peace be upon him:

The first scene: his sending with the signs to Pharaoh.

The second scene: the end of Pharaoh, not with Musa, peace be upon him, but with Allah, glorified is He, on the Day of Resurrection. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them into the Fire, and wretched is the destination to which they are brought. And they are followed in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection—wretched is the gift that is given.﴾ (98–99) [Hud].

Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had the task of strengthening the heart of Musa, peace be upon him, against panic, when he announced to him that he feared Pharaoh's people would kill him because he had killed a man among them. So Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said to him what Allah, glorified is He, mentioned in His saying: ﴿...You have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾ (25) [al-Qasas]. Thus he strengthened him and prepared for him a life in which he lived in safety for eight or ten years (*hijaj*), in confirmation of the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿He said, "I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it is from you. And I do not wish to burden you. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous." (27) He said, "That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me. And Allah is Witness over what we say."﴾ (28) [al-Qasas]. Thus Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, undertook a task in the story of Musa, peace be upon him.

From this and that, Allah, glorified is He, gives us the lesson that sound human nature has regulations that may coincide with the law of heaven, because Allah, glorified is He, does not prevent human minds from reaching the truth; but minds may reach the truth only after the bitterness of experience, just as Allah, glorified is He, legislated divorce in Islam, and then other non-Muslim lands adopted it after they had suffered its bitter hardship.

And just as Allah, glorified is He, prohibited wine, and then science proved its harms to health: were we obliged to postpone the command of Allah, exalted is He, until the mind reached those conclusions?

No; because Allah, glorified is He, has sent down in the Qur'an the law of heaven that protects a person from the evil of experience; because He who sent down the Qur'an, glorified is He, is the One who created us, and He is trustworthy over us. And the days have proven the truth of Allah's judgment, exalted is He, in everything He said, as is evident from the fact that non-believers in the Qur'an go to what the Qur'an revealed in order to apply it.

In the story of Musa, peace be upon him, there is a clear example of the will of Allah, glorified is He. Here is Pharaoh, the disbeliever, who raised Musa after he picked him up, so that he might be a comfort to his eye, although Pharaoh used to kill the children of that group.

Then Musa's sister watched her brother, and Allah, glorified is He, returned Musa, peace be upon him, to his mother.

The poet has depicted this situation by saying:
*If you do not find in your sons care*
*From Allah, then the hopeful one has lied and the expectant has been disappointed.*
*So Musa, whom Jibril raised, is a disbeliever,*
*And Musa, whom Pharaoh raised, is a messenger.*

The story of Musa, peace be upon him, has come here in brief, at the beginning and at the end, to show us that Shu'ayb had a role with one of the Messengers of firm resolve, namely Musa, peace be upon him.

Before he was sent, Musa's purpose, peace be upon him, was the water of Madyan, and there occurred what we may find in it a solution to the problems of the two sexes, man and woman, and it is the spearhead directed at Muslim societies, because some want women to display their charms, to seduce young men at the most violent times of adolescence.

But the Qur'an resolves this issue in a simple journey. Let us read Allah's saying, glorified is He, about Musa: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found besides them two women driving back [their flocks]...﴾ (23) [al-Qasas]. That is: they were holding back the livestock from approaching the water. This scene caught Musa's attention, and it was natural for him to ask: "Did you not come here to water the livestock?" And the Qur'an states the natural question: ﴿"What is your matter?"...﴾ (23) [al-Qasas]. Then the answer comes from the two women: ﴿They said, "We cannot water [our flocks] until the shepherds send their animals away; and our father is an elderly man."﴾ (23) [al-Qasas].

Thus we learn that the woman's going out had a cause: the father is an elderly man. The going out of the two women was not for the purpose of competing for the water, but out of necessity. They waited until the shepherds had watered, and indeed they remained veiled and at a distance. Therefore Musa, peace be upon him, stepped forward to perform the role of a man: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them...﴾ (24) [al-Qasas]. This is a characteristic of the general believing society, not a characteristic of a people, nor of kinship, nor of family, but the characteristic of the general believing society.

So when a person sees a woman who has gone out to work, and knows that there is a necessity that compelled her to do so, a Muslim man should meet her need.

I recall that when I went to Makkah in the year 1950 CE, my friend got out of his car in front of a house door. In front of the door there was a wooden board with loaves of dough that had not yet been baked, and he took it to the bakery, then returned it after baking to the same door. He told me: "This is the custom of the people of Makkah: if a person finds a board of unbaked dough, he should do that, because the presence of this board in front of the door indicates that the head of the house is absent."

All of this is derived from the phrase: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them...﴾ (24) [al-Qasas]. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to order the soldiers to knock on doors to ask the people of the houses about their needs.

The third and important matter is that a woman who goes out to a task must not become accustomed to it, but must take it only to the extent of necessity; when she finds an outlet for this necessity, she must hasten to that outlet. For this reason the girl said to her father Shu'ayb: ﴿"O father, hire him; the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one."﴾ (26) [al-Qasas]. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, concludes this situation with a faithful, wise and firm conclusion, saying to Musa: ﴿"I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it is from you..."﴾ (27) [al-Qasas].

Thus Musa, peace be upon him, knows that Shu'ayb does not give away his daughter like this without a dowry; no, there must be a dowry for her, and also her sister becomes forbidden to him.

This story has set out for us principles that resolve all the problems which the opponents of Islam boast about.

And here we find in the West contemporary cries demanding that the woman remain at home to care for the family and children; not because the woman is deficient, but because the perfection of the woman lies in performing the noblest task entrusted

1 - *Ghanā al-qawm fī diyārihim*: their people stayed long in their dwellings. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they were in their homes lying prostrate, (94) as if they had never prospered therein...(95)﴾ [Hud]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root *gh-n-y*].

2 - *Ba'ida, ba'dan wa bu'dan*: perished. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿...Away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away! (95)﴾ [Hud], meaning: destruction for Madyan just as Thamud were destroyed. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root *b-'-d*].

3 - *Ghanā al-qawm fī diyārihim*: their people stayed long in their dwellings. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they were in their homes lying prostrate, (94) as if they had never prospered therein...(95)﴾ [Hud]. And *ghaniyat al-dār bi-ahlihā*: the house was made populous by its people. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We made it a harvested field, as if it had not flourished yesterday...(24)﴾ [Yunus], meaning: as if it had not been inhabited. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root *gh-n-y*].

4 - *Qā'im*: active participle of *qāma*. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿...while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary...(39)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. And His saying: ﴿That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you; some of them are still standing and some are harvested (100)﴾ [Hud], meaning: some of them are still standing, inhabited by their people like a crop, and some have perished and become like harvested crops. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root *q-w-m*].

5 - *Al-atlāl*: plural of *ṭalal*, which is what remains visible of the traces of old dwellings. It is said: the *ṭalal* of everything is its visible trace. [See Lisan al-'Arab].

6 - *Al-rusūm*: plural of *rasm*, which is the remainder of a trace. It is said: it is what clings to the ground of them. The *rasm* of a house is what remains of its traces lying flat on the ground.

7 - *Al-dathūr*: the effacement and erasure of memory; everything that has been erased and whose trace has gone has become *dathar*. [Lisan, adapted].

8 - *Al-shā'ir*: he is Malik ibn al-Rayb al-Mazini, a poet among the witty, literary and bold, who became famous in the early Umayyad period. He witnessed the conquest of Samarqand, became ascetic, and fell ill in Marw; sensing death, he recited his poem, of which this verse is part, and its length is 58 verses, which Abu 'Ali al-Qali cited in full in his *Amali* [3/151–154]. He died in the year 60 AH. See al-A'lam by al-Zirikli [5/261].

9 - *Al-bu'd*: destruction; *ba'ida*: perished. So His saying, exalted is He: [...Away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away! (95)] [Hud], meaning: destruction for Madyan just as Thamud were destroyed. *Al-bu'd* is the opposite of nearness. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts!...(38)﴾ [al-Zukhruf], meaning: the measure of the distance of one of them from the other. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

10 - The Lord of Might, glorified is He, said: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming [Cry] (5)﴾ [al-Haqqah], meaning: they were destroyed by the Cry which exceeded its limit in its strength. *Al-tughyān* is exceeding the limit. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its limit, We carried you in the sailing ship (11)﴾ [al-Haqqah], meaning: it increased and exceeded its limit, drowning the lands. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/402].

11 - Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that by it We steady your heart. And there has come to you in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers (120)﴾ [Hud]. *Thabata al-amr*: it became firm and settled, the opposite of shaking and disturbance. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word...(27)﴾ [Ibrahim], meaning: He strengthens their faith through the correct, firm word, which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; that is a moral steadfastness. [See Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/105].

12 - *Al-hijjah* (with a kasra on the ha'): the complete year of twelve months; its plural is *hijaj*. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿...on condition that you serve me for eight years...(27)﴾ [al-Qasas], meaning: eight complete years. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

13 - *Ajara fulān fulānan ajran*: he rewarded him for a work or became his hired worker; the phrase of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿...on condition that you serve me for eight years...(27)﴾ [al-Qasas] has been explained in both senses. The dowry is metaphorically called *ajr*. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give them their due compensation (*ujūrahunna*)...(24)﴾ [al-Nisa'], meaning: their dowries. And He said: ﴿Then he will have his reward with his Lord...(112)﴾ [al-Baqarah], meaning: the reward of his deed. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/8].

14 - The Lord of Might, glorified is He, said: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son," while they did not perceive (9)﴾ [al-Qasas].

15 - Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group among them: slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was among the corrupters (4)﴾ [al-Qasas].

16 - Almighty God says: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty. Indeed, she was about to disclose him, had We not fortified her heart so that she would be among the believers. And she said to his sister, "Follow him," so she watched him from afar while they did not perceive. And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses beforehand, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will nurse him for you, and they will be sincere toward him?" So We returned him to his mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve, and that she would know that the promise of God is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Qasas]

17 - Musa the Samiri, whom Jibril raised, opposed his Lord's command through sedition, so he was isolated socially and the punishment was decreed upon him. This is unlike Musa the Messenger, peace be upon him.

18 - Warada, yaridu, wardan and wurudan: to arrive at a place or approach it, whether one enters it or not. Warada al-ma' means he went to the water, reached it and arrived at it. Its active participle is warid, and its passive participle is mawrud [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
Ummatan min al-nas: a large group of people from among them [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Makhluf].
Tadhuddan: they keep their sheep away from the water [Kalimat al-Qur'an].

19 - Ma khatbukuma: what is your affair? Or what is your aim? [Kalimat al-Qur'an].

20 - Yusdir al-ri'a: the shepherds turn their livestock away from the water [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
Al-sudur: returning and departing. It is said: he came to the well, then departed from it, meaning he returned. Sudur his animals: he brought them back after they had come to water [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

21 - Shakha al-insan yashaykhu: he grew old, or signs of old age appeared on him. The term shaykh is applied to one who has passed fifty years of age. It has many plurals, among them ashyakh, shuyukh and mashayikh. Of these, the one occurring in the Qur'an is the plural shuyukh. God Almighty says: ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become elders...﴾ [Ghafir (40:67)] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/363].

22 - Istamra'a al-ta'am: he found the food wholesome, meaning good and palatable. Istamra'a al-shay': he loved it and sought more of it [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted.

23 - Al-mahr: the dowry, its plural is muhur, and it is a charity whose plural is sadaqat. God Almighty says: ﴿And give the women their dowries graciously...﴾ [al-Nisa' (4:4)]. In Fiqh al-Sunnah [2/218], it is said: "The Sharia has not set a limit for its minimum or its maximum. People differ in wealth and poverty, and vary in ease and hardship, and every locality has its customs and traditions. All the texts indicate that the dowry need only be something of value, regardless of whether it is little or much. It is permissible to pay the dowry promptly or defer it, or to pay part of it promptly and defer the rest, according to people's customs and conventions."

24 - Combining two sisters is one of the prohibitions of temporary prohibition, which is lifted when its causes cease. This occurs by divorcing the sister with a final (irrevocable) divorce and after her waiting period has ended. The second case is her death. The evidence for this prohibition is the saying of God Almighty: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers and your daughters...﴾ up to His saying ﴿...and that you combine two sisters, except what has already occurred. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nisa' (4:23)]. See Fiqh al-Sunnah [2/169].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 96:

We know that when verses (ayat) occur in the Qur'an, they refer to three kinds of things: cosmic verses (ayat kawniyyah) that are witnessed by all people and seen by everyone, such as the verses of the night and the day, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the earth that is humbled, so that when water descends upon it, it stirs and swells(١). All of these are cosmic verses that draw the intellect to reflect that behind this precise cosmos there is a geometric design established by a capable God.

And there are verses that come to demonstrate the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from God, and these are the miracles, such as the she-camel of Thamud, which was a visible sign(٢), and the healing by Jesus, peace be upon him, of the blind from birth and the leper(٣), by God's permission.

Then there are the verses of rulings (ayat al-ahkam), which explain the requirements of the method (al-manhaj) through "do" and "do not".

Here the Truthful One, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ [Hud: 96].

So there are verses that indicate his truthfulness, and above that a manifest authority (sultan), which is either an authority of force that overpowers the dominant one, or an authority of proof that persuades the intellect.

The authority of force may subdue the one who dominates, but it does not subdue the heart, and God, glorified is He, wants hearts, not shells (qawalib). Therefore, He, glorified is He, said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe. If We willed, We would send down to them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3–4]. So: the Truthful One, glorified is He, seeks hearts, not shells, hearts that come to God, the Exalted, willingly without compulsion.

Therefore the more important authority is the authority of proof, because it persuades a person to act. Moses, peace be upon him, did not have an authority of force to display; rather he had the authority of proof, and this is the saying of the Truthful One, glorified is He: ﴿Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, obligated not to say about God except the truth. I have come to you with a clear evidence from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel"﴾ [al-A'raf: 104–105]. Pharaoh responded to him: ﴿He said, "If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you should be of the truthful." So he threw down his staff, and it was at once a manifest serpent. And he drew out his hand, and it was white to the observers﴾ [al-A'raf: 106–108]. The whiteness of the hand was an attribute inherent in Moses, peace be upon him, and also an occurrence that was temporary; it was not an illness like vitiligo, for example, as evidenced by the precaution in the words of the Most High: ﴿And draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease﴾ [Ta-Ha: 22].

As for the staff, it was the proof that prompted Pharaoh to bring the sorcerers, so that Moses would overcome them before Pharaoh and the chiefs, and the sorcerers would follow Moses and believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

We know that the Truthful One, glorified is He, sent Moses, peace be upon him, with nine signs, which are: the staff that becomes a serpent that swallows what the sorcerers had made, and the white hand without disease; then the House of Pharaoh was seized by years of drought and a shortage of crops and lives, because drought prevents planting and loss of wealth brings about famine. Likewise, the Truthful One, glorified is He, sent upon the people of Pharaoh the flood, the locusts, the lice, and the frogs. These are the nine signs(١٠) that the Truthful One, glorified is He, sent upon the House of Pharaoh, because of their not believing in the message of Moses, peace be upon him.

There are other signs that the Truthful One, glorified is He, sent to the people of Moses through Moses, peace be upon him: the uprooting of the mountain(١١), the striking of the sea with the staff(١²), then the striking of the rock with the staff so that twelve(١³) springs gushed forth, and likewise the descent of the Torah on tablets(١⁴).

So the discussion of the nine signs concerns the signs with which Moses was sent to Pharaoh; as for these, they came after the Exodus from Egypt or accompanied it, such as the striking of the sea with the staff.

The evidence that the story of Moses with Pharaoh is specific is that Moses had two missions: the first mission was with Pharaoh, and the second mission was with the Children of Israel.

Therefore we observe that the Most High, glorified is He, informs us at the end of the surah of the dispute between Moses, peace be upon him, and the Children of Israel: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Book, but it came to be disputed﴾ [Hud: 110]. So: his story with the Children of Israel comes after his being given the Book, that is, the Torah.

Here the Truthful One, glorified is He, speaks of the signs of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh, saying: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ [Hud: 96]. That is: an all-encompassing authority that leaves the adversary no place or escape. (١⁵)

1 - He, exalted is He, says: {…And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells and grows from every beautiful pair} [al-Hajj: 5]. "That is: when God sends down rain upon it, it quivers, meaning it moves with vegetation and is revived after its death, and swells, meaning it rises, then it produces what is in it of colors and kinds, of fruits and crops." Said by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir [3/208].
2 - He, exalted is He, says: {And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her…} [al-Isra': 59].
3 - He, exalted is He, quoting Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿And I heal the blind from birth and the leper, and I bring the dead to life, by God's permission…﴾ [Al 'Imran: 49]. Al-kamah (the blind from birth): one who is born blind or loses his sight; al-abras (the leper): one afflicted with a skin disease that produces white patches on the skin that disfigure. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
4 - Bakha'a nafsahu bakh'an wa bukhuwan: he killed it out of sorrow, anger, and grief. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footprints if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6], and He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/56], adapted.
5 - Haqiq 'ala an: eager to, or worthy of. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
6 - Mubin: its matter is manifest and not doubted. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
7 - Wa naza'a yadahu: he drew it out from the collar of his garment. Bayda': its radiance overcame the radiance of the sun. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
8 - Ila janahika: to your side, beneath the left armpit. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
9 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So the sorcerers were thrown down prostrate, saying, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 70].
10 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel…﴾ [al-Isra': 101]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So he threw down his staff, and it was at once a manifest serpent. And he drew out his hand, and it was white to the observers﴾ [al-A'raf: 107–108]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people…﴾ [al-Naml: 12]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of crops, that they might remember. But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours," and if evil afflicted them, they ascribed it as an omen to Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their omen is with God, but most of them do not know. And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not be believers in you." So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs; but they were arrogant and were a criminal people. And when the punishment fell upon them, they said, "O Moses, invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you. If you remove from us the punishment, we will surely believe in you and send with you the Children of Israel." But when We removed from them the punishment for a term they were to reach, they at once broke their word. So We took retribution upon them and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ [al-A'raf: 130–136].
11 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And [recall] when We shook the mountain above them as if it were a canopy…﴾ [al-A'raf: 171]. Natqa: lifted it from its place, shook it, and pulled it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
12 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So We inspired Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff," and it parted, and each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63]. Tawd: the firm, high mountain. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/408].
13 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So We said, "Strike the rock with your staff," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs…﴾ [al-Baqarah: 60].
14 - He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything a lesson…﴾ [al-A'raf: 145]. Al-alwah: plural of lawh, a broad surface of wood or other material on which one writes. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/206].
15 - Al-fakak: the ransom of a pledge or captive, that by which it is freed. The intended meaning here: escape. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit], adapted.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 97:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guided.(97)﴾

Al-mala' (the chiefs/notables): they are the people who fill the eyes (with their presence), and who occupy the front of the assemblies. It is said: "So-and-so is malʾ al-ʿayn," meaning that the eyes do not disdain him, because he is clear and evident.

So al-mala', then, are the nobles of the people, and they are usually the ones who make the tyrant's contempt for the subjects appear attractive to him.

The Truthful (subhanahu) says: ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a people of depraved defiance.(54)﴾ [az-Zukhruf]. When the Truthful (subhanahu) speaks of Pharaoh, the chiefs and the people, we find Him distinguishing and separating the chiefs on one hand from Pharaoh on the other, and likewise separating Pharaoh and the chiefs on one hand from the people on the other. Each of these three parties is dealt with by Allah (subhanahu) in its own manner.

Here Allah (subhanahu) tells us that the chiefs followed Pharaoh's command, the command which the Truthful (subhanahu) describes by saying: ﴿...and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guided (97)﴾ [Hud]. Right guidance (rushd) is the opposite of error (ghayy), and this statement shows us that the chiefs among Pharaoh's people did not deliberate over Pharaoh's command carefully, and their minds did not receive it with inquiry; had they done so, they would not have followed Pharaoh's command.

1 - Rushd (right guidance): the opposite of error (ghayy) and misguidance (dalal), and the opposite of foolishness (safah) and poor management. Rashada fulan: he hit upon the right way, the good and the truth. Denying rushd is denying truth, good and correctness. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/265], adapted.
2 - Khaffa al-haml: it became light and was not heavy. Figuratively: khaffa 'aqluhu: he became flighty and foolish. From this: istakhaffahu: he deemed his mind weak, subjugated it, led it according to his whim, and moved it to levity and folly. Allah says: ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him...(54)﴾ [az-Zukhruf]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/200]...

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 11, verse 98:

Allah, glory be to Him, shows us that the affair of Pharaoh was not rightly guided. He tells us what will happen to him and his people on the Day of Resurrection, and He says, exalted is He:

﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down to the Fire. And wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought down.﴾

The word "yuqaddimu" (he leads/goes before) comes from the root qaf, dal, and mim. When this root is used in speech or writing, it indicates coming forward to confront. One says "qadama fulan" (so-and-so came forward), which is evidence of his approaching you face to face. When one says "aqbala fulan" (so-and-so came toward), this means approaching with some determination. And "qadama al-qawm yuqaddimuhum" means that they advance in one direction, and whoever leads them goes before them.

From this it is understood that the chiefs followed Pharaoh, and the people followed Pharaoh and the chiefs. Since they followed him in this world, they must follow him in the Hereafter.

The Qur'an presents verses and explains them, such as the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will bring them around Hell on their knees. Then We will surely extract from every faction those who were the most insolent toward the Most Merciful. Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein.﴾ [Maryam].

So Allah, exalted is He, extracts from every group the strongest in vigor and domination, and casts him into the Fire, for He is most knowing of who deserves to be burned in the blazing Fire.

And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it. That is upon your Lord an absolute decree. Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.﴾ [Maryam].

Allah did not say "wa in minhum illa waridaha" (there is none of them but will pass over it). Rather He said: ﴿wa in minkum illa waridaha...﴾ [Maryam]: thereby the address is generalized to all, or He summons the disbelievers and leaves the believers apart.

Here Allah, exalted is He, says about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿...so He will bring them to the Fire. And wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought.﴾ [Hud]. When the Book of Allah, the Noble, speaks of "al-wurud" (coming to water), which is the Book revealed in clear Arabic tongue, we find that "al-wurud" comes to mean going to water without drinking from it.
