You say "warada yarudu warudan." If you wish to express drinking water together with arriving, say "warada yaridu wirdan," on the evidence that Allah, exalted is He, says here: ﴿...and wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾ [Hud]: that is, they feel misery at the moment they see the water of Hell and drink from it.

So the word "al-warid" applies to the act of drinking water, and may also apply to the people who come to water, as in His saying: ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd.﴾ [Maryam].

The pre-Islamic poet Zuhair ibn Abi Sulma said in his Mu'allaqa:

When they came to the water, its surface blue and its collected pools full, they set down the staves of the settled, encamped (traveller).

Here the poet describes the caravan at the moment they see waters blue, free of anything that clouds or troubles them, so the people set down their traveling staffs.

It was customary in the past for everyone who walked to carry a staff in his hand, like Moses, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿It is my staff; I lean on it, and I beat down leaves with it for my flock, and I have in it other uses.﴾ [Ta-Ha].

The poet says: "So he cast down his staff, and settled with his journey, as the eye of the traveller is comforted by return."

So when he saw the water blue, that means it is water unclouded.

We know that water has no color, but it is described as blue if it is free of impurities and extremely clear, so that the image of the blue sky is reflected upon it.

The poet describes his people when they reached clear water, stopped, and settled in the place.

Thus we find that "wurud" means going to water without drinking from it. The arrival at water gladdens the soul first, then what one drinks from it quenches and refreshes; one who comes to water undoubtedly suffers thirst that he wants to quench, and heat of the liver that he wants to cool.

Here Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿...and wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾ [Hud]. In this there is severe mockery, for they, the people of Pharaoh, at the moment they see the water feel that the quenching of thirst and cooling of heat is near, but they drink from the water of Hell, so wretched is what they drink. It feeds them first, then disappoints them afterward.

As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they seek relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal that scalds the faces...﴾ [Al-Kahf]: when they hear the word "yughathu" (they will be relieved), they understand that a relief is coming to them, but when they learn it is water like molten metal that scalds the faces, they suffer the bitterness of mockery.

And to Allah belongs the highest likeness: you may find someone who invites you to delicious food, and after that you wash your hands, and the one who invited you insists you take sweets, so your soul looks forward to the sweets, while the one who invited you has instructed the cook to mix the sweets with "shatta" (hot pepper), so your inside burns. Is there not in this a severe mockery?

Allah, exalted is He, makes clear to them that the watering-place came only to moisten the liver, but their livers will be kindled by what you drink of this water, and likewise the food that the people of the Fire eat.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And there is no food except from ghislin (pus).﴾ [Al-Haqqah]. Thus the calamity becomes two calamities.

Some people have understood the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it...﴾ [Maryam] to mean that all of them will come to Hell.

But Allah, exalted is He, also says: ﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein.﴾ [Maryam]. So Allah, exalted is He, gives all people an image of the Fire: when the believers see the Fire and its blaze, and do not enter it, they know how the word of faith saved them from it, so they praise Allah, exalted is He, for the deliverance.

Notes from the source (as they stand in the text):

1 - yuqaddimu qawmahu: he goes before them as the one who comes to water goes before. Fa-awradahum al-nar: he brings them into it by his disbelief and their disbelief.
al-warid al-mawrud: the entry into which one enters, which is the Fire. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
2 - jithiyyan: kneeling on their knees from the severity of the terror. 'Atiyyan: disobedience, or audacity, or immorality. Saliyyan: entering it or suffering its heat. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].
3 - waridaha: that is, reaching the Fire and arriving at it; some of them come to it to enter it, and some do not enter it, and their arrival and seeing it is so they realize the magnitude of Allah's blessing upon them in being saved from it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/330]. Warud in [Kalimat al-Qur'an]: waridaha, that is, passing over the extended bridge (al-Sirat) above it.
4 - hatama Allah al-amr hatman: He made the matter obligatory. Hadha amr hatm: a binding matter that cannot be avoided. Al-hatm: the executed decree. Allah said: ﴿...kana 'ala Rabbika hatman maqdiyyan﴾ [Maryam], meaning that the arrival of the disbelieving addressees at the Fire to be punished therein is an executed, binding decree. It was also said: the believers too will come to it so that they realize the magnitude of Allah's blessing upon them in being saved from it. Maqdiyyan: that is, judged and settled, with no one to repel it nor to revise it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/141].
5 - bi'sa al-warid al-mawrud: that is, the worst place a person comes to, where he meets painful punishment. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/330].
6 - al-warid: water or its place, or camels coming to water, metaphorically. Allah said: ﴿wa nasuq al-mujrimina ila Jahannama wirdan﴾ [Maryam], meaning a group who come to it and enter it as camels come to water. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/330].
7 - The poet of wisdom among the pre-Islamic poets, from the tribe of Mudar, born in the lands of Muzayna near Madina; his father, maternal uncle, and two sons Ka'b and Bujayr were poets, as were his sisters Salma and al-Khansa'; died in the year 13 BH. [See: al-A'lam by Khayr al-Din al-Zirikli].
8 - al-juman: what gathers of it in a well, a basin, or elsewhere. Placing the staves: a metaphor for settling, because travellers who settle set down their staves. Al-takhyim: pitching the tent. [See: Sharh al-Mu'allaqat al-Sab' by al-Zuzani, p. 82]. The mu'allaqa is in the tawil meter.
9 - hashsha al-shajar yahshushu hashshan: he struck it with a staff so its leaves fall for livestock to eat. Allah said: ﴿wa ahushshu biha 'ala ghanami﴾ [Ta-Ha], meaning I knock the leaves of the trees down for my flock to eat. Wa ma'arib ukhra: many other needs and purposes, such as warding off harm or other things. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/17], adapted.
10 - He is: Ma'qar ibn Himar. [Ibn Manzur said it in Lisan al-Arab, root: nawa].
11 - al-niyya and al-nawa: the direction the traveller intends, near or far; al-niyya and al-nawa together: distance; al-nawa: the dwelling; al-nawa: moving from one place to another or from one dwelling to another. Ibn Manzur cited this verse in Lisan, root nawa.
12 - al-iyab: return and coming back. Ab yu'ub: he returns. From it the saying of Allah: ﴿wa inna ilayna iyabahum﴾ [al-Ghashiya], meaning their return. Al-ma'ab: the place of return, both a time noun and a place noun. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/42].
13 - ka-al-muhl: like the dregs of oil or like molten metal. [Kalimat al-Qur'an]. Al-muhl: molten metal, tar, the dregs of boiling oil, and pus. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/242].
14 - al-ghislin: the washings of the bodies of the people of the Fire, or what flows from the skins of the people of the Fire of pus and other things the soul loathes and dislikes. Allah said: ﴿wa la ta'amun illa min ghislin﴾ [al-Haqqah]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/54].
15 - sa'arat al-nar: it blazed; as'arahā: kindled and inflamed it; sa''arahā (intensive): inflamed it. Allah said: ﴿wa idha al-jahim su''irat﴾ [al-Takwir], meaning kindled intensely. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/313].

And they are followed in this (world) by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection (too). Wretched is the gift that is given!

Al-Sha'rawi: Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And they were followed in this (world) by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift that is given (99).﴾

Meaning: the curse remained for them, and we Muslims have not ceased cursing them until now. Then they will proceed to the greater curse, which is the curse of the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Wretched is the gift that is given (99).﴾ "Rifd" is the gift, so is a curse in the Hereafter considered a gift?

This is also a mockery on their part, just as the saying of Allah, glorified is He, is a mockery: ﴿...and wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought (98).﴾ [Hud]

1 - Rafadahu yarfuduhu rifdan: he gave him and helped him. Al-rifd (ar-rifd) means gift and assistance. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they were followed in this (world) by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift that is given (99).﴾ [Hud], meaning: the gift bestowed upon them, which is the curse they were followed by in this world and the Hereafter. He called the curse "rifd" as mockery and derision. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/270]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 100:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you; of them some are still standing and some are reaped down.﴾

The Truth, glorified is He, has destroyed those towns with punishment, because they denied their prophets. The address is directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to strengthen his heart, and the Truth, glorified is He, is only making clear to him that the disbelievers will not escape punishment, just as Allah, glorified is He, seized the earlier disbelieving nations with punishment.

The saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿We relate to you…﴾ [Hud] requires that we distinguish between the common meaning of "story" (qissah) and its true meaning. Some people say: the Qur'an contains stories, and stories are usually filled with embellishment, and imaginary events are placed in them for the sake of plot.

To these we say: you have not understood the meaning of the word "qissah" in the Arabic language, for it means, in our language, the literal adherence to the events that occurred in it. It is derived from the expression "qassa al-athar" (to trace the track), and one who traces a track only follows the footprints until he reaches the thing sought.

Thus, the stories (qasas) of the Qur'an trace out the realities and say nothing other than them. As for what has become conventional among the common people as "stories," with the imaginations and captivating elements found in those tales, this is what is called linguistically "riwayat" (romances), and it is not considered a qissah.

The stories of destruction of the nations that disbelieved are a lesson for whoever does not take heed. People know that what the Qur'an narrates of stories is a reality, indicated by the remains of civilizations that have vanished, of which there remain stones and inscriptions on tombs.

We find among the remains of earlier civilizations what is still standing of pillars and inscriptions, and among them what is shattered.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says elsewhere in the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat]: that is, you witness among the traces what is standing and what is broken.

The Truth, glorified is He, says about those towns:

﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came, and they increased them in nothing but ruin.﴾

1 - The saying of the Exalted: ﴿That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you; of them some are still standing and some are reaped down﴾ [Hud]: that is, of them some remain and of them some are destroyed. And the Exalted said: ﴿…until We made them reaped, extinguished﴾ [al-Anbiya' 15], that is, We made them like the cut crop, that is, We destroyed them. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/156]..
2 - Qassa al-kalam or al-akhbar, yaqussuha qassan and qasasan: he followed them, related them and narrated them. The Exalted said: ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the stories…﴾ [al-Qasas 25], that is, he related to him his news and told him of it. And the Exalted said: ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you…﴾ [al-Nisa' 164], that is, messengers whose news We mentioned to you, and messengers whose news We did not mention to you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/120]..
3 - Qassa al-athar qassasan: he followed it. From it is His saying: ﴿…so they returned retracing their footprints﴾ [al-Kahf 64], that is, they followed their traces by tracing. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/120]..
4 - Al-qasas: a verbal noun applied to what is related of reports. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed there was in their stories a lesson for people of understanding…﴾ [Yusuf 111], and the Exalted said: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories…﴾ [Yusuf 3], and the Exalted said: ﴿We relate to you their news in truth…﴾ [al-Kahf 13]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/120]..
5 - Al-tathbib: destruction and loss; al-tabab: ruin. The Exalted said: ﴿…and the plot of Pharaoh was only in ruin﴾ [Ghafir 37]. And tabbabahu tatbiban: he destroyed him. The Exalted said: ﴿…and they increased them in nothing but ruin﴾ [Hud 101]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/96]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 101:

Here the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear that when He seized those peoples with punishment, He did not wrong them, because the meaning of wronging (zulm) is that a person is given a right and then that right is taken away from him.

In fact, those nations that disbelieved and were seized by God with punishment were the ones who wronged themselves through association (shirk), and those peoples denied the messengers who came with, in the hand of each of them, the proof of truthfulness and the signs of prophethood.

Thus these disbelievers wronged themselves. Therefore we must know that the Truth, glorified is He, is exalted above wronging anyone.

And when they associated other gods with God, the Exalted, why did those supposed gods not move and intervene to protect those who believed in them?!

The Truth, glorified is He, informs us that the stones they worshipped will curse them while they are in the Fire, and these stones will be fuel for the Fire.

The Truth, glorified is He, says of the Fire: ﴿So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones...(24)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Those who worshipped a man or some of the idols were only wronging, through ignorance, this human being they worshipped or those stones to which they prayed or which they sanctified.

The Muslim poet reflected on the Cave of Hira' and the Cave of Thawr, both of them being stones, and found that the Cave of Hira' witnessed the descent of revelation upon the Messenger (ﷺ), while the Cave of Thawr protected the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when he hid in it, together with the Companion Abu Bakr, during the migration from Makkah to Madinah. The poet imagined that the Cave of Thawr envied the Cave of Hira' and said:
"How often we envied Hira' when the Trustworthy Spirit came to you, bringing you with lights.
Hira' and Thawr have become equal; through both of them, the nation of stones seeks intercession."
So the Cave of Hira' witnessed Gabriel descending with light upon Muhammad (ﷺ), but the Cave of Thawr also gained honour for protecting the Messenger in the migration.

The poet says, speaking on the tongue of the stones:
"They worshipped us, while we are more worshipful of God than those who stand in prayer at the dawns.
They have wronged us through ignorance, just as they wronged the son of Mary and the disciples.
For the extremist is his recompense, and the one who exaggerates in it, the mercy of the Forgiving One will save him."

Thus their worshipped gods did not avail them anything, whether they were human or stones. They did not avail them anything and did not lift from them the punishment they received as a retribution in this world and a blaze in the Hereafter. And since they had called upon them besides God in this world, when the punishment came, those gods did not step forward to protect them from the punishment.

The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿...And they added nothing to them but perdition(101)﴾ [Hud]. That is: the abandonment by those gods they had associated with God, the Exalted, or worshipped besides God. This abandonment increases them in pain, psychological destruction and loss, because tatbib is cutting off and ruin.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he(1)﴾ [al-Masad]. Likewise is the seizing with which God seized the towns that denied their prophets.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe(102)﴾:

1 - Al-Waqud (fuel): that with which the fire is kindled, such as firewood and other things. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿The Fire, possessing fuel(5)﴾ [al-Buruj], meaning: possessing the wood thrown into it to increase its blaze; this shows the eagerness of the disbelievers sitting around it to increase its blazing, so that they might torment the believers with it with the most severe torment, as happened in the story of the People of the Trench. But in the Hereafter, the fuel of the Fire will be men and stones, and what is meant by men here: the disbelievers and sinners whose destiny is the Fire. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿...And those are the fuel of the Fire(10)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/348], with adaptation.
2 - Al-Asḥar (dawns): plural of al-sahr, with a fatha on the sin and the ha'. It is the last part of the night until the rise of dawn. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿...and those who seek forgiveness at dawn(17)﴾ [Al 'Imran], and He says: ﴿And at dawn they seek forgiveness(18)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/305].
3 - Al-Hawariyyun (the disciples): they are the disciples, who were the sincere and chosen companions of the prophets. God, the Exalted, says: {The disciples said: We are helpers of God...(52)} [Al 'Imran]. And al-hawari: the pure one, free of every impurity. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/177].
4 - Tabba, yatibbu, tabban and tababanan: he suffered loss and perished. God, the Exalted, says: {Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he(1)} [al-Masad], and it is a supplication against him for loss and destruction. He was first prayed against that his hands should perish, because they are the instruments of violence and harm. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/96].
5 - Al-Alim (painful): that which pains, extremely painful and agonizing. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿...and for them is a painful punishment because they used to deny(10)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. And al-alam: intense pain and agony. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/26], with adaptation.

That is: the seizing with which God seized the disbelieving towns is itself a living example for everyone who disbelieves.

God, may He be exalted, says:

﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes. Is there in that an oath for one of sound mind?﴾ [Al-Fajr]. That is: God, may He be exalted, swears so that every person of intellect will grasp the necessity of faith, and He gives as examples the peoples who were struck by the seizing of punishment. He, may He be exalted, says:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands, and Thamud who hewed the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes, who transgressed in the lands and increased corruption therein? So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.﴾ [Al-Fajr]. So He, may He be exalted, seized all of these with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

His saying here, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord...﴾ [Hud, 102]. That is: like the seizing with which were seized the towns that denied their messengers, and so wronged themselves.

The seizing here is punishment for deeds, as is shown by the fact that He saved Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, and seized his people because of their wrongdoing. The human essence is innocent, but it is the act that deserves punishment.

An example of this is found in the story of Noah, peace be upon him, when the Truth, may He be exalted, said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, it is unrighteous conduct...﴾ [Hud, 46]. What made Noah's son placed in this position is that his deed was unrighteous. Therefore Noah should not say, "He is my son," for destruction is not by reason of essence, blood or kinship, but by reason of deed. You do not hate a person who drinks wine for his essence, but for his deed. We know that sonship to the prophets is not sonship of essences, but sonship of deeds.

Likewise, we find the Truth, may He be exalted, alerting Abraham, peace be upon him, that he should not invoke it for all his offspring. When the Truth, may He be exalted, honoured Abraham, peace be upon him, and said: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 124].

The request and supplication came from Abraham, peace be upon him, to God, exalted is He: ﴿And from my offspring...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 124]. This is because Abraham, peace be upon him, wished that the imamate would extend to his offspring as well. The reply came from God, may He be exalted: ﴿...My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 124]. This matter remained at the core of Abraham's awareness, and he knew with certainty that sonship to the prophets is not sonship of essences, but sonship of deeds.

Hence we find Abraham's supplication, peace be upon him, when he settled his family in a valley without vegetation, and said: ﴿O my Lord, make this a secure city, and provide its people with fruits...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 126].

Here Abraham, peace be upon him, became attentive and added: ﴿...those of them who believe...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 126].

Then the reply came from the Truth, may He be exalted, clarifying the error of analogy, because provision is a gift of lordship (rububiyyah), in which the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, are equal. So do not confuse the gift of lordship with the gift of divinity (uluhiyyah), which is a charge (taklif). The gift of lordship is provision, and therefore the Truth, may He be exalted, said: ﴿...And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 126].

So you, O Abraham, prayed for provision of fruits for those who believe, because the core of your awareness comprehends the lesson. But there is a difference between the gift of divinity in charge and the gift of lordship in provision. Whoever disbelieves, his Lord will provide for him, grant him enjoyment for a little, and then he will have a different reckoning.

Therefore, the seizing of the wrongdoers by the Truth, may He be exalted, for their disbelief is the harshness of treatment toward one who opposes. The strength of the seizing varies with the strength of the one who seizes. If the one who seizes is God, may He be exalted, then it is the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

It is the seizing of those who wronged themselves with the utmost wrong, which is disbelief. If the wrong is against the rights of others, it is wickedness (fisq), and wronging oneself is also wickedness, because when the Truth, may He be exalted, forbids you to wrong another, He has also forbidden you to wrong yourself. The Truth, may He be exalted, describes His seizing of the wrongdoers in His saying: ﴿...Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ [Hud, 102]. That is: His seizing is painful, in proportion to the complete reach of His power, may He be exalted.

Suppose a person wronged another. The Truth, may He be exalted, has given this person the right to return evil with evil, so that emotions do not accumulate and grow.

Therefore the Truth, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished...﴾ [An-Nahl, 126], so that your emotions do not spend the night in you as oppression. But whoever has the strength to control the impulse should consider the Truth's saying, may He be exalted: ﴿...and those who restrain anger...﴾ [Ali 'Imran, 134].

So either you return evil with a punishment like it, or you restrain your anger, that is, you do not translate your anger into an impulsive act, or you rise to the higher level, which is to pardon, because God, may He be exalted, loves those who do good by pardoning.

Therefore, when they asked al-Hasan al-Basri: How does a person do good to one who has wronged him?

He answered: If a servant wrongs you, will that not anger his Lord with him? They said: Yes. He said: And when God is angry with the one who wronged you, will He not stand by your side? Will you not do good to one whom God makes stand by your side?

For this reason it is related of one of the righteous that he heard that a person had backbitten him. So he sent to him, along with his servant, a tray of early dates. The servant was astonished and asked: Why do you send him dates when he has backbitten you?

The knower of God said: Convey to him my gratitude and thanks, because he has given me charity from his good deeds when he backbitten me, and his good deeds are, without doubt, more precious than these dates.

Therefore it is said: One who pardons has more understanding than one who punishes, because the one who punishes punishes by his own strength, whereas the one who pardons leaves punishment to the strength of God, may He be exalted, a strength that has no limit.

Thus we understand the Truth's saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ [Hud, 102].

That is: a seizing that is painful in proportion to the strength of God, may He be exalted; it is a severe seizing, because severity means gathering one thing to another so that they are hard to separate, or gripping two things together so that neither can be loosened from the other. This is the utmost degree of strength.

1 - "Al-Fajr": an oath by God, may He be exalted, by a known time [the time of dawn]. "Wa-layalin 'ashr": the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah. "Wa-ash-shaf'i wa-l-watr": the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of 'Arafah. "Wa-al-layli idha yasr": when it passes and goes away, or when it is travelled through. "Hal fi dhalika": that is, in what has been mentioned, which We have sworn by. "Qasamun li-dhi hijr?": a sworn matter worthy of exaltation for people of intellect, yes. [The answer to the oath is: "Surely We shall punish the disbelievers"] [Kalimat al-Qur'an] of Shaykh Hasanayn Muhammad Makhluf.

2 - "Bi'ad": the people of Hud, named after their father. "Iram": the name of their forefather, after whom the tribe was named. "Dhat al-'imad": severity, or lofty well-built structures supported by pillars. "Jabu al-sakhr": they hewed the rock and carved their houses in it. "Dhi al-awtad": the many armies that strengthened his kingdom. "Sawt 'adhab": severe, painful, and lasting punishment. "Inna rabbaka labi-l-mirsad": He watches their deeds and recompenses them for them. [Kalimat al-Qur'an].

3 - The saying of God, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 124], that is: a model whom people follow. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿The Day We shall call every people by their leader...﴾ [Al-Isra', 71], that is, by their messenger, so it is said: "O followers of Abraham," and "O nation of Moses," and "O nation of Muhammad"; or by their book, so it is said: "O people of the Torah," "O people of the Gospel," and "O people of the Qur'an." [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/33].

4 - Dhurriyyah (offspring): for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine, from the progeny of a human being. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And he has weak offspring...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 266]. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And We sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their offspring prophethood and scripture...﴾ [Al-Hadid, 26]. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿...And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Satan﴾ [Ali 'Imran, 36]. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And from our offspring a Muslim nation for You...﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 128]. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of eyes...﴾ [Al-Furqan, 74], in the plural. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And from their fathers, their offspring, and their brothers...﴾ [Al-An'am, 87], in the plural, and it is written without an alif in the Mushaf. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And from my offspring? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 124]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/242], with adaptation.

5 - The gift of lordship is general, and the gift of divinity is particular. The general gift is for every creature, and the particular gift is for those under charge, through generous faith and pure certainty. [From the wisdom of Shaykh...].

6 - "'Aqabahu 'iqaban": he requited him for what he did, evil for evil. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished...﴾ [An-Nahl, 126]. Punishment and retaliation: inflicting a recompense for a sin. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿...Indeed your Lord is Forgiving and possessor of painful punishment﴾ [Fussilat, 43]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/29].

7 - "Al-kazimin al-ghayz": those who hold back their anger within their hearts [Kalimat al-Qur'an]. "Kazm al-ghayz": holding it back and restraining it within the self, and being patient with it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/163].

8 - God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous, who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon people. And God loves the doers of good.﴾ [Ali 'Imran, 133-134]. The Truth, may He be exalted, also says: ﴿Good and evil are not equal. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ [Fussilat, 34].

9 - He is al-Hasan al-Basri. It is related that a man said to him: So-and-so has backbitten you. So he sent to him dates on a tray and said: I have been informed that you have sent me gifts of your good deeds, so I wanted to reward you for them. Excuse me, for I cannot fully reward you. Cited by al-Ghazali in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (3/154).

10 - "Al-bawakir": plural of "bakur" or "bakurah," which is the first of the fruit to ripen, and also the early produce of anything. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root b-k-r], with adaptation.

11 - "Al-qura": plural of "qaryah," which is a large town, smaller than a city, or every place that is joined by buildings. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And ask the town in which we were...﴾ [Yusuf, 82], meaning the people of the town, a metonymy (majaz mursal) with a locational relation. Likewise His saying: ﴿And how many a town was stronger in strength than your town which expelled you—We destroyed them, and they had no helper﴾ [Muhammad, 13], meaning its people were stronger than the people of Makkah who expelled you. And His saying: ﴿When He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing...﴾ [Hud, 102], meaning He seizes their people while they are wrongdoers. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root q-r-y].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 103:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.﴾ (103)

For whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter: these verses that tell of what happened to the earlier nations are only drawing his attention to the necessity of believing that Allah, glory be to Him, holds every person accountable for belief and for deeds.

Whoever listens to the stories of the earlier peoples, takes a lesson from what came in them, and benefits from the experience they bring, has a far-reaching insight. Everything that happened to the earlier peoples is a striking sign.

For this reason it is said: "Every sign has offspring, which are the lessons drawn from the signs." Whoever does not believe will not take a lesson, in confirmation of the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it.﴾ (105) [Yusuf].

So, Allah, glory be to Him, has willed to draw our attention through signs so that we may take lessons from them and be among the people of understanding (ulu al-albab, "those possessing minds"). Then do not enter into the circle of those who do not fear the punishment: those who receive the punishment as disgrace in this world and a blazing fire in the Hereafter; and the punishment of the Hereafter has no end, and the humiliation in it is before all creation.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿...That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.﴾ (103) [Hud]. That is, the disgrace on this Day will be witnessed by all mankind, from Adam to the last of mankind; therefore it will be a resounding disgrace before those whom a person knows and before those whom he does not know.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered...﴾ (103) [Hud]: The word "majmu'" (gathered for) requires the existence of a "jami'" (one who gathers), and "al-majmu'" is proportionate to the power of the "jami'". How much more so when the One who gathers is the Truth, the Creator of all creation, glory be to Him and exalted.

Creation will not be gathered on that Day in heedlessness; rather they will be gathered while fully alert. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly.﴾ (42) [Ibrahim].

The Truth, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly...﴾ (97) [al-Anbiya].

Here He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...And that is a Day witnessed.﴾ (103) [Hud]: That is, all creation will witness this shameful exposure of those who did not take a lesson from the signs.

1 - "Majmu'" (gathered for): a passive participle from jama'a. "Al-amr al-jami'" is a great matter for which people are gathered. "Al-jami'" is an active participle from jama'a and is one of Allah's Beautiful Names. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Our Lord, You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt...﴾ (9) [Al 'Imran], and He, exalted, says: ﴿And when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they ask his permission...﴾ (62) [al-Nur] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, root j-m-')].

2 - "Mashhud" (witnessed): a passive participle. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾ (103) [Hud], meaning that people attend it and witness its terror, or the angels of punishment attend it. His saying: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ (78) [al-Isra'], meaning that the angels witness the recitation of dawn and record its reward. "Mashhad" is a noun of place, a noun of time, and a noun of origin (mim-prefixed verbal noun), as in His saying, exalted: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a tremendous Day﴾ (37) [Maryam] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, p. 359, vol. 1].

3 - ﴿Wa-ka-ayyin min ayah...﴾ (105) [Yusuf]: that is, "how many a sign." Or "many of the signs." [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Makhluf].

4 - "Mu'ridun": an active participle from "a'rada." One who "a'rada 'an al-shay'" has turned away from it, going off, not desiring it. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And he turned away, withdrawing his side﴾ (83) [al-Isra'] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, root '-r-d].

5 - "Al-albab": plural of "lubb," which is intellect. It occurs sixteen times in the Qur'an. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿...Only those of understanding will be reminded﴾ (19) [al-Ra'd].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 104:

Then the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says concerning the appointed time of this Day:

﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term.(1) (104)﴾:

Thus we know that the delay in the coming of the Day of Resurrection does not mean that it will not come; rather it will come, without doubt. But every event has an appointed time of birth, and in the succession of your own births there is that which makes you trust that the births of events are only determined by God.

The saying of the Truthful One, glory be to Him: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term..(104)﴾ [Hud].

It requires that we know that the word "ajal" (term) is applied once to the duration of a creature's life, from the moment of its birth to the moment of its end.

And the Truthful One says: ﴿..For every term there is a written decree.(2) (38)﴾ [al-Ra'd]. The word "ajal" is applied again to the moment of the end alone, in confirmation of the saying of the Truthful One: ﴿..So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.(3) (34)﴾ [al-A'raf]. Let us all know that every term, however long, is limited, and everything limited is few, however much it may seem many; therefore let us say that everything limited is few, as long as we are able to count it.

1 - Ma'dud (limited): a noun from the verb [ʿadda] (to count). The Almighty says: ﴿..numbered days..(80)﴾ [al-Baqara], meaning counted and few, which are the days of the month of Ramadan. He also says: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term (104)﴾ [Hud], and He says: ﴿Certainly He has enumerated them and counted them precisely (94)﴾ [Maryam]. And "ajal" (term): the duration of a thing, the limit of a time, the time of life, the time of a debt, or the time of death. What is meant here is the Day of Resurrection. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entries ʿ-d-d and ʾ-j-l], with adaptation.

2 - Kitab (writing/decree): it has several meanings, among them the Qur'an, the Torah, the Gospel, a letter, the verbal noun of kataba (to write), and that which is written and recorded in scrolls, and the agent noun of kataba. The Almighty says: ﴿That is the Book, there is no doubt in it..(2)﴾ [al-Baqara]. He says: ﴿Take this letter of mine and throw it to them..(28)﴾ [al-Naml]. He says: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God..(6)﴾ [al-Ahzab], meaning in His judgment and decree, or in the noble Qur'an in the verses on inheritance. He says: ﴿Were it not for a decree from God that preceded..(68)﴾ [al-Anfal], meaning, were it not for a prior decree from God recorded with Him, which cannot be changed, namely the permission of ransom. He says: ﴿..For every term there is a written decree (38)﴾ [al-Ra'd], meaning a recorded appointed time written down with God. He says: ﴿..Indeed, prayer has been prescribed for the believers at specified times (103)﴾ [al-Nisa'], meaning an obligation recorded with Him, glory be to Him, each prayer at a fixed and specified time. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry k-t-b], with adaptation.

3 - Ta'akhkhara and ista'akhkhara: the opposite of taqaddama (to advance). The Almighty says: ﴿Say: For you is an appointed day from which you cannot delay an hour nor advance (it) (30)﴾ [Saba'], meaning you cannot delay, nor seek postponement or deferral, nor advance, because it is fixed at a known time that cannot be advanced or delayed. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry ʾ-kh-r].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 105:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿On the day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them are the wretched and the happy.﴾ (105):

Here the Truthful, glorified is He, has gathered a group under a single ruling. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿no soul will speak...﴾ (105) [Hud]: meaning, no soul will speak except by the permission of Allah. Indeed, in the life of this world they used to speak with the freedom of power which Allah, glorified is He, granted them when He subjected their limbs to them.

The Truthful, glorified is He, made the limbs obedient to the command of the human being. And He, glorified is He, willed to make some of His creation examples of His power to strip away some of those limbs. So you find the mute who cannot speak; you find the paralysed who cannot move; you find the blind who cannot see, and other than that.

Through these examples, people come to recognise a clear truth: that the control they enjoy over their limbs is a gift bestowed upon them by Allah, exalted is He, and not a matter inherent in them.

The saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿On the day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission..﴾ (105) [Hud]: explains to us the reality of the subjection of the limbs to our obedience in this world. They submit to our will, because He, glorified is He, willed to subject them to our commands and our impulses; and none of us speaks except within the general permission of the will that the limbs be moved by it.

Allah, glorified is He, may withdraw this permission, so the limbs do not respond to the will. You find the Truthful, glorified is He, saying in another verse: ﴿They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and he speaks rightly.﴾ (38) [An-Naba'].

The Truthful, mighty and majestic is He, says in another verse: ﴿And some of them turn to others, questioning one another.﴾ (27) [As-Saffat].

There is another verse in which the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿This is a day on which they will not speak (35). Nor will they be permitted to offer an excuse.﴾ (36) [Al-Mursalat].

The Truthful, glorified is He, also says: ﴿On the day every soul will come pleading for itself..﴾ (111) [An-Nahl].

And in another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Stop them, for they are to be questioned.﴾ (24) [As-Saffat].

Thus it may seem to some that there are verses contradicting one another: there are verses that permit speech, and there are verses that deny the ability to speak.

I say: It must be understood that the speech which the wretched will be unable to utter on the Day of Resurrection is the beneficial, useful speech (5). Some will speak the sophistry that benefits nothing, such as their blaming one another, which the Qur'an mentioned in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve will say: "Our Lord, show us those who misled us (6) of the jinn and mankind; we will place them beneath our feet..﴾ (29) [Fussilat].

This is speech that does not intercede for its speaker and does not benefit.

So then: what is prohibited is the speech that is beneficial and useful; or the stations of the Resurrection vary, so there is a time in which they speak and a time in which they are seized, and they are dumbfounded and do not speak, and the Truthful, glorified is He, commands the obedient limbs to speak and bear witness against them (7).

The Truthful, glorified is He, divides the states of people into two categories, as in His saying, exalted is He, at the end of the verse: ﴿..Among them are the wretched (8) and the happy.﴾ (105) [Hud]: He brought the specific noun for each of the two categories: "wretched" and "happy"; because the noun indicates permanence, so wretchedness is fixed for the one described as wretched, and happiness is fixed for the one described as happy (9).

1 - Shaqiya, shaqan, shaqa'an, shaqawatan: his material or spiritual condition deteriorated, so he is wretched (shaqi); the comparative is ashqa. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They said: "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us..﴾ (106) [Al-Mu'minun], meaning the state of wretchedness, misguidance and corruption of souls. And the wretched (shaqi) is the one deprived of good. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿..And I have never been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, wretched (4)﴾ [Maryam], meaning: I was never before deprived of good when I called upon You. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root sh-q-y]..
2 - Nafs: the spirit, the essence and reality of a thing, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul..﴾ (189) [Al-A'raf], which is the soul of Adam, peace be upon him; and His saying: ﴿You know what is in my soul..﴾ (116) [Al-Ma'idah], meaning what I conceal in my conscience; and His saying: ﴿Nor do I absolve myself..﴾ (53) [Yusuf], meaning my own self; and His saying: ﴿And when you killed a soul and disputed over it..﴾ (72) [Al-Baqarah], meaning a person. The soul has states: it may be commanding (to evil), it may be self-reproaching, and it may be at peace and content, and its rank rises until it becomes well-pleasing, with whom Allah is pleased and whom He has pleased. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself..﴾ (28) [Al 'Imran], meaning His wrath. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim p. 278, vol. 2]..
3 - Jadala: he disputed, in truth and in falsehood. It is used for falsehood in His saying: ﴿Here you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world..﴾ (109) [An-Nisa'], and used for truth in His saying: ﴿And argue with them in the way that is best..﴾ (125) [An-Nahl]. Allah forbade the pilgrims to His House from all kinds of argument, to preserve the bond of love among them. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So there is no sexual immorality, no defiance, and no quarrelling during the Hajj..﴾ (197) [Al-Baqarah]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root j-d-l]..
4 - Qifuhum: detain them at the station of reckoning. [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Hasanayn Makhluf]..
5 - Meaning: they will not speak with a proof that is due to them; rather they will speak by acknowledging their sins, blaming one another, and casting their sins upon one another. As for speech and utterance with a proof in their favour, no. This is like saying to one who addresses you much and whose address is devoid of proof: "You have not spoken anything and you have not uttered anything"; so one who speaks without proof is named as one who does not speak. Said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3417)..
6 - "Adalla fulan ghayrahu": he caused another to fall into error. Ad-dalal: forgetting and loss. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿..And what they used to fabricate has vanished from them (30)﴾ [Yunus], meaning what they worshipped was lost to them. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whose effort was lost in the life of this world..﴾ (104) [Al-Kahf], meaning their deeds were wasted and did not achieve the hope placed in them, or they found no reward on the Day of Resurrection. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root d-l-l], adapted..
7 - The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿On the day their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do (24)﴾ [An-Nur]. Al-Suyuti cited in ad-Durr al-Manthur [6/165] from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the disbeliever will recognise his deeds, then deny and dispute. It will be said: 'These are your neighbours, who bear witness against you.' He will say: 'They have lied.' It will be said: 'Your family and your clan.' He will say: 'They have lied.' It will be said: 'Swear.' So they will swear, then Allah will seal their mouths, and their tongues, hands and feet will bear witness against them, and then He will admit them to the Fire." Attributed to Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh..
8 - Shaqiya (from the pattern of fariha): shaqa, shaqa'an, shaqawatan: his material or spiritual condition deteriorated, so he is wretched; the comparative is ashqa. Sa'ida (as in karuma) sa'ida, yas'adu, sa'adan, su'udan, sa'adatan: attained good: ﴿..Among them are the wretched and the happy (105)﴾ [Hud]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/353, 1/313], abridged and adapted..
9 - From Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿..Among them are the wretched and the happy (105)﴾ [Hud], I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, then what do we act for? For something already decided, or for something not yet decided?" He said: "Rather, for something already decided and the pens have run with it, O Umar; but each is made easy for that for which he was created." Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan [3111], Ibn Abi 'Asim in as-Sunnah [1/74], and Ahmad in his Musnad [1/6]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 106:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear to us the stations of those who were made wretched and the stations of those who were made happy. For this reason He turns away from using the noun to using the verb, so He, glorified is He, says:

﴿As for those who were made wretched, they will be in the Fire, where for them is groaning and wailing(١) (106)﴾:

Those who have passed judgment upon themselves with wretchedness, by their departure from the method of God, are gathered together in wretchedness; yet they enter the Fire as individuals and as groups.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups(٢).. (71)﴾ [al-Zumar].

And in another verse He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses(٣) its sister.. (38)﴾ [al-A'raf]:

Thus we understand that the disbelievers, in their established description, are wretched; but at the moment of entering the Fire they enter it as individuals. Rather, some of the disobedient Muslims enter with them, and each one of them receives the punishment appropriate to the sins and transgressions he committed; each one suffers a wretchedness proportionate to his sins. Thus they are united in wretchedness and differ in the type of wretchedness proportionate to their sins, and thus they are united in wretchedness and differ in the kind and quantity of torment; each according to his sins, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.

The Truth, glorified is He, uses here the verb "shaqu" (they were made wretched) to make clear to us that they are the ones who chose wretchedness; they brought it upon themselves. For the Truth, glorified is He, created His servants and left to each of them the right of choice, and sent down for them the method so that they might guard themselves, and He helps those who choose faith to obey.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, mentions in the same verse the state of those who brought wretchedness upon themselves, saying of them:

﴿.. For them in it is groaning and wailing (106)﴾ [Hud]: We know that one who breathes in the Fire will expel the air from his chest hot, just as he takes in the inhalation hot.

1 - Zafir (زفير): a strong expulsion of breath from the chest; and shahiq (شهيق): drawing the breath back into the chest. [Kalimat al-Qur'an by Shaykh Husnayn Makhluf].
2 - al-Zumar (الزمر): the plural of zumra, which is a company and a group. God the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups... (71)﴾ [al-Zumar], and God the Exalted said: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups... (73)﴾ [al-Zumar]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root z-m-r, adapted].
3 - al-La'na (اللعنة): wrath and removal from mercy; la'n is abuse and supplication for expulsion from God's mercy. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root l-'-n].

And the Most High continues describing what the people of misery receive in the Fire. He says:

﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is the Effector of what He intends (107).﴾

The word "khulud" (abiding forever) indicates a long stay, a stay that has a beginning but no end. When it is made eternal (abad), this is an emphasis on the eternity of abiding.

Those who are wretched enter the Fire starting from the moment of ﴿the Day when no soul speaks except by His permission (105)﴾ [Hud]. For the disbelievers, this is a punishment with no end.

As for the punishment of the Muslim who disobeys, for the sins he committed, it begins from the moment the reckoning ends and continues until the period of his punishment, proportionate to his disobedience, is over. After that, he enters Paradise.(2)

For this reason the Most High said: ﴿except as your Lord wills (107)﴾ [Hud]. Thus the Most High reduces the abiding in the Fire for those among the believers who are half-believers. And ﴿your Lord is the Effector of what He intends (107)﴾ means that nothing restrains Him.

Beware lest you think that the decree of God is restrained by anything. The decree is His act, and no one questions Allah about what He does, because the Essence of God is the Doer. If He wills to reduce the abiding in the Fire of a disobedient Muslim, the reduction will take place at the end. By this, the reduction of his abiding in Paradise is also realized, because he will not enter it except after he has completed his punishment.

With this understanding, the problem about which one hundred and fifty scholars have differed is resolved. Some of them thought that the Most High closes the gates of the Fire on those He has admitted into it, and that this continues without end. Likewise, whoever enters Paradise from the beginning will remain in it forever, and God will not bring the people of major sins into Paradise. Whoever holds this opinion is making equal the one who commits a major sin and the one who disbelieves in God, and this is inconceivable and far from the mercy of God.

Since some of these scholars based their opinion on the noble verse in Surat al-Jinn, in which the Most High says: ﴿except a message from Allah and His messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever (23).﴾ [al-Jinn]

We say: The Most High multiplies His gentleness toward the disbeliever until he believes, and toward the disobedient until he repents. This is from the mercy of God. The eternal perpetuation of punishment is mentioned in only two verses,(3) and this is evidence of the greatness of God's mercy and the breadth of His pardon.

For this reason it has been said of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he is a mercy to the worlds. The word "al-'alamin" (the worlds) is the plural of "'alam" (world), and the "'alam" is everything other than God, the Exalted.

For this reason there is also a mercy for the disbeliever, which is God's bounty to him in this world.

Thus we know that God is the One who possesses the laws of the cosmos. He did not leave them to act on their own; rather, He exercises His authority over them. And since the decree is His act, He changes it as He wills.

He is the Lord of time, place, and motion. Since He is the Lord of everything, He is the Effector of what He intends, and here the eternity of time is subject to His will and His purpose.

The words of the Most High: ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure (107)﴾ [Hud] convey to us that Paradise or the Fire must have something above them that shelters them, and must exist above some earth.

If someone says: The Most High has mentioned in the Qur'an that the sky will sway(4) and split apart(5),

we answer him: Do not take a verse of the Qur'an except by joining it with its counterparts.(6)

For this reason the Most High said: ﴿On the Day the earth will be replaced by other than the earth, and the heavens (48)﴾ [Ibrahim].

The Most High bequeaths the land of Paradise to whom He wills, for He Himself says on the tongue of the believers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And they say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, to settle in Paradise wherever we will (74)"﴾ [al-Zumar]. Or, because man has changes, and what is around him has changes.

It is remarkable that man, who is served by inanimate matter, by growing plants, and by animals that feel and move, may live longer than some of the creatures subjected to serve him, yet he has a shorter life than the sun and the moon.

But here the Most High depicts the lifespan of man in the Hereafter, as though He gives him a term that exceeds the longest lives we know. For this reason He said: ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure (107)﴾ [Hud]. When God makes something dependent on something else, that dependence must come to be.

The Most High speaks of the people of the Fire among the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle (40)﴾ [al-A'raf]. Will the camel pass through the eye of the needle? That is impossible.

For this reason I say: Let us take the conditional statements within the scope of His saying: ﴿Effector of what He intends (107)﴾ [Hud].

The words of our master Jesus, peace be upon him, have come in the Book:

﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise (118).﴾ [al-Ma'idah]

The context would have required him to say: "And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."

This is a superficial view of the meanings of the Qur'an, through human minds. But in the eloquence of the Most High, the matter is otherwise. The matter of punishment or forgiveness is entrusted to God alone, in His hand, and no one has the right to ask Him: Why did You do this? Why did You leave that?

Therefore this is the meaning of might. For this reason He is Mighty, and He is also Wise in whatever matter He decides, whether by punishment or forgiveness.

So He concluded with the closing phrase that establishes for the Most High either punishment or forgiveness.

Concerning the punishment of the disbelievers, He said: ﴿Effector of what He intends (107)﴾. And concerning those who obeyed and entered Paradise, He said:

﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift uninterrupted (108).﴾

1. (Fa'ala, yaf'alu, fa'ilun.) Fa'il is the active participle of fa'ala, and fa''al is an intensive form of fa'ala. The Most High said: ﴿And those who are active in zakah (4)﴾ [al-Mu'minun], and He said: ﴿...Indeed your Lord is the Effector of what He intends (107)﴾ [Hud]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root f-'-l, with adaptation.]
2. On the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "As for the people of the Fire who are its people, they will not die in it nor will they live. But some people will be touched by the Fire because of their sins, or he said, their misdeeds, so God causes them to die a death, until when they become charcoal, permission is given for intercession, and they are brought in clusters and scattered upon the rivers of Paradise. Then it is said: O people of Paradise, pour water over them, and they will sprout like a seed grows in the silt carried by a torrent." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih, hadith (185), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/5, 11).
3. This is in His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever; they will find no protector or helper (64-65)﴾ [al-Ahzab], and likewise in Surat al-Jinn: ﴿...And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever... (23)﴾ [al-Jinn].
4. Mara al-shay'u yamuru mawran: it moved, went, and came quickly. The Most High said: ﴿On the Day the sky will sway violently (9)﴾ [al-Tur]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root m-w-r.]
5. Yatafattaru al-shay'u wa-yanfatiru: it splits open. The Most High said: ﴿When the sky is split open (1)﴾ [al-Infitar], meaning it will split on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it (90)﴾ [Maryam], meaning they split from the horror of their disbelief and their claim that God has a son, as is understood from His saying: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something monstrous. The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin (88-90)﴾ [Maryam]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root f-.-r, with adaptation.]
6. Al-Damim: that which is joined to something else. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root d-m-m.] The intended meaning is to join similar verses together and to understand them in a comprehensive way.
7. Badal al-shay': its substitute. Badal al-kalam: its replacement, or its alteration so that it conveys a meaning other than what was intended. The Most High said: ﴿But those who did wrong changed it to a word other than what had been said to them (59)﴾ [al-Baqarah], meaning they changed it to other speech or distorted it so that it conveys a meaning other than what was intended. And His saying: ﴿Then substituted good after evil (11)﴾ [al-Naml], meaning doing good and fine deeds after doing evil. And the Most High said: ﴿...And if We willed, We could replace them with their likes, a complete replacement (28)﴾ [al-Insan], meaning We would make others in their place, as in His saying: ﴿...If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation (19)﴾ [Ibrahim]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root b-d-l.]
8. Bawwa'ahu: he settled him; bawwa'ahu fi al-ard: he established him in it and gave him power there. The Most High said: ﴿And when We settled Abraham at the site of the House (26)﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning We prepared it for him and empowered him over it. And concerning the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿He settles wherever he wills in the land (56)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning he would dwell in any place in the land of Egypt that he wished, and this is a metaphor for the breadth of his standing. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root b-w-', with adaptation.]
9. Al-sammu (the s may take three vowels) is a narrow hole. The Most High said: ﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle (40)﴾ [al-A'raf], meaning the hole of the needle. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root s-m-m.]
10. Judda al-shay', yajudduhu judhdhan: he cut, broke, or crumbled it. Al-judhadh: broken, crumbled pieces and debris. The Most High said: ﴿So He reduced them to fragments, except the largest of them (58)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. Al-majdhudh: that which is cut off. The Most High said: ﴿...a gift uninterrupted (108)﴾ [Hud], meaning it is a lasting gift that is not cut off. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root j-dh-dh.]
Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, gives the believers whatever He wills, and affirms their eternal abiding in Paradise; His giving to them is neither cut off nor withheld.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 109:

Then, after that, the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) says:

﴿So do not be in doubt (mirya)(1) about what these worship. They worship only as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished (ghayr manqus)(2).﴾ (11:109):

Was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then in doubt?

Was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in uncertainty?

No. Rather, this is the speech of the Highest Commander (al-Amr al-A'la), subhanahu, to one lower than Him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was already engaged in this matter. By this, the command of the Truthful One is directed toward continuity (al-dawam).

Just as the Truthful One said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer...(78)﴾ [al-Isra'].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was already establishing the prayer before this, but the saying of the Truthful One here represents the beginning of legislation (al-tashri').

Similarly, the Truthful One said in addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites...(1)﴾ [al-Ahzab].

Was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then not fearing Allah?

We say: No. Rather, it is for the perpetuation of taqwa (piety). When the Highest commands the lower with a matter he is already doing, the command is directed toward continuity: the following of his community to taqwa and turning away from hypocrisy and disbelief. It is an address to the Messenger and his community: for the Messenger there is continuity, advancement and protection, and for his community there is following the method of Allah.

Similarly His saying: ﴿O you who believe...(153)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. He, subhanahu, calls them by faith because they had believed in the belief of the One Divinity, and whoever among them hears this address must persist in faith.

Since he has believed in the One God before the address, he deserves to receive honour from the Truthful One by being addressed and described as among the believers. When they are called by this attribute, it is a sign of accepted nobility.

And when an attribute is requested from one in whom the attribute exists, know that He, subhanahu, requires the continuance and persistence of the attribute in him, and in persistence there is elevation.

As for the saying of the Truthful One here: ﴿...what these worship...(109)﴾ [Hud]: we find that, on verification, worship cannot be established for them, because the meaning of worship is the obedience of the worshipper to the command of the worshipped. These people worship idols, and idols have no method that those who believe in them follow.

Yet the Truthful One has established for them here that they worshipped idols, and they had said before: ﴿We only worship them so that they bring us nearer to Allah in zulfa(4)...(3)﴾ [al-Zumar].

This is faith that has lost the proof of reason (hujjiyat al-ta'aqqul al-iman), that is: that you yourself confront the matter of faith with your own being and discuss it, so that you enter it through the conviction of your own self.

They entered faith through the worship of idols by the persuasion of others, namely their fathers. Their faith is faith by imitation (taqlid), and in imitation there is the dryness of the sound nature (fitra), and it does not benefit.

We know that the Truthful One, exalted is He, has made attribution (al-nisba) in the cosmos either to establish a positive attribution or a negative attribution(5).

﴿...what they worship...(109)﴾ [Hud]: that is, according to what they called it worship, but it is not worship, because worship requires a command and a prohibition, and idols have no commands or prohibitions. Their worship is a traditional worship of the fathers; that is why they said: ﴿Nay, we follow what we found(6) our fathers upon...(170)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Therefore the Truthful One here decrees their recompense, saying, exalted is He: ﴿...And indeed We will give them their portion(7) undiminished (109)﴾ [Hud]: that is, We will give them their recompense in full, because they corrupt the cosmos, although the Truthful One has given you, concerning them, the right of choice in whether to do a thing or not do it; and if the movement of choice is not disciplined, social balance slides into imbalance.

Since man has the right of choice, the Truthful One has sent down for him the method that comprises the faith-based obligations.

When they imitated the fathers, they walked on the path of corrupting the cosmos; therefore the Truthful One gives them their portion of punishment in full.

What is understood from the word "portion" (nasib)(9) is that it is used for provision, and the Truthful One mentions it here to establish a portion of punishment, and in this there is mockery of them and derision of them.

1 - Al-mirya (with a kasra or damma on the m): disputation and doubt. The Almighty said: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord...(17)﴾ [Hud], and it is read mirya with a damma on the m. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root m-r-y].

2 - Al-naqs: a verbal noun of naqasa. The Almighty said: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits...(155)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Manqus is its passive participle; the Almighty said: ﴿...And indeed We will give them their portion undiminished (109)﴾ [Hud], that is, complete, without Us diminishing anything from it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root n-q-s].

3 - 'Abada Allah yu'abiduhu, 'ibada and 'ubudda: he obeyed Him, so he is 'abid (active participle). 'Abbada (doubled) means he subjected him and humbled him. The Truthful One said: ﴿And this is a favour of which you remind me, that you have enslaved (abbadta) the Children of Israel (22)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. The 'abd, in relation to people, is the slave owned as property; its plurals include 'ibad, 'abid, and 'abd. The 'abd, in relation to Allah, is the human being, free or enslaved; both are owned by Allah, subject to His rule and will. The worshippers of idols are worshippers of ideas that are fabrications and distortions from the fitra upon which Allah created people, and every worshipper of a deviant idea has deviated from the truth. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/3, 4, adapted].

4 - Al-zulfa: nearness, rank and degree. The Almighty said: ﴿And neither your wealth nor your children will bring you near to Us in nearness (zulfa)(37)﴾ [Saba'], that is, nearness, as a synonymous absolute object, or it brings you to a near degree and rank with Us. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root z-l-f].

5 - In the cosmos there are single words whose meanings we know, such as "the heavens" and "the earth", and we grasp the conception of the thing; but when we attach an attribute to this thing, this means attribution (nisba), such as our saying: "The earth is spherical." [Derived from the speech of the honourable Shaykh].

6 - Alfa al-shay': he found it. The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed they found their fathers astray (69)﴾ [al-Saffat], and He said: ﴿And they found her lord at the door...(25)﴾ [Yusuf], that is, they found him. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root l-f-y].

7 - Wafa ilayhi haqqahu: he delivered to him his right in full. It is transitive to two objects, so one says: wafahu haqqahu. The active participle, muwaff, is a defective noun. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/347].

8 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3423]:
"In it are three opinions:
One: their portion of provision; said by Abu al-'Aliya.
The second: their portion of punishment; said by Ibn Zayd.
The third: what they were promised of good or evil; said by Ibn 'Abbas."

9 - Al-nasib: the share and portion of a thing. The Almighty said: ﴿Those will have a portion of what they earned (202)﴾ [al-Baqarah], that is, they have a fortune, share and portion which is their right from their earnings. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root n-s-b].

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 11, verse 110:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{We indeed gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it. Had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed they are in disquieting doubt about it.} (110)¹

Surah Hud is the only surah in the Qur'an in which the mention of one messenger occurs twice. God, glory be to Him, mentioned that He commanded Moses, peace be upon him, to go to Pharaoh and to show him the signs, and He did not add more. Then He moved on from that delivery of the message and said, glory be to Him: {He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection… } (98) [Hud]. That is, He followed the opening of the message with the outcome that Pharaoh reaches on the Day of Resurrection, when he leads his people into the Fire.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, comes here to Moses, peace be upon him, after the beginning of his mission. For this reason He says, exalted is He: {And We indeed gave Moses the Book…} (110) [Hud].

We know that the mention of Moses, peace be upon him, at the beginning came in connection with what relates to Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, when Moses arrived at the water of Madyan. But what is remarkable is that when Shu'ayb is mentioned, the story of Moses with him is not mentioned; rather, the story of Moses with Pharaoh is mentioned.

We have learned that Moses, peace be upon him, did not come to Pharaoh except for one task: that he send the Children of Israel with him and not torment them.²

As for what follows after that, namely faith in God, it came as a subsidiary matter, because the mission of Moses, peace be upon him, was only for the Children of Israel. For this reason he came here with the Book, to convey it to the Children of Israel as a method of life. In the first passage, however, He, glory be to Him, mentioned the signs with which Moses was sent to Pharaoh.

We know that Surah Hud presents the processions of the messengers: Noah, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb and Abraham, peace be upon them all. The discussion of Moses, peace be upon him, came in it twice: once in his relationship with Pharaoh, and once in his relationship with the Children of Israel.

In each of these snapshots there is a fundamental task of the divine method for people in general, from the first, Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour is established. However, at the mention of each messenger it brings the snapshot that addresses a disease that is timely among his people.

The common element in the calls of all the messengers is His saying, glory be to Him: {Worship God; you have no god other than Him} (59) [al-A'raf].³ Then the matter differs from one messenger to another: some of them command their people not to worship idols, and others command their people not to diminish the measure and the scale.

Thus we find in every snapshot with every messenger the cure of a disease among the diseases of that nation. As for Islam, it came to cure the diseases of all humanity, and for this reason all virtuous values were gathered in the Qur'an as a method for humanity.⁴

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, does not relate the Qur'anic stories to us for entertainment, or to kill time, or to learn history; rather, so that we may draw the lesson from the message of each messenger to his nation to which he was sent, in order to treat its disease.

And since the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) will be the last era in which humans meet humans,⁵ and in it will be all the atmospheres and diseases of the world, it is therefore incumbent upon them to draw those lessons, because their message encompasses all time and all place.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: {And We indeed gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it…} (110) [Hud].

We know that if two matters precede a pronoun of the third person, it is correct for the pronoun to refer back to each of them.

His saying, glory be to Him: {…but differences arose concerning it…} (110): it is valid that the difference refers to the matter of Moses, and it is valid that the difference refers to the matter of the Book. Disagreement over one of the two leads to disagreement over the other, because there is an inseparable link between Moses, peace be upon him, and the Book that God sent down to him.

Thus the two matters meet: the matter of the message in the Book, and the matter of the messenger in his selection. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, did not make them two matters; rather, they are one matter, because the messenger is not separated from his method.

His saying, the Truth: {We gave Moses the Book…} (110): this is a matter related to the act of the Truth, glory be to Him. God has an essence, God has attributes, and God has acts.

He, glory be to Him, is exalted in His essence above any likeness. God has attributes, and they are not like all attributes. The Truth, glory be to Him, exists, and you exist, but His existence is eternal and everlasting, not subject to non-existence, whereas your existence is contingent and subject to non-existence.

We take everything related to God, glory be to Him, within the framework of: {There is nothing like unto Him…} (11) [al-Shura].⁶ So when the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks of an act, take every act that proceeds from Him through His infinite power, glory be to Him.

His saying, glory be to Him, here: {We gave Moses the Book…} (110) [Hud]: from it we understand that this act necessitated complete attributes: knowledge, wisdom, power, pardon, might and subjugation. There are many things that combine to achieve this giving.

Someone may ask: since Moses, peace be upon him, was given the Book and differences arose concerning it, why did the Truth, glory be to Him, not seize the people of Moses as He seized the people of Noah, or the people of 'Ad, or the people of Thamud, or the rest of the nations whom God seized with punishment?

We say: they were not saved from the punishment of God by their own power; rather, because the Truth, glory be to Him, made their punishment deferred,⁷ and it is the Day of Reckoning.

For this reason He said, in the same verse: {Had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, the matter would have been decided between them…} (110) [Hud]. Thus the Truth decided with a decisive judgment, just as He judged the earlier nations whose messengers' task was only to deliver the message, and whose messengers' task was not to fight in order to establish a call or to affirm a truth. For this reason it was heaven that intervened with the final command.

But the matter differed in the mission of Moses, peace be upon him, for the word of God, exalted is He, had already been issued concerning it, postponing the reckoning until the Day of Resurrection.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: {…And indeed they are in disquieting doubt about it} (110) [Hud]. It is as if they are in doubt about the Day of Resurrection and in doubt about the reckoning, like His saying, glory be to Him, at the beginning of the verse concerning the difference over the Book and Moses, peace be upon him.

**Notes (as they appear in the source):**

1. *Sabaqa* (سبق, to precede): *sabaqa* (intransitive) means to go forward, and *sabaqahu* (transitive) means to precede him. The active participle is *sabiq*, and the passive participle is *masbuq*. God says: {Had there not been a decree from God that preceded…} (68) [al-Anfal], meaning: that went before, and the judgment in it was established earlier, namely the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*). *Al-kalima* (the word) is God's decree and His judgment previously recorded in the Preserved Tablet. God says: {And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord} (110) [Hud], meaning: His decree to defer the judgment among people until the Day of Resurrection. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim*, 1/301; root s-b-q, k-l-m, adapted.]

2. *Rayb* (ريب, doubt): doubt. God says: {This is the Book about which there is no doubt} (2) [al-Baqarah]. One says *rabahu al-amr*, *yaribuhu*, *raybān* and *rayba*: he doubted it. *Al-rayb* also means the sudden calamity of time, and *rayb al-manun* means death. God says: {Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the calamity of death"?} (30) [al-Tur], meaning the occurrence of death. God says: {Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts} (110) [al-Tawbah], meaning: a source of doubt and hypocrisy. *Arabahu* means to bring him to doubt and to introduce doubt into his soul. The active participle is *murib*. God says: {…And indeed they are in disquieting doubt about it} (110) [Hud], as an emphasis, meaning: in a doubt that leads to doubt. *Arāba al-rajul*, so he is *murib*, means he became a place of suspicion and doubt, and people are not at ease with him.
