1 – "Zalafa ilayhi yazlifu zulfatan wa zulfa": he drew near and approached. The Exalted said: {When they saw it approaching (zulfah)...} [Al-Mulk] meaning nearness, and it is a description by the verbal noun in its own form, parsed as a circumstantial accusative (hal), meaning "in a state of nearness," that is, very near. "Zulfa" means nearness, rank and station. The Exalted said: ﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position (zulfa)...﴾ (37) [Saba'], meaning nearness, an absolute object of the same root, or they bring you a near rank and station with Us. "Zulfah" means a portion of the night, and its plural is "zulaf." The Exalted said: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at some hours (zulfan) of the night﴾ (114) [Hud], meaning times and periods of the night. It is said: at its beginning; and it is said: at any time within it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root z-l-f].

2 – "Al-tarf," with a fatha on the ra': the side and the extremity of a thing. The Exalted said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion (tarf) of those who disbelieved...﴾ (127) [Al 'Imran], meaning destroy a side of them, that is, a group of them. The Exalted said: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day...﴾ (114) [Hud], meaning morning and evening; and the intended meaning is all times, supported by His saying: ﴿...And during the hours of the night glorify Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ (130) [Ta-Ha], meaning all times. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root: t-r-f].

3 – "Al-zawal": the time when the sun is at the midpoint of the sky. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root: z-w-l].

4 – Mujahid said: the first end is the Subh prayer, and the second end is the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers; Ibn 'Atiyyah chose this. It is also said: the two ends are Subh and Maghrib, reported by Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan. Also from al-Hasan: the second end is 'Asr alone; Qatadah and al-Dahhak also said this. Al-Qurtubi transmitted it in his tafsir [4/3428].

5 – Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar [3/30]: "The majority held that the witr is not obligatory but a sunnah. Abu Hanifa differed from them and said it is obligatory, and it is also reported from him that it is fard. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I know of no one who agreed with Abu Hanifa in this. Among the evidences that the witr is not obligatory is what the two Shaykhs agreed upon from the hadith of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Five prayers in the day and night.' He said: 'Is there anything else obligatory on me?' He said: 'No, unless you volunteer.'"

6 – Fard: what is established by a definitive proof without doubt; its denier is a disbeliever and its neglecter is punished. It is of two kinds: fard 'ayn (individual obligation) and fard kifayah (communal obligation). Fard 'ayn is what every individual must perform, and it is not lifted from some by others performing it, like faith and the like. Fard kifayah is what all Muslims must perform, and it is lifted from the rest when some perform it, like jihad and the funeral prayer. As for wajib: it is the name for what is incumbent upon us by a proof that contains some uncertainty, like a report from a single narrator, analogy, a general statement that has been specified, and an interpreted verse, like the zakat al-fitr and the sacrifice. [Al-Ta'rifat by al-Jurjani, pp. 144, 222].

7 – Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir [4/3430] that the occasion of revelation of this verse was that a man of the Ansar was alone with a woman, kissed her, and enjoyed her short of intercourse. Al-Tirmidhi related from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I was intimate with a woman at the far end of the city, and I touched her short of sexual intercourse; here I am, so judge me as you wish." 'Umar said to him: "Allah would have concealed you had you concealed yourself." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him anything. The man left, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man after him and called him, and recited to him: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ (114) [Hud]. A man from the people said: "Is this for him alone?" He said: "No, rather it is for all people." Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hadith hasan sahih."

8 – Related by Muslim in his Sahih (233), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/484), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1086), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

9 – From Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever fasts the Day of 'Arafah, he is forgiven for the year before it and the year after it."

10 – "Hawl": skill, sharpness of perception, and ability to exercise precision in affairs. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root: h-w-l].

11 – Bu'rat al-shu'ur: the focal point of awareness; hashiyat al-shu'ur: its periphery. (These are the terms used by al-Sha'rawi in his explanation; the gloss is provided here for clarity.)

12 – [Translator's note omitted; text continues in part 2.]

13 – [Text as given.]

14 – [Text as given.]

١١ - On the authority of Mu'adh ibn Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever eats food and then says, 'All praise is due to Allah, who fed me this food and provided it for me without any power or strength from me,' his past and future sins will be forgiven. And whoever puts on a garment and says, 'All praise is due to Allah, who clothed me in this garment and provided it for me without any power or strength from me,' his past and future sins will be forgiven." Related by Abu Dawud in his Sunan [4023], and likewise Ibn Majah [3285].

١٢ - On the authority of Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "[Allah] said: 'Glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah.' For these are the enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat), and they cause sins to fall away just as a tree sheds its leaves, and they are among the treasures of Paradise."
Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib [2/248]: "Al-Tabarani related it through two chains, the better of which contains 'Umar ibn Rashid, and the rest of its narrators are relied upon in the Sahih. This chain is acceptable for corroborating reports. Ibn Majah related it through the route of 'Umar as well, in abridged form."

١٣ - Al-kaffarah (expiation): what Allah has prescribed of acts of devotion to wipe out sins and forgive them, such as the expiation for an oath, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So its expiation is feeding ten needy people...﴾ [al-Ma'idah] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry k-f-r]. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-'Arab [entry: k-f-r]: "The mention of kaffarah recurs in the hadith. It refers to the act or quality which by its nature covers over the sin, that is, wipes it out and conceals it."

١٤ - The phrase lafaza al-nawah (he uttered the date-stone) means he threw it out; lafaza al-kalimah (he uttered the word) means he said it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watchful observer, ready (atid).﴾ [Qaf] That is, every word a person speaks is recorded against him through an angel 'atid, and 'atid means present and prepared to record this statement in the book of good deeds and bad deeds. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entries l-f-z, '-t-d].
.

١٥ - Al-lamam: minor sins. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for minor faults (al-lamam)...﴾ [al-Najm] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry l-m-m].
Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿except for minor faults (al-lamam)﴾ [al-Najm]: "Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter, which the prayers expiate, is al-lamam, and it is less than every prescribed punishment. As for the limit of this world, it is every punishment which Allah has ordained in this world. As for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything which Allah has concluded with the Fire, deferring its punishment to the Hereafter." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir [4/256].

١٦ - Al-fahsha' (indecency): al-fahsh, which is the ugly and objectionable deed. Allah the Exalted says: {Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency...} [al-Baqarah]. That is, he orders you to stinginess or to ugly deeds in general, and among stinginess and indecencies are matters that are ugly and objectionable [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry f-h-sh].
And al-munkar (what is objectionable) is what the noble Shari'ah finds abhorrent and what sound minds reject. Allah the Exalted says: {Let there be among you a community calling to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong...} [Al 'Imran] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry n-k-r].

١٧ - On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him. Whoever intends a good deed and does it, ten to seven hundred times its reward is recorded for him. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is recorded against him, and if he does it, it is recorded." Related by Muslim in his Sahih [130], Kitab al-Iman.

١٨ - Bu'rat al-shay' (the focus of a thing): its center or its middle. Bu'rat al-shu'ur (the focus of feeling): its center, meaning the inner center of sensation and awareness [perception] in the brain. Linguistically, al-bu'rah is a pit (hufrah), derived from al-bi'r (well). As for al-bu'rah in "the science of physics," it is the point at which light, heat or sound rays converge when nothing stands in their way [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: entry b-'-r, with adaptation and addition].
.

١٩ - On the authority of 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: I had hemorrhoids (bawasir), so I asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side." Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad [4/426] and by al-Bukhari in his Sahih [2/584, 586 - al-Fath]. Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq said in Fiqh al-Sunnah [1/101]: "Whoever is unable to stand in an obligatory prayer prays according to his ability, for Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and he has his full reward without diminution."

٢٠ - This occurred on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj at Sidrat al-Muntaha. Al-Bukhari mentioned it at the beginning of the Book of Prayer [1/458]. In it the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then I was raised up until I reached a level where I heard the scratching of the pens. Allah made fifty prayers obligatory upon my community, so I returned with that, until I passed by Musa, who said: 'What did your Lord make obligatory for your community?' I said: 'Fifty prayers.' He said: 'Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.' So I returned, and He reduced part of it. I went back to Musa and said: 'He reduced part of it.' He said: 'Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.' So I returned to Him, and He said: 'They are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me.' I returned to Musa, and he said: 'Return to your Lord.' I said: 'I am ashamed before my Lord.'" [Hadith 349].

٢١ - Asraf: exceeded moderation and balance. Extravagance (israf) occurs in wealth and in other matters. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah...﴾ [al-Zumar]. That is, they exceeded moderation and balance in many matters, so they multiplied their sins against themselves. Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant (al-musrifin)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. Extravagance occurs in many matters, not in spending wealth alone. And among the sayings of the righteous: "There is no extravagance in good, and no good in extravagance" [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry s-r-f], with adaptation.

٢٢ - Qanata, yaqnutu, qunutan: his hope in good was cut off, or he despaired of it, so he is qani (one who despairs). Hafs recited with a fatha on the nun in the past tense in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired (qanatu)...﴾ [al-Shu'ara'], and in His saying: ﴿...so do not be of those who despair (al-qanitin)﴾ [al-Hijr]. It was also recited as "min al-qanitin" with a kasra on the nun, and the three vowels have been recited on the nun in His saying: ﴿...and who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ [al-Hijr].
Qunut is an intensive form. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿...and if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless (qanut)﴾ [Fussilat], that is, extremely despairing, devoid of security. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry q-n-t], with adaptation.

٢٣ - Fahusha, yafhushu, fahshan: he is fahish, that is, he exceeded the limit and did an ugly deed. Al-fahishah is an ugly act. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when they commit an indecency (fahishah)...﴾ [al-A'raf]. Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿And those of your women who commit indecency (al-fahishah)...﴾ [al-Nisa'], that is, adultery. And He says: ﴿And do not approach the indecencies (al-fawahish)...﴾ [al-An'am], that is, do not approach ugly and objectionable matters [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry f-h-sh]..

And the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And be patient, for indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost (115).﴾

The word "be patient" (isbir) has come to serve all the processes of steadfastness.

Likewise the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant in it (132)﴾ [Taha]. Patience is of two kinds: patience "upon" (ʿala) and patience "from" (ʿan). In acts of obedience, it is patience upon the hardship of the act of obedience, like your patience in getting up from sleep to pray the dawn prayer; and in guarding against sins, it is patience from desires.

Thus we know that patience in its absolute sense is required in both matters: in the command to obey, and in the negation of disobedience.

We know that Paradise is surrounded by hardships, so be patient upon hardships; and the Fire is surrounded by desires, so be patient from them.

Suppose a person desires to eat meat but does not have the price of it; he is patient from it and does not go into debt.

Therefore the ascetics say: there is no such thing as expensiveness, but there is such a thing as the cheapness of the self.

Hence we find someone who says: if something becomes expensive for me, I leave it, and it will be at its cheapest when it has become expensive.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And be patient over what befalls you (17)﴾ [Luqman]; and here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And be patient, for indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost (115)﴾ [Hud]. They are those who have entered the station of ihsan (excellence, doing what is beautiful), which is that one binds himself with the kind of what Allah has obligated, beyond what Allah has obligated, of prayer, fasting, zakat, or pilgrimage to the House of Allah; because worship is not a suggestion from a worshipper to a worshipped one, rather the Worshipped is the One who determines what brings you near to Him.

Try not to enter the station of ihsan by way of vows (nadhr), because it may be hard for you to fulfill what you have vowed; and make the time of choice and voluntary worship in your hand, so that you do not enter into a loving relationship of ihsan with Allah and then slacken from it, as if you—God forbid—had tested the love of Allah the Exalted and found Him not worthy of it, and in this there is arrogance on your part.

And if you see illuminations and outpourings upon one who has entered the station of ihsan and you deny them to him, you would be equating between one who stopped at what was obligated upon him and one who went beyond what Allah obligated of its kind.

Try this in yourself: keep to the command of Allah by observing the times of prayer; rise to pray the dawn prayer in the mosque; then be keen to perfect your work; and when noon comes, go to prayer in the mosque, and try to increase the rak'ahs of the Sunnah. You will find that the density of darkness has become thin in your depths, and it is filled with luminous illuminations that surpass the perceptions of the senses. Therefore do not consider it too much for one who trains himself in this spiritual discipline, when you find the Truth, glorified is He, has illuminated his insight with manifestations of means of perception and transparency. Thus we do not find anyone of the people of light and illumination claiming what is not his; and one of them may know things about another person who is not committed, and does not announce them to him, because Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has singled him out with things and attributes that he must not place in a position of boasting and ostentation.

When the Truth, glorified is He, presented this matter, He wished to set limits for the one who trains himself and for one who does not, in the story of Musa, peace be upon him, when Musa and his servant found a righteous servant. The Truth, glorified is He, described the righteous servant with His saying: ﴿...a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence (65)﴾ [al-Kahf].

The righteous servant said to Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿...Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me (67)﴾ [al-Kahf]. He explained to Musa—with the utmost courtesy—his excuse for not being patient, and said to him: ﴿And how can you be patient over that which you do not encompass in knowledge? (68)﴾ [al-Kahf].

Musa, peace be upon him, replied: ﴿...You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order (69)﴾ [al-Kahf].

The righteous servant said: ﴿...If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention to you its explanation (70)﴾ [al-Kahf]. But the events followed one another, and Musa did not remain patient; so the righteous servant said to him: ﴿This is parting between me and you... (78)﴾ [al-Kahf]. This is an eternal decree that one who trains himself in spiritual discipline and has entered the station of ihsan cannot meet with another who is not so trained on that basis; and let the one who is not trained keep courtesy just as the trained one keeps courtesy, and let him offer an excuse for the one who denies what he does not know.

And if the trained one had excused the untrained one, and if the untrained one had been courteous with the trained one, the balance of the cosmos would have been stable.

The Truth, glorified is He, shows us the station of ihsan and the reward of the doers of good in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs (15), taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed they were before that doers of good (16)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat].

The Truth, glorified is He, shows us the stages of ihsan, and that they are of the kind of what Allah the Exalted has obligated, in His saying: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night (17)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat].

The Truth, glorified is He, did not charge in Islam that the Muslim should sleep only a little of the night; the Muslim may pray ʿIshaʾ and sleep until dawn.

The stages of ihsan continue, and He says: ﴿And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness (18)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat]. The Truth, glorified is He, did not charge the Muslim with that, but whoever desires to rise to the station of ihsan does so.

He also says: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived (19)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat]. The Truth, glorified is He, did not specify this right here as a known right; rather He made it an unknown or undefined right. Allah the Exalted has not obligated upon the Muslim except zakat, but whoever desires the station of ihsan gives from his wealth to the beggar and the deprived.

Thus the believer enters the station of ihsan so that the Truth, glorified is He, may love him.

And to Allah belongs the highest likeness: we find that a person, when another loves him, gives him from his special qualities and overflows upon him from his abundant gifts, knowledge or wealth; so what of one who enters into a loving relationship with Allah, glorified and exalted is He?

1 - ishtabara (iṣṭabara): on the pattern of iftaʿala, and it indicates increase of patience and endurance. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant in it (132)﴾ [Taha]; and He says: ﴿So worship Him and be constant in His worship (65)﴾ [Maryam]; and He says: ﴿Indeed We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient (27)﴾ [al-Qamar]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root ṣ-b-r, with adaptation].
2 - ḥaffa: the people surrounded the House, or what is around it: they circled it and encompassed it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We surrounded them both with palm trees (32)﴾ [al-Kahf], meaning We made the palms encircle the two gardens. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root ḥ-f-f]. And ḥaffa al-shayʾ ḥaffan wa-ḥifafan: it circled around it and encompassed it. It is said: ḥaffa al-shayʾ bi-l-shayʾ wa-ḥawlahu, and min ḥawlihi. [al-Muʿjam al-Waseet: root ḥ-f-f].
3 - From Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih [2822]. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary: "As for hardships, it includes striving in acts of worship and persistence in them, patience upon their difficulties, restraining anger, pardoning, forbearance, charity, kindness to the one who wrongs you, and patience from desires. As for the desires with which the Fire is surrounded, the apparent meaning is the forbidden desires, such as wine, adultery, looking at a non-mahram woman, backbiting, using musical instruments, and the like. As for permissible desires, they are not included in this, but it is disliked to over-indulge in them, lest they lead to forbidden desires, or harden the heart, or distract from acts of obedience, or necessitate concern for acquiring worldly things to be spent on them."
4 - Patience is either upon the commanded things, which is obedience; or patience upon the forbidden things, which are the prohibitions; or patience upon what is decreed, and this is patience upon qadaʾ and qadar. If the three are realized, you are among the successful, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful (200)﴾ [Aal ʿImran].
5 - From Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not make vows, for a vow does not avail anything against what is decreed; it is only by it that something is extracted from the miser." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih [1640], al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan [1538], and likewise al-Nasaʾi [7/17]. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary: its meaning is that one does not bring this act of nearness as pure voluntary initiation, but brings it in exchange for the healing of a sick person or other things upon which the vow is contingent.
6 - rāḍa yarūḍu rawḍan wa-riyāḍan wa-riyāḍatan: he tamed it. It is said: rāḍa al-mahr (he broke the colt), rāḍa nafsahu bi-l-taqwa (he trained his soul through God-consciousness), rāḍa al-qawafi al-ṣaʿba (he tamed difficult rhymes). Itrāḍa: became trained; it is said: irtāḍa al-mahr: became tame; irtāḍat al-qawafi: became tamed. Riyāḍa, according to the Sufis, is the refinement of the moral character of the soul by constant performance of acts of worship and abstention from desires. [al-Muʿjam al-Waseet: root r-w-ḍ, with adaptation].
7 - ladun: a noun of place or time, meaning [ʿind] (near, with), built on sukun. When it is annexed to the first person ya', a wiqaya nun is placed between them and assimilated into its nun, as in His saying: ﴿...Indeed you have reached from my ladunni an excuse (76)﴾ [al-Kahf]. It comes annexed to the second person pronoun in His saying: ﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy (8)﴾ [Aal ʿImran]; to the first person plural pronoun nā in His saying: ﴿...And We taught him knowledge from Our presence (65)﴾ [al-Kahf]; and it is annexed to the third person pronoun, as in His saying: ﴿To warn of severe punishment from Him and give good tidings to the believers... (2)﴾ [al-Kahf]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root l-d-n].
8 - khabar: news of a matter, and information about a matter; like ʿalimahu and ʿalima bihi, in form and meaning; so he is knowledgeable of it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿...then ask about Him one who is knowledgeable (59)﴾ [al-Furqan]. And He says: ﴿I will bring you from it information (7)﴾ [al-Naml], meaning: news. And He says: ﴿And how can you be patient over that which you do not encompass in knowledge (68)﴾ [al-Kahf], meaning: knowledge. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root kh-b-r].
9 - dhikr: the Qur'an and all the revealed books. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian (9)﴾ [al-Hijr], which is the noble Qur'an. And He says: ﴿A mention of the mercy of your Lord toward His servant Zechariah (2)﴾ [Maryam], meaning: the account of Allah's mercy to His servant Zechariah. And He says: ﴿And We raised for you your repute (4)﴾ [al-Sharh], meaning: honored you and people's talk about you in goodness. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root dh-k-r].
It is mentioned in [Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari: p. 337], in the interpretation of this verse: ﴿...until I myself mention to you its explanation (70)﴾ [al-Kahf]: he says: "until I make mention" that for you are the actions which you see that I do, and which you disapprove of, and I explain to you their matter, and I begin informing you about them."
10 - hajaʿa yahjaʿu hujūʿan: he slept at night. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night (17)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root h-j-ʿ].
11 - saḥar (with fatḥah on the sin and the ḥaʾ): the last part of the night up to the break of dawn; its plural is asḥār. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿...and those who ask forgiveness in the predawn hours (17)﴾ [Aal ʿImran], and He says: ﴿And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness (18)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root s-ḥ-r].
12 - al-sāʾil: the poor person, or one who asks about something. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel him (10)﴾ [al-Duha], which may carry both meanings: the petitioner who seeks charity, and the questioner who inquires about something. And His saying: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers (6)﴾ [al-Aʿraf], meaning: We will surely hold people and messengers accountable on the Day of Resurrection. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root s-a-l].
al-maḥrūm: one prevented from good. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Rather, we have been deprived (67)﴾ [al-Waqiʿah], meaning: we have been deprived of the fruit of the garden and deprived of all good. Deprivation (ḥirmān) is prevention; and al-maḥrūm is also a passive participle and is applied to the poor. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived (19)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: root ḥ-r-m].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 116 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted says next:
﴿So why were there not among the generations before you those of virtue (1) who forbade corruption on earth, except a few of those whom We saved from among them? But the wrongdoers followed what they were given of luxury (2) therein, and they were criminals.﴾ (11:116):
The word "lawla" (why not / if only) here is hortatory (tahdid), and exhortation is only a urging toward an act whose time has not yet come. If the time has passed and the act cannot be made up in it, then "lawla" expresses regret and remorse.
In Surat Yunus the Exalted says: ﴿Why was there not a city that believed so that its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus...﴾ (10:98). He mentioned them with the signs. We know that "lawla" has two usages in the language. If it is followed by a nominal clause, it indicates the prevention of a consequence owing to the existence of a condition, as when one person says to another: "Had it not been for your father, so-and-so, I would have struck you for what you did wrong." In this case "lawla" is called "the particle of prevention owing to existence" (harf imtina' li-wujud).
When "lawla" is followed by a verbal clause, it is a particle of exhortation (tahdid), stirring up and urging the addressee to do something, just as you encourage a student to study. You say to him: "Had you studied diligently and earnestly last year, you would not have passed and reached this academic year."
In this there is an incitement to him to exert more effort. But if you say to a failing student: "Had you studied, you would not have failed," this is reproach and regret for what has passed, and a charging of his energy for what is coming; because the time has gone and the time for studying has ended. Therefore "lawla" here is for rebuke and reproach (3). The Exalted guides us to the fact that what remains are the things that stand firm before the events of time. The events of time come to overthrow first the trivial thing, then what is below it, then what is below that, and what remains is the strong thing, because it is firm against the events of time; and what remains is always the best.
The Exalted has explained to us that He destroyed the earlier nations because there was no group among them that forbade corruption on earth, and destruction came to those who refrained from resisting corruption by enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.
The Exalted has set for us the example of "what remains" in everything, and that it is what endures before events. In the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, the Exalted says: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day. (84) And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit corruption on the earth, spreading mischief. (85) What remains from Allah is better for you, if you are believers...﴾ (11:84-86). The meaning of that is that reducing the measure or the scale may increase the merchant's holdings, but he does not turn his attention to what is stored up.
Therefore Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice (4) and do not deprive (5) the people of their things﴾ (11:85).
So if you look at a thing that has gone, you have the capacity to realise through understanding that it is stored up for you and remains.
We have an example in the conduct of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the Mother of the Believers 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, when he asked her about a sheep that had been given to him as a gift. She knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved the shoulder (kataf) of the sheep (6), so she gave away the whole sheep except a part of its shoulder. When he asked her: "What did you do with the sheep?" she said: "It has all gone except its shoulder." 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, looked at it from this realistic viewpoint: that what remained of the sheep was only its shoulder, and that she had given away the rest of the sheep. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned her attention with a glance of faith and certainty, and said to her: "It has all remained except its shoulder" (7).
In this way the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at what remained of the sheep as good.
This is supported by a hadith the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O son of Adam, what is yours of your wealth is only what you eat and finish, or what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and let pass" (8).
The Noble Qur'an draws our attention to the seen and the stored: the Exalted says: ﴿Wealth and children are adornment of the life of this world; but the enduring good deeds (9) are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope (10)﴾ (18:46). The Exalted describes this stored-up thing by saying: ﴿...for reward and better for hope﴾ (18:46).
In another verse He says: ﴿...And the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for return﴾ (19:76).
Therefore you must look at the enduring things among things, for they are what one relies upon.
The Exalted draws our attention to this in more than one place of the Noble Qur'an, saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ (87:17). He says: ﴿And what is with Allah is better and more enduring﴾ (28:60). So beware of looking at what has gone; rather look at what remains.
When events grip a person in any matter, we find that the one whose faith is shallow panics over what has gone, while the one whose faith is firmly rooted is thankful to Allah for what remains.
Behold our master 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, may Allah be pleased with him, when his leg was severely wounded while he was on the way to Syria. When he reached the palace of the caliphate, the physicians said: "There must be anaesthesia so that we may amputate the diseased leg." He said: "By Allah, I do not wish to be heedless of my Lord even for the blink of an eye."
This statement meant that the operation to cut off the leg would be performed without anaesthetic. When the leg was cut off and they wanted to take it to bury it, so that it might precede him to Paradise, God willing, he said: "Bring it to me." They brought it to him, he took it in his hand and said: "O Allah, if You have tested me in one limb, You have granted me well-being in the other limbs." Thus the believer looks at what remains.
When the Noble Qur'an speaks of the ranks and stations of faith, it says once: ﴿Those will enter Paradise...﴾ (40:40), and it says of other people: ﴿Those upon them are blessings from their Lord...﴾ (2:157). Paradise endures by Allah's preserving it, but the mercy of Allah endures by the enduring of Allah; thus the rank of mercy is higher than the rank of Paradise. And so in every matter you find what is called "the enduring things."
Here the Exalted says: ﴿So why were there not among the generations (12) before you those of virtue who forbade corruption on earth, except a few of those whom We saved from among them...﴾ (11:116). That is: had there not been among people a remnant of good, a remnant of faith and a remnant of certainty, forbidding corruption on earth, Allah would have caused the earth to swallow up its inhabitants.
The remnants in all things are the result of choice and testing, in confirmation of the Exalted's saying: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth...﴾ (13:17). In the modern age we say: "Survival is for the fittest."
So the Exalted preserves life only through those who forbid corruption on earth, because they act in the light of Allah's method; and this method does not add to Allah's dominion, nor add any attribute of perfection to Allah, for He created the universe with all perfection in it; His method only sets right the movement of life and the movement of living beings.
Thus the method of heaven returns its good to the creatures of Allah, not to Allah who formed the universe in its perfection.
Read, if you wish, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the heaven He raised and set up the balance. (7) That you not transgress within the balance. (8)﴾ (55:7-8). Just as the Exalted raised the heaven without pillars and made matters stable and balanced, so you are to act justly in the universe in matters within your choice with a precise balance, for a crooked balance corrupts the movement of life.
Among the crookedness of the balance is that the idle person takes the produce of the labourer, and people see the idle one living in luxury from the theft of the labourer's produce, so they do likewise, and the matter comes to the spread of corruption.
The men of talent withdraw, so that one of them works no more than the measure of his need, for if the fruit of his work increases, it is not protected by justice.
Thus the movement of life is corrupted, the scales are thrown into disorder, and societies fall behind the caravan of life.
The Exalted says: ﴿So why were there not among the generations before you those of virtue who forbade corruption on earth...﴾ (11:116). And Allah the Exalted willed to make the nation of Muhammad ﷺ the best of nations on condition that they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong (14)...﴾ (3:110). He made it the final nation, because there is no messenger after the message of Muhammad ﷺ; previously, messages came after goodness had diminished in societies and in souls.
The Exalted set the method for the first of creation in the human soul, and immunity was internal to the human being: if he committed a sin, he would repent and return after blaming himself. But his affair might settle upon disobedience, and the "self-reproaching soul" (al-nafs al-lawwamah) disappears from him, and he submits to the soul that commands evil (al-nafs al-ammarah bi'l-su'). Then he finds in society someone to straighten him; but when society is corrupted, heaven intervenes by sending messengers. Except the nation of Muhammad ﷺ, for the Exalted has assured it that there will remain in it until the Hour, someone who calls to good, who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong; therefore there will be no prophets after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, affirming this meaning, said: "The scholars of my nation are like the prophets of the Children of Israel" (15).
The scholar is every person who knows a ruling of Allah the Exalted, and it is incumbent upon him to convey it to the people.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, memorises it, and conveys it to one who has not heard it, for many a bearer of knowledge is more retentive than one who hears" (16).
The Exalted says: ﴿...those of virtue who forbade corruption on earth, except a few of those whom We saved from among them. But the wrongdoers followed what they were given of luxury therein, and they were criminals (11:116)﴾. Allah the Exalted did save some of those who forbade corruption on earth.
We see examples of this in the town that was by the sea, where their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, when they had forbidden hunting to themselves; and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them.
The Exalted says: ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you advise a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him." (164) So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who wronged with a wretched punishment for what they used to defy (165)﴾ (7:164-165). Thus Allah the Exalted saved those who forbade evil in that town. Yet in some societies we see two elements:
The first: that there is no group forbidding corruption.
The second: that the door of luxury is thrown wide open, and the opening of the door of luxury wide open is a humiliation for humankind, for you may find a person whose means do not allow him luxury, so he increases those means through bribery, theft and usurpation.
All of that arises because a person sees people living in luxury with a comfort that their means do not qualify them to enjoy.
The Exalted says concerning the destruction of such societies: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, and they commit debauchery therein...﴾ (17:16). Some people understand this noble verse other than its proper sense: they take debauchery to be the result of a command from Allah the Exalted, whereas the truth is that they themselves opposed Allah's command. For the Exalted says: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion...﴾ (98:5). That is, the Exalted commanded the affluent to follow Allah's method, but they opposed the divine method by choice, and so they defied the command of their Lord.
In the noble verse which is the subject of our reflections: ﴿...and the wrongdoers followed what they were given of luxury therein...﴾ (11:116). His saying [wrongdoers] shows that the material of luxury in which they lived came from injustice, from seizing people's rights and sucking the blood of the labourers.
The root [taraf] means the blessing with which a person lives in comfort; from it come "utrif" and "utrif," and the word [utrif] means: it made him insolent...

1 -- Ulu al-baqiyah: people of discernment, reason and reflection on consequences, and people of enduring virtue and firm good. The Exalted said: ﴿So why were there not among the generations before you those of virtue...﴾ (11:116). Baqiyah: the remaining and the remnant thing [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root b-q-y].
2 - Taraf, yatraf taraf: to live in comfort; and Allah atrafahu: blessed him and gave him what he desired. The Exalted said: ﴿And We gave them luxury in the worldly life...﴾ (23:33), and said: ﴿and the wrongdoers followed what they were given of luxury therein...﴾ (11:116), meaning they pursued their desires and persisted in luxury, so it made them insolent and defiant [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root t-r-f].
3 - Lawla: a conditional particle that does not govern, indicating the prevention of the consequence owing to the existence of the condition; the conditional clause is nominal, and the predicate is omitted obligatorily when it is a general existence. When a pronoun follows it, it is a separate nominative pronoun, as in ﴿...Had it not been for you, we would have been believers (21:31)﴾ (34:31). The answer clause is verbal and is joined with the lam when affirmative, usually, and is stripped of it when negative. The Exalted said: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure...﴾ (24:21): the answer is stripped of the lam because it is negated by the particle [ma]. The answer of the conditional after "lawla" may be omitted when indicated by evidence, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful (24:20)﴾; the estimated answer is: "a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into," as the following verse in the same surah clarifies. "Lawla" is also used as a particle of offering and urging, like [hala], so it is specific to entering the present tense, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Why do you not ask forgiveness of Allah...? (27:46)﴾, and it enters a past verb in the sense of the present, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Why did You not delay me to a near term...? (63:10)﴾, meaning "why do You not delay me." "Lawla" is used for rebuke and reproach, specific to the past tense, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses...? (24:13)﴾, and His saying: ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say...? (24:16)﴾, and His saying: ﴿Why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves...? (6:43)﴾. "Lawla" here means [hala] for rebuke, supported by the reading: "Why, when Our punishment came to them" [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root l-w-l-a].
4 - Aqsata: he was just, and removed injustice or oppression. The Exalted said: ﴿...and act justly; indeed Allah loves those who act justly (49:9)﴾. The Noble Qur'an used the word [al-qist], with a kasra on the qaf and a sukun on the sin, meaning justice, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice...﴾ (7:29), meaning justice. And the Exalted said: ﴿And establish the balance with justice...﴾ (55:9), meaning justice. And the Exalted said: ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice...﴾ (11:85), meaning justice [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root q-s-t].
5 - Bakhasa haqqahu bakhsan: he diminished his right and did not pay it in full. The Exalted said: ﴿and do not deprive the people of their things...﴾ (7:85) [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: root b-kh-s].
6 - Abu al-Shaykh reported in "Akhlaq al-Nabi" ﷺ [p. 201] from Ibn 'Abbas: (The meat most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the shoulder). Al-Bukhari reported in his Sahih [4712] from Abu Hurayrah who said: (A meal of meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the foreleg was raised to him, and it pleased him).
7 - Reported by Ahmad in his Musnad [6/50] and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan [2470] from the hadith of 'A'isha. Al-Tirmidhi said: "A sahih hadith."
8 - Reported by Ahmad in his Musnad [4/24, 26], Muslim in his Sahih [2958], and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan [2342], and he graded it sound.
9 - Baqiya, baqa'an: the opposite of fana (to perish). Baqi: active participle, feminine: baqiyah. The Exalted said: ﴿And there will remain the face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour (55:27)﴾, and said: ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah remains (16:96)﴾ [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].

**al-Baqiyyah** (the remainder): the feminine form, meaning the remaining thing. Its plural of *baqiyyah* is *baqiyat*. The plural of *baqiyah* is also *baqiyat*. God Almighty says: ﴿...And the enduring good deeds are better in reward with your Lord and better in hope﴾ [al-Kahf 46], meaning that the beneficial, enduring deeds whose good remains among people are the best reward with God [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *baqa*].

10. **Amal** (hope): *amila yaamalu amalan*, *imlan* and *amalan* mean to hope, as in *raja yarju*. *Al-amal* means hope. God Almighty says: ﴿...And the enduring good deeds are better in reward with your Lord and better in hope﴾ [al-Kahf 46], because it is a hope with God that is certain, with no doubt about it [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *amal*].

11. **Mard**: a noun of place or time, or a mimy verbal noun. God Almighty says: ﴿And that to God is our return...﴾ [Ghafir 43], meaning our returning to Him, as a verbal noun; or our place of return to Him, as a noun of place or time. God Almighty also says: ﴿And when God intends harm for a people, there is no repelling it...﴾ [al-Ra'd 11], meaning there is no turning away of it and no reversing of it, as a verbal noun; it befalls them inevitably [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *radda*]. It is also stated in [*Kalimat al-Qur'an* by Shaykh Muhammad Hasanayn Makhluf] that the phrase [*khayr mardan*] means better in return and outcome.

12. **Afa al-nabt**: the plant increased and grew tall. *Afa al-qawm*: the people became numerous. God says: ﴿Then We substituted good for evil until they increased...﴾ [al-A'raf 95], meaning they became numerous, mighty and wealthy. *Al-afw* in wealth is what exceeds the needed expenditure. God says: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus...﴾ [al-Baqarah 219]. *Afa 'an al-dhanb afwan*: he overlooked the sin. *Afuww* is an intensive form, meaning one who pardons much. God says: ﴿Indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ [al-Hajj 60]. God says: ﴿Take what is easy and enjoin what is good...﴾ [al-A'raf 199], meaning take what people have left over and have given freely and willingly. Among the supplications of the Noble Qur'an: ﴿And pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah 286] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, vol. 1, pp. 27–28].

13. **Al-qarn** (generation) among people: the people of one era. God says: ﴿...So We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation﴾ [al-An'am 6]. Its plural is *qurun*. God says: ﴿And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged﴾ [Yunus 13] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *qarn*].

14. **Fasada**: *fasada fasadan*, and *al-fasad* is the opposite of *al-salah* (righteousness). *Afsadahu ghayruhu*: another made it corrupt. God says: ﴿...and they strive throughout the land in corruption. And God does not love corrupters﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64]. God says: ﴿...and do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah 60]. The word *mufsidin* (causing corruption) is a emphatic circumstantial clause for the meaning of the verb *ta'thaw*, meaning: do not cause corruption on the earth with corruption [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *fasada*].

15. **Zabad al-ma'** (foam of water): what rises on its surface when it churns and agitates, of scum and debris. *Zabad al-ma'adin* (metal dross): its impurities and waste. God says: ﴿So the torrent carries a rising foam...﴾ [al-Ra'd 17], and God says: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum...﴾ [al-Ra'd 17]. God, glorified is He, likened falsehood to the foam that is cast off and thrown away, because it benefits no one [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *zabad*].

16. **Jafa'at al-qidr**: the cooking pot threw off its foam when boiling. *Jafa al-sayl ghathaahu*: the torrent cast off its refuse, meaning it threw it out and expelled it. It is the custom of cooks to throw away what the pot has cast off, far away, so the food remains pure of impurities. God says: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scrap, but that which benefits people remains on the earth...﴾ [al-Ra'd 17], meaning it is of no benefit, and is cast far away, or goes to waste like scrap [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *jafa'a*].

17. **Makatha** (to remain): *makatha makthan* and *makuthan* mean he stayed in his place. It conveys deliberation and not hastiness. God says: ﴿So he remained not long...﴾ [al-Naml 22], meaning the hoopoe remained absent for a period, but not a long one. God says: ﴿...so it remains on the earth...﴾ [al-Ra'd 17], meaning it stays there a long time, thereby increasing its fertility. God says: ﴿Stay here; I have perceived a fire...﴾ [Ta-Ha 10], meaning remain in your place waiting. God says: ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated so that you may recite it to the people over a delay...﴾ [al-Isra' 106], meaning at a leisurely pace and calmly, without haste, over extended times [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *makatha*].

18. **Taghā** (to transgress): *taghā yatghū taghwanan* and *taghwā* mean to exceed the limit in oppression and aggression. *Taghā yatghā taghyanan*: he exceeded the limit. *Taghwā* is from the *waw* root, and *taghyān* is from the *ya'* root. God says: ﴿Who transgressed in the lands﴾ [al-Fajr 11], meaning they wronged and exceeded the limit in disobedience. God says: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾ [al-Haqqah 5], meaning by the cry that exceeded its limit in its violence [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *taghā*]. It is also stated in [*Kalimat al-Qur'an* by Shaykh Muhammad Hasanayn Makhluf]: God says: ﴿...and He set up the balance﴾ [al-Rahman 7], meaning He legislated justice and commanded it for creation; and ﴿that you not transgress...﴾ [al-Rahman 8], meaning lest you exceed justice and truth.

19. **Al-ma'ruf** (what is good): the opposite of *al-munkar*. It is what people have come to recognize and know to be good. God says: ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury...﴾ [al-Baqarah 263], and God says: ﴿...enjoin what is good and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf 199] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *'arafa*], with adaptation.

20. **Al-munkar** (what is wrong): what the noble Shari'ah finds reprehensible, and what sound minds disapprove of. God says: ﴿Let there be among you a community calling to good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong...﴾ [Al 'Imran 104] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *nakara*].

21. From Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "A group of my nation will continue to stand upon the command of God. Those who forsake them or oppose them will not harm them, until the command of God comes while they are dominant over the people." Narrated by Muslim in his *Sahih* [1073].

22. Al-Ajluni mentioned it in *Kashf al-Khafa'* [1744] and said: al-Suyuti said in *al-Durar*: "It has no basis." Likewise Ibn Hajar, al-Damiri and al-Zarkashi said.

23. Narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* [1/437] and Ibn Majah in his *Sunan* [232], from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.

24. **Shara'a**: it appeared and became prominent, so he is *shari'* (manifest), meaning conspicuous and apparent. Its plural is *shurra'*. God says: ﴿When their fish come to them on their Sabbath, appearing openly...﴾ [al-A'raf 163], meaning prominent and clear on the water [al-Qamus al-Qawim, vol. 1, p. 346].

25. **Wa'aza yaʻizuhu wa'dhan wa'izatan**: he advised him to obey and to do righteous deeds, and guided him to good. God, depicting the obstinacy of the disbelievers, says: ﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not of the admonishers"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 136]. Because of their extreme obstinacy and disbelief, both matters are equal to them: admonishment and non-admonishment.
*Al-mawi'zah* (admonition): what one is admonished with, whether speech or action. God says: ﴿...and an admonition for the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah 66], and God says: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition...﴾ [al-Nahl 125] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *wa'aza*].

26. **Al-ma'dhirah** (excuse): a mimy verbal noun, and a name for excuse and proof. *A'dhara*: he accepted his excuse and forgave him. God says: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord...﴾ [al-A'raf 164], meaning an apology to Him by exerting effort in striving to guide people. God says: ﴿And even if he presents his excuses﴾ [al-Qiyamah 15] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *'adhara*].

27. **Ba'isa yab'asu ba'san**: he became brave and fierce, so he is *ba'is*, meaning strong. It is said: a *fares ba'is*, meaning a strong, brave knight. God says: ﴿...And We seized those who did wrong with a severe punishment because they were defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-A'raf 165], meaning a severe punishment [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *ba's*].

28. **Fasaqat al-rutbah fusuqan wa fisqan**: the date emerged from its skin. From this physical meaning the figurative meaning was derived: *fasaqa al-rajul*, the man went out of obedience to God with a flagrant departure. *Al-fisq* is more general than disbelief; one may be a *fasiq* without being a *kafir*, like a disobedient Muslim. God says: ﴿...If a degenerate comes to you with information, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat 6]. God says: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was a degenerate? They are not equal﴾ [al-Sajdah 18], meaning a disbeliever who is not a believer. Thus *al-fusuq* here, in the last verse, means disbelief [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *fasaqa*], with adaptation.

29. **Amarna mutrafiha**: We commanded its affluent ones to obey God, but they transgressed and disobeyed. [*Kalimat al-Qur'an* by Shaykh Muhammad Hasanayn Makhluf].

30. **Akhlasa dinahu lillah**: he purified it and cleansed it of the impurities of polytheism and ostentation. God says: ﴿...So worship God, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar 2]. God says: ﴿Indeed, We chose them with an exclusive quality: remembrance of the Home [of the Hereafter]﴾ [Sad 46], meaning We chose them and specified them with a sublime virtue exclusive to them, which is the remembrance of the Hereafter. Remembering it and reminding others of it is the characteristic of the prophets and messengers, and it is a great virtue specific to them [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry *khalasa*].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 11, verse 117:

The Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says afterwards:

﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reforming.﴾ (11:117)

When you read or hear [*ma kana*], what comes to your mind is: *ma kana yanbaghi* (it was not fitting).

An example of this is our saying: "It was not proper for so-and-so to do such-and-such." This saying means that so-and-so did something that should not have come from him.

There is a difference between negating existence (*nafy al-wujud*) and negating the fittingness of existence (*nafy inbigha' al-wujud*).

The Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him.﴾ (36:69)

This does not mean that the nature of the Messenger ﷺ was dull, or that he—God forbid—could not appreciate beautiful meanings. Rather, he ﷺ was made (*jubil*) upon mercy, and the Truthful, glory be to Him, has said of him: ﴿It was by a mercy from God that you were gentle with them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you.﴾ (3:159)

So we understand His saying: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him...﴾ (36:69), namely that the Truthful, glory be to Him, did not will for him to be a poet.

In this way we understand that there is a difference between "negating existence" and "negating the fittingness of existence."

The Truthful, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly...﴾ (11:117). That is, it is not possible, and it is impossible, for God to destroy the towns unjustly, because the intention of the wrongdoer is to take the right of another so that he may benefit from it. Nothing that people possess can add anything to God, for He is the Giver of every thing. Therefore injustice is not applicable at all in the relationship between the Creator, glory be to Him, and mankind.

When the Truthful, glory be to Him, mentions the word "towns" (*al-qura*), which are places of dwelling, we should know that what is meant is "the inhabitants" (*al-makin*), as in the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea...﴾ (7:163)

And His saying also: ﴿And ask the town in which we were...﴾ (12:82)

The Truthful, glory be to Him, in verses like these two, and likewise in the verse we are now treating with these reflections, is asking about the inhabitants.

God, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly...﴾ (11:117). That is, He is exalted above destroying them by exceeding a limit. Rather, He has the right to destroy them with justice, because justice is a balance. If the weight is deficient, there is loss; and among justice is punishment. If the weight is full, there is reward.

In our human domain, at the moment we inflict punishment on the wrongdoer, we indeed trouble him, but we bring relief to all the wronged; and this is truly justice.

Among the errors of man-made positive legislation is the laxity in enforcing rights in litigation. A crime may occur today, and the sentence punishing the criminal is not issued until ten years later. The widening of the gap between the commission of the crime and the imposition of the penalty is one of the errors of positive legislation, for in this there is laxity in enforcing the rights of litigation, because the widening of the gap between the commission of the crime and the imposition of the penalty weakens the sense of the crime's atrocity.

For this reason the Islamic legislator (*al-mushrri'*) was keen that the time-gap between the occurrence of the crime and the imposition of the punishment should not be long. Punishing the criminal while the psychological impact is still hot in society makes society content with the punishment of the criminal, reminds everyone of the atrocity of what he committed, and balances the crime with its punishment.

The Truthful says here: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reforming (*muslihun*).﴾ (11:117)

In another verse the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...Your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were heedless.﴾ (6:131). Thus: it is necessary first to remove heedlessness. God, glory be to Him, has removed heedlessness from us by sending the messengers, by clarification, and by warning, so that there is no punishment except for a crime for which legislation had already been established.

Thus God, glory be to Him and exalted, has given us the clarification necessary for managing life. Then came, after that, the command for the necessity of reform: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reforming.﴾ (11:117). Reform in the universe is receiving what God has created for us in the universe of necessities, so that we may benefit from them; God has sufficed us the necessities of life and has commanded us to take up the means so that, through innovations, we may develop the luxuries of life.

The necessities of life, such as food, water and air, exist in the universe, and procreation is available through the existence of male and female among created beings. As for what we make of refinements in the ways of life and its comforts, this is the reform required of us.

We have said before that the reformer is one who leaves the righteous in its righteousness, or increases its righteousness in a way that leads to ease and comfort, and to reaching the goal with the least effort in the shortest time.

The towns whose people are reforming are not destroyed by God, because reform either comes as a result of following a method sent down from God, the Exalted, whereby human movement is balanced with the movement of the universe, and the movements do not conflict but support and reinforce one another, and the desired society comes into being.

Or these people have not believed in a heavenly method, but have been guided to a way of working that brings them ease, like the atheist nations that have been guided to something that organizes their lives; for God, glory be to Him and exalted, has not prevented human reason from arriving at drafting a law that gives people ease.

But this reason does not arrive at this law except after mankind has been worn down by hardships and difficulties. As for the heavenly method, God, glory be to Him, willed that through it He would protect people from themselves from fatigue, so that events do not bite them.

Thus we find that man-made laws, while they treat some of the ailments from which mankind suffers, do not yield the return of social perfection; whereas the laws of heaven protect mankind from the beginning, so that they do not fall into what pains them.

In this way we understand the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him: ﴿...while their people were reforming.﴾ (11:117). Because they are either following a heavenly method, or not following a heavenly method but still reforming themselves.

Therefore: the Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted, does not destroy towns because they are unbelieving; rather He leaves them in unbelief as long as they establish laws that regulate the rights and duties of their members, even if they pay the price of that in misery and pain.

But the believer must make God's method known to them. If they embrace it, that is their happiness; and if they do not accept it, then the believers should be content with these unbelievers by not opposing the faithful method.

For this reason we find—in the lands that Islam conquered—people who remained upon their religion, because Islam did not enter any land to compel the people to become Muslims; rather, Islam came with convincing proof together with the power that protects the human being's right to choose his creed.

God, majestic is His exaltation, says: ﴿God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.﴾ (60:8). So if some societies are not believers in God, yet are reforming, God, glory be to Him, does not destroy them; rather He gives them what they deserve in the life of this world, for He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (42:20)

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 118:**

Almighty Allah says, after that:

﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ.﴾ (11:118)

We know that man came into this universe after Allah, glory be to Him, had created in it all the means of life, made subservient by Allah's command to this man, so that he might carry out the task of khilafah (vicegerency) on earth. Those beings did not refuse to serve man, whether he was a believer or a disbeliever, because it is the Truth, glory be to Him, who summoned man into existence, and since He has summoned him, He, glory be to Him, will not withhold from him the means of this existence, namely the continuation of life and the continuation of the species.

This is the gift of lordship (ʿata' al-rububiyyah), which Allah guaranteed to all people, believers and disbelievers alike. It differs from the gift of divinity (ʿata' al-uluhiyyah), which is embodied in the faith-based code: "Do" and "Do not."

Whoever takes the gift of divinity together with the gift of lordship is among the happy in this world and the Hereafter.

So, the power of Allah, glory be to Him, has compelled the universe, without man, to carry out its task. It was possible for Him to make mankind one guided community that does not depart from the order that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, willed, just as the sun, the moon, the air, or any of the other subjected creatures have not departed from His will.

Because the Truth, blessed and exalted, has established for Himself absolute power to subjugate kinds to His purpose, in such a way that they cannot depart from it. This establishes Allah's power, but it does not establish His beloved-ness (mahbubiyyah).

What establishes His beloved-ness is that He creates creatures and grants them, in their makeup, choice (ikhtiyar).

He makes this choice such that each one of them is able to obey and able to disobey, so that they do not turn to faith and obedience except out of the beloved-ness of Allah, exalted.

Thus we know that the subjugated, overpowered universe has revealed to us the flow (sayyal) of power, and the kind to whom Allah has granted choice, if it obeys, reveals to us the flow of beloved-ness.

The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.﴾ (18:29)

But should man be left until pride comes to him that he always possesses choice? No. Although you are free to choose, beware of being deceived by this choice, because within you there is compulsion, and since there is compulsion within you, you must act with good manners. Do not imagine that you are free to believe in Allah or not to believe; do not imagine that you have escaped the grip of Allah, exalted. He holds your reins in the matters that are compelled, which preserve your life for you, such as animals, plants, and inanimate things, but He, glory be to Him, has distinguished you with reason.

The error of man is always that he gives names meanings opposite to what they name. The word "reason" (ʿaql) is derived from ʿaqal, which means "to tie" (rabat). So do not run wild with your reason in what is not required of it, because the task of reason is to restrain your unruliness. And always remember: in whose grip are you, in whose reins are you, and in which matters are you compelled?

Since you are compelled in some things, choose to be compelled to the method of Allah, glory be to Him, and preserve your good manners with Allah. Know that He has granted you all your existence, whether in what you are free to choose or in what you are compelled to.

Look at those whom the Truth, glory be to Him, has deprived of some things they used to think were intrinsic qualities in them: you will find one who tries to move his leg unable to move it, or who tries to raise his hand and cannot.

If such things were intrinsic in man, they would not disobey him. This is evidence that they are gifts from Allah, and if He wills, He takes them back, for He, glory be to Him, takes them to discipline their owner.

Since man is of this form, let him say to himself: beware of being deceived by the idea that Allah has placed in you a corner of choice. Remember that on the basis of this corner you receive the obligation from Allah with "Do" and "Do not." For the meaning of "Do such-and-such" is that you are able not to do it, and the meaning of "Do not do such-and-such" is that you are able to do it, because you have a zone of choice. But in your other corners you have a zone of compulsion and subjugation. So act with good manners in the zone of choice, as you have acted with good manners in the zone of necessity and compulsion.

Allah, glory be to Him, has described man as ungrateful (kanud), saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful.﴾ (100:6). This is because man sometimes forgets that the first task of his reason is to understand its limits, and to say to himself: since animality is compelled in me, and since inanimateness is compelled in me, let me be well-mannered with my Lord, and make my zone of choice follow the purpose of the method of Allah.

If you wanted to make a statistic of "Do" and "Do not," you would find that what has no obligation of "Do" or "Do not" is not less than ninety-five percent of the movement of life, and it is the permissible (mubah).

Allah, glory be to Him, sent down the obligation so that the movement of your whole life might be regulated by it, if you make the obligation your aim. It will not take more than five percent of the movement of life, and its good returns to you.

So when the obligation says to you: you must give zakat from your wealth, you must estimate the return, because if you become poor and in need, there will come to you from the zakat of others what meets your needs. From the "Do" that you adhere to and others adhere to comes the fruit that fills any weakness in the community of faith, through mutual compassion arising from certainty in the method.

And when the obligation says to you: do not transgress against the sanctities of others, it restricts your freedom in outward appearance, but it protects your sanctities from being violated by others. And when you understand all the commands of the obligation, you will find them in your favor, whether the command is "Do" or "Do not."

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community...﴾ (11:118). The "law" (lau) indicates impossibility (imtinaʿ). That is: Allah, exalted, did not make mankind one community, but made them differ.

Some of those who wish to enter Islam through some criticism have said: Does this verse not contradict the saying of Allah: ﴿Mankind was one community, then Allah sent the prophets...﴾ (2:213)? The holders of this view thought that humans did not turn to their Creator from the beginning, and then Allah sent the prophets to draw their attention to the method.

We say to these: No. The Truth, glory be to Him, has guaranteed to people their strength and the foundation of their lives, and likewise He guaranteed them the faith-based method from the time He commanded Adam and his wife to descend to earth to carry out the task of vicegerency in it. Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.﴾ (20:123)

If these people were to investigate the verses that deal with this matter, which are three verses, then here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community...﴾ (11:118).

And in the verse which they thought contradicts the verse about which we are reflecting, He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Mankind was one community; then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed over it except those who were given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of animosity among themselves. So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ (2:213)

Thus we know that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, sent down the method with Adam, peace be upon him. Then heedlessness set in, so people differed, and Allah sent the prophets to judge in what people differed over.

So the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community...﴾ (11:118) means that, had He willed, He, glory be to Him, would have made all people upon guidance, because after creating them, sending them down to earth, and sending down the method for them, they were upon guidance. But by virtue of the property of choice which Allah granted them, they differed.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...but they will not cease to differ.﴾ (11:118). That is: they will continue in disagreement.

In the next verse the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes an exception, saying:

﴿Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."﴾ (11:119)

1. (Abā) He refused, with iba' and ibaʾah; and ta'abba ʿalayhi means he resisted. Abā al-shayʾ means he disliked it and did not approve of it. In the Mighty Revelation: ﴿Allah refuses except to perfect His light...﴾ (9:32). And in the proverb: "The two litigants are content, but the judge refuses," said of one who demands a right that his companions have relinquished. [Al-Muʿjam al-Wasit, root abā], adapted.

2. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast—the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you request, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ (41:30-32).

3. He, exalted, says: ﴿...And if He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ (16:99). And He says: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community...﴾ (5:48). And He also says: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy...﴾ (42:8).

4. Sāla yasīlu sayalan, sayalanan, masīlan, masālan; he is sāʾil, and sayyāl: it flowed and overflowed. It is said: the land and the like flowed, and flowed with what was in it. The horses flowed over him: they moved from every direction and gushed forth. "The flood carried them away," and "the sea surged with us": they fell into a severe matter, and we fell into something even more severe. And "the blaze flowed": it extended and appeared on the forehead and the bridge of the nose.
The sayyāl of divine power (sayyāl al-qudrah al-ilahiyyah) is the manifestation of its effects in all created beings, and its spread and comprehensiveness over everything in the universe, what we know of it and what we do not know. [Al-Muʿjam al-Wasit, root sayl], adapted.

5. Because man is free in what he can replace, and compelled in what he cannot replace. Thus choice has limits linked to capacity, and to human ability.

6. Al-zimām: the thread tied to the nose-ring or the halter, then tied to the end of the rein. It is said: "He is the zimām of his people," meaning their leader, their foremost, and the one in charge of their affairs. And he is the zimām of the matter: its owner. And "he threw the reins of his matter into his hand": he entrusted it to him. And "Allah possesses your reins": that is, He possesses all your affairs. [Al-Muʿjam al-Wasit, root zamm], adapted.

7. ʿAqala yaʿqilu ʿaqlan: he perceived things as they truly are. ʿAqala al-baʿir: he drew his wrist to his upper arm and bound them together with the ʿiqal, so that it would remain kneeling. Al-ʿaql: that by which thinking and the conception of things as they truly are occur, as in His saying: ﴿...after they had understood it﴾ (2:75), that is, they perceived it as it truly is and knew it with firm knowledge. He, exalted, says: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾ (67:10), that is, if we had perceived the matter as it truly is. The Qur'an has often criticized those who do not use their minds, and urged the use of reason. Among that is His saying: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ (2:44). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root ʿaql], adapted.

8. Jamaḥa: he hastened. Al-juмūḥ: the man who rides his desire and cannot be turned back. [Mukhtar al-Qamus, root jamaḥa].

9. The expressions "Do" and "Do not" revolve around the requirements of the method, as command and prohibition. The obligatory (fard), the required (wajib), the recommended (sunnah), and the desirable (mustahabb) are commanded; the forbidden (haram) and the disliked (makruh) are prohibited. For the command there is its gift, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿We are your allies in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you request﴾ (41:31). And for the prohibition there is its punishment, or forgiveness from Allah.

10. Kanada al-niʿmah yakindaha: he denied it and did not thank for it, so he is kānid; the intensive form is kanūd. He, exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ (100:6), that is, extremely ungrateful and denying. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root kanada].

11. Law: a conditional particle that is not jussive, and its meaning is the impossibility of the condition because of the impossibility of the consequence. He, exalted, says: ﴿If We willed, We would have made it crumbled debris...﴾ (56:65). Its consequent is often connected with the lam of emphasis, and sometimes it is not, as in His saying: ﴿If We willed, We would have made it salt water, so why do you not give thanks?﴾ (56:70). The consequent is rarely connected with lam when it is negated, as in His saying: ﴿And if whatever trees are on earth were pens...﴾ (31:27), then He said: ﴿...the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ (31:27). The consequent of law may be omitted, as in His saying: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains were moved, or the earth was cut through, or the dead were made to speak...﴾ (13:31). The consequent is omitted, its estimate being: this great Qur'an would do that, but Allah has not made a Qur'an with this description. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/206].
Law may also be used as a verbal particle like "an" (that), and this is common after the word "wadda" (to love) and "ahabba" (to wish) and what resembles them, as in His saying: ﴿Each of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years﴾ (2:96), that is, he wishes for a life of a thousand years, and the interpreted infinitive is the object of the verb "yawaddu."
Law may also be used for wishing, as in His saying: ﴿If only we had a return, so we could disown them as they have disowned us﴾ (2:167). This is on the tongue of some of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, who wish to return to the world in order to disown the great ones whom they followed in the world but who then disowned them in the Hereafter. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root law].

12. Hadāhu al-ṭarīq yahdīhi hadyan wa hidayatan wa hudan: he taught him it, made him know it, and guided him to it, so he is hādin. In figurative usage: hadāhu al-haqq, or hadāhu ila al-haqq: he showed him the truth and guided him to it.
Al-hudā: the verbal noun of the verb "hadā," and it comes with the meaning of right guidance, and is described by it for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿This is the Book, there is no doubt in it, a guidance for the righteous﴾ (2:2).
