That is, a guide for the righteous, and this is when we stop at His saying: "there is no doubt in it" (2:2), so the Book is a guidance for the righteous, meaning a guide for them. But if we stop at His saying: "This is the Book" (2:2), then "guidance" is a verbal noun meaning guidance, that is: in the Book is guidance for the righteous, with no doubt in that. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root hadā], adapted.

13. Ḍalla al-kāfir: he was absent from the convincing proof, deviated from the straight path, and did not know the truth. Al-ḍalāl: forgetfulness and loss, as He, exalted, says: ﴿Say, "If I have strayed, I have strayed only against myself"﴾ (34:50). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root ḍalla].

14. Shaqiya shaqan, shaqaʾan, shaqawatan: his material or spiritual condition became bad, so he is shaqī. He, exalted, says: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us"﴾ (23:106), that is, the state of wretchedness, misguidance, and corruption of souls. And He, exalted, says: ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you for you to be distressed﴾ (20:2), that is, that you should grieve and suffer sorrow over their disobedience. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, root shaqiya], adapted.

15. Al-ghaflah: a lapse that befalls man from lack of guarding and lack of alertness. The Truth says: ﴿You were certainly in heedlessness of this...﴾ (50:22). It also comes with the meaning of failing to perceive the truth and failing to be guided to it. The Truth says: ﴿Those are the heedless﴾ (7:179).
Ghafala ʿan al-amr ghufulan: he left the matter, deliberately or not. Aghfalahu, transitive with the hamzah, means he left it deliberately; aghfala ghayrahu ʿan al-amr: he made another neglect it. The Truth says: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance...﴾ (18:28), that is, We made him heedless of Our remembrance. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted and rearranged, p. 57, vol. 2].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 11, verse 119:

Meaning: that the Truth, glory be to Him, created mankind for mercy and for difference.

Whenever we see a demonstrative ("ism ishara") or a pronoun referring back to a previous statement, we look at what came before it. What came before here is: ﴿And they will not cease to differ (118), except those on whom your Lord has mercy (119)﴾ [Hud]. And the Truth, exalted is He, when He spoke of the creation of man, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me (56)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat]. The meaning of worship ('ibadah) (1) is obedience to God, glory be to Him, in "do" and "do not", and this is the legal (shar'i) intended meaning of worship. However, the social intentions have been governed by the characteristic of choice, so difference occurred, and this difference arose from the multiplicity of desires.

Had our desires been one, we would not have differed. But we differ as a result of the difference of desires: this one's desire is rightist; that one's desire is leftist; a third's desire is communist; a fourth's desire is capitalist; a fifth's desire is existentialist, and each one has a desire (2).

Therefore the Truth, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires (3), the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted (71)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. The world could not have been set right if God, glory be to Him, had followed the diverse desires of humanity. But the affairs of this world can be set right when its voluntary movement proceeds from one desire. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"None of you truly believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought."(4)

In our daily life we observe that the works by which the movement of life proceeds, and in which no obligation is imposed, we find difference in them inevitably; because the Truth, exalted is He, if He had willed, would have created us all geniuses in every field of life, or would have created us all poets, or doctors, or philosophers.

And if He, glory be to Him, had willed that, who would carry out the other works? If we were all doctors, who would carry out agriculture and other work? If we were all engineers, who would carry out trade and other work?

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to make our talents differ so that the world would be linked to one another by a bond of complementarity and necessity, not a bond of favour.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We apportion among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We raise some of them above others in degrees (5), that some of them may take others in service (6)...(32)﴾ [az-Zukhruf]. Thus we know that raising in degrees does not mean that foolish, reckless view (7) which claims that in that distribution there is an elevation of the rich and a belittling of the poor; for reality confirms that every person is elevated in one respect because of what he does well in it, and is elevated over in another respect because of what he does not do well, which another does well, and that other is complementary to him.

Thus humans exchange what the difference of their talents achieves (8), and difference of talents is the foundation of cohesion.

For this reason we have said: the sum of each person's traits and talents is equal to the sum of every other person's traits and talents, and there is no preference except by piety; and the worth of every man is what he does well.

You may see the owner of a luxurious car begging a car-repair mechanic, who wears worn (9) and dirty clothes, to repair his car; and the mechanic says to him: I have no time to repair your car. The owner of the luxurious car persists in pleading; so the mechanic is pleased, his heart softens toward the condition of this man, the owner of the luxurious car, and he goes to repair it.

Therefore I say: if you look at one who is beneath you in any aspect of life, do not be deceived by what you excel and are distinguished in over him; rather say to yourself: this person must be excellent in some field.

We know that God, glory be to Him, has no sons whom He would single out with complete talents while leaving another without a talent.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿And they will not cease to differ (118), except those on whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them...(119)﴾ [Hud]. And if the difference (10) is in destinies and methodology, this is what generates disbelief or belief. We should know that disbelief has a message; indeed it is necessary so that the believer may sense the sweetness of faith. Had disbelief had no function, God would not have created it.

I have said in the past: disbelief assists faith, just as pain assists health; for were it not for pain we would not have come to the physician to diagnose the disease and prescribe the healing medicine, by God's leave.

Therefore we say: pain is the messenger of health.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿And they will not cease to differ (118), except those on whom your Lord has mercy...(119)﴾ [Hud]. And if you look closely at difference, you will find it is the very essence of harmony.

An example of that: the difference of your children in the foods they love. You find one son preferring the breast of the chicken, another preferring its lower part, the "thigh" (al-warik), and you laugh at this difference, because it is a difference on the surface, but its inner reality is harmony. If we all agreed in temperaments, we would find contention and opposition; and this is what spreads among those of the same profession.

And to one who asks: is creation for difference or is creation for mercy?

We say: creation is for difference and for mercy together, because the aspect is separate.

Then He says, glory be to Him, in the same verse: ﴿...And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together" (119)﴾ [Hud]. The Truth, glory be to Him, has known from eternity who will choose belief and who will choose disbelief, and this is one of the attributes of God's eternal knowledge, exalted is He. Therefore He says, glory be to Him: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, meaning: God, glory be to Him, knew which of His servants would choose to act in this world the deeds of the people of the Fire, and who would choose to act the deeds of the people of Paradise, due to the precedence of His eternal knowledge of His servants' intentions and choices.

We have previously given an example—and to God belongs the highest likeness—of the dean of a college who announces to the professors the necessity of nominating the outstanding students in each department, because there are prizes awaiting them. Each professor nominates the names of the outstanding students in whom he has perceived brilliance and dedication to knowledge. The dean asks professors from outside his university to set surprise examinations for the entire student body; and the dean is surprised by the excellence of the students in whom their professors perceived brilliance and dedication to knowledge; and here the dean verifies the truthfulness of the professors' foresight, who work under his leadership.

But a surprise may occur: one of these students may fall short because of an illness that afflicted him, or an emergency that befell him, such as nervous exhaustion, fatigue, or otherwise; and thus the professors' assessment is upset. But the Truth's assessment, glory be to Him, is free of error, and what He knows from eternity is certainly realized; therefore He has shown us that it is eternal knowledge, and He challenges the unbeliever to change it.

We all know that the Truth, glory be to Him, revealed His noble saying: ﴿Perish (tabbat) the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he (1)﴾ [al-Masad]. Abu Lahab heard it, and did not respond to it by declaring faith—not even hypocritically.

The Truth's saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ shows us that when the Truth, glory be to Him, says something, it has already been accomplished; there is no repelling of His will. As for us, we must precede every promise with an act we will perform, by saying: ﴿unless God wills...(24)﴾ [al-Kahf]; for the Truth says to us: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow" (23), except [with the qualification], "If God wills..." (24)﴾ [al-Kahf]. In this there is respect for our human condition, faith in the overwhelming dominance of Power, and recognition of the reality that we are among the contingent beings; for every event requires an agent, an object upon which the act falls, a place, a time, and a cause; and none of us possesses any one of those elements.

If you say "unless God wills" you have protected yourself from being a liar, or from promising what you cannot do; but if the One who speaks is the owner of everything, and no power can turn Him from what He has said, then He alone is able to carry out what He says.

Therefore we have said: every act attributed to God, exalted is He, is stripped of time; we do not say "past tense act," "act that will happen in the future," or "present tense act," because those categories are measures for human acts; but the acts of God, glory be to Him, are not measured by the same standard. So when He, glory be to Him, decrees a matter, we take it as though it had already occurred.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it (1)﴾ [an-Nahl].

His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿has come﴾ means: the matter has been decreed, even if it has not yet been executed; so do not hasten it. This is the challenge of overwhelming sovereignty, and no power exists capable of preventing the occurrence of a matter that God, exalted is He, has willed; He judges in what He owns, and none contests Him, glory be to Him.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿Surely I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together...(119)﴾ [Hud]: its cause is that mankind and jinn are the two burdened ones (17).

1 - 'Abd Allah ya'budu-hu 'ibadatan wa 'ubudatan: he obeyed him, so he is 'abid. God says: ﴿They did not use to worship Us (63)﴾ [al-Qasas] and God says: ﴿You alone we worship...(5)﴾ [al-Fatihah] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: entry [ʿ-b-d]] with adaptation.
2 - God says: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [lost in] excess (28)﴾ [al-Kahf].
3 - Hawiya-yahwa-hu hawan: he loved him; it is used most often for falsehood and for harmful appetites. God says: ﴿So do not follow [your] desire...(135)﴾ [an-Nisa'], meaning what your souls desire and crave, which leads you astray from the truth. And God says: ﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the right way...(77)﴾ [al-Ma'idah] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/310, 311].
4 - Ibn Abi 'Asim recorded it in his Kitab al-Sunnah [1/12] from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr; Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali cited it in Jami' al-'Ulum [p. 460] and graded it weak.
5 - Darajah: the step by which one ascends and descends; it is used figuratively for rank and standing in virtue and honour, and in reward with God. God says: ﴿They are degrees with God...(163)﴾ [Al 'Imran], meaning they are different stations in virtue and reward, each according to his deeds. God says: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne...(15)﴾ [Ghafir], meaning God possesses the lofty stations, in which He causes to dwell whomever He wills of His close servants; and God is高 exalted above the highest degrees, glory be to Him [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/225].
6 - Sakhkhara-yusakhkhiru-hu: he humbled, subdued and subjected him. God says: ﴿that some of them may take others in service...(32)﴾ [az-Zukhruf]. Sakhkhara with the intensive form means: he subjected and overpowered him so that he carries out what is wanted from him without the subject's will or choice; from it is God's saying: ﴿and the clouds subjected between heaven and earth...(164)﴾ [al-Baqarah] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/306].
7 - Al-ru'unah: foolishness; a014 "arrun" is one reckless in his speech [Lisan al-'Arab, root r-'-n].
8 - The difference of talents is for human complementarity, facilitating the movement of life; unlike the difference of desires, which corrupts the movement of life.
9 - Rath: old and worn-out of anything; athwath al-thawb: it became shabby [Lisan al-'Arab, root r-th-th].
10 - If the difference is in destinies and methodology, it produces that thing and its opposite.
11 - Tamma al-amr yatimmu tamman wa tamaman: it was completed and realised; it is complete and perfect, and it may be sensory or abstract. God says: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice...(115)﴾ [al-An'am], meaning it was completed and realised; and tamma al-shay': its parts were completed. God says: ﴿So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights...(142)﴾ [al-A'raf], meaning the number set for the communion of Musa, peace be upon him, was completed; and atamma al-shay': he perfected it in the best manner. God says: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you...(3)﴾ [al-Ma'idah], meaning in the most perfect manner, without deficiency [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/101, 102] with adaptation.
12 - Al-jinnah (with a kasra on the jim): the jinn. God says: ﴿[from] the whisperer who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5), of the jinn and mankind (6)﴾ [an-Nas] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/132].
13 - Tabba-yatubbu tabban wa tababan: he lost and perished. God says: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he (1)﴾ [al-Masad]: an invocation against him with loss or destruction; and He first invoked that his hands perish, because they are the instrument of violence and harm. Al-tabab: destruction. God says: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin (37)﴾ [Ghafir]; and tabbaba-hu tatbiban: he destroyed him. God says: ﴿and they added to them nothing but ruin (101)﴾ [Hud], meaning destruction and loss [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/96].
14 - Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir [3/71], from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse, that a group of Quraysh asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about three matters, after consultation with the Jews: "Ask him about youths who went forth in the earliest age; what was their affair, for they had a remarkable story. Ask him about a man who wandered (tawwaf) and reached the eastern and western parts of the earth; what was his story. And ask him about the Spirit: what is it?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I will inform you tomorrow of what you asked," and he did not say, "If God wills." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) remained fifteen nights without God revealing to him anything about that, and Gabriel did not come to him, until the people of Mecca began to spread rumours, saying: "Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today is the fifteenth day; we have awaited it and he has told us nothing of what we asked him." Then this verse was revealed, and this surah [al-Kahf], in which is the account of what they asked about.
15 - Amr Allah: His punishment for those who persist in polytheism and in denying His messenger [said by al-Qurtubi 5/3789]. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir [2/561]: ("He, exalted is He, informs of the drawing near and approach of the Hour, expressing it in the past tense that indicates certainty and occurrence without doubt").
16 - Ista'jala al-amr: to seek it quickly and hastily; God says: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them...(11)﴾ [Yunus] [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/9].
17 - Al-thaqalan: mankind and jinn, because they are like two heavy loads upon the earth's surface. God says: ﴿We will attend to you, O two burdened ones (31)﴾ [ar-Rahman], which is a statement whose intent is threat and warning [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/108].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 120 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:
﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We strengthen your heart. And in this has come to you the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.﴾ (11:120)

When you notice the tanwin (nunation) in His words "all" (﴿kullan﴾), know that what is intended is the story of every messenger that the Truth, glory be to Him, related in the Noble Qur'an.

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, speaks of an action He has brought about, we may consider whether this action derives from one of His attributes or from an existing name. It is then right for us to take the name and take the action from it, as in His words: ﴿He created you...﴾ (16:70). From this we know that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator. But if an action comes whose root is not among the Most Beautiful Names of God, beware of deriving a name for God from that action.

An example of this is His words, glory be to Him: ﴿And all that We relate (naqussu)...﴾ (11:120). The one who relates here is God, glory be to Him, but no one may say that God is "qassas" (the one who retaliates or relates in that sense), just as no one may say that God is "makir" (a schemer), although God has said: ﴿They plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ (8:30). Likewise, no one may say that God is "al-mukhadi" (the deceiver), although the Truth, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive God, but He is deceiving them﴾ (4:142). Thus we learn the courtesy of speaking about God, who is characterized by every attribute of perfection and majesty, and we confine ourselves to saying that such an action came by way of mushakalah (an expression by way of association with a related term) since it has no place among the Most Beautiful Names of God.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers...﴾ (11:120).

"Anba'" is the plural of "naba'", which is a great news item of importance, such that one's state changes upon knowing it. The news of the messengers, peace be upon them, is scattered in various fragments throughout the surahs of the Noble Qur'an, clarifying what each messenger brought, treating the disease from which his people suffered, and also what each messenger endured from the obstinacy of the people to whom he was sent. The mention of those news items in the Qur'an was to strengthen the heart of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the Messenger would encounter hardships and difficulties in the call.

The Qur'an has mentioned some of those situations. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿They were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When will the help of God come?"﴾ (2:214).

The Truth, glory be to Him, describes the state of the believers: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about God assumptions﴾ (33:10). Situations such as these require strengthening the heart, meaning calming it upon the logic of faithful certainty in a Lord who sent a messenger to convey a method, and God, glory be to Him, would not send a messenger to convey a method and then hand him over to his enemies.

So when the news of the messengers and the hardships they faced is mentioned to him, the difficulties he faces become easier for him, and his heart is strengthened.

The "fu'ad" is what we call the "qalb" (heart). It is the vessel of beliefs. That is, the brain receives from the senses, which are the means of perception: an eye that sees, an ear that hears, a nose that smells, a mouth that tastes, and a hand that touches. Thus the information is generated, which the brain classifies and arranges as intellectual propositions.

The brain then examines those intellectual propositions until an intellectual proposition is verified with a soundness that no later evidence overturns. The brain then drops it into the fu'ad so that it becomes a conviction (aqidah), which does not float back up to the intellect to be debated anew. This is why they call it "aqidah," from "uqdah" (a knot), so it does not waver afterward.

Therefore, the fu'ad is the vessel receptive to the propositions that the brain has finished refining with a refinement that has reached the truth, and it drops them onto the heart so that it may direct the movement of life according to their requirements.

By way of example: we find a young man who thinks about his future. He studies the advantages and disadvantages of various professions in order to choose the specialization that suits his talents and his dreams. Then he studies the sensory data he has received through his senses in order to refine it with his mind. What his mind concludes, he drops into his heart, so that it becomes a conviction by which he directs the movement of his life.

An illustration of this: it has become settled in people's conscience and minds that fire burns. But from where did this certainty that fire burns come? We say it came from a sensory matter, in that people witnessed that whoever is touched by fire is burned.

It is necessary, then, that the heart be firm, not wavering.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart...﴾ (11:120). This is because the fu'ad is the vessel whose task is to be prepared to receive the word of truth, to accept the alert of reminder, the weight of admonition, and the full descent of what comes from the Truth, glory be to Him. What comes from the Truth, glory be to Him, is also truth, and truth is that which is fixed and to which no change occurs.

The essence of truth is the wellspring of belief from which obedience to the obligation (taklif) issues forth. A person must be confident of the wisdom of the One who imposes the obligation before he accepts the obligation. Therefore it was necessary that proof of the existence of the Truth, glory be to Him, the summit of the highest existence, come first, before the admonition comes. Faith in the highest existence, which does not change and to which changing circumstances do not occur, must precede the coming of that admonition.

This is because admonition may require of a person something he dislikes to commit himself to. Here it issues from the Truth, glory be to Him, who created, and He cannot cheat or deceive His creatures, and He conveys it to you through a messenger from Him, glory be to Him.

Admonition may be disliked if it comes from a human being like you, because he will only admonish you by means of a perfection that he possesses, in order to enumerate a deficiency in you. If the admonisher does not possess the perfection with which he admonishes, the one being admonished will respond to the admonisher, saying: "Let him admonish himself first."

This is why we find the words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Greatly hateful in the sight of God is that you say what you do not do﴾ (61:3). This is because an admonisher who admonishes with what he does not practice on himself gives the one admonished an argument to reject the admonition, so he says to himself: "If there were good in this matter, he would have practiced it himself."

Thus the noble verse has shown the position of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as one who strengthens, and also the position of the believers in his message as those who remind the Messenger that they too will be exposed to hardships. Some of the obligated may see, for example, that lowering the gaze is a deprivation of a passing desire, and does not plumb the depths of understanding, which holds that in lowering the gaze there is a command for all believers to lower their gaze from what is forbidden. And one may see in zakat that it is a taking from his wealth, and does not plumb the depths of understanding, which holds that in zakat there is a security for him should changing circumstances come upon him and he becomes poor. At that point society will provide him with the social security that protects him and his dependents from the consequences of begging.

Depth of understanding is something required, because the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ (4:82). This is because when you reflect on the meanings, you will know that the obligation is an honor for you, and you will say to yourself: "God imposed nothing on me except for the good of myself, even if it becomes apparent that it is for the good of people."

Among the hardships also is what the believers encounter from the harm of those who profit from corruption: those who live off benefiting from corruption and confront anyone who wants to eliminate corruption. This is because corruption on earth does not survive unless there is someone who profits from it, and the one who profits from corruption resents and openly declares enmity toward everyone who opposes him.

Therefore, the position of the enemies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a natural position in favor of their interests. But they, out of their folly, defined the good by their immediate interests in the life of this world, and did not consider the outcome of their affair in the Hereafter, whether bliss or punishment.

Had they possessed insight, they would have known that it is in their interest that someone exist who would correct them, so that they would not send ahead for themselves an evil that awaits them in the Hereafter.

Had they been perceptive, they would have known that the Messenger, just as he came for the benefit of the oppressed who are exploited by corruption, also came for their benefit. Had they possessed any measure of reason, they would have been among the supporters of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it would have been obligatory upon them, whenever their souls suggested to them the pursuit of corruption and they heard from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, what awaits them as a result of this corruption, that they follow him and thank him, because he freed them from the evil force present within them.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear to His Messenger: you are not a novelty among the messengers, and every messenger was exposed to hardships just as you are exposed to similar ones. You are the Seal of the Prophets, and because the religion you brought will not be followed by any other religion, all the hardships must therefore be concentrated upon you. So be completely certain that you will encounter hardships.

Therefore We strengthen your heart with what We relate to you of the news of the messengers, because this heart is what will receive the faithful realities from the summit of "There is no god but God," until it becomes a reminder that reminds you and the believers with you.

Thus the verse has shown the position of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as one who strengthens, and the position of the believers as those who remind the Messenger, because they too will be exposed to hardships.

We all know what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar when they pledged allegiance to him at al-'Aqabah to support him, and they said: "If we are faithful to what we have pledged to you, what will we have?" The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say to them: ("You will possess the world, and you will become masters of Persia and Byzantium"), but he said to them: ("For you is Paradise").

This is because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that some of them would die before those victories were achieved. So he promised them the common measure in which those who die after declaring their faith are equal with those who will live to witness those victories.

Thus we have made clear how the noble verse included the strengthening of the heart of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and how this heart is prepared to receive the truth, the admonition, and the reminder of the believers with him.

This is the first side. What then of the second side, the side that denies the Messenger?

It was necessary for the Truth, glory be to Him, to speak here of those who deny the Messenger, because summoning meanings makes the soul receptive to hearing about the other side.

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has spoken of strengthening the receptacle of reception, of admonition, and of reminding the believers at the moment their resolve weakens, it is necessary then that He, glory be to Him, speak of the other category, the category of deniers. He, glory be to Him, makes clear to His Messenger that he may challenge them and not be intimidated.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says:
﴿And say to those who do not believe: "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working."﴾ (11:121)

---

1. "Thabbatahu": made him firm and established. God said: ﴿And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ (17:74), meaning: We made you firm and removed from you the causes of weakness. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/105]

2. The words of the Exalted, ﴿in this the truth...﴾ (11:120): "That is, this surah," said Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and a group of the early scholars. Al-Hasan in one narration from him, and Qatadah, said: "in this world." The correct view is: in this surah, which includes the stories of the prophets and how God rescued them and the believers with them, and destroyed the disbelievers. There came in it true stories and a truthful report, an admonition by which the disbelievers would be restrained, and a reminder by which the believers would be reminded." So said Ibn Kathir in his tafsir [2/465].

3. The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And God created you, then He causes you to die...﴾ (16:70).

4. Qassa (al-kalam aw al-akhbar): he relates it, yaqussuha, qassan and qasasan: he follows it, narrates it, and recounts it. God said: ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the stories, he said, "Do not fear..."﴾ (28:25). And qassa al-amr qassan: he followed it. From this is God's words: ﴿So they returned, retracing their footsteps, following the trail﴾ (18:64). "Qasas" is a verbal noun applied to what is narrated of news. From it is God's words: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ (12:3). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, vol. 2, p. 120]

5. Makara yamkuru makran: he devised evil against another secretly and by deceit. God said: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot you hatched in the city﴾ (7:123), and God said: ﴿Then there is a plot against Our signs﴾ (10:21), meaning a bad scheme intended to turn them from their proper course and to bar people from them. When plotting is attributed to God, glory be to Him, its meaning is the nullification of the plotting of the plotters and the infliction of punishment upon them from where they do not perceive, as in His words: ﴿And they plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of plotters﴾ (3:54), and His words: ﴿And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive﴾ (27:50). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/231, 232]

6. Khada'ahu yakhda'uhu khada'an wa khad'ah: he showed him the opposite of what he concealed in order to bring him into something disliked without his knowing. God said: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is God...﴾ (8:62). Khadaahu: he deceived him, or attempted to. God said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive God, but He is deceiving them...﴾ (4:142), meaning they display faith out of hypocrisy in order to deceive God and His Messenger and the believers, while God nullifies their deception, exposes their affair, and punishes them for their deception. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/188]

7. "Al-mushakalah": mentioning a thing by the wording of something else, because it occurs in its company, either in reality or by estimation. The first is like God's words: ﴿You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Yours...﴾ (5:116), and His words: ﴿And they plotted, and God plotted...﴾ (3:54). The mention of "soul" and "plotting" in reference to the Creator is only for the sake of mushakalah with what is with Him. An example by estimation is God's words: ﴿The baptism of God...﴾ (2:138), meaning the purification of God, because faith purifies souls, so faith was expressed as "the baptism of God" by mushakalah through this indication. [Al-Itqan of al-Suyuti, 3/282]

8. Zalzala al-shay': he shook it with a violent, repeated motion. God said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ (99:1), meaning the earthquake struck it at the establishment of the Hour. And God said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ (22:1). And God said: ﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ (33:11), meaning they were disturbed, feared, became anxious, and were violently agitated, by way of comparison with a physical object. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/288]

9. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [1/949]: ("The Messenger here is Shu'ayb according to the view of Muqatil, and it is al-Yasa' according to al-Kalbi, who said: this applies to every messenger sent to his nation who exerted himself in that until he said: 'When will the help of God come?' It is narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: it means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the occasion of the revelation of the verse points to this. And God knows best.")

10. This was in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), in Shawwal of the fifth year after the Hijrah according to the correct and well-known view. In it Quraysh and those who followed them allied with the Jews of the tribe of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah, and their total was ten thousand, while the Muslims were three thousand. The Muslims remained besieged within Madinah for nearly a month. [Abridged from the tafsir of Ibn Kathir, 3/470]

11. Zaagha yazigh zaighan wa zighanan: he inclined from the target. Zaagha al-basar: it was disturbed and did not perceive what it saw, or deviated from its aim so that it saw nothing. God said: ﴿The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ (53:17), meaning the gaze of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not deviate from seeing the angel, nor did it transgress and see more than was before it, rather he saw the angel with a true vision. And God's words describing the terror of some people in Madinah when the enemies surrounded them in the Battle of the Confederates: ﴿And when the eyes shifted...﴾ (33:10), meaning they were disturbed from the intensity of fear. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/294], adapted.

12. Al-hanjarah (the larynx) in language: the gullet and the throat. Scientifically it is called the windpipe, through which breath passes out and in. God said: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾ (33:10), as a metaphor for the intensity of distress and constriction.

13. Al-dhunun (the assumptions): what arises in the soul from a sign is a probable doubt, and its verb is among the verbs of probability, of the pattern "nasara." Al-zann (assumption) is a verbal noun, and al-zann is also the name for this thought that arises in the soul. God said: ﴿They follow not except assumption, and indeed assumption avails nothing against the truth﴾ (53:28). Its plural is "dhunun." It was read: ﴿and you assumed about God assumptions﴾ (33:10), with the alif of "al-dhununa" in pause and without the alif in continuation, is a reading. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/417]

14. Mahhasa al-shay' wa mahhasahu: he purified it of its defects. It is said: the metal was refined by fire, meaning purified of what mixed with it; the sword was polished; God purified the repentant from sins, meaning cleansed them of them; and mahhasa fulanan: he filled him and tested him. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]

١٥ - **al-Mawʿiẓa** (admonition): what one is admonished with, whether by speech or by action. The Most High says: ﴿And an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqara], and His saying: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition...﴾ [al-Naḥl]. He admonished him (*waʿaẓahu yaʿiẓuhu waʿẓan waʿiẓatan*): he advised him to obey and guided him to doing good [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, 2/345].

١٦ - **Maqatahu yamqatuhu maqtan**: he hated him intensely for a shameful deed he had committed.
**Maqt Allah** (the wrath of God): His anger, His retribution and His punishment, as in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve will be called out to, "The hatred of Allah is greater than your hatred of yourselves..."﴾ [Ghafir], meaning: God's anger against you is greater than your hatred of one another and your retaliation against one another. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it was an immorality and hateful and an evil way﴾ [al-Nisaʾ], meaning: the marriage to a woman whom one's father had previously married is a shamefully grave deed, and it causes people to hate and detest its perpetrator intensely, and it causes God's wrath, His retribution against its doer, because it is disobedience to fathers and a mixing of lineages [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 3/231].

١٧ - **al-Ṭarf**: the side of the eye; it is also applied to the eye and to sight. The Most High says: ﴿They look from a hidden side of the eye...﴾ [al-Shura], meaning: from the corner of the eye, furtively. And His saying: ﴿And with them are women restraining their gaze, with beautiful eyes﴾ [al-Saffat], meaning: lowering their gaze out of chastity. And His saying: ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you...﴾ [al-Naml], meaning: your sight, that is, the time it takes to close and open the eye [al-Qamus al-Qawim, entry: ṭarf].

١٨ - **Sabarahu sabran**: he estimated its depth, or tested it. One says: sabara al-jurḥ (he probed the wound): he measured its depth with a probe; and sabara fulānan (he tested so-and-so): he tested him to know what he had. **Al-ghawr**: every low part of the land; the *ghawr* of anything is its bottom and depth. One says: sabara ghawrahu: he clarified its reality and secret. One says: fulān baʿīd al-ghawr: a cunning, shrewd person; māʾ ghawr: sunken water, deep-seated. In the Revealed Book: ﴿Say: "Have you considered if your water should sink into the earth, who then will bring you flowing water?"﴾ [al-Mulk] [al-Muʿjam al-Waṣīṭ, entries: sabara and ghawr].

١٩ - **Dabbara al-amr**: he looked into its consequences and its outcomes, so as to arrive at what he sees as good for himself. His saying: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne, arranging the affair...﴾ [Yunus], meaning: He decrees it, determines it and executes it according to His wisdom and His will. His saying: ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾ [al-Naziʿat], they are the angels who manage the affairs of creation by God's permission and in accordance with His wisdom and will.
**Tadabbara**: he reflected on the outcomes and consequences of matters, or reflected in order to know the realities of matters. The Most High says: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad], meaning: have they been incapacitated and blinded, so that they do not contemplate the meanings of the Qur'an and perceive the profound wisdom in it, so that they believe? Between the interrogative hamza and the conjunctive fāʾ there is always an elided verb, which we have explained here as: "Have they been incapable, so that they do not reflect?" And His saying: ﴿Did they not ponder the word...?﴾ [al-Muʾminun], meaning: have they been incapable, so they did not ponder? The original is *yatadabbaru*; the tāʾ was changed to dāl and assimilated into the dāl [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/221].
.

٢٠ - **al-Maṣāliḥ al-ānīya** (immediate interests): the hasty ones, relating to (*al-Ān*), which is the immediate, present matter. It is an adverb of the present time, always defined with *al-*, and built on fatḥa. The Most High says: ﴿They said, "Now you have brought the truth"﴾ [al-Baqara] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/45].

٢١ - Therefore the Lord of Might said of them: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but of the Hereafter they are heedless﴾ [al-Rum]. Then the Truth turns their attention to the universe and what is in it, and to the end of the deniers, saying: ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. But indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers. Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in power and who tilled the earth and populated it more than these have populated it? And their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves. Then the end of those who did evil was that they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them﴾ [al-Rum].

٢٢ - The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says to His Messenger (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): ﴿Say, "I am not something new among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf], meaning: I was not an innovator, originating from my own self what I call to; I only follow what is revealed to me.

٢٣ - The Truth, glory be to Him, says addressing His Prophet: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you, but it is not you that they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah. And messengers had been denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and were harmed until Our victory came to them. And there is none to alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the messengers﴾ [34] [al-Anʿam].

٢٤ - This was at the Second Pledge of al-ʿAqaba, the Great One. When the people gathered for the pledge to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿUbada al-Anṣari said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, do you know what you are pledging to this man?" They said: "Yes." He said: "You are pledging to him to wage war on the red and the black of mankind. So if you see that when your wealth is afflicted by calamity and your nobles are killed you will hand him over, then leave him now, for by Allah, if you do that, it is disgrace in this world and the Hereafter. But if you see that you will fulfill what you have invited him to, despite the loss of wealth and the killing of nobles, then take him, for by Allah, he is the good of this world and the Hereafter." They said: "We will take him despite the calamity of wealth and the killing of nobles. What then is for us, O Messenger of Allah, if we fulfill it?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand," and he extended his hand, and they pledged to him [Sirat al-Nabi by Ibn Hisham, 2/55].

٢٥ - **al-Khawr**: weakness. Khāra al-rajul: the man weakened and broke down. **al-Khawwār**: the weak one who has no endurance in hardship [Lisan al-ʿArab, entry: khawara].

٢٦ - **al-Makāna**: elevation of rank, dignity and deliberation. The Most High says: ﴿Say, "O my people, work according to your position..."﴾ [al-Anʿam], meaning: with dignity, deliberation and insight. It was also read as *ʿalā makānatikum* in the plural [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/232].
And **al-makāna** is the state in which a person is, whether of power or weakness, faith or disbelief. From this is His saying: ﴿Work according to your position...﴾ [Hud], meaning: according to the state you are in. And His saying: ﴿And We would have transformed them in their places...﴾ [Yasin], meaning: in the state they were in during their obstinacy and disbelief [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/179, 180].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 121:

Meaning: "Do what you will." This means that the Prophet (ﷺ) relies on a strong foundation of faith in a God whom it does not dismay that the adversary prepares himself against him. He (ﷺ) and those with him do not confront the adversary with their own persons, nor with their number and equipment; rather, they confront him with the firm pillar on which they lean, which is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He.

In our daily lives we see that any commander in a battle feels confident when he learns that reinforcements will reach him from the homeland for which he fights, because they will strengthen his power. How much more so, then, with the aid that comes from One whose resources never run out (1), and against whom no one can seek protection; He grants protection and no one can be given protection against Him.

Accordingly, we observe that the prophets took shelter under that canopy. Moses (peace be upon him), when Pharaoh almost caught up with him, and his people saw that there was no escape for them, the sea before them and the enemy behind them, cried out: ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken.(2)..(61)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. But Moses (peace be upon him) reassured them: ﴿Never! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.(62)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. Moses (peace be upon him) knew that he was supported by the power of God, not by the power of his people, and God (glorified be He) aided him with a new miracle: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff..(63)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. So the sea split, opening between its waters a dry path. Moses (peace be upon him) and his people walked on it. Moses considered cutting off the way to his enemy, so that he would not follow the same path that had been split by God's command through the miracle of striking the sea with the staff. Moses (peace be upon him) wished to strike the sea a second time so that it would return to its former state of flowing water. God (glorified be He) said to him: ﴿And leave the sea calm(3); indeed, they are an army to be drowned.(24)﴾ [al-Dukhan]. That is: leave it as it is, so that Pharaoh will be deceived and walk on the dry path; then God (glorified be He) will return the sea to what it was. Thus God (glorified be He) saved and destroyed with one thing (4), and this is something that none can accomplish except God alone (glorified be He and exalted).

Thus God (glorified be He) bestows upon those who believe in Him the ability to challenge the disbelievers. Faith as a whole is a battle of challenge: a challenge concerning the truthfulness of the Messenger as one who conveys from God, accompanied by a miracle that indicates his message; and a challenge concerning the support of the Messenger and those with him from a small believing group, who then overcome the large disbelieving multitude.

God (glorified be He) says: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God. And God is with the patient.(249)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Thus the challenge spreads in the battles of faith.

Every messenger was distinguished by a miracle with which he first challenged; then its role ended, so that after it a method was sent down to him from heaven to give good news of it to his people. But the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was distinguished by a miracle that does not end, and it is the very substance of his method, because he is a messenger to all times and all places (5); therefore there had to be a miracle that accompanies the method until the Day of Resurrection.

Accordingly, we find every believer in the Muhammadan message saying: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and the Qur'an is his miracle until the Hour arises.

And God (glorified be He) says here: ﴿And say to those who do not believe: Work according to your position.. (121)﴾ [Hud].

We know that each of us has a place, that is, a space and a body (6). It is said: so-and-so has a standing (makanah) among the people, that is, he has a distinguished position, which if he leaves, no one else can fill; it is a place that indicates honor, greatness, sovereignty, prominence and eminence of rank.

So His true word: ﴿Work according to your position.. (121)﴾ [Hud]: that is, work (7) according to the measure of your capacity, in equipment and in number, for Muhammad (ﷺ) has a Lord who will guide and support him. In this there is a threat to them, not a command to them, because as disbelievers they will never comply with an order from their enemy.

Had they complied with the command of Muhammad and the Lord of Muhammad, they would not have been disbelievers; rather, they would have become among the obedient.

When He (glorified be He) says to them at the end of the verse: ﴿Indeed, we are working.. (121)﴾ [Hud], the meaning is that all that lies within your capacities is limited, because you are among the transient, the newly originated (8); but the action of God (exalted be He) is not limited, because He (glorified be He) is eternal, without beginning, and no limits confine Him. The work of the originated, created being will not contradict the work of the Eternal, Eternally Pre-existent; the power of the created, originated being is bestowed upon it by another, whereas the power of the Truth (glorified be He) is intrinsic to Him.

We know that any work is measured by the power of its doer. The error of those who turn away from God's method is that when a work comes, they forget who did the work; if the work were from human action, it would be right for a human to speak, but when the work is from God (exalted be He), the human must keep to his limits.

An example of this: those who disputed about the matter of the Night Journey, concerning which the Truth (blessed and exalted be He) said: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed.. (1)﴾ [al-Isra'].

They said: We travel to it on the backs of camels for a month, so how does he claim that he reached it in a single night?

The reply to them was: Muhammad did not say that he traveled from the Sacred House to the Farthest Mosque by his own power; rather, he was taken by night, and the one who did that act was God (glorified be He), not Muhammad, so this act is measured by the power of God and not by the power of Muhammad.

1 - God (glorified be He) says: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they might increase in faith along with their faith; and to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth; and God is ever Knowing and Wise (4)﴾ [al-Fath], and He (exalted be He) says concerning the battle of Hunayn: ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see.. (26)﴾ [al-Tawbah]..
2 - Adraka: he overtook him, reached him. God (exalted be He) says: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him..(90)﴾ [Yunus], figuratively, as if drowning were a pursuing enemy that caught Pharaoh and destroyed him.
Al-darak (with a fatha or sukun on the ra') is a verbal noun meaning attainment and catching up. God (exalted be He) says: ﴿You will not fear being overtaken, nor will you be afraid.(77)﴾ [Ta-Ha], i.e., you need not fear that Pharaoh and his soldiers will overtake you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/226]..
3 - Rahā al-bahru yarhū rahwan: the sea became still, so it is rahin. Rahw is a verbal noun described by its own form, as God (exalted be He) says: ﴿And leave the sea calm..(24)﴾ [al-Dukhan], with its waves still, so that they would be deceived and descend into it; or with the soul still, in which case it is a circumstantial clause relating to the object, the sea, or to the subject, the hidden pronoun "you," which is Moses (peace be upon him), meaning: he would be calm and reassured of deliverance. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/279]..
4 - So God (glorified be He) saved Moses and those with him, and destroyed Pharaoh and his soldiers with one thing, and this is evidence of the absoluteness of His power..
5 - From Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I have been favoured over the prophets in six ways: I have been given concise speech (jawami' al-kalim), I have been supported by terror (al-ru'b), spoils of war have been made lawful for me, the earth has been made for me a purifier and a place of prayer, I have been sent to all creation, and the prophets have been sealed with me." Related by Muslim in his Sahih [523], Book of Mosques..
6 - Al-jirm: the body or substance; it is embodied, so it occupies a place and space in the medium in which it is..
7 - The imperative here is for threat, which is one of the varieties of the sciences of rhetoric (balaghah)..
8 - Al-ahdath: things that come into being, that is, they had no existence and then came to be, and the factors of annihilation and change come upon them..
9 - Asra bihi: made him travel, or carried him with him to journey by night. God (exalted be He) says: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night..(1)﴾ [al-Isra'], and this indicates that God was a companion to the Messenger (ﷺ), aiding and helping him in his night journey. And His word: ﴿So travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued.(23)﴾ [al-Dukhan], God (glorified be He) commanded Moses (peace be upon him) to lead his people in a night journey, being for them a guide, helper and director. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/312], adapted..
10 - Al-barakah: increase of good, growth and happiness. God (exalted be He) says: {We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth..(96)} [al-A'raf], and Allah blessed a thing, blessed in it, upon it, and around it. God (exalted be He) says: {So when he came to it, he was called: Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it..(8)} [al-Naml], and His word: {Lit from a blessed tree, an olive..(35)} [al-Nur], meaning: great in good, abundant in benefit. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/65].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 122:

The Truthful One (Al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And wait, indeed We are waiting.(1) (122)﴾:

In this verse we perceive warning and threat. The disbelievers await the promise of Satan to them, and the believers await the promise of the Most Merciful to them.(2)

Therefore the believers will say to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true; so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?...(44)﴾ [al-A'raf]. In the disbelievers' waiting there is a threat to them, and in the believers' waiting there is a strengthening of their hearts. Had the future events not come as the Qur'an said, the believers would have doubted, but the believers did not doubt. Thus we are assured that the statement of waiting could only have come from one who is certain that what is in this statement will be realized.

Reality has also come to support some of the events that came in the Qur'an.

Did not the word of the Truthful One, glory be to Him, come down: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.(3) (45)﴾ [al-Qamar]? The revelation of this wise saying came at a time of the weakness of the beginning,(4) to the extent that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him,(5) said: "What multitude will be routed?" For ʿUmar at that time was perceiving the weak state of the believers and the inability of some believers to protect themselves. Then came the Battle of Badr, so that the believers saw the truth of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had foretold.

It is remarkable that he ﷺ marked on the ground the sites where some of the great disbelievers would fall, and even the places where they would be struck, and this came as a Qur'an recited through the ages, such as the words of the Truthful One: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout.(7) (16)﴾ [al-Qalam]. Thus the Truthful One, glory be to Him, willed that the reality should come to confirm the truthfulness of the Messenger ﷺ, just as He willed to send down to the Messenger snapshots from the stories of the messengers who preceded him, to strengthen his resolve, to make his heart firm, and to remind the believers so that they might increase in faith.

(1) Intazarahu: to watch for it and anticipate it. The Exalted said: ﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed they are waiting (30)﴾ [al-Sajdah], i.e., watch what will befall them; indeed they are watching. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/272].
(2) The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and failed you...(22)﴾ [Ibrahim].
(3) Wallā al-muhārib duburahu: a metaphor for his fleeing. The Exalted said: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs (45)﴾ [al-Qamar], i.e., they will flee. The plural of dubur is adbār. The Exalted said: ﴿And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped (111)﴾ [Al 'Imran], i.e., they will flee from you in defeat. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs (45)﴾ [al-Qamar], i.e., the army they gathered will be routed, or their group will be routed. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/127] with adaptation.
(4) Ibn ʿAbbas said: Between the revelation of this verse and Badr there were seven years, transmitted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir [9/6546].
(5) Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir, attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim, that ʿUmar said: "What multitude will be routed? What multitude will be overcome?" ʿUmar said: "When the day of Badr came, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ leaping in his armour, and he was saying: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs (45)﴾ [al-Qamar], and on that day I understood its interpretation."
(6) Muslim recorded in his Sahih (2873) from Anas ibn Malik who said: "We were with ʿUmar between Makkah and Madinah, and he began to tell us about the people of Badr, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to show us the sites where the people of Badr would fall, the day before, saying: 'This is the fall of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills.' ʿUmar said: By the One who sent him with the truth, they did not deviate from the boundaries that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had set." Similarly Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad [3/219, 258], and in it: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "would place his hand on the ground here and here, and not one of them moved from the place of the Messenger of Allah's hand."
(7) Al-Khurtum: the nose or the front of the nose; the nose is a symbol of honour among the Arabs, and it is said "proud of noses" meaning honourable. Branding on the nose is humiliation and degradation. The Exalted said: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout (16)﴾ [al-Qalam], i.e., We will humiliate him with the utmost humiliation. It was said that these verses were revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who was struck on his nose with a sword on the day of Badr before his death, and the verse was confirmed concerning him, informing of what would happen to him before it happened. Two of his sons embraced Islam, one of them our master Khalid ibn al-Walid, the Sword of Allah, conqueror of Iraq and subduer of the Romans. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/119].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 11, verse 123 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes Surah Hud with His noble words:
﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen (ghayb) of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter returns. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (123)

That is: what has come in the mention of this Wise Reminder is a matter unseen from you, which Allah, glory be to Him, informs you of through what is sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Allah, glory be to Him, willed to preserve this Wise Reminder, as an assurance from Him that when He informs us in the Qur'an of a report whose time has not yet come, we know that He has informed of it by virtue of His eternal knowledge of the cosmos and what takes place in it, and by virtue of His absolute power that controls what becomes of those He chooses among creatures, believers and disbelievers alike. So when the Qur'an tells us of something hidden from man, we should know that it is a report of absolute truthfulness.

There is much that is hidden from man. There is a veil between man's means of perception and some of the things perceived. Sometimes the veil is a veil of time: when Allah, exalted is He, reports a matter we did not witness, from a remote past that has penetrated (awghala) deeply into time, which the Prophet ﷺ did not read in any book nor heard from any teacher, this is an unveiling of the veil of the past.

For this reason, scholars call some surahs of the Qur'an "the 'mā kunta' verses of the Qur'an," such as the Truth's words: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens (aqlam), [to see] which of them would be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾ (Al 'Imran, 44), and other verses that begin with His words: "mā kunta" (you were not).

There were people in that past who perceived what had become unseen to the Messenger and those with him; yet Allah made this unseen manifest to the Messenger who never sat with a teacher, by the testimony of his enemies. Likewise, Allah, glory be to Him, unveiled for His Messenger the veil of time and the veil of place.

Whoever has the veil of time and the veil of place unveiled for him, the veil of the future is also unveiled for him. The One who unveiled this is the Truth, glory be to Him, who decreed the coming of this world and what will happen in it until the Hour is established.

Allah, glory be to Him, has concealed in the Qur'an matters which, if they had been unveiled at the time of the Prophet's mission, the discussion of them would have been beyond the level of minds and comprehension. He, glory be to Him, spoke of future events concerning the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which none of them could have anticipated.

There was a battle between the two most advanced civilisations contemporary with Islam: the civilisation of Persia and the civilisation of Rome. The two civilisations were contending for dominance and the expansion of spheres of influence. Persia, which does not believe in a god, defeated the Roman Empire, which professed Christianity and did not believe in the message of Muhammad, the Seal.

Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ grieved over the defeat of those who believed in a God in the heavens. So Allah, glory be to Him, consoled His Messenger, and the Truth, glory be to Him, sent down a Qur'an to be recited through the ages and all times, bearing the prophecy of the Romans' victory after their defeat by the Persians.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ (Ar-Rum, 1-5)

Thus the prophecy comes in the Qur'an bearing a specification of the time of the Romans' victory: "within a few years," and "bid'" (a few) refers to from three to nine years.

If it is said: "That is the prophecy of Muhammad," we say: Did Muhammad know the news of the two armies or the secrets of the internal politics of both?

The Romans' victory came as the Qur'an specified, and this was a tearing away of veils: the veil of time, the veil of place, and the veil of people. Allah, the Lord of absolute unseen, revealed it to His Messenger ﷺ.

The absolute unseen is that which none knows except the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, and which has no preliminaries. Allah unveils it to whom He chooses, in confirmation of His words, glory be to Him: ﴿[He is] the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to one He has approved of among messengers...﴾ (Al-Jinn, 26-27). This absolute unseen differs from the restricted unseen, which has preliminaries, through which a person may take steps and arrange them until he reaches the discovery of a secret of the cosmos.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except for what He wills...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 255).

Thus we know that all discoveries were present in the cosmos and hidden within it, and Allah, exalted is He, made for each concealed thing a birth. The steam engine and its use in motion had a birth; electricity had a birth; the discovery of the atom as a force and a source of energy had a birth. Every discovery and invention has a birth, and the births of the unseen follow one another in the future. In their birth is the faith of certainty in the One who concealed them and manifested them, Allah, the Wise.

This birth may come through investigation and research; or Allah may manifest it without research; or He may manifest it by chance, as He manifested the law of buoyancy arising from the principle of "Archimedes," and as the Truth, glory be to Him, manifested the law of gravity by chance. That is: a cause among causes made one of His servants search for something, and something appeared to him that he was not seeking. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, attributed the encompassing (of knowledge) to Himself, glory be to Him.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter returns...﴾ (Hud, 123). He did not say: "to Him the whole matter returns" in the sense of... rather, because He, glory be to Him, has fixed every creature according to a measure.

And to Allah belongs the highest likeness: as you set the alarm clock for a specific time, and as the fighter sets the bomb to explode at a specific time, and the whole cosmos is arranged according to this arrangement.

And Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Ya-Sin, 82). So everything returns to Allah at the time Allah has willed.

Or: the matter is everything related to a living being. Because the Truth, glory be to Him, has created in the cosmos things and reserved their ownership to Himself, glory be to Him; the Truth does not benefit from them, but man benefits from them, though he does not approach them or own them. Like the sun, which sends forth its rays, and man benefits from its light and heat, yet it does not enter into man's ownership, because it is among the fundamentals of life. Therefore He did not give man, whom Allah distinguished with the faculty of choice, the right of ownership of it or of approaching it, so that he would not tamper with it.

Likewise, all the fundamentals of life the Truth, glory be to Him, placed in His sole authority, and He did not entrust any of His creatures with them, such as the earth with its elements, and likewise water and air, so that no one tampers with the breaths of air belonging to another.

Allah willed to place the fundamentals in His hand without giving ownership of them to anyone, out of mercy towards us, for He, glory be to Him, knew that man, with the changes to which he is subject, may misuse those fundamentals.

Allah subjected these fundamentals to serve all creatures, and subjected some creatures for man to govern, and some other creatures man could not subject; and even man's own strength, Allah, glory be to Him, willed to make subject to change: the strong proceeds to weakness, and the poor may become rich.

Thus it is established for us that all we possess is granted to us by Allah, exalted is He, and there is nothing in us that is intrinsically ours; and what we possess today does not go beyond a temporary ownership. When the Day of Resurrection comes, everything we possess returns to Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Ghafir, 16)

Likewise, the limbs bear witness against man, because they depart from the subjection they had in the world.

And since the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (Hud, 123), He, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 6). The Truth, glory be to Him, had been alerting mankind since the revelation of the Qur'an to the importance of what lies beneath the soil of treasures with which Allah, exalted is He, favours His servants, that He owns them.

And we now live by extracting what is stored beneath the soil.

And when the Truth, glory be to Him, says here, in the verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿And to Him the whole matter returns...﴾ (Hud, 123), there in is a warning to every person, so that he acts seeking salvation on a day when he will have no way over himself on the Day of Resurrection.

Let every person know that everything he enjoys is from the overflowing bounties of the Supreme Truth, who gave man his power from the innermost of His might, glory be to Him, and gave him richness from the innermost of His richness, glory be to Him, and gave him wisdom from the innermost of His wisdom, glory be to Him, and gave him [grasping and] extending from the innermost of His power, glory be to Him: the overflowings belong to the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

When He wills, He strips away all bounties and the matter returns to Him, for the whole matter belongs to Him, glory be to Him.

If the Qur'an tells you of a matter whose preliminaries are hidden from you, know that the One who revealed this Book does not lose from His knowledge the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was certain that when Allah commanded him to threaten the enemies of the religion, He was reassuring him that the return of all matters is to Him, glory be to Him.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him were assured that if the enemies of the religion are not requited in this world, tomorrow all matters will return to Allah; and even if the Truth has granted them possessions, He will strip them of that ownership in the Hereafter; and even if He gave them choice in this world, the choice to believe and obey or to disbelieve and disobey, that choice will be removed from them in the Hereafter, and every owner of a dominion, his dominion passes after him to Allah.

Since the matter is so, let us worship Allah alone, glory be to Him, for He is the owner of the matter in the past, His is the matter now, and His is the matter in what is to come.

He, glory be to Him, who willed, made for man three times: a time that preceded the existence of Adam; a time from after Adam until the existence of each of us; then a future time without end. Thus each of us has a past time, a present time, and a future time, and each of us revolves in the orbit of events.

It is logical, after you have enjoyed your existence in life and matured intellectually, that you ask about your past and the history of the human race.

In this case you are dependent on the trustworthiness of the narrator: does he speak the truth or lie? Especially if the account concerns the history before Adam; you must say to yourself: "None can tell me of that except the One who created me."

And when His Messenger, Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, informs you of the beginning of creation, saying: "Allah was, and there was nothing with Him" (1).

This means that the only truthful one from whom we can accept speech about what passed before Adam is Allah, exalted is He.

And if you ask: why did I find myself in my time and not in another time? Here you will say to yourself, if you are a believer: "The will and volition of the One who brought me into existence is what preferred my existence in this time over any other time."

You must ask yourself: what is required of me?

And you will find that what is required of you is movement in life, because that movement is the dividing line between life and death. The Truth says: ﴿He brought you into being from the earth and made you inhabit it (61)﴾ (Hud). Allah, exalted is He, has given you reason to think, given you energy to act, and subjected to you the cosmos with the provision hidden in it, so that you may extract it and make your living from it.

Thus it becomes clear to you that everything requires you to move, and in your movement you need energy that you take from what is above you and give to what is below you; therefore you take energy from what is above you and give to what is below you.

And you know that the highest of what is required of you is that you pray before Allah five times every day, to charge your energy and go out into life after renewing your allegiance to the One who created you and created all the worlds; and if you stand well before Allah, your future will come built upon that excellence.

The Truth, glory be to Him, gives us an example of these two movements, saying: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade...﴾ (Al-Jumu'ah, 9). This is a movement in which a person takes energy from above: hastening to the remembrance of Allah and leaving trade for the sake of the remembrance...

---

1. Ghayb (unseen): the verb ghāba yaghību means to be hidden from the eye or from human knowledge; the noun ghayb names what is absent and hidden. Allah says: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 3). The ghayb is what is absent from the eyes, such as Paradise, Hell, angels and jinn; its plural is ghuyūb. Allah says: ﴿Indeed You, You are the Knower of the unseen things﴾ (Al-Ma'idah, 109). [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/64].

2. Awghala fi al-shay' wughūlan: entered into it; wagala: went far and went away; tawaghala fi al-ard: went far into the earth; likewise awghala fi al-'ilm (went deep into knowledge). [Lisan al-'Arab, root w-gh-l].

3. Allah says: ﴿And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾ (Al-'Ankabut, 48). Mujahid said: the People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad ﷺ neither wrote nor read, so this verse was revealed. Al-Nahhas said: it is a proof of his prophethood to the Quraysh, since he did not read or write and did not mix with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Mecca; so he brought them reports of the prophets and nations, and doubt and suspicion were removed. [See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 7/5241].

4. Al-aqlam: plural of qalam, an arrow or a piece of wood resembling it on which a sign was written indicating a portion given to whoever drew it by his name; they used it in lots. Among its use in lots is His saying: ﴿When they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be responsible for Mary...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 44). Here aqlam means the arrows of drawing lots; the lot was cast and the arrow of Zakariyya won, so he became guardian of Mary. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/132].

5. Kafalahu yakfuluhu kafalan wa kafalah: sheltered, cared for and reared him; akfalahu al-yatim, and kafalahu al-yatim: entrusted him with its guardianship and care, as in His saying: ﴿And Zakariyya became her guardian﴾ (Al 'Imran, 37), making him her guardian; and Allah says: ﴿So he said, "Entrust her to me and make me overcome in speech"﴾ (Sad, 23), i.e., he said: make me her guardian, caring for her affairs, having authority. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/167].

6. These are nine verses in the Qur'an, including the verse of Al 'Imran that the Shaykh mentioned here, and including:
- ﴿These are among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you; you did not know them, neither you nor your people, before this...﴾ (Hud, 49).
- ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they resolved their affair while they were plotting﴾ (Yusuf, 102).
- ﴿And you were not at the western side when We conveyed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses﴾ (Al-Qasas, 44).
- ﴿But We produced generations, and lifetimes passed over them. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending [messengers]﴾ (Al-Qasas, 45).
- ﴿And you were not beside the mount when We called, but it is a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they might remember﴾ (Al-Qasas, 46).
- ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, but it is a mercy from your Lord; so never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾ (Al-Qasas, 86).
- ﴿And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾ (Al-'Ankabut, 48).
- ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants...﴾ (Ash-Shura, 52).

7. Tamara al-shay': hid it; al-matmurah: a pit beneath the earth, or a place beneath the earth prepared secretly in which food and wealth are hidden, i.e., concealed. [Lisan al-'Arab, root t-m-r].

8. In the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ grief over the defeat of the Romans, who are People of the Book, is clear evidence that Islam is the comprehensive unity of the heavenly religions, and that all religions are like one body: when one limb complains, the rest of the body responds with wakefulness and fever. The hadith...
