Indeed, the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ feeling of defeat and his grief over it is evidence of the breadth and universality of Islam, in confirmation of the Almighty's words: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah and what We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein...﴾ (Ash-Shura, 13).

9 - *Yasru*: he uncovers from his heart its grief (*al-umm*) and removes it. *Wa-sara 'anhu*: the fear was uncovered from him. This image recurs in the hadith, especially in the description of the descent of revelation upon him, and all these usages carry the meaning of uncovering and removal [Lisan al-'Arab, root: s-r-w].

10 - *Adna al-ardh* (the nearest land): the nearest of it. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: If the battle was at Adhri'at, between the lands of the Arabs and Syria, then it is "the nearest land" measured from Makkah. If the battle was at al-Jazirah, a place between Iraq and Syria, then it is the nearest land measured from the land of Kisra. And if it was in al-Urdunn (Jordan), then it is nearer to the land of the Romans [quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 7/5260].

11 - *Al-bid'*: it is what lies between three and nine. Al-Tirmidhi reported in his Sunan [3194] from Nayyar ibn Mukram al-Aslami, who said: When there was revealed: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will overcome, within a few years...﴾ [al-Rum], Persia was then dominant over the Romans on the day this verse was revealed, and the Muslims loved the Romans to prevail over them, because they and the Romans were People of the Book. Concerning this, God the Exalted said: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God; He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Rum]. The Quraysh, however, loved Persia to prevail, because they and the Persians were not People of the Book nor a faith that awaits resurrection. When God the Exalted revealed this verse, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) went out crying in the outskirts of Makkah: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will overcome, within a few years...﴾ [al-Rum]. Some men of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: "That is a wager between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will overcome the Persians within a few years. Shall we bet you on that?" He said: "Yes." This was before the prohibition of gambling. Abu Bakr and the polytheists agreed upon the wager, and they said to Abu Bakr: "How much will you stake?" (The *bid'* is from three years to nine years.) "Set between us and you a middle term to which we will refer." He said: So they set between them six years. He said: The six years passed before they [the Romans] prevailed, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's stake. When the seventh year came, the Romans prevailed over the Persians. The Muslims then blamed Abu Bakr for setting six years, because God the Exalted had said: "within a few years." He said: And many people embraced Islam at that time. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hadith that is ṣaḥīḥ, ḥasan, gharīb.

12 - *Al-ghayb*: a verbal noun, and what is hidden and concealed is also called by it. The Truth (al-Haqq) said: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen...﴾ [al-Baqarah]. *Al-ghayb* is what is hidden from the eyes, such as Paradise, Hell, the angels and the jinn. Its plural is *ghuyub*. God the Exalted said: ﴿And You are the Knower of the unseen matters﴾ [al-Ma'idah, 109] [al-Qamus al-Qawim, vol. 2, p. 64].

13 - God the Exalted described the sun in His Qur'an, saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance...﴾ [Yunus], and He said of it: ﴿...and made the sun a lamp﴾ [Nuh]. *Al-siraj* is the lamp that gives light and emits heat.

14 - God the Exalted says: ﴿God is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you; and He subjected to you the ships to sail through the sea by His command, and He subjected to you the rivers. And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constant in their courses, and He subjected to you the night and the day﴾ [Ibrahim]. These two verses gather the basic elements of the cosmos of which the noble Shaykh al-Sha'rawi spoke: the heavens, the earth, water, fruits, ships, the sea, rivers, the sun, the moon, the night, and the day.

15 - In this regard the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful﴾ [al-Rum, 54].

16 - God the Exalted says: ﴿Do they not see that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. And for them in them are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin, 71–73].

17 - This is in His saying: ﴿On the day when the enemies of God are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks. Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins: "Why did you bear witness against us?" They will say: "God has made us speak, who made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned." And you did not conceal yourselves so that your hearing and your eyes and your skins would not bear witness against you, but you assumed that God does not know much of what you do﴾ [Fussilat, 19–22].

18 - *Al-thara*: moist earth, or earth in general. God the Exalted said: ﴿And what is beneath the soil﴾ [Ta-Ha, 6], meaning: beneath all the layers of the earth [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/107].

19 - The expression "grasping" (*al-qabḍ*) is used as a metaphor for straitened livelihood, and "spreading" (*al-basṭ*) as a metaphor for its abundance, as in His saying: ﴿And God grasps and spreads, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah, 245], meaning: He narrows provision and widens it for whomever He wills [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/96], with adaptation. And "spreading the hand" is used as a metaphor for generosity and liberality, or for extravagance and excessive spending of wealth. God says of Himself: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills...﴾ [al-Ma'idah, 64], a metaphor for generosity and liberality [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/66].

20 - *'Azaba al-amr ya'zubu*: it went far away, became hidden, and its pursuit became difficult. God the Exalted said: ﴿Nor is hidden from your Lord the weight of an atom's particle on earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear record﴾ [Yunus, 61], meaning: nothing is hidden from Him or far from Him, so He knows the small and the great of matters and things [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/18].

21 - *Al-khiyar*: a noun derived from choosing. "Khayyartuhu bayn al-shay'ayn" means: I delegated to him the choice. *Takhayyara al-shay'*: he chose it. *Al-ikhtiyar* means selection, and likewise *al-takhayyur* [Lisan al-'Arab, root: kh-y-r], with adaptation.

22 - This has come in many verses, among them:
- ﴿Say: The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve...﴾ [al-Kahf, 29].
- ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan, 3].
And the general principle of Islam is: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become distinct from error...﴾ [al-Baqarah, 256].

23 - *Al-hadath* among the events of time: a calamity that descends. *Hadthan al-dahr* and its events: its vicissitudes and misfortunes [Lisan, root: h-d-th].

24 - On this the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation...﴾ [al-Kahf, 51]. And He said concerning the creation of the angels: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf, 19].

25 - It was reported by Ahmad in his Musnad [4/431], and by al-Bukhari in his Ṣaḥīḥ [3191], from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn, and its complete wording is: "God was, and nothing was with Him. His throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Reminder (al-Dhikr) everything, and He created the heavens and the earth."

26 - *Ista'mara fi al-makan*: he made him settle it and cultivate it. Ibn Manzur said in [Lisan al-'Arab, root: '-m-r]: "*Ista'marakum fiha*" means: He permitted you to build it and to extract its resources, and He made you its builders.
